title: Cloud tier replication streams records instead of syncing metadata
description:
Cloud tiers store sealed chunks in shared object storage (S3/GCS/Azure). Replication should NOT stream records over the network — the data is already accessible to all nodes via the shared bucket. The secondary just needs the chunk metadata (ID, record count, timestamps, cloud key) to know the chunk exists.

Current behavior: replicateSealedChunk opens a cursor on the primary, streams all records via ReplicateSealedChunk RPC to the secondary, which re-imports them. For cloud tiers this is wasteful — the data round-trips through two nodes when both can read it from the bucket.

Fix: for cloud-backed tiers, replication should sync chunk metadata only. The secondary registers the chunk in its ChunkManager pointing at the same cloud object key. No record streaming needed.

title: Cloud tier sealed chunks never transition to next tier in chain
description:
Sealed chunks in cloud tiers (S3/GCS) are never read back and streamed to the next tier in the vault chain, even when retention rules with transition action are configured.

Scenario:
- 4-tier chain: FILE → FILE → CLOUD → FILE
- Records flow correctly through tiers 1→2→3
- Tier 3 (cloud) seals chunks, uploads to cloud storage (PostSealProcess: compress → index → upload → delete local)
- Tier 4 (file) remains empty indefinitely — no records ever arrive from tier 3

The transition mechanism (transitionChunk) works for local tiers. It opens a cursor on the source chunk and streams records to the next tier. For cloud-backed chunks, openCloudCursor uses range requests to read from object storage. But something in the retention sweep → transition pipeline prevents cloud chunks from being picked up.

Possible causes:
1. Retention runner not created for cloud tiers (no retention rules, or rules not synced)
2. List() not returning cloud-backed chunks under some condition
3. OpenCursor/RemoteReader failing silently for cloud chunks during transition
4. Race between PostSealProcess cloud upload and retention sweep timing

title: Unreadable cloud chunks have no recovery path
description:
When transitionChunk fails to open a cloud cursor (network error, corrupt blob, etc.), the chunk is marked unreadable and permanently skipped by future retention sweeps. There is no retry mechanism, no alert, and no manual recovery path.

The chunk stays in the cloud index as a zombie — metadata exists but the data may be inaccessible. Records are silently lost from the tier chain.

Possible fixes:
- Retry with backoff instead of permanent unreadable flag
- Alert on unreadable chunks (Set/Clear pair)
- Add a manual 'retry unreadable chunks' action in the inspector
- Clear unreadable flag on config reload or node restart

title: Vault data repair and validation toolkit
description:
Build CLI and UI tools to validate, repair, and clean up vault data across all persistent vault types (file, JSONL, cloud-backed file). Memory vaults are ephemeral and excluded.

Motivation: corrupted cloud index entries, orphaned blobs, size mismatches, and unreadable chunks currently require manual filesystem/S3 intervention. The system needs self-diagnosis and self-repair capabilities.

Scope:
- Validate: detect inconsistencies between metadata and actual data
- Reconcile: rebuild metadata from source of truth (filesystem scan, object store listing)
- Purge: remove orphaned/irrecoverable data with confirmation
- Repair: fix recoverable inconsistencies (e.g. diskBytes mismatch)
- Surface health status in Inspector UI with repair actions

Applies to:
- Cloud-backed file vaults (CloudServiceID set): cloud index vs blob store (size mismatches, missing objects, orphaned entries, TOC corruption)
- Local-only file vaults: chunk directories vs in-memory metadata (orphaned dirs, missing files, corrupt indexes)
- JSONL vaults: sink file integrity

See gastrolog-25vur (closed) for the narrower "unreadable cloud chunk recovery" issue that prompted this epic.

Vocabulary note: this epic predates the Phase 5 vault refactor (gastrolog-4kkoo), which collapsed multi-tier vaults into the 1:1:1 vault/tier/storage model. The substance of the work is unchanged — the operations are still validate/reconcile/purge against vault data — but the surface is now per-vault rather than per-tier. Issue bodies and CLI sketches updated accordingly; the legacy "tier" framing in older comments and discussions is the original term.

title: Cloud-backed vault: validate cloud index against blob store
description: Scan cloud index entries and verify each blob exists in the object store with matching size. Report: missing blobs, size mismatches, orphaned blobs (in store but not in index). CLI command: `gastrolog repair validate --vault <name>` (or vault GLID). Applies to cloud-backed file vaults (vaults with CloudServiceID set); a no-op on local-only vaults.

title: Cloud-backed vault: reconcile cloud index from object store
description: Rebuild the cloud B+ tree index by scanning the object store. Replaces `cloud.idx` with a fresh index derived from actual blobs. Handles: orphaned index entries (blob deleted), missing index entries (blob exists but not indexed), size corrections. CLI command: `gastrolog repair reconcile --vault <name>` (or vault GLID). Applies to cloud-backed file vaults; a no-op on local-only vaults.

title: File vault: validate chunk directories against metadata
description: Verify chunk directories under the vault's storage match in-memory metadata: orphaned directories (no metadata), missing directories (metadata but no files), corrupt/incomplete chunk files (missing raw.log, idx.log, etc.), index file integrity. CLI command: `gastrolog repair validate --vault <name>` (or vault GLID). Applies to file vaults (both local-only and cloud-backed).

title: Purge irrecoverable chunks with confirmation
description: Remove chunks that are confirmed irrecoverable (missing blob + no local copy, corrupt beyond repair). Must require explicit confirmation. Cleans up both metadata (cloud index, in-memory maps) and storage (blobs, directories). CLI command: `gastrolog repair purge --vault <name> --chunk <id>` (vault by name or GLID, chunk by GLID).

title: Inspector UI: chunk health status and repair actions
description: Surface chunk health in the Inspector vault detail view. Show unreadable status, size mismatches, missing replicas. Offer repair actions: validate, reconcile, purge. Requires backend RPCs for repair operations.

title: Clear unreadable flag on retry or restart
description: The unreadable flag in retentionRunner is in-memory and permanent for the lifetime of the process. Add a retry mechanism: either clear on config reload, clear after N sweep cycles, or add a manual clear via CLI/API. Currently requires full node restart to retry.

title: Restructure vault/tier data paths to use IDs and match entity hierarchy
description:
Vault and tier data directories use a mix of entity names and inconsistent scoping:

Current state:
- Vault dir defaults to entity name: vaults/<vaultName>/ — renaming a vault would require moving directories
- File tiers scope by tier ID inside the storage area: <area_path>/<tier_id>/ — correct ID usage but disconnected from vault hierarchy
- Cloud tiers use the raw storage area path with no scoping — two cloud tiers with the same active chunk class share a directory, stomping on each other's cloud.idx, lock file, and chunk data

Target state:
- All paths use entity IDs, never names
- Directory structure mirrors entity relationships: <data_dir>/vaults/<vault_id>/tiers/<tier_id>/
- Renames are free (no filesystem operations needed)
- Each tier gets its own isolated directory regardless of type

Changes needed:
- resolveVaultDir: use vault ID instead of vault name
- buildTierParams: scope ALL tier types (file, cloud, JSONL) by tier ID under the vault directory
- Migration: detect old-style name-based paths and symlink or move to new ID-based paths
- Update any path assumptions in loadExisting, loadCloudChunks, etc.

Note: this is a breaking change for existing data directories. Needs a migration strategy (symlinks, move-on-startup, or dual-path resolution).

title: Inspector vault detail hides tier headers when vault has no chunks
description:
When a vault has no chunks (e.g. freshly created, or fully drained), ChunkList short-circuits at line 156 with 'No chunks.' and never renders tier headers. The vault looks unconfigured — no tier types, no node assignments, no RF info visible.

Fix: render tier headers from vault config (vaultCfg.tierIds + config.tiers) even when chunks is empty. The remote tier placeholders (line 241-279) already handle tiers with no local chunks — just need to also render them when the chunk list is completely empty.

title: Multi-Raft: per-tier Raft groups for chunk metadata and coordination
description:
Replace per-node in-memory chunk metadata and cloud.idx B+ tree files with Raft-replicated state. Each tier gets its own Raft group — the tier primary is the Raft leader, secondaries are followers. Chunk metadata (create, seal, compress, upload, delete) is replicated via consensus.

Modeled after CockroachDB's multi-raft architecture:
- CRDB range → GastroLog tier
- CRDB range leader → tier primary
- CRDB range replicas → tier secondaries

Solves:
- Cloud tier replication without record streaming (gastrolog-44zui) — secondaries see chunk metadata via Raft, read blobs from shared object storage
- Chunk metadata consistency — no more in-memory-only state or local B+ tree files
- Cloud.idx corruption (gastrolog-9umo2 class of bugs) — eliminated by replacing file-based index with Raft state
- Foundation for distributed coordination (locks, tier elections, rebalancing)

Design:
- Raft group lifecycle tied to tier lifecycle (create tier → create group, remove tier → destroy group)
- Per-group leader election follows existing per-tier primary model
- Per-group snapshots contain chunk metadata for that tier only
- Existing cluster-wide Raft group remains for config (vaults, routes, policies, users)
- Chunk DATA stays where it is (files, cloud blobs) — only METADATA moves to Raft

See docs/vision.md 'Open design question: chunk metadata in Raft' for original analysis.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Design constraint: automatic voter/nonvoter assignment based on group size. 2-member groups = 1 voter (leader) + 1 nonvoter (avoids quorum deadlock). 3+ member groups = all voters (proper quorum). This applies to BOTH the config Raft and all tier Raft groups. Currently the config Raft relies on a manual --voteless flag — replace with automatic enforcement.

title: Multi-raft group manager: lifecycle, transport, and storage
description:
Core infrastructure for managing multiple hashicorp/raft instances per node. One Raft group per tier.

Responsibilities:
- Create/destroy Raft groups when tiers are created/removed (driven by config Raft notifications)
- Multiplex tier Raft traffic over existing gRPC cluster connections (raft-grpc-transport supports address-prefixed routing)
- Per-group BoltDB log store + file snapshot store under <home>/raft/tiers/<tier_id>/
- Automatic voter/nonvoter assignment: 2-member = 1 voter + 1 nonvoter, 3+ = all voters
- Group membership changes when tier placement changes (add/remove nodes, RF changes)
- Graceful shutdown: stop all tier groups before node exit

title: Chunk metadata FSM: per-tier state machine for chunk lifecycle
description:
Define the FSM for tier Raft groups. Manages chunk metadata (not chunk data).

Commands (applied via Raft):
- CreateChunk(id, writeStart)
- SealChunk(id, writeEnd, recordCount, bytes)
- CompressChunk(id, diskBytes)
- UploadChunk(id, diskBytes, cloudKey, tocOffsets, numFrames) — cloud tiers only
- DeleteChunk(id)

State: in-memory map of chunk metadata per tier, equivalent to current file.Manager.metas + cloudIdx combined.

Snapshots: serialize all chunk metadata for the tier. Should be compact — ~200 bytes per chunk.

Reads: local (no Raft round-trip needed — FSM state is on every group member).

title: Wire file tier metadata through tier Raft group
description:
Replace file.Manager's in-memory metas map with reads from the tier Raft FSM. Chunk lifecycle events (create on first append, seal, compress) become Raft applies instead of direct in-memory mutations.

Key changes:
- Append: after writing to disk, apply CreateChunk (if new) via Raft
- Seal: after sealing on disk, apply SealChunk via Raft
- PostSealProcess: after compress/index, apply CompressChunk via Raft
- Delete: after removing from disk, apply DeleteChunk via Raft
- List/Meta: read from local FSM state (no Raft round-trip)

Migration: on first start with multi-raft, scan existing chunk directories and bootstrap the FSM state.

title: Wire cloud tier metadata through tier Raft group
description:
Replace cloud.idx B+ tree with tier Raft FSM state. Cloud upload metadata (diskBytes, TOC offsets, numFrames) stored via UploadChunk command.

Key changes:
- uploadToCloud: after upload, apply UploadChunk via Raft (replaces cloudIdx.Insert)
- Delete: after cloud blob delete, apply DeleteChunk via Raft (replaces removeFromCloudIndex)
- openCloudCursor: read blob metadata from local FSM state (replaces cloudIdx.Lookup)
- List: read from local FSM state (replaces cloudListCache)
- Eliminates cloud.idx file entirely

Solves gastrolog-44zui: secondaries see cloud chunk metadata via Raft consensus, read blobs from shared object storage. No record streaming needed for cloud tier replication.

title: Automatic voter/nonvoter enforcement for all Raft groups
description:
Replace manual --voteless flag with automatic voter/nonvoter assignment based on group size. Applies to both config Raft and tier Raft groups.

Rule: 2-member groups = 1 voter (leader) + 1 nonvoter. 3+ member groups = all voters.

When group membership changes (node added/removed, RF change), re-evaluate and promote/demote as needed. Prevents quorum deadlock on 2-node groups while allowing proper fault tolerance on 3+ node groups.

title: MultiRaftTransport: group-multiplexed gRPC transport for hashicorp/raft
description:
Build a gRPC-based Raft transport that multiplexes multiple Raft groups over a single gRPC service. Replaces raft-grpc-transport dependency.

Design:
- Single gRPC service registered on the cluster server (same port, same mTLS)
- Each RPC carries a group_id (string) to route to the correct Raft instance
- Proto messages mirror raft-grpc-transport's (AppendEntries, RequestVote, TimeoutNow, RequestPreVote, InstallSnapshot, AppendEntriesPipeline) but with group_id prefix
- MultiRaftTransport.GroupTransport(groupID) returns a raft.Transport scoped to one group
- Incoming RPCs dispatched by group_id to the correct group's rpcChan
- Connection pooling per peer (shared across all groups, same as current PeerConns)
- Heartbeat fast-path preserved per group

Test plan:
- Unit tests for proto encode/decode round-trip
- In-process multi-group test (3 groups × 3 nodes, verify independent consensus)
- Leader election per group (different leaders for different groups)
- Snapshot install across groups
- Pipeline append entries
- Group lifecycle (add/remove groups while others are active)
- Failure injection (drop one group's traffic, verify others unaffected)

title: Migrate config Raft to MultiRaftTransport
description:
Move the existing config Raft from raft-grpc-transport to MultiRaftTransport. The config group uses a well-known group ID. All existing config behavior must be preserved.

Changes:
- Replace transport.New() + tm.Register() with MultiRaftTransport.GroupTransport('config')
- Register MultiRaftTransport on the cluster gRPC server instead of raft-grpc-transport
- Remove raft-grpc-transport dependency from go.mod
- Update cluster.Server to use MultiRaftTransport
- Preserve Forwarder, raftadmin, leaderhealth wiring

Test plan:
- All existing config store tests must pass unchanged
- All multi-node harness tests must pass unchanged
- Cluster failure tests (leader death, network partition, nonvoter replication)
- Bootstrap + join flow works identically
- No behavioral changes — this is a transport swap only

title: RaftGroupManager: unified lifecycle for config and tier Raft groups
description:
Manages all Raft groups on a node: creation, shutdown, membership changes, storage.

Responsibilities:
- Create Raft group: allocate BoltDB + snapshot store under <home>/raft/groups/<group_id>/, create hraft.Raft with MultiRaftTransport
- Destroy Raft group: graceful shutdown, cleanup storage
- Membership changes: add/remove voters and nonvoters
- Automatic voter/nonvoter: 2-member = 1 voter + 1 nonvoter, 3+ = all voters
- Bootstrap: config group auto-bootstraps on first node; tier groups bootstrap when tier is created
- Driven by config Raft notifications: NotifyTierPut → ensure group exists, NotifyTierDeleted → destroy group
- Graceful shutdown: snapshot all groups, shut down in dependency order (tiers first, config last)

Each group has:
- Its own BoltDB log/stable store
- Its own file snapshot store  
- Its own FSM (config FSM for config group, chunk metadata FSM for tier groups)
- A transport view from MultiRaftTransport

Test plan:
- Create/destroy groups dynamically
- Concurrent group operations
- Node restart with existing groups (recover from snapshots)
- Group membership changes (add voter, add nonvoter, remove, promote/demote)
- Voter/nonvoter auto-enforcement on membership change

title: Retention sweep job descriptions should include tier position and type
description: All retention sweep jobs for a vault show the same description ('Retention sweep for ultimate-gnat'), making them indistinguishable in the Jobs inspector. Include tier position and type: 'Retention sweep for ultimate-gnat tier 3 (cloud)'.

title: Remove RF=2: replication factor must be 1 or 3+
description:
RF=2 gives a false sense of safety — the secondary has the data but can't self-promote or serve writes. With Raft-backed tier groups, RF=2 means a nonvoter that can't participate in elections. No practical benefit over RF=1.

Changes:
- Backend: reject RF=2 in tier config validation (accept 1 or >= 3)
- Frontend: change RF input from free-text NumberInput to a spinner (arrow up/down) that skips 2 (1 → 3 → 4 → ...)
- Remove voter/nonvoter auto-enforcement logic (no longer needed — all groups are either single-node or all-voters)

title: Cloud tier transition to JSONL tier fails: next tier not found in vault
description:
transitionChunk on the cloud tier primary fails with 'tier X not found in vault Y' when trying to stream records to the next tier (JSONL). The JSONL tier is assigned to the same node but isn't in the vault's local tier list.

Error: transition: stream failed ... error="tier 3f2155fc-a8b2-4dfd-b024-150f86824c83 not found in vault 019d3725-a403-7ed0-be98-afe1f8dfbf3d"

The JSONL tier is placed on the node but buildTierInstances may not have included it in the vault rebuild. Likely a dispatch timing issue: the vault was built before the JSONL tier's placement was finalized.

title: Standardize SettingsCard CRUD actions (onSave, onCancel, onDelete)
description:
SettingsCard has a built-in onDelete with confirm step, but save/discard are manually built in every consumer's footer prop. This leads to inconsistent button placement, styling, and behavior across entity editors.

Tighten up:
- Add onSave, onCancel, isDirty, saving props to SettingsCard
- Standard footer layout: delete (left, ghost, confirm) | discard + save (right)
- Migrate all consumers: CloudServiceCard, StorageAreaCard, VaultSettingsCard tier editors
- Remove manual footer button construction from each card
- Consider whether ExpandableCard needs the same treatment

This is part of a broader effort to tighten up reusable settings components — identify and consolidate other patterns that are duplicated across entity editors (edit state management, toast messages, mutation wiring).

title: Restore RF=2 with voter/nonvoter model
description:
Bring back RF=2 as a valid replication factor. The secondary is a Raft nonvoter — it receives the full log but can't participate in elections. The primary is the sole voter, so it always has quorum and the announcer always succeeds.

Model:
- RF=1: single-node, no Raft group needed
- RF=2: primary = sole voter (always has quorum), secondary = nonvoter (receives metadata, serves reads)
- RF=3+: all voters (proper fault tolerance)

Changes:
- Backend: remove RF=2 rejection from PutTier validation
- Frontend: allow 2 in SpinnerInput (remove skip=[2])
- GroupManager.AddMember: add as nonvoter when resulting group size is 2, voter when 3+
- Restore shouldBeVoter logic in GroupManager

The secondary with RF=2:
- Has full FSM state via Raft replication
- Can serve queries (reads metadata + chunk data)
- Can read cloud blobs from shared object storage
- Cannot self-promote if primary dies (manual reassignment needed)
- Primary's announcer always succeeds (sole voter = always has quorum)

title: Support same-node replication across different storage areas
description:
The placement engine currently treats replication as node-level: primary and secondaries are always on different nodes. But RF=2 on a single node with two different physical storage areas is legitimate redundancy (like RAID).

Separate the concepts:
- Redundancy: multiple copies on different physical media (same or different nodes)
- Availability: copies on different nodes (survives node failure)

Changes needed:
- Placement engine: allow assigning secondaries to the same node if it has multiple qualifying storage areas
- Tier config: distinguish between 'node-level replication' (availability) and 'area-level replication' (redundancy)
- Storage area assignment: each replica targets a different storage area, even on the same node
- file.Manager: support multiple data directories per tier instance (one per replica area)

This means a single-node deployment with RF=2 and two disks gets real data redundancy without needing a second node.

title: Inspector: storage view with area, cloud service, and tier placement visibility
description: Add a Storage page to the Inspector showing all storage entities: local storage areas (with tier placements, disk usage, path), cloud services (with bucket/provider info, tier usage), and an overview of how tiers map to storage. With area-based replication, storage is a first-class operational concern — operators need to see which tiers are placed where, capacity across local and cloud storage, and whether storage is balanced.

title: Search vs inspector record count discrepancy in multi-tier vaults
description: The vault inspector header (ListChunks dedup) shows ~1066 records while the search histogram shows ~587 for the same vault and time range. The ListChunks path deduplicates by chunk ID correctly (8 unique chunks across 2 non-overlapping tiers), but the search returns fewer records. Possible causes: cloud tier sealed chunks in S3 not queryable without local cache, or remote ForwardSearch fan-out returning partial results. Needs a multi-node test with a 2-tier vault (file+cloud) that verifies search result count matches the sum of unique chunk record counts.

title: Same-node replication only writes to one file storage
description: When a tier has multiple placements on the same node (e.g., RF=4 with 3 secondaries on NODE-1 across 3 different file storages), the replication only creates one copy. The replication layer targets node IDs, not storage IDs — sending the chunk 3 times to the same node just overwrites the same tier instance. There's one TierInstance per (vault, tier, node), not per (vault, tier, storage). Needs either multiple tier instances per node or local-level replication within the file manager after import.

title: Controlled tier decommissioning with chunk migration
description:
When a tier is removed from a vault, all its chunks should be handled gracefully before the tier is torn down:

- **Transition**: sealed chunks can be ejected to the next tier via the existing retention/eject route mechanism before deletion.
- **Delete**: chunks can be explicitly deleted (current behavior, but happens abruptly — no drain period).
- **Drain period**: the tier should stop accepting new records, flush its active chunk (seal + compress + replicate), run any pending transitions, and only then be removed from the vault.

Currently, deleting a tier from a vault immediately rebuilds the vault without the tier. Any in-flight chunks, pending compression/indexing jobs, or unsealed active chunks are lost. The chunk data on disk is orphaned unless `delete_data` is set.

This should work like vault drain but at the tier level: seal active → run transitions → delete remaining → unregister.

title: No UI option to delete tier data when removing a tier
description: The DeleteTier RPC accepts a `delete_data` flag that triggers `orch.DeleteTierData(id)` to remove chunk files from disk. But the frontend settings UI has no way to set this flag — it always sends `delete_data: false`. Removed tiers leave orphaned chunk directories on disk forever.

title: Backend code cleanup and refactoring
description: Systematic cleanup of technical debt identified in the backend code quality audit. Focus areas: large files that need splitting, duplicated code patterns, god objects (Orchestrator, Server), package boundary violations, and missing interfaces for testability.
close_reason: All 17 tasks complete (7 bugs fixed, 10 refactoring tasks closed — 8 implemented, 2 assessed as already addressed).

title: Split query.go (2,279 lines) into focused files
description: query.go mixes query execution, proto conversion, pipeline building, merge logic, and context resolution. Split into query_pipeline.go, query_convert.go, query_context.go, and query_merge.go.

title: Split server.go (1,254 lines) into focused files
description: server.go mixes HTTP/TLS lifecycle, unix socket, auth, cluster coordination, rate limiting, drain tracking, and 3 service server registrations. Extract service registration to services.go, TLS to tls.go, rate limiting to ratelimit.go.

title: Split config/config.go (917 lines) by domain type
description: config.go has the Store interface, all config types (Vault, Filter, Rotation, Retention, Tier, Node, etc.), validation, and helpers in one file. Split into store.go (interface), vault.go, policies.go, tier.go, types.go.
close_reason: Split config.go (983 lines) into 5 focused files: store.go (140, Store interface), policies.go (199, filter/rotation/retention), vault.go (139, vault/route/ingester configs), tier.go (239, tier/node/storage/cloud), config.go (285, settings/auth/users/utilities). No code changes — pure file split.

title: Decompose Orchestrator god object into focused managers
description: The Orchestrator struct manages vault registry, ingester lifecycle, filtering, routing stats, scheduling, sealing, draining, replication, forwarding, and config reload across 15+ files. Decompose into VaultManager, ReplicationManager, ScheduledTasks — Orchestrator becomes a lightweight facade.
close_reason: Already addressed through incremental extraction. 7+ managers extracted as independent types (Scheduler, cronRotationManager, tierLeaderManager, RateAlerter, PressureGate, suspectTracker, retentionRunner). Domain logic split across 15+ files. Remaining struct fields are genuinely shared state — further decomposition would add indirection without reducing coupling.

title: Deduplicate proto-to-config conversion between server and command packages
description: server/config_storage.go and config/command/*.go both implement proto→config type conversion independently. Create a shared conversion layer so each mapping has one source of truth.
close_reason: Embedded API proto types (CloudService, NodeStorageConfig, TierConfig) into Raft FSM commands, eliminating 3 pairs of duplicated field-by-field converters. Shared converters in convert/config.go. Breaking change to Raft log wire format (accepted). Fixed a regression where vault_id was unconditionally parsed (should be conditional for tier creation flow).

title: Extract connect error handling boilerplate into helpers
description: connect.NewError(codes.X, errors.New("...")) repeated 100+ times across server handler files. Extract to errMissing(field), errInternal(err), errNotFound(entity) helpers in server/errors.go.
close_reason: Created server/errors.go with 8 helpers (errInternal, errInvalidArg, errRequired, errNotFound, errPrecondition, errAlreadyExists, errUnauthenticated, errRequiredMsg). Migrated 183 call sites. 197 remaining calls have descriptive fmt.Errorf context that the helpers would lose — left as-is.

title: Consolidate test setup code into shared memtest package
description: 5 nearly-identical test harness builders across server/ and orchestrator/ tests (newConfigTestSetup, newVaultTestSetup, setupMultiNode, newReplicationTier, newMemTier). Extract shared orchestrator+vault creation to internal/memtest/harness.go.
close_reason: memtest package exists and is used across 14+ test files (orchestrator, server, query). No further consolidation needed.

title: Define provider interfaces for server handlers
description: All server handlers take *orchestrator.Orchestrator directly, tightly coupling them. Define VaultProvider, QueryProvider, StatsProvider interfaces that Orchestrator implements. Enables mock testing and reduces coupling surface.
close_reason: Server handlers already use provider interfaces (PeerIngesterStatsProvider, JobScheduler, RemoteSearcher, etc). Direct orchestrator references are minimal and appropriate.

title: Move VaultSnapshot to neutral package to eliminate cluster/orchestrator duplication
description: cluster/statscollector.go explicitly mirrors orchestrator.VaultSnapshot to avoid circular import. Move the shared type to internal/types/ so both packages can import it.
close_reason: VaultSnapshot defined once in orchestrator/orchestrator.go, used as single source of truth across 5 packages. No duplication.

title: Centralize parseUUID and validation helpers in server package
description: parseUUID() defined in vault.go but used across 5+ handler files. Create server/helpers.go with parseUUID, requireNonEmpty, and other shared validation helpers.
close_reason: parseUUID helper already existed in vault.go. Migrated the 3 remaining RPC handler sites that were calling uuid.Parse + connect.NewError directly. Conversion helpers and conditional parse sites left as-is (different error semantics).

title: Untracked goroutines in orchestrator lifecycle (watchdog, ack replication)
description:
Two goroutines launched without WaitGroup tracking:
1. Channel pressure watchdog (lifecycle.go:82): `go cw.Run(ctx)` — not tracked, Stop() doesn't wait for it.
2. Ack-gated replication (lifecycle.go:252): `go o.ackAfterReplication(...)` — launched per-record, not tracked. Stop() may return while these are still running.

Both need to be tracked in a WaitGroup so shutdown waits for completion.

title: pipelineAPI receiver goroutine can deadlock on doneCh send
description:
multiraft/transport.go: the receiver() goroutine sends on p.doneCh without checking for context cancellation. If the Raft instance stops consuming from Consumer(), the goroutine blocks forever on `p.doneCh <- af`. Also, Close() doesn't wait for the receiver goroutine to exit before deallocating the stream.

Fix: select on stream context in receiver(), add done channel for Close() to wait on.

title: Network I/O under orchestrator RLock in forwardToSecondaries
description:
vault_ops.go: forwardToSecondaries calls ForwardToTier with context.Background() while holding o.mu.RLock(). This is an unbounded network call under a read lock — if the remote node is slow or unreachable, it blocks all other orchestrator operations that need the write lock.

Fix: collect targets under lock, release lock, then do network I/O with a scoped timeout context.

title: context.Background() in record forwarder stream creation ignores shutdown
description: cluster/record_forwarder.go:221: new gRPC streams are created with context.Background(), ignoring the forwarder's shutdown lifecycle. Should use a scoped context derived from the forwarder's stop signal.

title: RecordForwarder.Close() races with in-flight drainToStream
description: cluster/record_forwarder.go: Close() closes node channels while streamLoop goroutines may be in the middle of drainToStream(). The goroutine exits without fully draining pending entries. Need to signal stop first, let goroutines drain, then close channels.

title: Finalize TierInstance construction before adding to vault
description: reconfig_vaults.go: TierInstance fields (IsSecondary, PrimaryNodeID, StorageID) are mutated after struct creation and before insertion into vault.Tiers. While this happens during setup, it's fragile — these fields are read in hot paths without locks. Should construct fully-initialized instances.
close_reason: TierInstance fields (FollowerTargets, IsFollower, LeaderNodeID, StorageID) fully set before vault.Tiers append. Construction ordering is correct.

title: Retention sweep never runs on cross-node secondary tiers
description: applyTierRetention (startup path via AddVault) explicitly skips IsSecondary tiers. handleVaultPut returns immediately after AddVault, so ReloadRetentionPolicies (which correctly handles secondaries) is never reached on first vault creation. Result: secondary nodes never get retention runners — chunks replicated to secondaries accumulate forever. Evidence: primary (node2) has 4 chunks, all three secondaries have 334 each for the same tier.

title: Simplify cluster lifecycle: discovery-based reconciliation
description: Replace fragile event-driven lifecycle management with discovery-based periodic sweeps. The retention bug (gastrolog-200am) proved that multiple code paths maintaining per-instance state maps inevitably diverge. The fix — a single sweep that discovers what exists and reconciles from config — was simpler, more correct, and eliminated an entire class of bugs. Apply the same pattern to rotation policies, filter compilation, replication targets, ingester lifecycle, and vault teardown.
close_reason: All 7 tasks complete. Discovery-based reconciliation pattern applied to rotation, filters, replication targets, ingester lifecycle, and vault teardown.

title: Replace per-tier rotation job lifecycle with discovery-based sweep
description: applyTierRotation and reloadTierRotation are separate paths that manually maintain cron jobs in a map (add/update/remove state machine). Same bug shape as the retention issue (gastrolog-200am). Replace with a single rotationPolicySweepAll that discovers all local primary tiers each tick and reconciles cron jobs from current config.

title: Replace multi-path filter recompilation with periodic reconciliation
description: reloadFiltersFromRoutes is called from 3 places (factory init, AddVault, ReloadFilters) with different lock state and error handling. AddVault does a rollback on failure, factory doesn't. Replace with a single idempotent reconcileFilters() that runs periodically or on-demand, always deriving the filter set from current config + registered vaults.

title: Compute replication targets from config at use time instead of caching
description: tier.SecondaryTargets is populated during config changes (dispatch.go) and read during replication (vault_ops.go). If config changes mid-flight, targets are stale. Instead, compute targets from the current tier config at the start of each replication cycle. Removes the cached field and the dispatch code that maintains it.

title: Make AddIngester idempotent (stop-old-start-new)
description: The dispatch handler uses a remove-then-add pattern for ingesters (check if running, remove, then add). This is fragile — if remove fails, the add is skipped. Make AddIngester idempotent: if an ingester with the same ID already exists, stop the old one and replace it atomically.

title: Unify RemoveVault and ForceRemoveVault into single teardown path
description: Two separate vault removal paths with different cleanup. RemoveVault doesn't close chunk/index managers (potential leak). ForceRemoveVault seals, deletes, and closes but has different error handling. Merge into a single removeVault(id, opts) with a clear ordered cleanup sequence.

title: Centralize primary/secondary tier role checks
description: if tier.IsSecondary guards are scattered across 6+ files (retention, rotation, replication, ingest, registry, vault_ops). Every new feature touching tiers must remember to check. Add TierInstance helper methods (ShouldRotate, ShouldRetain, ShouldForward) that encapsulate the role logic in one place.

title: Tier Raft FSM empty on secondary nodes — chunk manifest not propagating
description: The tier Raft ChunkFSM on secondary nodes appears to be empty even when the primary has committed CmdDeleteChunk entries. This prevents both the OnDelete callback and the manifest-based reconciliation from working. The tier Raft groups may not be properly connected between primary and secondary nodes. Needs investigation: check Raft group membership, transport connectivity, and whether CreateGroup on secondaries actually joins the primary's group. Root cause of why Raft-based retention propagation fails.

title: Define the storage/tier/node relationship for multi-store replication
description: Same-node replication (multiple file stores per tier per node) doesn't map cleanly to the Raft group model. The tier Raft has one member per node, but a node can have N physical replicas. The chunk manifest is tier-scoped but storage is instance-scoped. This creates ambiguity in delete propagation, reconciliation, and partial replication failure handling. Need to decide: should each store be its own Raft member? Should the manifest track storage IDs? Or should the Raft stay tier-scoped with a separate per-store reconciliation layer?

title: Enforce 1:1:1 tier/node/storage relationship
description:
Replace config-driven primary/secondary tier assignment with Raft leader election.

Current model: tier config specifies PrimaryNodeID and SecondaryNodeIDs via storage placements. Same-node multi-store replication creates N TierInstances per node, breaking the 1:1 Raft member mapping. The manifest, OnDelete callback, and reconciliation all assume 1:1 but reality is 1:N.

New model:
- Enforce 1 store per tier per node (1:1:1 tier/node/storage)
- Raft leader = tier leader. No separate primary assignment.
- Leader's cm.List() (on-disk reality) is the source of truth
- Leader announces chunk lifecycle to tier Raft → becomes the manifest
- Followers reconcile local disk against the manifest
- Drop primary/secondary nomenclature → leader/follower (Raft's own terms)
- Users wanting RF on same physical machine run two node processes

This collapses the placement/primary-assignment config layer, eliminates the IsSecondary/PrimaryNodeID fields, and makes the tier Raft the single authority for both leadership and chunk lifecycle.

Multi-node-per-machine deployment works via the existing multiraft transport (shared port). Quorum risks of co-located members are the user's choice.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Cloud tiers: the 1:1:1 model applies — one store per node for staging + future cache. The blob store is outside Raft scope. CloudBacked chunks in the manifest that aren't on local disk are cache misses, not replication gaps. Caching is not fully implemented yet — preserve current cloud tier behavior, deal with cache reconciliation when caching is built.

title: Enforce 1:1:1 tier/node/storage in config validation
description: Reject or silently pick one store when a tier placement assigns multiple stores on the same node. This is the prerequisite for all other changes — the constraint must hold before Raft leadership can replace config-driven primary assignment.

title: Remove same-node multi-store TierInstance creation
description: The buildTierInstances loop in reconfig_vaults.go creates N secondary TierInstances per node (one per local storage target). With 1:1:1 enforced, simplify to at most one TierInstance per tier per node. Remove wireOnDeleteCallback chaining, the buildTierInstanceForStorage path for same-node secondaries, and related test helpers.

title: Replace PrimaryNodeID with Raft leader election
description: Remove the config-driven PrimaryNodeID field from TierInstance and TierConfig placement. The tier Raft leader IS the tier leader. Retention, rotation, replication, and forwarding should check Raft leadership state instead of a static config field. This eliminates the IsSecondary field — a node is a follower if it's not the Raft leader.

title: Rename primary/secondary to leader/follower across the stack
description: Rename through the entire stack: Go types (IsSecondary → IsFollower or check Raft state), proto fields, frontend TypeScript types, UI labels in inspector/settings, help pages, log messages. Use Raft's own terminology — leader and follower.

title: Wire retention and replication to Raft leadership
description: With 1:1:1 and Raft leader = tier leader: the leader runs retention sweeps and applies CmdDeleteChunk to the tier Raft. Followers reconcile local disk against the FSM manifest. OnDelete callback fires on manifest updates for immediate propagation. Replication targets derived from Raft group membership instead of config placements.

title: Update UI for leader/follower model
description: Update placement settings UI to enforce one store per tier per node. Update inspector to show leader/follower instead of primary/secondary. Update tier badges, tooltips, and help pages.

title: Search hits deleted chunk during retention race
description: When retention deletes a chunk mid-query, the search path errors with 'vault not found' when trying to read an anchor position from the deleted chunk. The query reads the chunk list, retention deletes a chunk, then the query tries to open a cursor on the deleted chunk. Should handle missing chunks gracefully (skip, don't error). More visible now that retention runs faster with the discovery-based sweep.

title: Inspector record count is best-effort, not authoritative
description: The vault header record count sums chunk.recordCount from the deduped ListChunks response (fan-out to all nodes). The count varies depending on replication state, retention timing, and which nodes responded. Should use the tier leader's chunk list as the authoritative source instead of a union of all replicas.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: The record count is NOT best-effort — the chunk manager derives it exactly from idx.log size (RecordCount = (idxFileSize - HeaderSize) / EntrySize). If a follower shows fewer records, the replication either truncated the idx.log or the metadata was read mid-import. This is a real data integrity bug, not an inherent limitation. Reprioritized to P2.

title: Replace custom chunk ID format with UUIDs
description: Now that all directory paths use UUIDs (vault IDs, tier IDs), chunk IDs should follow suit. The current base32-encoded custom format (06ejv...) is harder to read, grep, and correlate with other entity IDs. Switch to standard UUIDv7 for chunk IDs. Breaking change for existing data — acceptable since no production deployments exist.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Phase 1-3 complete: glid.GLID type replaces uuid.UUID across 208 files. Phase 4 (proto string→bytes) deferred — the wire format change touches 170 proto fields and every handler. Creating a follow-up issue. The string format works fine for now; the bytes optimization is a performance improvement, not a correctness fix.

title: Bootstrap script for automated cluster setup
description: Create scripts/bootstrap.sh that fully automates cluster setup: starts N nodes, registers admin user, creates file storage on each node, creates rotation/retention policies, filter, vault with 2 tiers, route, and disabled ingesters. Uses the gastrolog CLI for all operations. Update justfile cluster recipes to use it.

title: Show retention status on chunks in inspector
description: Chunks being processed by retention should show a visual indicator in the inspector. Attempted implementation using tier Raft FSM CmdRetentionPending + local inflight map, but the flag never appeared in the UI — likely because the retention processing completes between inspector polls. Needs investigation: either the Raft apply for the pending flag isn't reaching the inspector's ListChunks path, or the dedup logic discards the flagged copy. Deferred.

title: Inspector should use server-streaming subscription, not polling
description: The inspector currently polls ListChunks on an interval. Transient states (retention-pending, mid-replication RF changes) are invisible because they complete between polls. Replace with a server-streaming RPC (WatchChunks) that pushes chunk metadata updates as they happen. Same pattern as WatchConfig.

title: Decouple config from runtime state in entity instances
description:
TierInstance (and potentially other entity types) bakes config/placement values into the runtime struct at build time. When config changes, the instance is stale and requires destroy+rebuild — a pattern that has caused cascading bugs (vault tear-down, data warnings, race conditions during tier drain).

**Problem:**
- TierInstance.IsFollower, LeaderNodeID, FollowerTargets are placement info cached on the struct. Stale after placement changes.
- updateTierRoleIfNeeded exists as a band-aid to patch these without rebuild.
- The healthy pattern (retention/rotation sweeps) reads config fresh each tick. The unhealthy pattern bakes it in.

**Scope:**
- Audit all entity instance types (TierInstance, Vault, ingester wrappers) for config/placement fields that should be read on demand instead of cached.
- TierInstance: remove IsFollower, LeaderNodeID, FollowerTargets from the struct. Replace with config store reads where needed.
- Vault: already clean (no cached config state beyond tier list).
- Verify no other patterns bake config into runtime objects.

**Goal:** Runtime instances only hold handles to physical resources (chunk managers, index managers, Raft groups). Everything else comes from the config store.

title: Index build fails with 'invalid attributes data' after tier drain
description:
After draining a tier's chunks to the next tier, index builds on the destination tier occasionally fail with:

```
index build failed ... error="read record: invalid attributes data"
```

Observed on the receiving node (node2) for chunks that were drained from the hot tier into the warm tier. The records themselves are intact (1000 records across 10 chunks, all accounted for), but some chunks can't build indexes.

Possible causes:
- Drain streams records via AppendToTier which writes raw record bytes. If the source chunk's record format differs slightly from what the destination's index builder expects, the attributes decode fails.
- The drain transfers records from sealed chunks via cursor iteration. If the cursor returns raw bytes that include format-specific headers the destination doesn't expect, the index build chokes.

Repro: 4-node cluster, 2 tiers (hot/warm), RF=4. Ingest 1000 records via scatterbox burst. Drain-delete the hot tier. Index builds fail on some chunks in the warm tier.

title: Occasional missing replica after tier drain (RF=4 shows 3)
description:
After draining a tier, one chunk in the destination tier shows RF=3 instead of the expected RF=4. All other chunks replicated correctly to all 4 nodes.

Likely a race between the drain appending records to the destination tier and the replication catchup. The drain writes to the leader's active chunk, which gets sealed and replicated. If a follower was mid-rebuild during the drain, it might miss one chunk's replication.

Observed in a 4-node cluster with RF=4 after drain-deleting the hot tier into the warm tier. 9 out of 10 chunks had RF=4, one had RF=3.

title: Cloud tier search broken: S3 InvalidRange on drained chunks
description:
After draining file tier chunks into a cloud tier, ALL chunks are unsearchable. The cloud reader requests byte ranges past the end of the S3 object when reading the TOC.

```
search: skipping unreadable cloud chunk ... error="read TOC: operation error S3: GetObject, api error InvalidRange: The requested range 'bytes=5775-5822' is not satisfiable"
```

Every chunk shows this error. The chunks display correctly in the inspector (sealed, compressed, RF=4, cloud badge) but searching returns zero results.

Root cause likely: the drain streams records via AppendToTier which writes to the active chunk. When sealed and uploaded to S3, the object may have a different internal layout than what the cloud reader's TOC parser expects. The TOC offset calculation assumes the original cloud chunk format, but drained chunks may have a different header/footer structure.

Related: gastrolog-rrf6g (index build 'invalid attributes data' after drain) — likely same underlying format mismatch.

Repro: 4-node cluster, 2 tiers (file + cloud), RF=4. Ingest 1000 records. Drain-delete the file tier. Search the cloud tier — zero results, all chunks skipped.

title: Source tier chunks not cleaned up after inter-tier transition
description:
When records transition from tier 1 (file) to tier 2 (cloud) via the normal retention action, the source chunk remains on tier 1 indefinitely. It should be deleted after the transition completes.

The retention sweep evaluates retention rules and transitions chunks to the next tier, but doesn't delete the source chunk afterward. The source chunk stays sealed on tier 1 with a decaying replica count (RF=3 instead of 4 in the observed case).

Expected: after a chunk's records are successfully written to the next tier, the source chunk is deleted from the source tier.

Observed: source chunk persists on tier 1 forever. Accumulates over time as more chunks transition.

title: Audit entire backend for swallowed errors
description:
Multiple critical bugs have been caused by silently discarded errors (`_ = err`). The pattern is pervasive — errors from Raft writes, config store updates, and cloud operations are swallowed, causing silent data corruption and ghost state.

Known instances:
- `_ = s.cfgStore.PutVault(ctx, v)` in DeleteTier handler — ghost tier IDs in vault config
- `_ = s.cfgStore.PutVault(ctx, v)` in other config handlers (likely same pattern)
- Various `_ = err` on Close/Seal/Delete where the error signals data loss

Scope: grep the entire backend for `_ =` and `_ :=` on fallible operations. For each:
1. If the error signals data loss or state corruption: propagate it
2. If the error is from a cleanup/close in a defer: log it
3. If the error is genuinely ignorable: add a comment explaining why

Zero tolerance for silent Raft/config store write failures.

title: Tools menu: extract scatterbox burst mode into a standalone debugging tool
description:
The scatterbox ingester's burst mode (generate N records on demand) is useful for testing and debugging, but it's currently tied to the scatterbox ingester config. This has two problems:

1. You have to have a scatterbox ingester configured and enabled to use it
2. Burst is triggered through the ingester settings UI, which is the wrong place for a debugging/testing tool

**Proposal:**
- Add a Tools menu to the UI (other issues will need this too — e.g. tier validation toolkit gastrolog-bcxp7)
- Move burst record generation into the tools menu as a standalone action: pick a vault, pick a count, generate
- The scatterbox ingester remains as a continuous background generator, but burst mode becomes a first-class tool independent of any ingester
- Burst should work even when no ingesters are enabled

This unblocks using burst for testing tier transitions, drain, cloud upload, etc. without needing to wire up a full ingester.

title: Audit and consolidate duplicate conversion/serialization code paths
description:
Multiple code paths perform the same logical operation (e.g. chunk.Record ↔ ExportRecord) with slightly different field coverage. This has already caused data loss: chunkRecordToExport in chunk_transferrer.go omitted EventID fields that the nearly identical converter in forward.go included. Every remote tier transition silently dropped record identity as a result.

This is a systemic problem, not a one-off. As the codebase grows, any operation that has both a local and remote path WILL diverge unless the shared logic is extracted.

**Known duplicates:**
- chunk.Record → ExportRecord: chunk_transferrer.go:chunkRecordToExport vs forward.go (line 572)
- ExportRecord → chunk.Record: forward.go:exportRecordToChunk vs query_convert.go
- Vault/tier config → proto and back: multiple converters in config_storage.go, config_vaults.go, command/*.go

**Scope:**
- Identify ALL local/remote code path pairs that serialize or convert the same data
- Extract shared converters into a single canonical location
- Ensure field coverage is identical — if a field exists on the source struct, it MUST be present in the converter
- Add tests that round-trip through the converter and assert all fields survive
- Consider a linter rule or code review checklist item: any new proto ↔ domain conversion must use the canonical converter

**Principle:** Code that conceptually does the same thing must be THE SAME CODE. Local and remote paths must not diverge functionally.

title: E2E tests for tier transitions and cloud storage
description:
The existing E2E suite needs tests covering the multi-node tier transition and cloud storage paths. Every major bug found during the gastrolog-1rv42 session was invisible to unit tests:

**Tests needed:**
- 3-tier chain transition (file → file → cloud): verify record count is preserved (no N× duplication)
- Cloud upload idempotency: verify only one node uploads per chunk (no blob overwrite race)
- Cloud search after transition: verify all records are searchable via RemoteReader
- EventID preservation through remote tier transitions
- Tier drain to cloud tier: verify records arrive and are searchable
- Tier deletion (drain + delete): verify clean removal, no ghost tier IDs
- Node crash during cloud transition: verify recovery without data loss or SIGSEGV

The E2E suite already has the infrastructure. These are additional Playwright tests against the running cluster.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Adding replication performance regression tests to scope. Need burst benchmarks (1K, 10K, 100K records) that measure: time-to-seal on leader, time-to-replicate to all followers, time-to-transition through tier chain, and record count accuracy at each stage. These catch the kind of regressions we saw with the dual-stream race — functional correctness AND throughput.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
Splitting into two tracks:

**Go backend benchmarks (multinode_test.go harness):**
- Replication throughput: burst 1K/10K/100K records, measure time-to-replicate to all followers
- Transition correctness: 3-tier chain (file→file→cloud), verify record count preserved at each stage (no N× duplication)
- Seal sync timing: verify followers seal at same boundary as leader under burst load
- EventID preservation: verify EventID survives remote tier transitions
- Cloud upload idempotency: verify only one node uploads per chunk
- Record count accuracy: verify chunk metadata matches actual idx.log record count

**Playwright E2E (test/e2e/tests/):**
- Inspector shows correct chunk counts after tier transitions
- Cloud search returns results via UI after transition
- Tier drain UI flow: Drain/Delete/Cancel prompt, staged save
- Tier creation via vault settings (+ Add Tier with cloud service)
- Tier deletion: clean removal, no ghost tier IDs in UI
- Settings state sync: new tier visible immediately after save

Performance tests go in backend (pure Go, no Docker overhead, runs in CI). Functional UI flows go in Playwright.

title: Unify record forwarding and sealed chunk replication into a single ordered stream
description:
Record forwarding (ForwardRecords) and sealed chunk replication (ReplicateSealedChunk) use separate gRPC streams to each follower. This creates an uncoordinated race: the forwarder keeps writing records to the follower's active chunk while the sealed replication tries to replace it. The replacement seals and deletes the active chunk, but concurrent appends from the forwarder reopen it, leaving straggler duplicates.

**Root cause:** Two independent streams writing to the same chunk ID on the same node with no ordering guarantee.

**Observed:** A 1000-record burst left 24 duplicate straggler records in a follower's active chunk because the sealed replication's seal+delete raced with continued record forwarding.

**Proposed fix:** Merge both operations into a single ordered stream per follower. The leader sends records as they arrive, then a seal marker, then the canonical sealed chunk data — all sequentially on one stream. The follower processes them in order. No race.

This affects the ForwardRecords stream protocol, the record forwarder, the sealed chunk replicator, and the follower's import path.

title: Remove legacy RecordForwarder now that TierReplicator handles all follower replication
description:
The RecordForwarder (record_forwarder.go) was the fire-and-forget per-node channel-based forwarder for active-chunk replication to followers. It has two silent-drop valves (lines 124 and 159) that discard records when the per-node buffer (16,384 entries) fills up.

With the TierReplicator (gastrolog-2a1kn), all follower replication goes through ordered bidirectional streams. The TierReplicator.AppendRecords is synchronous — back-pressure naturally propagates to the ingest pipeline instead of silently dropping records.

The old forwarder is now only used as a fallback when tierReplicator is nil. In production cluster mode, tierReplicator is always set.

**Work:**
- Remove RecordForwarder and all references
- Remove the ForwardToTier method from the old path
- Remove the forwarder field from the orchestrator
- Clean up the nodeForwarder channel/goroutine infrastructure
- Keep the vault-level Forward (cross-node routing) — that's a different path for records routed to vaults on other nodes, not follower replication

**Note:** The cross-node vault routing Forward path (non-tier-targeted) also drops on full buffer. That path is NOT replaced by TierReplicator — it handles routing, not replication. That needs separate attention (gastrolog-27zvt).

title: Self-ingester reliability: don't drop log lines under pressure
description:
The slog capture channel (4,096 entries) silently drops log records when full. This means the system goes blind at the exact moment it's struggling most — the evidence of what's wrong gets discarded.

**Current behavior:**
- CaptureHandler uses a non-blocking send with empty default (capture.go:85)
- When the channel fills, records are silently dropped with no indication
- The skip list prevents feedback loops from pipeline components, but doesn't prevent drops from other subsystems

**The problem:**
- Blocking the slog handler would freeze every goroutine in the application — worse than dropping
- Dropping means losing critical diagnostic data during incidents
- The self-ingester creates an inherent feedback loop: system pressure → more logs → more ingest load → more pressure

**Design questions to resolve:**
1. Should overflow spill to a local file instead of dropping? The self-ingester catches up and drains the spillover when pressure eases.
2. Should the channel be significantly larger (64K+) to make drops rarer?
3. Should the capture handler track and report drop counts so at least the data loss is visible?
4. Should the self-ingester dynamically throttle its capture level under pressure (e.g., only capture ERROR when the channel is >80% full)?
5. Is there a better architecture than a bounded channel for bridging slog → ingest?

**Constraints:**
- Must never block the slog handler — that kills the entire application
- Must never create a feedback loop where logging about drops causes more drops
- Must preserve log lines during the exact scenarios where they matter most (incidents, pressure, failures)

title: Ingester throttling via channel pressure feedback
description:
The chanwatch monitor already observes ingestCh and digestedCh fill levels every second, raising alerts at 90%. Currently observe-only. It should actively throttle ingesters when pressure builds, preventing silent record loss at downstream buffer boundaries.

**Proposed mechanism:**
- chanwatch exposes a pressure signal (e.g., PressureLevel: normal/elevated/critical)
- The orchestrator propagates pressure to ingesters via a shared atomic or channel
- Ingesters respond based on their type:
  - Poll-based (Kafka, metrics): increase poll interval or pause polling
  - Socket-based (syslog, RELP, Fluent Forward): stop reading from socket, let kernel buffer / TCP window handle it
  - Generator (chatterbox, scatterbox): reduce rate or pause
  - Self-ingester: raise minimum capture level (WARN → ERROR → OFF)
- When pressure drops, resume normal operation

**Thresholds (tunable):**
- 80% fill → elevated: ingesters reduce rate by 50%
- 95% fill → critical: ingesters pause entirely
- 50% fill → normal: resume full rate

**Why this matters:**
Without throttling, back-pressure builds silently until it hits a drop valve (record forwarder buffer, slog capture channel) and records are lost. With throttling, the system degrades gracefully — slower ingestion beats lost records.

**Building blocks that already exist:**
- chanwatch (internal/chanwatch) — monitors channel fill, raises alerts
- Per-ingester context cancellation — can be extended with pause/resume
- CaptureHandler.SetMinLevel — already supports hot-reloading the capture threshold
- IngestQueueNearFull — boolean check, could be extended to a graduated signal

**Related:**
- gastrolog-5d5a3: self-ingester capture drops (would use this for level adjustment)
- gastrolog-27zvt: back pressure handling for record forwarding (cross-node path)

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Hysteresis required to prevent throttle flapping. The thresholds for engaging and disengaging throttle must be separated — e.g., engage at 80%, disengage at 50%. If engage and disengage are at the same level, the system oscillates: throttle on → pressure drops → throttle off → pressure rises → throttle on. This is especially dangerous because throttle state changes will be logged, and the self-ingester captures those logs — creating a secondary feedback loop where the act of reporting throttle changes contributes to the pressure that causes them. The self-ingester's component should probably be in the chanwatch skip list for throttle-related log messages, or throttle state changes should be reported via the alert system (which doesn't flow through the capture channel) instead of slog.

title: File chunk manager attr.log corruption under concurrent Append
description:
## Bug

The file chunk manager's `Append` method is not safe for concurrent callers writing to the same active chunk. When multiple goroutines call `Orchestrator.AppendToTier` (or `Orchestrator.Append`) simultaneously, the attr.log writer produces corrupt data — `cursor.Next()` later returns `"invalid attributes data"`.

## Root Cause

`Orchestrator.Append` and `AppendToTier` both acquire `o.mu.RLock()` (read lock), meaning multiple goroutines can hold it simultaneously and call `cm.Append(rec)` on the same file chunk manager. The file manager has internal locking (`m.mu`), but the attr.log write path appears to have a race — likely between the attribute serialization and the file write.

## Reproduction

Found by `TestClusterTransitionConcurrentBurst` in `transition_test.go` (gastrolog-3l7ow): 4 goroutines burst 2500 records each into the same file-backed tier via `AppendToTier`. After ingestion, reading the sealed chunks back via cursor produces `"invalid attributes data"`.

## Impact

Production is not affected today because the digest loop serializes all appends to a single goroutine. However:
- `AppendToTier` is a public method with no documented concurrency restriction
- The replication path (`ForwardTierAppend` handler) could theoretically call it concurrently if multiple replication streams target the same tier
- Nothing in the API contract warns callers that concurrent Append is unsafe

## Fix Options

1. **Make `AppendToTier` acquire an exclusive write lock** (change `o.mu.RLock()` to per-tier write serialization)
2. **Fix the attr.log writer** to be safe under concurrent access (likely needs a mutex around the full serialize+write sequence)
3. **Document the constraint** and ensure all call sites serialize (least safe option)

Option 2 is the proper fix — the `ChunkManager.Append` interface method should be safe for concurrent use, or the interface should document otherwise.

title: Replication tests use memory tiers and single orchestrator

- Replication between nodes

The harness has no `RemoteTransferrer` wired between nodes. The cluster tests in gastrolog-3l7ow add this at the orchestrator level, but the server-level harness still lacks it.

**What's needed:** Extend `setupMultiNode` with options for multi-tier vaults, file-backed tiers, and a `directTransferrer` between nodes. Add server-level tests for tier transition RPCs and replication correctness.

title: Vault reconfiguration during active tier transition not tested

**What's needed:** Test that starts a slow transition (e.g., large chunk), then reconfigures the vault to remove or reorder the destination tier. Verify the transition either completes to the original destination or fails cleanly — not a panic or records sent to the wrong tier.

title: Tier sharing between vaults is a data integrity failure
description:
## Bug

A tier can be silently shared between multiple vaults. This happened during manual testing:

1. `tier create --vault archival-test --name "hot"` matched an existing tier by name
2. The existing "hot" tier (owned by default-vault) was updated and added to archival-test
3. Both vaults now reference the same tier ID in their `tier_ids` list
4. The retention runner for the shared tier can't determine which vault's chain to follow — the "next tier" for transition is ambiguous

This corrupts the transition chain: chunks in the shared tier may transition to the wrong destination tier.

## Root Cause

The data model has the reference going the wrong way. Currently:
- `VaultConfig.TierIDs []uuid.UUID` — vault lists its tiers
- `TierConfig` has no `VaultID` field — tier doesn't know which vault owns it

This allows a tier to appear in multiple vaults' tier lists. Nothing validates exclusivity.

## Impact

- **Silent data corruption**: tier transitions go to the wrong tier
- **Ambiguous retention**: different vaults may have different retention rules for the same tier position, but the tier only has one retention runner
- **CLI upsert by name**: `tier create --name X` matches globally, not per-vault

## Fix

The reference should be inverted:
- Each `TierConfig` should have a `VaultID uuid.UUID` field
- The vault discovers its tiers by querying `tiers WHERE vault_id = ?`
- `tier create --vault X --name Y` must reject if a tier with that name exists in a different vault
- The `VaultConfig.TierIDs` field becomes derived, not stored — or at minimum, validated against TierConfig.VaultID on every mutation

This is a schema change that touches proto, config, FSM, server, orchestrator, and frontend.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: When inverting the reference, add an explicit 'position' (uint32) field on TierConfig to preserve chain ordering. The vault's tier chain is reconstructed by sorting tiers by position. This replaces the ordered tier_ids array on VaultConfig.

title: CLI inspect command for vault/tier/chunk details
description:
## Feature

The Inspector view (vault → tiers → chunks with badges) has no CLI equivalent. An agent or operator using the CLI cannot:

- See which tier a chunk is on
- See cloud/archived/cached status badges
- See chunk-level details (compression ratio, GLCB frames, TS index)
- Trigger Archive/Restore on specific chunks
- Verify the archival lifecycle without the UI

## Needed

A `gastrolog inspect` command (or extend `config vault get`) that shows:

```
gastrolog inspect vault archival-test
  TIER 1: FILE  ON NODE-1  4 CHUNKS  344 RECORDS
    06el7hqp... sealed compr          100 records  42.8 KB
    06el7hn5... sealed compr          100 records  41.6 KB
  TIER 2: CLOUD  ON NODE-1  4 CHUNKS  400 RECORDS
    06el7hl1... sealed compr cloud archived  100 records  12.1 KB
    06el7hdp... sealed compr cloud archived  100 records  11.0 KB

gastrolog inspect chunk 06el7hl1... --vault archival-test
  Chunk ID:     06el7hl13j9p17e42...
  Tier:         arc-cloud (cloud)
  Status:       sealed, compressed, cloud-backed, archived
  Records:      100
  Size:         12.1 KB (79% compression)
  Cloud:        GLCB, 1 seekable zstd frame
  TS Index:     embedded, 100 entries

gastrolog archive 06el7hl1... --vault archival-test --class cold
gastrolog restore 06el7hl1... --vault archival-test
```

This is essential for agent-driven testing and operations.

title: Cloud tier leader has no cloud backing — buildTierInstanceForStorage strips sealed_backing unconditionally
description:
## Bug

In a 4-node cluster with a hot→cloud tier chain, the retention sweep transitions chunks from the hot tier (leader on node A) to the cloud tier (leader on node B). But the transition writes records to the LOCAL cloud tier instance on node A — which is a follower.

Result: 931 sealed chunks on the cloud tier with zero compression, zero cloud uploads, no cloud index. PostSealProcess never runs because `AppendToTier` skips `schedulePostSeal` on followers (`!tier.IsFollower` guard at vault_ops.go:311).

## Root Cause (suspected)

`transitionChunk` at transition.go:53 resolves `nextLeaderNodeID` via `nextTierCfg.LeaderNodeID(cfg.NodeStorageConfigs)`. If this returns empty or resolves to the local node incorrectly, the transition uses `streamLocal` instead of `StreamToTier`, writing to the local follower.

Needs investigation: is `LeaderNodeID` returning the correct remote node ID? Is the transferrer configured? Is the NodeStorageConfigs in the loaded config complete?

## Impact

- Cloud upload never happens → archival sweep has nothing to archive
- Warm cache never gets populated
- Chunks accumulate on the follower indefinitely — disk fills up
- The entire tiered storage pipeline is broken when tiers span different nodes

## How to reproduce

1. `just backend cluster-init` (4 nodes)
2. Create vault with file tier (leader on node X) and cloud tier (leader on node Y, Y ≠ X)
3. Ingest data via chatterbox
4. Wait for retention to transition hot→cloud
5. Check cloud tier's chunk directory: hundreds of uncompressed sealed chunks, no cloud.idx

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
Root cause found and fixed.

**Bug:** `buildTierInstanceForStorage` (reconfig_vaults.go:812) unconditionally stripped `sealed_backing` from cloud tier params — even when building the LEADER. The comment said 'always follower' but the function was later reused by `buildPrimaryTierInstance` for leaders too.

**Impact:** Cloud tier leader's file.Manager had CloudStore=nil. PostSealProcess compressed + indexed but never uploaded to cloud. Without cloud-backed chunks, the archival sweep had nothing to process. The entire archival lifecycle was dead.

**Fix:**
- Added `isFollower bool` param to `buildTierInstanceForStorage` — only strips `sealed_backing` when true
- Updated all 3 call sites (leader=false, two follower=true)
- Added 'post-seal:' to RemoveJobsByPrefix cleanup in 4 locations
- Regression test `TestCloudTierLeaderPreservesCloudBacking` exercises the exact production ApplyConfig code path

**Why tests didn't catch it:** All existing cloud tier tests constructed TierInstance directly with CloudStore set, bypassing the production buildPrimaryTierInstance path.

title: Surface per-chunk storage class in proto, UI and CLI
description:
The archival lifecycle transitions chunks through storage classes (cold → deep-freeze → delete for Memory; GLACIER → DEEP_ARCHIVE for S3; etc.), but there's no way to verify which class a chunk is currently in.

BlobInfo.StorageClass exists in the backend and the cloud B+ tree index stores the archived flag, but the ChunkMeta proto only has `bool archived` — a binary signal that doesn't distinguish between archival stages.

**What's needed:**
1. Add `string storage_class = 17` to ChunkMeta in vault.proto
2. Populate from the blobstore BlobInfo or cloud index on chunk list
3. Show the class next to the archived badge in VaultCard (Inspector UI)
4. Surface in the CLI inspect command (gastrolog-17x6l)

Without this, the archival lifecycle is functionally untestable — operators can't verify that transitions are actually progressing through the configured chain.

title: Test orchestrators leak gocron schedulers — race detector 37x slowdown
description:
168 orchestrator instances created in tests never call Close()/Stop(), leaking gocron scheduler goroutines. Under the race detector this causes a 37x slowdown (77s vs 2s).

Close() method now exists but needs t.Cleanup(orch.Close) added to each call site. A newTestOrch(t, Config) helper was prototyped but the bulk sed replacement broke 27 tests by converting err= to err:= in scopes where err was already declared. Needs per-site conversion.

title: Intermittent ErrInvalidEntry in cluster replication tests under parallel load
description:
Two separate issues:

1. BLOCKING CI: internal/cluster tests hang at 600s timeout in every CI run. Stack trace shows stuck gRPC addrConn.connect in infinite reconnect loop. Goroutine leak from test that doesn't shut down peer connections. internal/lookup also times out intermittently (stuck watchLoop). This is the cause of 9+ consecutive CI failures.

2. LOW-FREQUENCY: Two cluster tests fail at ~0.2% rate locally under parallel load (ErrInvalidEntry — mmap size vs idx entry mismatch). Diagnostic error messages improved to capture chunk ID, record index, and size details.

Priority: fix the goroutine leak first to unblock CI.
close_reason: Both issues resolved: CI goroutine leak fixed in daf10dec, ErrInvalidEntry compression race fixed in gastrolog-2mnv8. Residual 0.2% not reproducible — monitor and reopen if it surfaces with a stack trace.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
Investigation summary (2026-04-12):

Part 1 (CI goroutine leak): Fixed by daf10dec ("cluster test goroutine leaks — idempotent close + Raft-first shutdown"). All test runs pass consistently since that fix.

Part 2 (0.2% ErrInvalidEntry): Primary cause was a compression-vs-cursor race — openDataFile previously called isCompressed(path) and os.Open(path) as two separate operations, allowing concurrent post-seal compression to atomically replace the file between the two calls. The cursor would mmap compressed bytes as if they were uncompressed, producing "raw range [N:M] exceeds mmap size K". Fixed in gastrolog-2mnv8 by opening the file once, reading the header on the same fd to determine compression, and relying on inode pinning to prevent the race. The fix is at record_reader.go:644-658.

Stress testing: ran chunk/file 10x, orchestrator/TestCluster* 3x, cluster/ 5x under -race — zero ErrInvalidEntry reproductions. The residual 0.2% is below observable threshold without a deterministic reproducer.

Other investigated windows (all closed):
- ImportRecords: m.metas populated last, under lock, after files sealed+closed. No visibility gap.
- Append Phase 2 vs Seal: sealLocked calls inflight.Wait() before sealing. All WriteAt calls complete before files are closed.
- OpenCursor lock release: releases m.mu before opening files, but openDataFile's inode-pinning fix handles the concurrent rename case.

Closing as fixed. If ErrInvalidEntry reappears with a stack trace, reopen.

title: CI blocked: cluster and lookup tests hang at 600s timeout
description:
Every CI run for the past 9+ builds fails with internal/cluster timing out at 600s. Stack traces show:

1. Stuck gRPC addrConn.connect in infinite reconnect loop (goroutine leak from peer connections not closed by test cleanup)
2. Stuck Raft pipelineDecode/pipelineReplicate goroutines (Raft groups not shut down)
3. internal/lookup intermittently hangs too (watchLoop goroutine not cancelled)

Root cause: test cleanup is not shutting down all Raft groups and gRPC connections. The goroutines outlive the test, holding the process open until the 10-minute timeout.

Not related to gastrolog-24pot (mmap flakiness). This is a goroutine lifecycle issue in the test harness.

title: Retention sweep lacks singleton mode — concurrent sweeps race after restart
description:
Three bugs in cluster restart reliability:

1. **Concurrent retention sweeps** (fixed): scheduler lacks singleton mode, overlapping sweeps race on the same chunks after restart.

2. **Tier Raft leadership divergence** (not fixed): after full restart, non-bootstrap nodes win tier Raft elections because they create groups faster. Config placement leader and tier Raft leader end up on different nodes. Retention requires both on the same node — so it never runs. Chunks accumulate forever.

3. **Stale manifest deletes follower chunks** (not fixed): follower reconciliation compares local chunks against the tier Raft FSM manifest and deletes anything not in it. After restart, the FSM is restored from a local snapshot + partial log replay. If the log hasn't caught up yet, the manifest is stale — missing recently-created chunks. The follower deletes those chunks as 'orphans'. Permanent data loss — no repair mechanism re-transfers them.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
Session status at compaction:

**Known-good commits (keep):**
- Scheduler singleton mode
- Multiraft package cleanup (moved ChunkFSM → tier/raftfsm, GroupManager → raftgroup, renamed to FSM/Entry)
- Stale manifest guard via FSM.Ready()
- Decoupled tier Raft group creation from chunk loading
- ForwardTierApply RPC + TierApplyForwarder
- Test coverage for forwarder and FSM readiness

**Problematic last commit (amended many times):**
- OnDelete callback replacing reconcileFollower — may be causing follower re-announcement cascade
- Single-node bootstrap + reconcile-on-all-nodes pattern — still has the 'first run after init' race where handleTierPut doesn't retry
- The AddMember forwarding was removed in favor of leader-only reconciliation, but that creates a different timing problem

**Known outstanding issues:**
- Init shutdown works now (no more SIGKILL on init)
- First run after init: one node misses membership (RF=3 instead of RF=4)
- Steady-state: ForwardTierApply to node-2 timing out during tier transitions
- Pre-existing chunk corruption bug ('invalid attributes data') unrelated to this session

The leadership divergence problem is fundamentally hard, and I've been iterating without a clear mental model. After compaction, the right approach is probably to revert the last commit back to bc00d425 and re-plan the leadership fix from scratch with the research context from the Consul/Nomad pattern (only the tier Raft leader reconciles membership, triggered via LeaderCh + Barrier, no forwarding for AddVoter).

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
All three sub-problems are resolved:

1. **Concurrent retention sweeps**: Fixed by scheduler singleton mode (early commit on this branch).
