4. **Background work drain**. Stop the scheduler (cancel its context, wait for its WaitGroup). Stop the chunk announcer's submission goroutine. Stop tier_leader_manager epochs.
5. **Replication drain**. Stop the tier replicator (close all open streams, wait for in-flight sends to error out). After this point no orchestrator code should call into the cluster forwarder.
6. **Raft shutdown**. For each tier raft group on which this node is the leader, attempt LeadershipTransfer to a healthy peer. Then call Shutdown() on each group, wait for the future. Same for config raft.
7. **Close listeners**. Now safe to close cluster gRPC server listener, API listener, unix socket. There are no more handlers to satisfy.
8. **Phase = Stopped**.

## Required noise suppression

Components must check the shutdown phase before logging WARN/ERROR for events that are EXPECTED during shutdown:

- 'replication: failed to forward record to follower' -> downgrade to debug (or skip the call entirely) when shutting down
- 'chunk metadata announce failed: raft is already shutdown' -> debug
- 'failed to make requestVote RPC' -> hraft does this internally; we should suppress the wrapping logger or accept it as transient noise during teardown
- 'failed to pipeline appendEntries' -> same

Rule of thumb: any WARN/ERROR that fires because of an action this node deliberately initiated (its own shutdown) is wrong. Only log warnings for things that were unexpected.

## Acceptance criteria

After this work:
- Total shutdown lines from a clean four-node teardown should be < 30 lines (one INFO per phase per node + a small constant for raft handshakes)
- ZERO lines containing 'failed to forward', 'connection refused', 'raft is already shutdown', 'EOF' during a planned shutdown
- All four nodes shut down in similar wall-clock time (<500ms each)
- The cluster.go GracefulStop fallback timeout never fires (verified by removing it temporarily and confirming clean shutdown still works; can be re-added afterward as a watchdog)

## Files likely to change

- internal/cluster/cluster.go (Stop, GracefulStop pattern)
- internal/orchestrator/lifecycle.go (Stop ordering, ingester drain)
- internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go (shutdown phase atomic)
- internal/orchestrator/vault_ops.go (fireAndForgetRemote, sealRemoteFollowers — phase check)
- internal/cluster/peer_conns.go (already has graceful invalidate, may need similar treatment)
- internal/cluster/tier_replicator.go (Close ordering)
- internal/cluster/forward_rpc.go and forward.go (interceptor for inbound drain)
- internal/server/lifecycle.go (top-level shutdown ordering)
- internal/raftgroup/groupmanager.go (LeadershipTransfer + Shutdown ordering)
- internal/multiraft/transport.go (suppress benign EOF logs during shutdown)

## Out of scope

- Reducing the 5-second wall-clock timeout (correct fix is to make it never fire, not to shrink it)
- Ingester-level changes beyond context cancellation
- Per-ingester graceful protocols (e.g. MQTT QoS handshakes) — those are separate concerns

## Discovery

Surfaced 2026-04-08 during the resilience-sweep aftermath, after gastrolog-31riw was fixed. The user reviewed the cluster.log shutdown trail and noted the noise. Consistent with the broader 'do it properly' principle that drove the per-call timeout fix in gastrolog-4rp6i — that fix was correct (cluster forwarders MUST have outer-level timeouts as a safety net against silent wedges) but exposed the lack of an inbound shutdown drain on the receiving side.

title: CLI --addr flag should use URL scheme for unix sockets
description: The --addr flag accepts http://host:port for network connections but a bare file path for unix sockets (e.g. data/node1/gastrolog.sock). This is inconsistent. Should use a URL scheme for everything: unix:///path/to/sock for sockets, http://host:port for network. The bare-path form can be kept as a fallback for backwards compatibility but the canonical form should be URL-based.

title: PostSealProcess index build attempted on unsealed follower chunk
description:
After `config vault seal`, PostSealProcess emits WARN: `index build failed ... error="chunk is not sealed"`.

`SealActive` seals the active chunk on the leader tier instance's chunk manager, but follower storage instances on the same node still have the chunk as active/unsealed. Somewhere in the post-seal or replication pipeline, an index build is triggered against a chunk manager where the chunk hasn't been sealed yet.

Log line:
```
[node1] time=2026-04-11T01:10:00.451+02:00 level=WARN msg="index build failed" vault=019d699f-eb7a-75cc-8373-6feda687bcb9 tier=019d699f-ed4a-7a48-ac6d-215d7dbdadb0 storage=019d699f-dac3-7347-8d52-bb571b91b930 component=chunk-manager type=file chunk=06enja31ihsq9bg7o5dij65f3g error="chunk is not sealed"
```

Needs investigation: is this from replication timing, RebuildMissingIndexes on startup, or the seal not propagating to all storage instances?

title: Remove legacy ChunkTransferrer fallback paths replaced by TierReplicator
description:
Similar to gastrolog-5c6fp but for ChunkTransferrer. Several ChunkTransferrer methods exist only as fallback paths for when tierReplicator == nil, which is never the case in production cluster mode. Since TierReplicator handles all replication now, these are dead code waiting to be removed.

Dead fallback methods in internal/cluster/chunk_transferrer.go:
- **ForwardTierAppend** — replaced by TierReplicator.AppendRecords. Still used in replication.go:51 (ackAfterReplication) — needs conversion.
- **ForwardSealTier** — replaced by TierReplicator.SealTier. Still used in replication_test.go tests — needs conversion.
- **ForwardDeleteChunk** — replaced by TierReplicator.DeleteChunk. Used in retention.go:568 as a fallback branch guarded by `if r.orch.tierReplicator == nil`.
- **ReplicateSealedChunk** — replaced by TierReplicator.ImportSealedChunk. Used in replication.go:193 as a fallback branch.

Methods that look transferrer-related but serve a different purpose (KEEP):
- **TransferRecords** — cross-node chunk migration for MoveChunk/DrainVault. Not replaced by TierReplicator.
- **StreamToTier** — inter-tier transition. Different path from follower replication.
- **WaitVaultReady** — probe utility, not replication.

Work:
1. Convert ackAfterReplication (replication.go:51) to use TierReplicator.AppendRecords
2. Convert replication_test.go seal-tier tests to use TierReplicator.SealTier
3. Remove the fallback branches in retention.go:568 and replication.go:193
4. Delete ForwardTierAppend, ForwardSealTier, ForwardDeleteChunk, ReplicateSealedChunk methods from ChunkTransferrer
5. Clean up any server-side handlers that only served these paths

Also check eject.go:213 which uses ForwardAppend (transferrer, not RecordForwarder) — determine if that's still needed.

title: Dead code audit: transferrer mocks, replaceForwardedChunk, chunk-ID sync workarounds
description:
Follow-up from gastrolog-572d7. While converting the transferrer-based replication paths to TierReplicator, the following dead-or-suspect code was flagged but left alone for scope control. Audit each one and clean up.

## 1. Test-only dead methods on transferrer mocks
Several test mocks in orchestrator/ still have ForwardTierAppend, ForwardSealTier, ForwardDeleteChunk, ReplicateSealedChunk methods even though those are no longer on the RemoteTransferrer interface. Harmless but noisy.
- internal/orchestrator/vault_transfers_test.go (mockTransferrer)
- internal/orchestrator/eject_test.go (ejectFakeTransferrer)
- internal/orchestrator/transition_test.go (transitionFakeTransferrer)
- internal/orchestrator/transition_markunreadable_test.go (streamErrTransferrer)
- internal/server/multinode_tier_test.go (mnTransferrer)

Work: delete the dead methods from each mock type.

## 2. replaceForwardedChunk is likely obsolete
internal/orchestrator/vault_ops.go's replaceForwardedChunk seals and deletes a 'forwarded' chunk before replacing it with the canonical sealed version. Its purpose was to handle a race where a follower had a partial, uncompressed forwarded copy that needed to be replaced by the leader's canonical sealed chunk.

Now that TierReplicator.AppendRecords preserves the leader's chunk ID end-to-end, the 'forwarded' and 'canonical' versions ARE the same chunk. The function may be fully obsolete. Audit its call sites in ImportToTierStorage and determine if it can be deleted.

## 3. SetNextChunkID workarounds
Several test paths manually call SetNextChunkID on follower chunk managers to sync chunk IDs before appending. This was a workaround for the old forward path that used fresh chunk IDs. With TierReplicator.AppendRecords syncing IDs natively, some of these manual SetNextChunkID calls are now no-ops. Audit:
- replication_test.go (various catchup tests)
- transition_test.go (various cluster tests)

Delete any SetNextChunkID calls whose purpose is purely to sync with a leader that now syncs automatically.

## 4. ImportRecordMessage proto field usage
api/proto/gastrolog/v1/cluster.proto's ImportRecordMessage has VaultId, TierId, ChunkId, Record. After the TierReplicator migration, verify which fields are still needed by the surviving callers (TransferRecords, StreamToTier). Some combinations may be dead.

## 5. forwardingStatsAdapter in app.go
The forwardedReceived counter on cluster.Server is still incremented in forwardRecords and streamForwardRecordsHandler. Check whether the stats plumbing in app.go's forwardingStatsAdapter still consumes it or if it surfaces anywhere in the UI. If no consumer, delete the counter.

## 6. chunk_transferrer_test.go reduction
After gastrolog-572d7 removed TestForwardSealTierTimeoutOnHangingPeer, only TestStreamToTierTimeoutOnHangingPeer remains. The hangingGRPCServer fixture might be inlinable into the single remaining caller, or the test file may benefit from consolidation with adjacent cluster tests.

title: Alert on sustained high rotation and retention rates
description:
When a tier's rotation policy is too aggressive for the actual ingest rate
(e.g., a 100-record rotation policy against 1000 rec/sec chatterbox = 10
rotations/sec), the pipeline collapses into rotation-bound throughput.
Every rotation fires the full seal pipeline: chunk seal, post-seal index
builders (tsidx/attr/token/kv/json), TierReplicator fan-out to followers,
possible Raft commit, retention sweep, new chunk allocation. At >1/sec
sustained this dominates the write loop, digestedCh backs up, and the
pressure gate (gastrolog-4fguu) starts flapping.

From the operator's perspective the only visible symptom is "ingest feels
slow" and the ingest-pressure alert pulsing. There's currently no signal
that points at the real root cause — rotation rate. Same class of issue
applies to retention: a too-short retention window against a busy tier
will trigger continuous deletes, producing the same kind of overhead.

Observed during gastrolog-4fguu testing: 100-record rotation against
1000 rec/sec chatterbox collapsed throughput; bumping to 10000 records
per rotation restored smooth operation.

## Proposed approach

1. Track rotations-per-second and retention-deletes-per-second per tier
   in the orchestrator (sliding window, say 30s).
2. Wire both into alert.Collector with Set/Clear pairs when sustained rate
   exceeds a threshold. Suggested thresholds (subject to tuning):
   - Rotation: >1/sec for 30s → Warning; >5/sec for 30s → Error
   - Retention: >10 deletes/sec for 30s → Warning
3. Alert message should name the specific tier and include the observed
   rate so the operator can jump straight to the misconfigured policy.
4. Consider exposing current rates in the metrics ingester's system record
   so they show up in dashboards without requiring alert wiring.

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups if desired)

- Refusing to rotate faster than some hard minimum (could mask real
  high-volume scenarios; needs more thought).
- Config-time heuristic warnings at policy save.

## Acceptance criteria

- High rotation rate surfaces as an operator-visible alert, not just a
  silent throughput drop.
- Alert clears automatically when rate drops.
- Tests: misconfigured rotation policy triggers the alert within 30s;
  clearing the policy clears the alert.
- Same for retention delete rate.

## Related

- gastrolog-4fguu (ingest pressure gate — the mechanism that currently
  masks the rotation problem behind generic ingest-pressure alerts)
- feedback_use_alerts.md principle: every persistent degraded state needs
  a Set/Clear pair, not just a log line

title: Cloud tier retention leaves local cache behind after expiring chunk
description:
When a chunk expires from a cloud tier via retention, the cloud copy (S3/GCS/Azure blob) is deleted but the locally cached chunk data remains on disk. The inspector shows the cloud_backed tag disappearing, but the chunk directory stays.

Expected: retention expiry on a cloud tier should delete both the cloud blob AND the local cache directory.

Observed: cloud blob is deleted, local cache persists indefinitely. Over time this leaks disk space on every node that cached the chunk.

Likely root cause: the retention expireChunk path calls cm.Delete(id) which may only handle the cloud-side deletion for cloud-backed chunks, without cleaning up the local file cache. Or the cloud tier's Delete implementation removes the blob but not the local directory.
close_reason: Non-issue: cloud blob and local cache are cleaned up in separate retention sweep passes. The cloud tag disappears first (blob deleted), then the local directory is removed on the next sweep cycle (~1 minute later). Both sides are cleaned up — just not atomically in a single pass.

title: Durability handoff between tiers (durable ack protocol)
description:
Source tier must not delete a chunk until the destination tier has durably received and replicated its records. Currently, tier transitions stream records and delete source chunks without a durable ack — a destination tier failure between receive and replication loses data.

The handoff sequence per the vision doc:
1. Source tier leader streams records from a sealed chunk to destination tier leader
2. Destination tier leader appends and replicates to its followers
3. Destination sends durable ack back to source
4. Only then does the source mark the chunk as eligible for retention delete

This is a two-phase commit at each tier boundary. Cost is one extra round-trip per chunk transition.
close_reason: Two-phase transition handoff with receipt-based confirmation. Source marks TransitionStreamed, writes CmdTransitionReceived receipt to destination tier Raft (majority-durable). Confirmation sweep checks receipt before expiring source. Transitions run as one-shot scheduler jobs (non-blocking sweep). Terminal tier returns without expiring.

title: Cloud tier S3 failure during startup permanently kills vault on that node
description:
When a vault has a cloud tier and the S3/MinIO endpoint is unreachable during node startup, the vault initialization fails entirely and the vault is permanently skipped on that node. No retry. Replication to that node fails forever with "vault not found" until the node is restarted with S3 available.

Root cause: vault initialization is all-or-nothing. The cloud tier's chunk manager calls ListObjectsV2 during init to discover existing cloud chunks. If S3 is down, the init fails and the entire vault is skipped via "vault failed to initialize, skipping."

Observed in cluster.log:
  node2: vault failed to initialize, skipping: build tier ... create chunk manager: load cloud chunks: list cloud chunks: operation error S3: ListObjectsV2, exceeded maximum number of attempts, 3, ... dial tcp [::1]:9000: connect: connection refused

Impact: nodes 1, 2, 4 all failed to register the vault. Node 3 (which succeeded) is the tier leader, ingesting and trying to replicate to all three — producing hundreds of "vault not found" errors per second, permanently.

Fix options:
1. Retry vault initialization on a backoff loop until it succeeds
2. Degrade gracefully: register the vault with non-cloud tiers functional, retry the cloud tier in the background
3. The rotation sweep already rediscovers config every 15s — hook vault re-init into that sweep for vaults that failed startup

Option 2 is ideal — queries against non-cloud tiers work immediately, cloud tier catches up when S3 comes online.

title: Align tier Raft leader with placement leader via TransferLeadership
description:
The TierInstance has two competing leadership concepts:

1. IsFollower bool (static, set at build time from config placement)
2. IsRaftLeader func() bool (dynamic, from Raft election)

These should always agree but don't during startup, failover, or partition.
Every time code uses the wrong one, it's a bug:
- gastrolog-68fqk: cloud backfill used IsLeader() instead of IsRaftLeader()
- Multiple prior issues with retention, replication, and transition checks

Fix: remove IsFollower/IsLeader(). Derive leadership from the tier Raft
group. If Raft says you're the leader, you're the leader. If there's no
Raft group (single-node), you're always the leader. One source of truth.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Revised approach after tracing all 42 leadership callsites: keep placement-derived IsFollower/IsLeader for all operational decisions (retention, rotation, replication, archival, cloud, search, drain). Add TransferLeadership to align the tier Raft leader with the placement leader — performance optimization, not correctness change. The TierApplyForwarder already handles disagreement.

title: Flaky transition burst tests — follower cleanup race
description: TestClusterTransitionLargeBurst, TestClusterTransitionBurstNoOrphans, and TestClusterTransitionThreeTierChainBurst intermittently fail with 1 chunk directory lingering on a follower after a 100-chunk concurrent burst. The race is between the transition sweep expiring chunks and the follower reconciliation deleting local files. Passes on re-run. Needs deterministic waiting instead of fixed timeouts.

title: RebuildMissingIndexes spams cloud-backed chunks on every restart
description:
RebuildMissingIndexes runs on startup and checks IndexesComplete for every sealed chunk. Cloud-backed chunks that were adopted (local data files removed, only .idx files remain) fail the completeness check, so the system schedules index rebuild jobs that can't succeed (no data files). This produces dozens of 'rebuilding missing indexes' log lines on every restart for every node.

Fix: skip cloud-backed chunks in RebuildMissingIndexes — their indexes live in the GLCB blob, not on local disk.

title: Replication forward to dead peers has no backoff — log spam on every record
description:
When a follower node goes down, fireAndForgetRemote still tries to forward every ingested record to the dead peer. Each failure produces a WARN log line. With a high-rate ingester (chatterbox), this means hundreds of 'replication: failed to forward record to follower' lines per second, all with the same 'connection refused' error.

Needs a circuit breaker or exponential backoff per follower target. After N consecutive failures (or a connection refused), skip the target for a cooldown period. Clear the circuit when the peer comes back (successful forward or Raft heartbeat).

title: Replication catchup log verbosity — INFO per chunk is too noisy
description:
When a node recovers and replication catchup runs, every chunk transfer produces an INFO log line ('replication catchup: chunk transferred'). With hundreds of chunks to catch up, this floods the cluster log.

Should log a summary at INFO ('catchup: transferred N chunks to follower X') and individual transfers at DEBUG.

title: Cluster self-healing after node failure
description:
A single node outage + restart exposes multiple recovery gaps. The cluster should converge to a healthy state automatically within seconds of a node returning, without operator intervention.

Observed failures after killing node2 and restarting:

1. **No replication backoff** — every ingested record produces a WARN log to the dead peer (gastrolog-2b1xp, already tracked)
2. **Raft quorum loss with voteless nodes** — the voteless feature causes tier Raft groups to lose quorum even when enough physical nodes are alive. Voteless nodes are registered as voters in tier Raft groups but can't participate. Need to either remove voteless or exclude voteless nodes from tier Raft voter lists.
3. **Multiple active chunks after restart** — when a follower loses contact with the leader, its active chunk diverges. On restart, both the old and new active chunks coexist. The reconciliation loop should seal stale active chunks and converge to a single active.
4. **Low RF after recovery** — sealed chunks from the outage period aren't replicated to the returning node. Replication catchup runs but is slow and noisy (gastrolog-1qyc8, already tracked). More fundamentally, the system should proactively detect under-replicated chunks and schedule catchup.
5. **Tier Raft groups 'not registered' after restart** — returning node takes time to register tier Raft groups. During this window, elections fail, snapshots fail, transitions fail. The cluster should handle this gracefully (retry, wait for registration, don't spam).
6. **Transitions fail during recovery** — tier 0 → tier 1 transitions fail because the destination tier leader can't be reached. Should retry automatically, not give up.
7. **Corrupt chunks from interrupted writes** — 'invalid attributes data' errors on chunks that were being written when the node died. Need detection + quarantine.

The root disease: the cluster treats node failure as an exceptional event instead of a normal operating condition. Every subsystem (replication, transition, Raft, reconciliation) needs to handle unavailable peers gracefully with backoff, retry, and convergence.

title: Panic in token indexer: index out of range during cloud chunk index build
description:
Node3 panicked during post-seal index building for an adopted cloud chunk:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 0

goroutine 21624 [running]:
encoding/binary.littleEndian.PutUint32(...)
gastrolog/internal/index/file/token.(*Indexer).fillPostingsToFile.func3(...)
  indexer.go:407
gastrolog/internal/tokenizer.IterTokens(...)
  token.go:45
gastrolog/internal/index/file/token.(*Indexer).fillPostingsToFile(...)
  indexer.go:389
gastrolog/internal/index/file/token.(*Indexer).Build(...)
  indexer.go:154
```

The chunk was just adopted from cloud (06eo6phhjdp631bdutli0co8ag). The index builder opened a cloud cursor, iterated tokens, and tried to write a posting entry to a zero-length byte slice at fillPostingsToFile line 407.

Likely cause: the postings buffer wasn't allocated or was reset to nil/empty before the write. Might be a race between the adopt (which removes local data files) and the index builder (which expects local files), or a bug in how cloud cursor records are fed to the token indexer.

title: Separate config from system state
description:
The cluster-level Raft group (currently called 'config Raft') should be renamed to 'system' and split into two sub-structures:

- **config**: operator-controlled. Tiers, vaults, routes, filters, storage assignments, cloud services, ingesters, retention/rotation policies. Changes only when the operator changes it.
- **runtime**: cluster-controlled. Tier leadership (derived from tier Raft elections), node health, replication status. Changes autonomously as the cluster operates.

The Leader: true flag in tier placements must go. Tier leadership belongs in system.runtime, derived from tier Raft elections — not declared by the operator in system.config.

Tier Raft groups remain separate (per-tier chunk metadata FSM). But which node leads which tier is tracked in the system Raft group's runtime sub-structure.

This is a prerequisite for gastrolog-1s3mf — you can't unify tier leadership until config stops claiming to know who the leader is.

title: System Architecture: config/runtime split, unified tier leadership, stable Raft groups
description:
Fundamental rearchitecture of how GastroLog manages cluster state. Three interconnected changes that must be done in the right order:

## 1. Rename config Raft to system Raft, split config from runtime (gastrolog-43xgf)
The cluster-level Raft group becomes 'system' with two sub-structures:
- **config**: operator-controlled (tiers, vaults, routes, policies, storage assignments)
- **runtime**: cluster-controlled (tier leadership, node health)

The Leader: true flag in tier placements goes away. Tier leadership is runtime state, not config.

## 2. All nodes in all tier Raft groups
Stop adding/removing tier Raft members when storage changes. All nodes are always members of every tier Raft group. Nodes without storage participate in consensus but don't store chunk data. Storage assignment is a runtime decision, not a Raft membership change.

## 3. Unify tier leadership via TransferLeadership (gastrolog-1s3mf)
After a tier Raft election, proactively transfer leadership to the preferred node (per system.runtime). The tier leader IS the tier Raft leader — enforced by TransferLeadership, not by static config flags.

## Order of operations
1. gastrolog-43xgf: config/runtime split (prerequisite for everything)
2. Stable tier Raft groups (all nodes always members)
3. gastrolog-1s3mf: TransferLeadership to align tier Raft leader with tier leader

## Research
See docs/distributed_leadership_patterns.md for patterns from CockroachDB, TiKV, etcd, Kafka/Redpanda.

title: All nodes in all tier Raft groups — decouple storage from Raft membership
description:
Stop reconfiguring tier Raft groups when storage is added/removed. All nodes are always members of every tier Raft group. Nodes without storage for a tier participate in consensus (voting, FSM replication) but don't store chunk data. Storage assignment becomes a system.runtime decision, not a Raft membership change.

Benefits:
- No disruptive AddVoter/RemoveVoter when storage changes
- Stable quorum — node count per tier never changes
- Simpler operations — storage is a runtime toggle, not a Raft reconfiguration

Tradeoff: more Raft traffic (every node in every tier group). Acceptable at tens of tiers. At hundreds, needs MultiRaft batching (see docs/distributed_leadership_patterns.md).

Depends on gastrolog-43xgf (config/runtime split).

title: Remove --voteless flag, use Raft non-voting members instead
description:
The --voteless CLI flag creates nodes that can't participate in tier Raft elections but are still registered as voters in tier Raft groups. This caused quorum loss during the node failure test (gastrolog-10h56) — a voteless node counted toward quorum but couldn't vote.

Replace with hashicorp/raft AddNonvoter (learner nodes). Non-voters:
- Receive log replication (can serve reads, hold data)
- Don't participate in elections or quorum calculations
- Can be promoted to voter when needed

This is the standard pattern used by etcd (Learner) and TiKV (Learner replica).

title: MultiRaft: batch heartbeats and fsync across tier Raft groups
description:
hashicorp/raft runs independent goroutines, timers, and heartbeats per group. At enterprise scale (hundreds of vaults x 3+ tiers = 1000+ Raft groups per node), this won't scale:

- 1000+ heartbeat round-trips per node-pair per tick
- 1000+ independent fsyncs per tick (log append)
- 1000+ goroutine sets with separate election timers

Needed: a MultiRaft layer (like CockroachDB/TiKV) that:
1. Coalesces heartbeats per node-pair (one heartbeat covers all groups)
2. Batches log appends into a single fsync per tick across all groups
3. Multiplexes Raft messages over a single gRPC connection per node-pair
4. Shares a single tick loop across all groups

This likely means replacing or wrapping hashicorp/raft with a custom multi-group implementation. The tier Raft group management API should be abstracted now so this swap doesn't require rewiring the orchestrator.

Reference: CockroachDB's MultiRaft runs the entire system on 3 goroutines regardless of range count. TiKV batches all group ticks in a single thread with one WriteBatch per tick.

See docs/distributed_leadership_patterns.md for details.

title: Extract runtime state from system.Config into system.Runtime
description:
system.Config contains runtime state that the operator didn't put there. Extract into system.Runtime:

## Runtime state currently in Config

1. **TierConfig.Placements** (entire array) — already marked 'system-managed' in the proto comment. The operator sets replication factor and storage class; the system decides where to place replicas and who leads. Includes:
   - Storage assignments (which storages hold replicas)
   - TierPlacement.Leader (who leads the tier)

2. **NodeConfig** — nodes join via enrollment, not operator creation. Node presence is a runtime fact discovered by the cluster.

3. **NodeStorageConfig** — storage is discovered at enrollment, not manually configured. The operator doesn't type in disk paths; the node reports what it has.

4. **ClusterTLS** — generated at cluster-init (CA, certs, join token). Not operator-configured.

5. **SetupWizardDismissed** — UI state, not config.

## What the operator actually controls

- Tier definitions (name, type, vault, position, policies, cloud service, cache settings)
- Replication factor (how many replicas)
- Storage class (what KIND of storage to use)
- Vaults, routes, filters, ingesters, policies, cloud services, certs, settings

## What the system controls

- Placements (which specific storages hold replicas)
- Leadership (who leads each tier)
- Node membership (who's in the cluster)
- Storage discovery (what each node has)
- Cluster identity (TLS material)

All five categories need to move from system.Config into system.Runtime, with the system Raft FSM managing both.

title: Suppress tier Raft replication noise for dead peers
description: When a node dies, the tier Raft leaders spam ERROR logs every 10 seconds trying to replicate/snapshot to the dead voter. hashicorp/raft does this by design — it keeps retrying all voters. Two fixes needed: (1) suppress or downgrade the log level for peers known to be unreachable, (2) remove dead nodes from tier Raft desired members after a grace period so replication stops entirely. CockroachDB handles this by rebalancing replicas away from dead nodes after 5 minutes.

title: Follower nodes rebuild indexes for every replicated chunk on every restart
description: RebuildMissingIndexes fires on startup for every sealed compressed chunk on follower nodes. With 60 chunks per follower, that's 180 unnecessary index rebuilds across a 4-node cluster on every restart. The indexes are rebuilt correctly but the work is redundant — they were already built on the previous run. Root cause: follower replication (ImportSealedChunk) triggers postSealWork which builds indexes, but the index-complete flag isn't persisted across restarts. On restart, IndexesComplete() returns false for replicated chunks, triggering a rebuild.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: The 60-per-node rebuild spam was caused by the placement persistence bug (SetTierPlacements not going through Raft). With that fixed, placements survive restart, tiers keep their storage paths, and index files are found correctly. Only 8 rebuilds remain — cloud tier chunks after failover snapshot restore, which is expected (snapshot doesn't include index files). Closing as fixed by gastrolog-292yi placement replication fix.

title: Catchup fails when recovering node hasn't finished building tiers
description: When a node rejoins the cluster, the placement manager detects the new follower and immediately triggers catchup. But the recovering node is still in ApplyConfig — the vault exists but tiers haven't been added yet. ImportToTier returns 'vault not found' (misleading — the tier within the vault isn't registered). Catchup logs 9 transfer failures and gives up. The node ends up with the tier but missing the chunks, leaving them under-replicated. Fix: either (1) retry catchup on transient 'vault not found' errors, or (2) delay catchup until the follower signals readiness, or (3) the recovering node triggers its own catchup after all tiers are built.

title: Move system Raft group to shared WAL, drop boltdb dependency
description: The config Raft group still uses raft-boltdb for its LogStore/StableStore (data/<node>/raft/raft.db). All tier groups already use the shared WAL (gastrolog-5zd43). Move the config group to its own WAL (separate from the tier WAL, since it has a different lifecycle — ShutdownLast) and remove the raft-boltdb dependency entirely. This simplifies the storage stack to one mechanism (raftwal) and removes a transitive dependency (bbolt).

title: Coalesce Raft heartbeats across all groups into a single RPC per peer
description:
The multiraft transport multiplexes all Raft groups over a single gRPC connection per peer, but each group still sends its own heartbeat message independently. At enterprise scale (500+ Raft groups — hundreds of vaults × 3+ tiers + system group), this means 500+ AppendEntries(empty) RPCs per heartbeat tick per peer.

CockroachDB batches all groups' heartbeats into a single RPC per peer per tick. We should do the same: intercept outgoing heartbeats in the transport layer, collect them for a short window, and send one batched RPC containing all groups' heartbeat metadata. The receiving node demultiplexes and feeds each group's Raft instance.

This covers all Raft groups — tier groups AND the system Raft group.

title: Proto ID fields: string to bytes wire format optimization
description: Follow-up from gastrolog-2ycwz. Change all 170 proto ID fields from string to bytes (16 bytes raw GLID). The wire encoding is identical (both are length-delimited), so this is backward-compatible with existing Raft logs/snapshots. The change reduces message sizes and eliminates string encoding/decoding at the boundary. Requires updating the convert package and all server handlers that parse IDs from proto. The glid.GLID type already has .Bytes() and FromBytes() ready.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Done — 171 bytes ID fields across 10 proto files (matches the ~170 target). The 2 remaining string ID fields are both node_id in fsm.proto, and stay as strings intentionally: hashicorp/raft defines type ServerID string, so node IDs cross the raft API as strings. Converting them to bytes would force round-trip conversions at every raft boundary with no wire savings.

title: Fix E2E test suite after GLID migration
description: The GLID migration (gastrolog-2ycwz) changed all proto ID fields from string to bytes and all display formats from UUID to base32hex. The E2E suite hasn't been run since. Known issues: docker-entrypoint.sh passes removed --bootstrap flag, preventing cluster startup. Likely issues: global-setup.ts may construct requests with string IDs, test assertions may match UUID patterns, any test that creates/inspects entities by ID may break against the new base32hex format. Needs a full pass through all 175 tests across 18 spec files.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: E2E coverage gaps identified during GLID migration testing. The existing 175 tests cover auth, search, settings CRUD (vaults/ingesters/policies/routes), inspector, keyboard shortcuts, cross-node propagation, and pipeline ingestion. Missing coverage: lookup creation/editing (all types), managed file upload/download/sync, cloud service config, node storage config, certificate management, tier transitions/retention, cluster node removal/suffrage, export-to-vault, vault merge/migrate. Multiple bugs (crypto.randomUUID, empty optional IDs, CSV BOM, managed file pull filename, lookup reload) would have been caught by these missing tests.

title: Fix failing TestClusterTransitionThreeTierChainBurst
description: Consistent failure (not flaky) — follower nodes retain chunk directories after full chain transition. Cursor reads 1 record on follower after transition should read 0. Likely a chunk delete not propagating to followers correctly.

title: Frontend react-doctor score regressed from 90 to 86
description: 12 errors, 45 warnings across 30/294 files. Key regressions: HeaderBar setState in useEffect, HelpDialog ref access during render, ExportButton/ScatterboxForm try-finally not supported by compiler. 9 array-index key warnings, 9 missing keyboard handlers, 7 missing roles. Score needs to return to 90+.

title: Lookup settings broken + missing features
description:
Bugs: (1) Created CSV/JSON lookups disappear on reload — proto bytes ID mismatch in save/load path. Likely affects all lookup types. (2) JSON file selector shows 'No files uploaded yet' even when files exist.

Missing features: (3) CSV lookups can't be edited after creation. (4) JSON lookup files have no preview. (5) No 'Manual' / 'Static' lookup type — an inline table editor where operators enter key-value rows directly without uploading a file. Useful for small, hand-maintained mappings (e.g. host→team, code→label).

title: Parallelize E2E tests with isolated cluster-per-worker + cloud storage backends
description: Currently all 174 E2E tests run serially (workers: 1) against a single 3-node cluster in ~4 minutes. Each Playwright worker could get its own isolated 3-node cluster on different port ranges. This eliminates shared state constraints and makes every spec parallelizable. Add MinIO (S3), Azurite (Azure Blob), and fake-gcs-server (GCS) containers to enable E2E coverage of cloud tier creation, archival transitions, restore, and reconciliation — currently untested. Estimated per-worker: 3 gastrolog nodes + 3 cloud backends = 6 containers. 3 workers = 18 containers, ~3GB RAM, runtime ~1.5 minutes.

title: useSystemMutation invalidates every query cache on every mutation
description: Every mutation hook (vault create, tier save, ingester toggle, filter edit, etc.) uses useSystemMutation which invalidates system, vaults, stats, and chunks — regardless of what actually changed. A single lookup column toggle triggers 9 backend calls. Each mutation hook should only invalidate the query keys it actually affects. usePutSettings was fixed as a one-off; the rest need the same treatment.

title: Replace JSONPath with jq (gojq) for JSON lookup transformation
description: Current JSON lookups use github.com/theory/jsonpath (RFC 9535 JSONPath) which can only select, not transform. Users need to reshape complex JSON into flat lookup tables (e.g. extract name+version from package-lock.json). Replace with github.com/itchyny/gojq (3,700 stars, actively maintained, pure Go, compile-once/run-many, goroutine-safe). jq is already known by the target audience (SREs). Migration surface: 3 files (~60 lines). Server-side preview already wired via PreviewJSONLookup RPC. Frontend preview renders results as a reusable PreviewTable component (shared with CSV preview). Extract PreviewTable from CsvSection as part of this work.

title: Binary lookup file format for JSON/CSV lookup tables
description:
Replace the intermediate CSV file format used by JSON (and potentially CSV) lookup tables with a purpose-built binary format optimized for mmap'd lookups.

## Current state
JSON lookup: source JSON → jq transform → writes CSV temp file → mmap CSV → heap-allocated `map[string]int` key index → CSV row parsing on each lookup.

CSV lookup: mmap source CSV → same heap index + per-lookup row parsing.

## Proposed format
Sorted binary file with two sections:
1. **Key index**: sorted keys with value-data offsets — enables O(log n) binary search directly on mmap'd bytes, eliminating the heap `map[string]int` entirely.
2. **Value data**: row values as length-prefixed strings in a contiguous blob per row (all value columns are always read together).

## Benefits
- Zero heap for the index — binary search on mmap'd sorted keys replaces the hash map.
- No CSV parsing overhead on each lookup — values are length-prefixed, no quoting/escaping.
- The only heap allocation per lookup is the result `map[string]string` returned to the caller.
- Same format can back both JSON and CSV lookup engines.

## Notes
- All value columns are added to the record on every lookup (`field_suffix` pattern), so per-column offset within a row is unnecessary.
- First occurrence wins for duplicate keys — the writer deduplicates during the sort.
- Duplicate key count should be surfaced as a warning (already implemented in the CSV path).

title: YAML file lookup tables
description:
Add YAML as a supported file format for file-backed lookup tables, alongside JSON and CSV.

## Rationale
YAML parses to the same `map[string]any` / `[]any` structure as JSON. The entire jq transform → temp file → mmap pipeline is reusable — only the initial parse step changes (`yaml.Unmarshal` instead of `json.Unmarshal`). Same jq expressions, same key/value column config, same mmap'd storage.

## Scope
- New `YAMLFileLookupEntry` proto message (or extend JSON to accept both)
- Backend: detect format from file extension or explicit config, use the appropriate unmarshaler
- Frontend: YAML file upload + same jq/key/value column UI as JSON
- Same 10 MB file size limit as JSON

title: Drag-to-reorder columns in static lookup table editor
description:
The static lookup table editor hardcodes the first column as the key. There's no way to change which column is the key after defining the table — you'd have to delete and recreate.

Add drag-to-reorder on column headers so users can shuffle columns into any position. First column remains the key, but now you control what's first. Drag handles on headers, smooth reorder animation, cell values follow their column.

This applies to both the add form and the edit card body in StaticSection.tsx.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Column and row reorder mechanics work (manual pointer tracking, state-driven re-renders). Visual design needs iteration in-browser — multiple attempts at layout, spacing, and element visibility haven't landed right. The EditableGrid component is functional but needs a design pass with dev tools.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Drag-to-reorder works mechanically (manual pointer tracking, both axes). Visual design needs in-browser iteration — repeated blind CSS attempts have not converged. Shelving for now.

title: Cloud tier: excessive backfill churn and log noise in multi-node clusters
description:
In a multi-node cluster with a cloud-backed tier, the logs show repeated cloud backfill uploads and chunk adoptions every 1-2 minutes across multiple nodes.

## Observed behavior
- Multiple nodes (node1, node4) independently schedule `cloud backfill: scheduled uploads count=1` — only the tier leader should be uploading.
- Every upload triggers `chunk adopted from cloud` on 2-3 other nodes, all at INFO level.
- This repeats every minute for every sealed chunk, producing significant log noise during normal operation.

## Expected behavior
- Only the tier leader uploads chunks to cloud storage. Follower nodes should not schedule uploads.
- Routine backfill uploads and adoptions should log at DEBUG, not INFO. INFO should be reserved for first-time uploads or errors.

## Two distinct problems
1. **Duplicate uploads**: multiple nodes uploading the same chunks wastes bandwidth and cloud API calls.
2. **Log noise**: steady-state cloud sync operations are too verbose at INFO level.

title: Add Discard button to all settings cards missing one
description:
Settings cards that allow editing should have a Discard button to revert unsaved changes. Currently only FileStorageCard, VaultSettingsCard, and StaticSection have one.

Missing Discard on:
- Lookup cards: HTTP, JSON, CSV, MMDB, MaxMind
- IngestersSettings
- UsersSettings

Pattern: show Discard (ghost button) next to Save when the card has unsaved changes. Clicking reverts all fields to the last saved state. See StaticSection and FileStorageCard for the existing implementation.

title: Ingester classification field (passive/active)
description:
Add a passive/active classification to ingesters, derived from the ingester type factory.

- Passive ingesters (listeners): bind a port and passively accept incoming data. Examples: syslog, RELP, HTTP, GELF.
- Active ingesters (collectors): actively pull from data sources. Examples: tail, docker, journald.
- The factory already knows whether an ingester binds a port or reads files — derive the classification from that.

Changes required:
- Proto: add classification enum to ingester config
- Go: factory returns classification, wire through orchestrator
- Frontend: surface classification in ingester cards, use it to conditionally show/hide NodeID selector

This is the foundation for all other ingester HA work.

title: Passive ingester HA — run listeners on all nodes
description:
Passive ingesters (syslog, RELP, HTTP, GELF) with empty NodeID should run on every node in the cluster.

- Empty NodeID = run on all nodes (current behavior only runs on the creating node)
- Records are routed to the correct tier via the existing record forwarder regardless of which node receives them
- No failover logic, no placement manager — every node accepts traffic, LB distributes
- UI shows "all nodes" instead of a node selector for passive ingesters

Depends on the ingester classification field being in place.

title: Active ingester HA — placement manager + Raft checkpoint replication
description:
Active ingesters (tail, docker, journald) get automatic failover via placement management and Raft-replicated checkpoint state.

- Placement manager assigns active ingesters to nodes (same pattern as tier placement)
- Checkpoint state (file offsets, cursor positions, bookmarks) replicated via Raft — small payloads, low-frequency updates
- If a node dies, the Raft leader reassigns its active ingesters to surviving nodes
- The new node picks up from the replicated checkpoint — no data gap, no re-read from beginning
- Only one instance active at a time (Raft leader election prevents split-brain)
- If the data source isn't reachable from the new node (truly node-local path), the ingester fails to start — that's a configuration concern, not a system limitation

This would be novel — no comparable system replicates collector checkpoint state. But GastroLog already has Raft consensus, cross-node record forwarding, and a tier placement manager. The building blocks are in place.

Depends on the ingester classification field being in place.

title: Per-node local ingesters — self + metrics
description:
Both the self ingester and metrics ingester should become per-node local collectors, each node ingesting only its own data.

Self ingester:
- Each node captures its own slog output locally
- Already has the CaptureHandler pattern — ensure it runs on every node automatically

Metrics ingester:
- Currently assigned to a single node, collects cluster-wide metrics via gossip — single point of failure
- Move to per-node local collection: each node ingests only its own metrics (CPU, memory, disk, goroutines, etc.)
- Drop gossip-based metric collection — the data is already local
- Reduces unnecessary gossip traffic

Both:
- Queries fan out across all nodes to get the full cluster picture (same as log search)
- Not user-configurable — they run automatically on every node
- Not failover candidates — inherently node-local, no reassignment needed

title: Ingester node selection and placement infrastructure
description:
Shared infrastructure for ingester HA. Replace single node_id with node_ids (repeated bytes) on IngesterConfig. Multi-select node picker (checkboxes) in the UI. Raft runtime structures track which ingesters are running on which nodes.

COMPLETED: Proto change, Go types, FSM serialization with backwards-compatible migration, orchestrator filtering, server handlers, conflict detection (node set overlap), frontend hooks/settings/inspector/validation, NodeMultiSelect component.

title: Passive ingester HA — listen on all selected nodes with retry
description:
Passive ingesters (listeners) attempt to run on ALL selected nodes simultaneously.

Port bind fails → pending, retry every 3-5s with jitter. Port bind succeeds → register and run, cancel retry. Config change → cancel-and-replace keyed by ingester ID. Node dies → port frees → another node's retry succeeds within seconds.

Numeric badge shows running count vs selected count. Muted when all running, warn when degraded, error when none.

Currently: Run() error is discarded (lifecycle.go:253), goroutine exits silently, ingester is dead. This issue adds retry with jitter for passive ingesters.

title: Active ingester HA — Raft-placed single-node with checkpoint replication
description:
Active ingesters (collectors) run on exactly ONE selected node at a time, Raft-coordinated.

Raft leader assigns the active node, preferring non-leader nodes. Same placement pattern as tier storage. Node dies → Raft reassigns from selected set. Checkpoint state replicated via system Raft group for seamless failover.

title: Ingester node selection and placement infrastructure
description:
Shared infrastructure for ingester HA across both passive and active modes.

## Proto
- Replace single node_id (bytes) with node_ids (repeated bytes) on IngesterConfig.
- Operator selects allowed nodes via multi-select checkboxes in the UI.
- Raft runtime structures track which ingesters are actually running on which nodes.

## Frontend
- Multi-select node picker (checkboxes) replaces the single-node dropdown.
- Numeric replica badge per ingester (same pattern as tier/chunk replica badges): muted when healthy, warn when degraded, error when insufficient.
- Listener/collector badge already in place from gastrolog-4js27.

## Backend
- PutIngester accepts node_ids instead of node_id. Migration: existing single node_id converts to one-element node_ids.
- Raft runtime state: ingester placement map (ingester ID → set of nodes actually running it), synchronized via system Raft group.
- Ingester status aggregation across nodes for the replica badge.

This issue does NOT implement the scheduling strategies — it only builds the shared infrastructure that both passive and active HA depend on.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Duplicate of gastrolog-1h7o6 (closed 2026-04-16) — same title/description created minutes apart. The infrastructure work shipped under that issue. Closing as superseded.

title: Passive ingester HA — listen on all selected nodes with retry
description:
Passive ingesters (listeners: syslog, RELP, HTTP, fluentfwd, OTLP) attempt to run on ALL selected nodes simultaneously.

## Behavior
- Each selected node independently tries to start the listener.
- Port bind fails → mark as pending, retry every 3-5 seconds with jitter.
- Port bind succeeds → register and run normally, cancel retry.
- Config change → cancel-and-replace retry context keyed by ingester ID.
- Node running the listener dies → port frees up → another node's retry succeeds within seconds.
- The port itself acts as the distributed lock — no placement coordination needed.

## Status
- Numeric badge shows how many nodes are running vs how many were selected.
- Muted when all selected nodes are running. Warn when degraded. Error when none running.

## No new config fields
- Uses node_ids from the shared infrastructure (gastrolog-2ty8a).
- No replication factor — the operator controls which nodes via checkboxes, passive ingesters try all of them.

title: Active ingester HA — Raft-placed single-node with checkpoint replication
description:
Active ingesters (collectors: tail, docker, journald, kafka, mqtt) run on exactly ONE of the selected nodes at a time, coordinated via Raft.

## Placement
- Raft leader assigns the active node from the selected set.
- Prefer non-leader nodes — the leader already has higher CPU/memory pressure.
- Same placement pattern as tier storage.
- If the assigned node dies, Raft detects via membership and reassigns to another selected node.

## Checkpoint replication
- Checkpoint state (file offsets, cursor positions, bookmarks) replicated via system Raft group.
- Small payloads, low-frequency updates (every N records or every few seconds).
- On failover, the new node resumes from the replicated checkpoint.

## Status
- Numeric badge shows 1/N (running on one of N selected nodes).
- Warn if the active node is degraded. Error if no node is running.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Duplicate of gastrolog-ju7hk (closed 2026-04-17) — same title/description created minutes apart on 2026-04-16. The actual HA work shipped under branch gastrolog-ju7hk. Closing as superseded.

title: Retention chunk delete forwarding should retry on failure
description:
Retention chunk delete forwarding should retry on failure.

Root cause investigation reveals a deeper issue: under heavy concurrent load (race detector + full test suite), the transition deletes chunks from the leader's tier 0, then forwards deletion to followers. But followers may still be receiving replication for those same chunks. The chunk exists on disk (files present, cursor reads records) but the metadata state is transitional, causing the delete to either fail or target the wrong chunk.

The forward retry (5 attempts with exponential backoff) and the test polling (60s) help but don't fully solve the race between replication AppendRecords and deletion forwarding.

Fix: the transition should coordinate with the replication pipeline — stop replicating a chunk before transitioning it, or the delete forwarding should wait for in-flight replication to complete.

title: Non-storage nodes skip tier Raft group registration on dynamic tier add
description:
When a tier is created after its vault (normal frontend flow: PutVault then PutTier), dispatch.go:applyTierMembershipChange only calls rebuildVaultIfTierMissing → AddTierToVault when tierBelongsHere (this node is a storage leader or follower for the tier).

Non-storage nodes (voters without storage placement) hit the early return at the end of applyTierMembershipChange and never call createTierRaftGroup. But the design from gastrolog-292yi is that every node votes in every tier Raft group.

With RF=1 (1-tier memory vault): 1 storage leader + 3 non-storage voters → 3 never register → election can't get quorum → log spam:

  Election timeout reached, restarting election
  failed to make requestVote RPC ... error="raft group <id> not registered"
  pre-vote campaign failed, waiting for election timeout

AddTierToVault already handles the non-storage case (calls createTierRaftGroup and returns). The fix is in dispatch.go: drop the tierBelongsHere gate for the create path, keep it for the remove path.

Hit during manual testing — the disabled-vault flag was a coincidence, this bug is pre-existing.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Verified on 4-node cluster — raft election spam gone, tier comes up cleanly.

title: Broadcast system improvements
description:
Epic tracking a handful of small improvements to the cluster broadcast system (NodeStats / NodeJobs dissemination). The design is solid and genuinely extensible via proto oneof + subscriber pattern; these are targeted fixes, not a rewrite.

## Children

- Parallel per-peer send with per-peer timeouts (fix head-of-line blocking from slow peers + propagate caller context deadline)
- Evict peer-cache entries on Raft membership change (close unbounded-growth gap for removed-and-never-returning nodes)
- Broadcast observability metrics (counters for send total / failures / latency; message age histograms)
- Remove redundant periodic job broadcast once event-driven path is trusted

## Explicitly out of scope

- Replacing the oneof envelope — it's the right shape.
- Adding ack/retry/delivery guarantees — these are stats, not mutations; best-effort is correct.
- Gossip protocol — full mesh makes it a non-starter here. See gastrolog-cak0u.
- Dedup / replay buffer for missed broadcasts — no real need unless a concrete problem shows up.

title: Broadcast Send is sequential and ignores caller deadline
description:
\`Broadcaster.Send\` in backend/internal/cluster/broadcaster.go:46-59 iterates peers in-order and calls each peer's RPC synchronously. A slow peer blocks every subsequent peer on that broadcast. Additionally, the \`ctx\` parameter is accepted but not used to bound per-peer RPC duration — callers with a 1-second deadline still give each peer the full duration one after another.

## Fix

- Fan out per-peer sends on goroutines, bounded by a WaitGroup.
- Derive a per-peer timeout from the caller's ctx (e.g. \`context.WithTimeout\` off the inbound ctx for each peer), or fall back to a configured default when ctx has no deadline.

## Acceptance

- A single unresponsive peer doesn't delay broadcasts to others.
- Caller-side ctx cancellation actually cancels in-flight per-peer calls.
- Existing first-failure-only log suppression (broadcaster.go:62-72) still works.

title: Peer-cache entries never expire when a node is permanently removed
description:
\`PeerState\` and \`PeerJobState\` entries are TTL'd only on read (peerstate.go:55, peerjobstate.go:46). If a peer is removed from the Raft configuration (scale-down, node permanently decommissioned), its cached entry lingers in the map until something calls \`Get\`/\`GetAll\` — and even then, only that entry is touched. Over time on a cluster that churns nodes, the maps grow unboundedly.

## Fix

Hook into Raft configuration-change events and explicitly delete removed node IDs from \`PeerState\` and \`PeerJobState\`. Either:
- Subscribe to Raft observer events (hashicorp/raft supports \`RegisterObserver\`), or
- Have \`PeerConns\` notify peer-state holders when it observes membership changes (it already reads Raft config in peer_conns.go:191-202).

## Acceptance

- Scaling a cluster down removes the evicted node's entries from both peer state holders within one Raft config-apply.
- No regression in transient-disconnect handling (TTL-based lazy expiry still applies for in-flight flaps).

title: Broadcast observability metrics
description:
The broadcast system has zero metrics today. Silently dropped sends, slow peers, stale peer data are all invisible. Add a minimal set of counters/histograms so operators can see broadcast health:

- \`broadcast_send_total{type,peer}\` — counter per message type and peer.
- \`broadcast_send_errors_total{type,peer}\` — counter per message type and peer.
- \`broadcast_send_duration_seconds{type,peer}\` — histogram.
- \`broadcast_peer_message_age_seconds{type,peer}\` — gauge, how old the most-recent cached peer message is (per type).

Hook into the existing alert system for degraded conditions where it makes sense (e.g. \"stats from peer X are N seconds stale\").

## Out of scope

Frontend surfacing — just backend metrics for now.

title: Remove redundant periodic job broadcast
description:
\`StatsCollector.Run\` broadcasts NodeJobs every tick (statscollector.go:136) AND the \`SetOnJobChange\` callback in app.go:559 triggers a broadcast on every local job transition. That's ~2 broadcasts per tick on a busy node plus event-driven pushes — redundant.

Once the event-driven path is trusted (likely after the broader live-updates epic), remove the tick-driven NodeJobs broadcast and keep only the event-driven one.

## Depends on

Live-updates-rewrite epic (kill frontend polling). Don't drop the tick broadcast until the event-driven path is known to be reliable end-to-end.

## Acceptance

- Only event-driven NodeJobs broadcasts remain.
- Idle cluster: zero NodeJobs traffic. Busy cluster: one broadcast per job state transition, coalesced if needed.

title: Event-driven UI updates / kill polling
description:
Epic to move every frontend-visible live surface off polling (whether pure React Query \`refetchInterval\` or fake streams with internal timer loops) and onto proper event-driven server streams.

## Today's state (audit 2026-04-17)

True push:
- \`WatchSystem\` (configSignal) ✓
- \`WatchSystemStatus\` (statsSignal) ✓
- \`WatchChunks\` ✓

Fake push / pure polling:
- \`WatchJobs\` — 500ms hash-diff loop in job.go:86
- \`useIngesterStatus\` — 5s React Query poll
- \`useJob\` — 1s React Query poll while running
- \`useChunks\` active-chunk stats — 5s merge poll

## Approach

Introduce a local event broker (fan-out pub/sub with bounded per-subscriber buffers) in the scheduler and any other domain components that need one. Domain events (job transitions, ingester assignment changes, etc.) are published once; watchers subscribe and receive deltas. Cross-node peer events arrive via the existing broadcast path (no transport change needed) and get re-published into the local broker so remote events reach local subscribers identically.

## Out of scope

- Cross-node transport rework — current broadcast is already event-driven, covered by the broadcast improvements epic (gastrolog-1kr8f).
- Gossip protocol — full mesh makes it a non-starter (see gastrolog-cak0u).
- Rewriting surfaces that are already true push.
- Rewriting the \`invalidate-and-refetch\` mutation pattern — already push-backed via WatchSystem.

## Children

- Scheduler event broker (foundation)
- Rewrite WatchJobs to use the broker
- Kill useJob polling (subsume into WatchJobs subscription)
- Add WatchIngesterStatus stream
- Active-chunk live stats — event granularity decision (question)

Follow-on (tracked under broadcast epic, depends on this epic): gastrolog-5et04 (remove redundant periodic NodeJobs broadcast once event path is trusted).

title: Scheduler event broker (foundation)
description:
Add a fan-out pub/sub event broker to the orchestrator scheduler. Publishes per-transition events; multiple subscribers receive them independently via bounded per-subscriber buffers.

## Events

- JobScheduled (name, description, schedule, kind)
- JobStarted (id, started_at)
- JobProgress (id, chunks_done, records_done)
- JobCompleted (id, completed_at, status)
- JobFailed (id, error, error_details)

## Broker contract

- \`Subscribe() (<-chan Event, cancel func())\` — returns a bounded channel + cancel.
- Bounded buffer per subscriber (e.g. 256). Slow subscriber: drop-oldest with a counter, or disconnect — pick one, document.
- Broker methods are safe for concurrent use, non-blocking on publish (publish never blocks on a slow subscriber).

## Migration

- Replace the single-slot \`SetOnJobChange\` callback (scheduler.go:225).
- The existing stats-collector consumer (app.go:559) migrates to a subscription and calls \`BroadcastJobs\` on event.
- No behaviour change for the cluster broadcast side yet.

## Tests

- Multi-subscriber fan-out: N subscribers each receive the same event stream.
- Slow subscriber: doesn't block other subscribers' delivery.
- Subscribe / cancel: no leaks, cancelled subscribers stop receiving.
- Concurrent publish + subscribe: no data races.

title: Rewrite WatchJobs to subscribe to the scheduler event broker
description:
\`WatchJobs\` in backend/internal/server/job.go:86-114 is a 500ms hash-diff polling loop that sends the full merged job list (local + cached peer jobs) every time the hash changes. Events that transition within one 500ms window are coalesced; the stream is fundamentally snapshot-based instead of event-based.

## Rewrite

1. On subscribe: send an initial snapshot (current merged job list) to bootstrap the client.
2. Subscribe to the scheduler event broker (from gastrolog-5mcqm) and stream per-event deltas afterwards.
3. \`PeerJobState\` publishes peer-arrived events into the same broker so remote job transitions reach local subscribers on the same stream.

## Wire format

Decide between:
- (a) Stream typed events: \`{kind: JobUpdated, job: <Job>}\`, \`{kind: JobRemoved, id}\` — smaller on-wire, frontend applies deltas.
- (b) Continue streaming full Job objects on each event (client merges by id).

Lean (b) for simplicity unless profiling shows it matters.

## Tests

- New RPC integration test: subscribe → trigger a job transition → observe event on stream within one scheduler tick.
- Multi-subscriber: two concurrent watchers both receive events independently.
- Cancel: client disconnect cleans up the subscription.

title: Kill useJob 1s polling (subsume into WatchJobs subscription)
description:
\`useJob\` in frontend/src/api/hooks/useJobs.ts:153-169 polls GetJob every 1s while the job is running. Once WatchJobs streams proper per-transition events (gastrolog-49bek), \`useJob(id)\` can be a pure client-side selector over the watched job list — no RPC loop needed.

## Approach

- Remove \`refetchInterval\` from \`useJob\`.
- Derive \`useJob(id)\` from the \`useWatchJobs\` cache: filter the watched list by id.
- Fall back to a one-shot \`GetJob\` only if the job isn't in the watched set yet (cold-load case) — don't keep polling.

## Acceptance

- Opening a running-job inspector shows live updates without any periodic refetch.
- Network tab: zero periodic requests for job inspector pages.

title: Add WatchIngesterStatus stream (replaces useIngesterStatus polling)
description:
\`useIngesterStatus\` polls \`GetIngesterStatus\` every 5 seconds (frontend/src/api/hooks/useIngesters.ts:20-31). Replace with an event-driven stream.

## Backend

- Add event source on the ingester manager. Events: ingester assignment changed, alive flag changed, failure state changed.
- New \`WatchIngesterStatus\` server-streaming RPC: initial snapshot, then event deltas.
- Cross-node: existing broadcast path already publishes NodeStats; augment or piggyback so peer ingester status reaches local subscribers.

## Frontend

- Replace \`useIngesterStatus\` with \`useWatchIngesterStatus\`.
- Follow the existing \`useWatchSystem\` / \`useWatchSystemStatus\` pattern.

## Out of scope

- Changing what ingester-status data is exposed — same shape, just delivered via push.

title: Active-chunk live stats — event granularity decision
description:
\`useChunks\` today polls every 5 seconds to refresh active-chunk byte/record counters (frontend/src/api/hooks/useVaults.ts:63-101). The main WatchChunks stream is event-driven but fires on lifecycle events (create / seal / delete), not on every append. So live-counter updates come from the 5s poll.

## Question

Do we want mid-chunk live counters, or is seal-boundary granularity enough for operator UX?

## Options

1. **Events at seal/rotation boundaries only.** Cheapest. No mid-chunk counter updates; the UI shows the last sealed chunk's count + a "writing..." affordance for the active one.
2. **Throttled event on every N records or every M seconds (backend-side).** E.g. publish a \`ChunkProgress\` event at 1 Hz if anything was appended since the last publish. Keeps live counters visible without per-record events.
3. **Keep the 5s poll for active-chunk stats only, push everything else.** Pragmatic middle ground — acknowledges active-chunk counters are a different class of data.

## Recommend

Option 2, scoped to file-backed tiers only (memory tiers don't need it). Decision + design before implementation.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Decision: Option 2 — throttled 1 Hz ChunkProgress event, scoped to file-backed tiers. Active-chunk counters tick at 1 Hz when anything has been appended since the last publish; otherwise silent. Reuses the existing WatchChunks stream with a new event kind. Implementation under this issue.

title: Per-peer tx/rx byte counters on inter-node gRPC transport
description:
Expose Bytes/sec tx + rx between each node pair as a first-class metric. Useful for spotting replication-hot links, congested tier-transfer paths, and noisy cross-node broadcasters.

## Scope

Covers ALL inter-node gRPC traffic, not just broadcast:
- Raft (system group + tier groups via multiraft)
- Broadcast (NodeStats / NodeJobs)
- Tier replication (AppendRecords / SealTier / ImportSealedChunk / DeleteChunk)
- Query forwarding (ForwardSearch, GetContext, etc.)
- Chunk streaming / drain

## Approach

Install a gRPC \`stats.Handler\` on both client and server sides of the inter-node transport. The handler sees every RPC's wire bytes via \`InPayload\` / \`OutPayload\` events and tags by:
- peer node ID (from connection metadata)
- direction (tx / rx)
- optionally: RPC service + method

Aggregate into per-peer counters; expose as prometheus metrics.

## Metrics

- \`cluster_peer_bytes_sent_total{peer,service,method}\` — counter
- \`cluster_peer_bytes_received_total{peer,service,method}\` — counter
- Leaving Bytes/sec to PromQL (\`rate(...)\`).

## Out of scope

- Payload inspection or per-message-type accounting (that's the broadcast metrics issue gastrolog-54157).
- Bandwidth shaping / QoS — counters only, no enforcement.

## Notes

- PeerConns (backend/internal/cluster/peer_conns.go) already owns the client-side connection pool — install the stats handler there.
- Server side: install on the gRPC server the inter-node services register with.
- Tag high-cardinality labels (method) only if it's cheap; per-peer tx/rx is the primary view.

title: Reclassify ingester HA axis from active/passive to singleton/parallel
description:
Current code uses `ListenAddrs != nil` (passive = listener) as the signal for HA placement in `placementManager.reconcileActiveIngesters`. Non-listeners get HA singleton placement; listeners run on every selected node.

This conflates two orthogonal axes:
- **how data arrives**: listener (accepts connections) vs collector (generates / pulls)
- **HA semantics**: singleton (exactly one node, Raft-coordinated failover) vs parallel (run on every selected node)

Whether singleton is the right choice for a given ingester instance depends on broker/source behavior (e.g., Kafka consumer groups, MQTT shared subscriptions) — so it has to be a per-instance config toggle, not a factory-level decision. But for some ingesters singleton is semantically meaningless (per-node-local data sources: docker, self, tail, metrics) — for those the factory should hide the toggle entirely.

## Design — two layers

1. **`IngesterRegistration.SingletonSupported bool`** — factory-level hint. When `false`, the singleton toggle is hidden in the UI and ignored by placement (belt-and-suspenders against stale config).
2. **`IngesterConfig.singleton bool`** — per-instance toggle. Defaults to `false` (parallel).

Effective: `singleton := reg.SingletonSupported && cfg.Singleton`.

## Categorization

| Ingester | SingletonSupported | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| chatterbox, scatterbox | true | synthetic — both parallel (exercise all nodes) and singleton (failover test) are legit |
| kafka, mqtt | true | depends on broker: consumer groups / shared subs → parallel, naive broker → singleton |
| docker, self, tail, metrics | false | per-node-local source — singleton would lose 3/4 of cluster data |
| http, relp, otlp, fluentfwd, syslog | false | listener — OS port coordination, concept doesn't apply |

## Changes

1. Proto: add `bool singleton = ...` to `IngesterConfig`.
2. Orchestrator: add `SingletonSupported bool` to `IngesterRegistration`.
3. Placement (`app/placement.go`): rename `reconcileActiveIngesters` → `reconcileSingletonIngesters`. Replace the `isPassiveIngester` gate with `isSingletonIngester` that reads `reg.SingletonSupported && cfg.Singleton`. Parallel ingesters need no central assignment — skip them.
4. Dispatch (`app/dispatch.go`): update `shouldRunIngester` — parallel ingesters run on every node in `NodeIDs`, singleton ingesters consult `GetIngesterAssignment`.
5. UI: add the `singleton` checkbox to the ingester form, rendered only when the registered type is `SingletonSupported`.
6. CLI: `--singleton` flag on `gastrolog ingester put`. Warn and ignore when type doesn't support it.
7. Audit each existing ingester registration and set `SingletonSupported` per the table above.

## Scope note

Supersedes `gastrolog-1dex0` (active HA) / `gastrolog-4pn18` (passive HA) as currently specified. `gastrolog-4z596` (per-node local ingesters: self + metrics) is subsumed — both become parallel-only via `SingletonSupported: false`.

The orchestrator's existing `Passive` concept (port-bind retry semantics for listeners) is unchanged. That stays tied to `ListenAddrs != nil` and has nothing to do with placement.

title: Canonicalize node identity in raft StableStore, remove home/node_id auto-regenerate
description:
## Problem

`<home>/node_id` is currently the canonical source of each node's raft ServerID and the identity stamped on every record the node produces. [home.go:124-128](backend/internal/home/home.go#L124-L128) uses a `readOrCreate` pattern that **silently generates a fresh GLID when the file is missing** and writes it back:

```go
func (d Dir) NodeID() (string, error) {
    return d.readOrCreate("node_id", func() string {
        return glid.New().String()
    })
}
```

If the file is deleted (backup restore with a missed file, operator cleanup, template-copied data dir, etc.) the node silently mints a new identity, writes a new `NodeConfig` to the FSM with that new ID, and becomes a stranger to its prior raft membership. No error, no warning. Regression introduced by `13ca5c2e` (gastrolog-25z9) when multi-node support was bolted onto a previously single-node raft that used a hardcoded `"gastrolog-1"` ServerID.

## Fix

Move canonical identity into the system-raft group's StableStore under the reserved key `gastrolog:node_id`, stored as **16 raw bytes** (the underlying `[16]byte` of `glid.GLID`).

### Why StableStore

- Already crash-safe, fsync'd, and batch-written by `raftwal`
- Lifetime tied to raft data — cloning/wiping raft state also clones/wipes identity (consistent)
- Our own code — no external library constraints on key format or value encoding
- Natural neighbor to `CurrentTerm`/`LastVoteCand` which raft itself persists there

### Startup flow (new `resolveIdentity`)

1. Open system-raft WAL (idempotent — raft would open it anyway shortly)
2. `Get([]byte("gastrolog:node_id"))`
3. Branch:
   - **Found** → decode 16 bytes to `glid.GLID`, use as `conf.LocalID`
   - **Missing + no `--join-addr`** → bootstrap: `glid.New()`, `Set` raw bytes, fsync, bootstrap raft with that ID
   - **Missing + `--join-addr=...`** → enrollment RPC returns assigned ID, `Set`, fsync, join
   - **Missing + existing raft log** → fatal, clear error: *"node identity not found in raft data — this data directory is corrupt or was created outside the bootstrap/enrollment flow"*

### Migration for existing clusters

One-shot on startup: if StableStore key is absent **and** `<home>/node_id` file exists, read the file, write to StableStore, log a one-time warning. Current 4-node dev cluster survives with no manual intervention.

### `<home>/node_id` role after fix

Reverts to strictly advisory. Written once during bootstrap/enrollment as a human-readable convenience (`cat data/node1/node_id` still works). Never read by the runtime as canonical — if missing, diverges from StableStore, or contains garbage, the runtime ignores it and rewrites it from StableStore on next boot.

## Scope

- New `Load/SaveNodeID` helpers on the WAL (or small wrapper)
- `resolveIdentity` in [app.go:574-591](backend/internal/app/app.go#L574-L591) rewritten to consult StableStore first
- `home.NodeID()` retired; replaced with advisory `WriteNodeIDCache`
- Bootstrap path writes the generated ID to StableStore before raft bootstrap
- Enrollment path writes the received ID to StableStore before raft join
- Tests: single-node bootstrap, multi-node enrollment, restart with intact StableStore, restart with wiped file + intact StableStore (file rewritten), restart with wiped StableStore + existing raft log (fatal), migration from pre-fix data dir

## Impact on cluster.sh

None. The init flow (`node 1 with no --join-addr`, `nodes 2-4 with --join-addr`) drives the same bootstrap/enroll branch that exists today; only the ID persistence mechanism changes.

## Out of scope

- EventID gaining `NodeID` field (separate issue)
- Chatterbox singleton/parallel bug (tracked in gastrolog-2kcw4, debugged after this lands)

title: Add NodeID to EventID — resolve multi-node ingester identity collision
description:
## Problem

With singleton/parallel HA classification now in place (gastrolog-2kcw4), an ingester can run concurrently on multiple nodes in parallel mode — e.g. chatterbox on all 4 nodes. Each node's orchestrator independently maintains per-ingester sequence counters, so two nodes emit records like:

    EventID{IngesterID=X, IngestTS=t, IngestSeq=5}

with the same values. The only thing currently distinguishing those records is the `node_id` string attr set in [lifecycle.go:357](backend/internal/orchestrator/lifecycle.go#L357), which is not part of the identity key. That's an identity collision on the primary EventID tuple — indexes, dedup paths, and any downstream consumer keyed on EventID will conflate records from different nodes.

## Fix

Promote NodeID from an attr to a first-class EventID field. With 61kjk merged, `localNodeID` is a guaranteed-unique 16-byte GLID, so the representation is naturally fixed-size.

### Struct changes

    type EventID struct {
        IngesterID glid.GLID
        NodeID     glid.GLID   // NEW — 16 bytes
        IngestTS   time.Time
        IngestSeq  uint32
    }

### Record frame impact (file tier)

[record.go](backend/internal/chunk/file/record.go): `IdxEntrySize` grows from 58 → 74 bytes. Add `idxNodeIDOffset = 58`. Update Encode/DecodeIdxEntry, BuildRecord, BuildRecordCopy, offset-invariant tests.

### Record frame impact (cloud tier)

[chunk/cloud/writer.go](backend/internal/chunk/cloud/writer.go) / [reader.go](backend/internal/chunk/cloud/reader.go): append 16 bytes to the per-record frame alongside IngesterID. Bump format version, fail-fast on mismatch.

### Proto

Record proto in `vault.proto` and `query.proto` gains `bytes node_id` (16 bytes). Regenerate both sides.

### Stamp site

[orchestrator/lifecycle.go::digestAndForward](backend/internal/orchestrator/lifecycle.go): remove the `msg.Attrs["node_id"]` stamp; set `record.EventID.NodeID = glid.Parse(o.localNodeID)` (or equivalent — localNodeID is already a GLID string). Keep backward compat: scanner still surfaces `node_id` as a derived first-class field in query results.

### Query layer

[query/scanner.go](backend/internal/query/scanner.go) and [aggregate.go](backend/internal/query/aggregate.go): replace `node_id` attr lookups with `rec.EventID.NodeID.String()`. The UI-visible field name stays `node_id`.

### Data wipe

No production cluster — bump format version and let existing chunks be unreadable. Operator wipes data dir.

## Scope

- Proto field add (Record, Vault Record)
- EventID struct
- File tier index entry: IdxEntrySize 58→74, new offset, encode/decode, tests
- Cloud tier frame: +16 bytes, version bump, tests
- digestAndForward stamp
- scanner/aggregate field extraction
- FrontendĀ (generated proto pulls new field; decoding in DetailPanel and record views)

## Tests

- Record roundtrip with distinct NodeIDs preserves identity
- Two parallel chatterboxes on different nodes produce non-colliding EventIDs
- Multi-node query returns node_id as a derived field with correct per-record value
- File tier: old-format chunk rejected with clear error
- Cloud tier: old-format frame rejected with clear error

## Why now

Pre-61kjk, singlenton/parallel didn't exist, so ingester_id was effectively unique per emitter. Post-2kcw4, chatterbox et al. run parallel across N nodes, and EventID collisions are a live bug the moment two nodes emit records in the same microsecond with matching per-node sequence numbers — measured in hours of runtime at any realistic throughput.

## Out of scope
