6. Inspect chunks → all stuck at `replica_count=3`. gastrolog-3's `/vaults` is empty.

## Why this points to per-vault Raft, not catchup or replication

- The catchup mechanism (`SweepMissingReplicas` at [vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go:706](backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go#L706)) is correctly designed for exactly this scenario. It runs on followers every 20s and uses `RequestReplicaCatchup` RPC to pull missing chunks from the leader.
- It's gated on `r.tier != nil` and `r.fsm != nil` — both depend on a healthy per-vault Raft state.
- gastrolog-3 never gets to that state. The pre-vote-loop is the root.

## Likely surface

The cluster comment at [dispatch.go:577-582](backend/internal/app/dispatch.go#L577-L582) says "Every node participates in every vault-ctl Raft group whether or not it has a storage placement (gastrolog-292yi)". So when gastrolog-3 joined the cluster Raft, it should have been added to every existing per-vault Raft group as a voter. Either:

1. The membership-add for existing per-vault groups is missing or racy — gastrolog-3 doesn't know it's a member, so it tries to elect itself instead of waiting for heartbeats.
2. The per-vault Raft transport routing isn't reaching gastrolog-3, even though cluster Raft does.
3. The per-vault group's voter list still contains the pre-expand 3 nodes; gastrolog-3 is rejected as a non-voter.

Worth checking `raftgroup.GroupManager.AddVoter` flows and how new cluster members propagate into existing per-vault groups.

## Related

- gastrolog-3rmly (closed): originally framed as "catchup doesn't fire on RF growth"; correctly diagnosed as duplicate of this ticket.
- gastrolog-3tn5g (closed): partial-success visibility for replication. Independent of this; its WARN logs would surface this scenario at the leader side ("replicated to fewer followers than expected") once a chunk is sealed and replication tries to push to gastrolog-3.

## Test coverage

The existing multinode tests should be extended with a "join after vaults exist" scenario — start cluster with 3 nodes + a vault, wait, add a 4th node, verify the new node converges into the per-vault Raft group within a bounded window.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
Original framing was wrong. The vote-loop logs were a red herring — the actual root cause is **the RequestReplicaCatchup RPC client at chunk_replicator.go:262 silently dropped tier_id**, leftover from gastrolog-257l7 (vault refactor). Server validation rejected with 'tier_id: expected 16 bytes, got 0', so SweepMissingReplicas never recovered any chunks on followers.

Fix: drop tier_id from the catchup RPC entirely (the proto comment already said it was 'retained transitionally'). End-to-end:
- proto: dropped tier_id from RequestReplicaCatchupRequest
- client RequestReplicaCatchup: dropped tierID param
- server requestReplicaCatchup: dropped validation
- replicaCatchupFn / SetReplicaCatchupFn: dropped tierID
- orchestrator CatchupSelectedChunks: dropped tierID, looks up vault.Instance directly
- SweepMissingReplicas: dropped tierID from the call

Backend tests + frontend tsc clean.

Note: this only addresses the catchup RPC. The broader 'eliminate every tier reference' sweep (4150 matches across 196 files) is its own piece of work — should file separately.

title: Finish tier elimination — gastrolog-257l7 closed prematurely, residue everywhere
description:
gastrolog-257l7 ("Phase 1: tier collapse") and parent gastrolog-55dej were closed 2026-05-06/05-08 with acceptance: "main does not contain substantive code uses of tier_id, TierConfig, TierPlacement, TierInstance". That criterion was not met:

- gastrolog-6c32m: live cluster broken because `RequestReplicaCatchup` proto kept `tier_id` and the client dropped it on the floor. Fixed surgically; the rest of the residue remains.
- ~4150 matches of "tier" across 196 files (proto, Go, TS, tests, docs).

## Scope (incremental, one branch)

### Proto wire
- Drop `tier_id` from `ChunkReplicationCommand` (renumber tags)
- Drop `tier_id` from `ImportRecordMessage` (StreamToTier path)
- Audit remaining messages for stale `tier_id`

### Server handlers (cluster pkg)
- Drop tierID from `RecordTierAppender`, `SealTierExecutor`, `TierRecordImporter`, `DeleteChunkExecutor` signatures + impls
- Rename: `TierRecordImporter` → `ChunkImporter`, etc.

### Client (chunk_replicator.go)
- Drop tierID from `AppendRecords`, `SealVault`, `ImportSealedChunk`, `DeleteChunk`
- Drop tierID from `streamKey` (key on vaultID + nodeID)

### Orchestrator internal
- Drop tierID from `replicateToFollower`, `replicateToTarget`, `findLocalTier`, `AddTierToVault`, `RemoveTierFromVault`, `ensureVaultCtlTierMetadata`, `FollowerTargets`, etc.
- Rename: `tier_leader_manager.go` → `vault_ctl_leader_manager.go`; `tierLeaderManager` type → `vaultCtlLeaderManager`
- Rename: `tier_drain.go`, `tier_instance.go` → `vault_*`

### Logging / comments
- Drop `tier=` slog fields where redundant with `vault=`
- Strip "tier" from comments where it's just stale terminology (per CLAUDE.md "user-facing docs describe current system")

### Tests
- Rename `vault_tier_test.go` → `vault_test.go`
- Drop tierID from test fakes
- Delete tests that only existed to exercise multi-tier shapes

### Frontend
- Drop `TierId` from generated TS types (falls out of proto regen)
- Drop tier-named props and field names (NodeBadge, IngesterCard, etc.)
- Update help docs

## Acceptance

- `rg -n '\btier' backend/ frontend/` returns only:
  - vault-ctl Raft references (correct: it's the vault control plane)
  - historical references in CHANGELOG.md / commit-message-bodies
- gastrolog-6c32m + multi-node tests pass
- Cluster up/down/expand round-trip works

## Out of scope

- vault-ctl Raft itself (correct name, stays)
- Anything in docs/vault_redesign.md (historical)

title: Add 'transfer chunks' retention disposition: move sealed chunks to a target vault unchanged
description:
Today VaultConfig.RetentionDisposition supports two values: `delete` (drop matching records) and `route` (stream records through the routing engine). Add a third value, `transfer`, that re-homes the sealed chunk to a different vault unchanged — no record decode, no re-route, no re-ingest. The target vault is operator-selectable per source vault.

Where `route` is the right tool when records should be filtered, re-tagged, or re-fanned-out, `transfer` is the right tool when the records themselves shouldn't change but their *home* should — long-term archive vaults, per-tenant migration, or cold-storage tiers downstream of a hot vault.

## Scope

- New config: VaultConfig.RetentionTransferTargetVaultID *glid.GLID (or similar), required when disposition is `transfer`.
- UI: dropdown of vaults next to the disposition selector when `transfer` is chosen.
- Proto + Go + TS + UI label + help docs (per the rename-through-the-stack rule).
- Single-node + multi-node tests, happy + unhappy paths.

## Design questions that need decisions before implementation

1. **Transition mechanism.** Three options: (a) file-system move where source and destination share storage, fall back to copy+delete otherwise; (b) always copy+delete with a vault-ctl Raft hand-off; (c) re-point the FSM entry without moving files (only works when storage layout is shared). What's the right default?
2. **Acknowledgement / atomicity.** Receipt-protocol-style ack from destination before source FSM deletes the chunk (like CmdRequestDelete does today)? Or eager source-side delete with destination eventually-catches-up via reconciliation?
3. **Replication factor mismatch.** Source RF=3, dest RF=1: do we drop replicas after transfer, or keep all three until retention on the destination culls them? Source RF=1, dest RF=3: do we re-replicate (chunk transfer fan-out) before deleting source?
4. **Vault type compatibility.** File → file is obvious. File → cloud? Cloud → file? Memory → file? Disallow? Require explicit conversion?
5. **Destination state.** Disabled vault, draining vault, missing vault — what does the source do? Pause? Error? Fall back to `delete`?
6. **Retention on destination.** Does the transferred chunk inherit the destination's retention rules from the moment it lands (could re-fire retention immediately), or is it grandfathered for some window?
7. **Chunk ID collision.** Destination already has a chunk with this ID — skip, replace, or error?

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
## Current state of the drain feature (audit for design-question #1)

The existing drain machinery is **not directly reusable as a feature**, only as primitives. Audit:

- **`DrainVault(ctx, vaultID, targetNodeID)`** — wired, but internal-only. Called automatically from `app/dispatch.go:210` when the placement reconciler observes a vault placement change that moves the vault to a different node. No proto RPC, no CLI command, no UI control. Operator-invisible side effect of `CmdSetVaultPlacements`.

- **`DrainInstance(ctx, vaultID, mode, targetNodeID)`** — **dead code**. Declared in `orchActions` interface (`app/dispatch.go:34`), defined in `orchestrator/vault_drain.go:53`, but zero production callers. The whole `vaultDrainState` machinery + `DrainMode` enum (`DrainDecommission` / `DrainRebalance`) exists only because tests exercise it.

- **`CancelDrain` / `IsDraining`** — wired into the internal `DrainVault` flow only (`app/dispatch.go:152–153, 207`).

**Implication for this issue:**
- Cannot piggy-back on a "drain feature" as if it were a complete operator-facing capability — it isn't one.
- The reusable surface is lower-level: `drainOneChunk` (per-chunk transfer worker inside `drainInstChunks`) and the chunk-replication primitives (`replicateToFollower`, `ImportSealedChunk`).
- Design-question #1 (transition mechanism) should pick between the chunk-replication primitives directly and the lifecycle-reconciler receipt protocol (`CmdRequestDelete` / pendingDeletes / SweepPendingObligations) — the drain code's worker loop is a candidate but not the obvious winner, because its surrounding invariants are "this vault is leaving this node," not "this chunk's home is being changed cluster-wide."

**Separately worth noting:** the dead `DrainInstance` mode machinery + `vaultDrainState` (decommission/rebalance modes) are themselves a "remove completely" candidate. They look load-bearing in code review but are uncallable in production. Not in scope for this issue, but a future agent reading them will assume they matter.

title: Rotation policy changes don't apply until next sweep (or never)
description:
## Symptom

Changing a vault's rotation policy in the settings UI (or editing an existing policy's contents) does not immediately take effect on the active chunk. The config is updated correctly, but the chunk manager continues to apply the previous policy until either:

1. The next 15-second `rotationSweep` tick runs AND the new threshold is already exceeded by current state, OR
2. Records are appended that cross the new threshold via the Append-path `ShouldRotate` check.

If neither condition is met, the new policy effectively never fires on the current chunk. The user is 'fucked' for the duration of the previous policy's natural lifetime (e.g. 24h on an age-based policy that has been replaced by a record-based one).

The behaviour is inconsistent: sometimes mid-flight policy switches work, sometimes they don't. The 'sometimes works' case is when the new threshold is already exceeded by the current chunk state at the moment the 15s sweep tick fires.

User reports the issue is **worse in Kubernetes**, where leadership and placement churn may be amplifying secondary issues (suspected `IsFollower` flapping — separate investigation).

## Root cause

`Orchestrator.ReloadRotationPolicies` in [backend/internal/orchestrator/reconfig_policies.go:30-43](backend/internal/orchestrator/reconfig_policies.go#L30-L43) is a no-op stub. It was stubbed in commit `deedbc54` ('fix: discovery-based rotation sweep') on the rationale that the 15-second `rotationSweep` job would reconcile everything.

Result: every config-change notification — `NotifyRotationPolicyPut`, `NotifyRotationPolicyDeleted`, `NotifyVaultPut` — flows through `configDispatcher.applyExistingVaultChanges` ([backend/internal/app/dispatch.go:250-269](backend/internal/app/dispatch.go#L250-L269)) and calls the no-op. There is no synchronous apply path; everything is gated by the 15-second sweep tick.

This regresses the pre-deedbc54 behaviour where the dispatcher would hot-swap the policy on every leader's chunk manager the moment the FSM committed the change.

## Fix

Restore real work to `ReloadRotationPolicies`: iterate registered vaults, find each leader instance's `VaultConfig` and resolved `RotationPolicyConfig` in the loaded system, build the chunk-side policy via `policyCfg.ToRotationPolicy()`, and call `vaultInst.Chunks.SetRotationPolicy(policy)` immediately. Skip followers (sweep still stamps `NeverRotatePolicy` on them).

Cron-schedule changes can continue to lag until the next sweep tick (15s) — they fire on minute boundaries anyway. The threshold-based bound is the urgency-critical one.

## Acceptance criteria

- Switching a vault's `RotationPolicyID` (or editing the assigned policy) immediately applies the new policy to the active chunk manager on every leader node, without waiting for the 15-second sweep.
- Subsequent appends evaluate the new policy.
- If the new policy's bound is already exceeded by current chunk state at the moment of the FSM commit, the active chunk seals within a couple of sweep ticks (existing `CheckRotation` path).
- Followers continue to use `NeverRotatePolicy`.
- Regression test: single-node test that proposes a policy change and asserts the chunk manager's policy is the new one without waiting on the 15s sweep.
- Multi-node cluster test that exercises the same flow across leaders and followers.

## Out of scope

- Suspected secondary bug where `IsFollower` may flap during placement churn on Kubernetes (separate investigation; tracked separately if reproduced).
- Retention policy reload (`ReloadRetentionPolicies` is also a no-op with the same shape; same fix should apply but tackle in a follow-up if not bundled here).
closed_reason: Synchronous hot-swap restored; validated in k8s — policy changes now apply immediately on the leader's chunk manager. Merged into gastrolog-1bgvm for the k8s rebuild.

title: Settings UI doesn't refresh after creating or editing entities
description:
## Symptom

When users add or change entities in the Settings UI — not just rotation/retention policies or vaults, but multiple entity kinds — the settings views frequently fail to refresh to include the newly created or edited entity. The user must manually reload or navigate away and back to see the change.

This is intermittent ('many times'). It is a clear regression: previously the settings UI updated immediately on entity mutations.

## Why this should work

GastroLog has a push-based config refresh path (gastrolog-4oc3, see [MEMORY.md](../.claude/projects/-Users-kluzz-Code-gastrolog/memory/MEMORY.md#config-push-updates-gastrolog-4oc3)):

- Backend: `configDispatcher` fires `configSignal.Notify()` after FSM mutations. `notify.Signal` ([backend/internal/notify/signal.go](backend/internal/notify/signal.go)) broadcasts via a close-and-recreate channel pattern.
- Frontend: `useWatchConfig()` in [frontend/src/App.tsx](frontend/src/App.tsx) subscribes to a `WatchConfig` server stream and invalidates the `['config']` and `['settings']` query caches on each message.
- `useConfig()` has `staleTime: 60_000` as a safety net plus `structuralSharing` via `protoSharing` to suppress no-op re-renders.

Every user-visible mutation should land in two places: the FSM `Apply` (which mutates the store) AND a `configSignal.Notify()` (which kicks the stream). If either is missing for a given mutation kind, the UI silently goes stale.

## Hypotheses to investigate

Order roughly by likelihood given recent activity:

1. **Missing `Notify` calls in the FSM dispatcher path for some mutation kinds.** Audit every case in [backend/internal/app/dispatch.go](backend/internal/app/dispatch.go) `configDispatcher.Handle` and verify each `Notify*` notification kind triggers `configSignal.Notify()` either directly or via a downstream call. Recent tier-eradication and refactors (e.g. gastrolog-2boj1) may have dropped the signal call from one of the handlers.

2. **Settings views querying a key that `useWatchConfig` does not invalidate.** `useWatchConfig()` invalidates `['config']` and `['settings']`. If a tab queries `['ingesters']`, `['routes']`, `['storages']`, etc. as a separate key, those go stale. Grep `frontend/src/api/hooks/` for `useQuery` calls whose keys are not in that set.

3. **`structuralSharing` / `protoSharing` false-equal.** If proto identity comparison treats the new list as equal to the old (e.g. new entity has the same encoded bytes for some reason, or list-level comparison short-circuits), the UI will not re-render. Worth a one-off log to confirm new messages arrive on the stream when the bug repros.

4. **`buildFullSystem` omitting fields.** Precedent: gastrolog-3flfp 5c/N `fix(server): include LogLevels in buildFullSystem` was exactly this shape — the WatchConfig payload omitted a field, and a tab depending on it never saw updates. Likely candidates: any entity kind added or renamed since the tier eradication.

5. **Connect-RPC stream lifecycle.** The stream may be silently disconnecting on some clients (especially the Cursor embedded browser tab — see [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md#cursor-embedded-browser-tab) — but that is secondary).

## Reproduction approach

- Open Settings on a multi-node cluster.
- Create a new ingester, route, storage, rotation policy, retention policy, vault, and log level — one at a time.
- For each, check whether the new entry appears in the corresponding list within ~1 s.
- Cross-reference any failure to refresh against the FSM notification kind on the backend side and the React query key on the frontend side.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every Settings UI list view updates immediately (within one stream tick, <1 s) when an entity of its kind is added, edited, or deleted.
- `buildFullSystem` includes every entity collection consumed by the Settings UI.
- `configDispatcher` fires `configSignal.Notify()` for every user-visible mutation.
- A test exists that asserts the WatchConfig payload contains a new entity after a `Put*` FSM apply.

## Out of scope

- Performance tuning of the WatchConfig stream.
- Connect-RPC reconnect logic for the Cursor embedded browser tab pathology.

## Related

- gastrolog-4oc3 (the original push-update implementation)
- gastrolog-3flfp 5c/N (`buildFullSystem` precedent: a tab went stale because the proto payload omitted a field)
- gastrolog-1rj63 (sibling regression: backend dispatcher was no-op for rotation policy reloads — possibly the same class of post-tier-eradication regression)
closed_reason: Followers now wait for local FSM Apply after Forward before returning. SystemServer mutation handlers see post-mutation state when building the response snapshot. Validated in k8s — settings UI refreshes immediately after creating/editing entities.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
## Root cause located

This is a Raft multi-node read-after-write race.

`SystemServer` mutation handlers (e.g. `PutRotationPolicy` in [backend/internal/server/system_policies.go](backend/internal/server/system_policies.go)) follow this pattern:

```go
if err := s.sysStore.PutRotationPolicy(ctx, cfg); err != nil { ... }
s.notify(...)
fullCfg, err := s.buildFullSystem(ctx)   // ← reads local store
return &PutRotationPolicyResponse{System: fullCfg}, nil
```

On the leader, `sysStore.PutRotationPolicy` calls `raft.Apply` which is synchronous w.r.t. local FSM Apply — so `buildFullSystem` reads fresh data. Fine.

On a **follower**, `raft.Apply` returns `ErrNotLeader`, the code falls back to `forwarder.Forward(ctx, data)` ([backend/internal/cluster/forwarder.go:41-51](backend/internal/cluster/forwarder.go#L41-L51)) which sends the command to the leader via gRPC. The leader's `forwardApply` handler applies and returns — but the follower's own FSM is not guaranteed to have caught up at that point. `forwardApply` ([backend/internal/cluster/forward.go:699-709](backend/internal/cluster/forward.go#L699-L709)) returns an empty response.

So on a follower-handled mutation:
1. Forward returns once the leader has applied.
2. `buildFullSystem(ctx)` runs on the follower, reading from the follower's **local** FSM store — which is still pre-mutation.
3. Response carries a stale snapshot.
4. Frontend `setQueryData(['system'], stale)` writes stale into cache.
5. `useWatchSystem` sees `streamVer == memVer` (both at the new index from the mutation response) → **skips invalidation**.
6. UI stays stale until something else advances the version past the mutation's index.

This matches the 'many times' intermittence: when the UI is connected to the leader pod (or the follower's FSM happens to catch up between Forward returning and `buildFullSystem` reading), the response is correct. Otherwise it's stale.

Kubernetes amplifies it because pod load-balancing routes the UI to arbitrary pods on each session.

## Fix shape

Extend the `ForwardApply` RPC to return the applied Raft log index:

```proto
message ForwardApplyResponse {
  uint64 applied_index = 1;
}
```

Leader's `forwardApply` handler returns `future.Index()` from the `raft.Apply` call.

Follower's `raftstore.Store.applyRaw`, after `Forward` returns successfully, polls `s.raft.AppliedIndex()` until `>= applied_index` (with a bounded timeout from the existing `applyTimeout`). Once caught up, return — `buildFullSystem` on the follower now reads fresh data.

Same shape applies to the sibling cluster commands; the vault-ctl forwarder is a separate path but has the same architectural issue if it has the same pattern.

## Smaller alternative (frontend-only, weaker)

`useSystemMutation.onSuccess` could schedule a delayed `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['system'] })` ~200ms after the mutation, betting that the follower's FSM has caught up by then. Doesn't fix the underlying staleness — just gives the cluster a second window to settle — and re-introduces the follower-lag refetch race that the current setQueryData path was added to avoid.

The backend fix is the right one.

title: Active chunk record count oscillates in inspector UI
description:
## Symptom

In the inspector view, the active chunk's record count visibly jumps up and down between refreshes (the user described it as 'going mental'). The underlying data is correct: a 5-second-refresh search over `last=5m` shows record counts climbing steadily, and when a chunk seals (the rotation policy fires at the configured bound — 1000 records in the reproduction), the sealed chunk's count is stable. Only the **active** chunk's displayed count oscillates.

The symptom is much worse in Kubernetes than on local dev clusters — consistent with peer-to-peer RPC latency variance widening tail timeouts.

## Root cause

[backend/internal/server/vault_chunks.go:115-187](backend/internal/server/vault_chunks.go#L115-L187) — `dedupChunkReports` plus `moreAuthoritative`.

`ListChunks` is a fan-out RPC: every node hosting the vault contributes its view of every chunk it knows about. `dedupChunkReports` merges per-chunk entries by ID and picks the 'most authoritative' version via:

```go
func moreAuthoritative(a, b *apiv1.ChunkMeta) bool {
    return a.Sealed && !b.Sealed
}
```

For two **active** chunk reports (both `Sealed = false`), `moreAuthoritative` returns `false` in both directions. So `a.best` stays at whichever report arrived **first** into the dedup map — there is no tiebreaker on freshness.

Insertion order:

1. Local chunks (the API node, [vault_chunks.go:39-57](backend/internal/server/vault_chunks.go#L39-L57)).
2. Remote fan-out in placement order — leader at index 0, then followers ([vault_chunks.go:208-218](backend/internal/server/vault_chunks.go#L208-L218)).

If the API node is the vault leader, local goes in first with the authoritative count → stable display.

If the API node is **not** the leader, the leader sits at `remoteNodes[0]` and is fanned out in parallel via `peerFanOut` with a bounded per-peer timeout. **When the leader peer misses the deadline**, the loop skips it (`if !ok[i]`, [vault_chunks.go:85](backend/internal/server/vault_chunks.go#L85)) and the first follower's report wins — followers do not replicate active-chunk record growth (only sealed chunks are replicated, per `feat: sealed chunk replication, replacing record-level mirroring`), so followers carry a stale or zero `RecordCount` for the active chunk. Each `WatchChunks` tick is a fresh fan-out; whether the leader makes the deadline is a coin flip in Kubernetes.

Result: the displayed count flip-flops between the leader's true count and a follower's stale count.

## Fix sketch

`moreAuthoritative` needs a tiebreaker for the active-chunk case. The natural one is `RecordCount` (monotonic during a chunk's lifecycle):

```go
func moreAuthoritative(a, b *apiv1.ChunkMeta) bool {
    if a.Sealed != b.Sealed {
        return a.Sealed
    }
    return a.RecordCount > b.RecordCount
}
```

`Bytes` is an alternative tiebreaker and may be safer if there is a path where one report transiently has a higher `RecordCount` without the corresponding bytes (race between two announcements). Verify before locking in.

**Cross-node correctness check before fixing**:
- Is `RecordCount` ever reported higher by a non-leader than the leader? Should not happen given sealed-only replication, but worth grepping the announcement/replication paths to be sure.
- Does any path overwrite `RecordCount` to a smaller value during a lifecycle transition (e.g. seal → compress)?

**Tests required (CLAUDE.md mandates single + multi-node, happy + unhappy + edge):**

- **Single-node**: `dedupChunkReports` unit test with two active-chunk reports — assert the higher `RecordCount` wins.
- **Multi-node**: cluster test where the API node is a non-leader and the leader temporarily times out; assert the merged `ListChunks` result still reflects the leader's authoritative count on the subsequent tick.
- **Edge**: equal `RecordCount` (tie) — deterministic outcome via secondary key (e.g. `Bytes`).
- **Sealed**: existing sealed → unsealed preference unchanged; sealed wins regardless of `RecordCount`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Active chunk record count in the inspector grows monotonically between refreshes for the duration of a chunk's active lifetime, on **every node** the UI may be connected to.
- A leader peer timeout no longer flips the displayed count to a follower's stale value; the previous leader value persists.
- New unit + multi-node tests guard the regression.

## Related

- gastrolog-1rj63 (rotation policy hot-swap regression — separate symptom, same family of cluster-side fallout from the tier-eradication sweep)
- gastrolog-2nxij (settings UI refresh — separate symptom in the same UI-disagreement-with-backend-state family)
closed_reason: moreAuthoritative tiebreaks on RecordCount among unsealed views; active-chunk record count grows monotonically in the inspector across all nodes.

title: Policy changes during fresh-cluster warm-up are silently dropped
description:
## Symptom

On a freshly-started k8s cluster, the first 3-4 rotation-policy switches behave flakily: sometimes they take effect, sometimes the chunk manager keeps applying the previous policy. After roughly 3-4 switches, the cluster settles and every subsequent switch is picked up immediately.

This is observed on top of the gastrolog-1rj63 hot-swap fix. That fix removed the unconditional 15-second polling delay. What remains is a narrower race window: changes that fire while the vault instance is still being built on the local leader node are silently dropped, and the operator has to fire the change again (or wait for the rotationSweep tick) before it takes effect.

## Root cause hypothesis

[backend/internal/orchestrator/reconfig_policies.go](backend/internal/orchestrator/reconfig_policies.go) (the gastrolog-1rj63 fix):

```go
for vaultID, vault := range o.vaults {
    vaultInst := vault.Instance
    if vaultInst == nil || vaultInst.IsFollower {
        continue   // ← silently dropped
    }
    ...
}
```

`vault.Instance` is populated asynchronously by [buildVaultInstance](backend/internal/orchestrator/reconfig_vaults.go#L600-L648) after `AddVault` is called. On a fresh cluster, the build window is wide enough to span several user actions:

1. Operator creates the vault → `NotifyVaultPut` → `handleVaultPut` → `AddVault` starts the async build.
2. Operator immediately edits or switches the rotation policy → `NotifyVaultPut` (or `NotifyRotationPolicyPut`) → dispatcher fires `ReloadRotationPolicies` → `o.vaults[id].Instance == nil` → `continue` → **no apply**.
3. Build completes ~seconds later; `vault.Instance` is set with whatever `vaultCfg` snapshot was passed into `AddVault` (the snapshot from step 1, missing the step 2 change).
4. Within ~15 s the `rotationSweep` tick runs, finds the vault, reads current config, applies the latest policy → eventually correct.

Net effect: each policy change that arrives during the build window is silently dropped at the dispatcher path, and only the sweep catches up. The operator sees 'switching is flakey as heck the first 3-4 switches'.

## Compounding factors (to investigate)

- **Placement convergence.** Cluster-wide `vaultCfg.Placements` are reconciled against `NodeStorageConfigs` to determine leader/follower roles. On a fresh cluster, these may not settle on the first FSM-apply round. A node that briefly thinks it is a follower stamps `NeverRotatePolicy` on every rotationSweep tick, swallowing user policy.
- **Vault-ctl Raft group election.** Each vault has its own Raft group. Elections settle within seconds but the first events after creation may land before there is a stable leader.
- **`IsFollower` flag is never flipped back to false.** A follower that gets promoted keeps `IsFollower = true` until the orchestrator rebuilds the instance.

## Fix shape

Cheapest improvement: when `buildVaultInstance` finishes and assigns `vault.Instance`, re-read the *current* config and apply the latest rotation policy to the new instance — covers config changes that arrived during the build window.

```go
// After: vault.Instance = ti
if !ti.IsFollower {
    if latest, err := o.loadSystem(ctx); err == nil && latest != nil {
        if vaultCfg := findVaultConfig(latest.Config.Vaults, vaultID); vaultCfg != nil && vaultCfg.RotationPolicyID != nil {
            if policyCfg := findRotationPolicy(latest.Config.RotationPolicies, *vaultCfg.RotationPolicyID); policyCfg != nil {
                if policy, err := policyCfg.ToRotationPolicy(); err == nil && policy != nil {
                    ti.Chunks.SetRotationPolicy(policy)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

(Better: factor the apply path into a helper used by both `ReloadRotationPolicies` and the post-build re-apply, so they cannot diverge.)

Add a slog warning at the silent-skip in `ReloadRotationPolicies` so missed applies become visible to operators rather than disappearing into the sweep window.

Investigate the `IsFollower`-never-flipped-back lifecycle as a follow-up.

## Acceptance

- Policy changes that arrive between `AddVault` and `vault.Instance` being set are applied as soon as the instance is built, without waiting for the 15 s sweep.
- A log line is emitted on each dispatcher-time skip so operator-visible 'lost' applies are diagnosable.
- Multi-node test that fires a rotation-policy change before `AddVault` completes and asserts the new policy is in effect on the next append.

## Related

- gastrolog-1rj63 (hot-swap fix — assumed `vault.Instance` was ready, which is not always true on fresh clusters)
- gastrolog-1bgvm (active-chunk dedup oscillation — same family of cluster-side fallout from tier eradication)
- gastrolog-2nxij (settings UI refresh — same dispatcher-vs-async-state race shape)
closed_reason: Role transitions now apply the role-appropriate rotation policy immediately via ApplyRotationPolicyForRole. Validated in k8s — policy switching is reliable from the first switch, no warm-up flakiness.

title: Empty rotation/retention policies can be created and assigned silently
description:
## Symptom

The Settings UI allows creating a rotation policy with all of `MaxBytes`, `MaxAge`, `MaxRecords`, and `Cron` left unset. The policy saves successfully and can be assigned to a vault, but it never fires — `ToRotationPolicy()` returns `(nil, nil)` for an empty policy, and the chunk manager keeps whatever policy it had before.

For an operator the failure mode is silent: 'I assigned the new policy but rotation never fires.' No error at create-time, no error at assign-time, no warning in the UI. The vault either uses its previous policy or, if none, the factory default (typically `DefaultMaxChunkBytes` from the chunk manager).

Same shape almost certainly applies to retention policies: `RetentionPolicyConfig` with all of `MaxAge`, `MaxBytes`, `MaxChunks` unset also yields `(nil, nil)` from `ToRetentionPolicy()`.

## Root cause

[backend/internal/system/policies.go](backend/internal/system/policies.go) — `ToRotationPolicy()` (line 66-101) builds a slice of sub-policies, and if `len(policies) == 0` returns `(nil, nil)`. The conversion is correct as a pure transformation. The bug is upstream: no validation rejects the empty config at the PutRotationPolicy boundary.

[backend/internal/server/system_policies.go](backend/internal/server/system_policies.go) — `PutRotationPolicy` validates the policy by calling `ToRotationPolicy()` and treating non-error as success. But `(nil, nil)` is a non-error: the handler stores the empty policy in the FSM.

[frontend/src/components/settings/PoliciesSettings.tsx](frontend/src/components/settings/PoliciesSettings.tsx) — the rotation-policy create/edit form lets the user submit with all four fields blank.

## Fix shape

Three places need a guard, in priority order:

1. **Backend: `PutRotationPolicy` rejects an empty policy** with `InvalidArgument` if `MaxBytes`/`MaxAge`/`MaxRecords`/`Cron` are all nil or empty. Same for `PutRetentionPolicy` (`MaxAge`/`MaxBytes`/`MaxChunks` all nil). This is the authoritative gate — covers CLI parity (`gastrolog rotation-policy put …`) without separate work.
2. **Frontend: form validation disables the Save button** while the policy is empty, with an inline hint near the field group ('at least one condition required').
3. **Optional defensive**: `ToRotationPolicy()` returns an error rather than `(nil, nil)` when the slice ends up empty — catches the case where some future caller bypasses the handler. Keep `(nil, nil)` semantics only for callers that explicitly opt into 'no rotation' via a dedicated path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Submitting a fully-empty rotation policy via the UI shows a validation error and does not call `PutRotationPolicy`.
- Submitting an empty policy via the CLI (or any future caller) returns `InvalidArgument` and does not mutate the FSM.
- Same coverage for retention policies.
- Tests in `system_test.go` (or equivalent) assert the empty-policy rejection on the server side.

## Out of scope

- Retroactively cleaning up existing empty policies in the store. Operators who created one can fix it by editing or deleting it.

## Related

- Closed sibling: gastrolog-1rj63 (rotation hot-swap regression in the same family of post-tier-eradication cluster-correctness gaps)
closed_reason: Backend rejects empty rotation/retention policies with InvalidArgument; frontend disables Save when no condition is set. Validated in native cluster.

title: Histogram tooltip clips at top of chart on tall bars
description:
## Symptom

ECharts histogram tooltip uses the default positioning (above the cursor). When the user hovers over a bar near the top of the chart area — i.e. the visible record-count is high and the cursor is near the chart's top edge — the tooltip is rendered above the cursor and clips off the top of the chart container.

The operator recalls a prior fix that flipped the tooltip below the cursor when there wasn't room above. That fix isn't present in the current code path (no `tooltip.position` callback in [frontend/src/hooks/useHistogramOption.ts](frontend/src/hooks/useHistogramOption.ts)). Either it was lost in a refactor (most likely the c7373c38 visx → ECharts migration or the d425015d decompose into hooks) or it was on a different chart and the operator's memory is conflating them.

## Fix

Add a `tooltip.position` callback to the ECharts option that:
- Flips the tooltip below the cursor when `cursorY < tooltipHeight + gap`.
- Otherwise places it above (matching ECharts default).
- Clamps horizontally so the tooltip doesn't slide off the right edge near the latest bar.

## Acceptance

- Hovering near the top of the histogram (high record counts) shows the tooltip below the cursor, fully visible.
- Hovering on shorter bars keeps the tooltip above the cursor as before.
- Hovering near the right edge of the chart shows the tooltip with its right side clamped to the viewport.
closed_reason: tooltip.position callback flips below cursor when room above is tight; operator confirmed in dev build

title: AllNodes ingesters only start on creator node after cluster restart
description:
On cold cluster restart, ingesters configured with all_nodes=true only start on the node whose ID appears in the (legacy) NodeIDs list, not on every node as intended.

**Root cause**: orchestrator/factory.go:254-257 (cold-start path) does not consult AllNodes:

```go
// Selected-node gate: if NodeIDs is non-empty, this node must be in it.
if len(recvCfg.NodeIDs) > 0 && !slices.Contains(recvCfg.NodeIDs, o.localNodeID) {
    return nil
}
```

The runtime hot-path (app/dispatch.go:381 shouldRunIngester) correctly short-circuits on AllNodes:

```go
if !cfg.AllNodes && len(cfg.NodeIDs) > 0 && !slices.Contains(cfg.NodeIDs, d.localNodeID) {
    return false
}
```

So config edits after startup correctly fan out, but cold restart gates non-creator nodes.

**Observable symptoms**:
- UI ingester badge stuck at "1/4" after cluster restart for AllNodes ingesters
- Only one node logs `starting ingester …` on boot; others show `ingesters=0`
- Per-node CLI `config ingester status` reports `Running: true` everywhere (reads FSM alive map which has one entry; flagged true for any entry) and total `Messages Ingested ≈ N` (peer-broadcast aggregate from the one running node), masking the bug
- FSM `node_status` map has only the creator node marked alive

**Fix**: mirror dispatch.go in factory.go — `if !recvCfg.AllNodes && len(recvCfg.NodeIDs) > 0 && !slices.Contains(...)`.

**Tests**: multi-node harness — create an AllNodes=true ingester with non-empty NodeIDs=[node-A], simulate cluster restart, assert ingester runs on every node (orch.ListIngesters() includes the ID on each, FSM alive map has every node).

title: AllNodes ingesters absent from non-creator nodes in node inspector
Inspector and Settings read ingesters from two separate caches
description:
Settings and Inspector consume ingester data from different React Query caches that update on different schedules. Settings updates instantly after a save; Inspector lags by one ListIngesters round-trip and can drift across tab switches.

**Two caches today**:

| Consumer | Hook | Query key | Source RPC | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `IngestersSettings.tsx` | `useConfig` | `["system"]` | `GetSystem` | `IngesterConfig[]` |
| `InspectorDialog` / `EntityListPane` / `NodeDetailPane` / `IngesterCard` | `useIngesters` | `["ingesters"]` | `ListIngesters` | `IngesterInfo[]` (adds `node_status` + `running`) |

**Symptom**: when toggling AllNodes on an ingester in Settings and then jumping to Inspector → Nodes → click each node, the per-node ingester list is briefly stale. Settings sees the change immediately (the mutation’s response carries the new System config, and `useSystemMutation` writes it directly into `["system"]` via `setQueryData`, bypassing the Raft-follower race). Inspector waits for `invalidateQueries(["ingesters"])` to round-trip a fresh ListIngesters, which can race with subsequent UI clicks.

**Architectural fix**: collapse to one source of truth. Two viable shapes:

1. **Drop `["ingesters"]` entirely.** Inspector reads `IngesterConfig[]` from `useConfig()` (same as Settings); per-card runtime state (`node_status`, counters) comes from the existing `useIngesterStatus(id)` server-stream hook. No second cache, no fan-out invalidation, no race.
2. **Make `["ingesters"]` write-through.** Have `useSystemMutation` synthesize `IngesterInfo[]` from the response’s `IngesterConfig[]` and `setQueryData(["ingesters"], ...)` alongside `["system"]`, leaving `node_status` to be filled in by the next stream tick. Less invasive but keeps the cache duplication.

Option 1 is the cleaner end state and removes a real source of UI drift; option 2 is a stopgap. Prefer 1 unless something binds the inspector to ListIngesters specifically.

**Out of scope**: the `structuralSharing` type bug (`IngesterConfig.equals` on `IngesterInfo[]` swallowing `node_status` deltas) is being fixed under gastrolog-3fftf and is independent of the cache split.

title: Frontend domain model layer — stop leaking proto into components
description:
**Problem.** The frontend has no model layer between the wire format (proto-es generated types from `api/gen/`) and React components. React Query is the cache, hooks are thin RPC wrappers, components consume raw proto messages and reinvent the same derivations (ID encoding, eligibility filters, status badges, name lookups) in every site that needs them. Single-field changes ripple across many components — witnessed three times this week in gastrolog-my66y / gastrolog-3fftf / gastrolog-3syzn, all symptoms of the same flatness.

**Quantified pain (May 2026 grep)**:
- 39 component files import generated proto types directly from `api/gen/`
- 295 inline `encode()` calls across 42 component files (Uint8Array → string GLID)
- 40 component files reference `Uint8Array` directly
- Ingester eligibility (`allNodes` / `nodeIds`) duplicated across 4+ component files
- Node name lookup (`config?.nodeConfigs.find((n) => encode(n.id) === nodeId)`) duplicated across NodeBadge, IngesterCard, NodeDetailPane, EntityListPane
- ~20 inline `JobKind.*` / `JobStatus.*` checks, ~11 inline `VaultType.*` checks

**End state.** A thin model layer in `src/api/model/` with:
- Typed entity wrappers (`Ingester`, `Vault`, `Node`, `Job`, `Route`) that own ID-to-string conversion and computed properties (`eligibleNodes`, `runningCount`, `displayName`, etc).
- Hooks in `src/api/hooks/` return model instances, not proto types.
- Components import only from `src/api/model/` and `src/api/hooks/` — never from `src/api/gen/`. ESLint rule enforces.
- Push pipeline (WatchSystemStatus, WatchChunks, etc.) unchanged; cache layer (React Query) unchanged.

**Non-goals.** No state-management rewrite (no Redux/Zustand). No backend changes. No runtime cost — models are plain objects/classes constructed from the proto, no reactivity overhead. Settings forms can keep editing IngesterConfig directly; the model layer is for *read* paths.

**Approach.** Work entity-by-entity. Foundation first (ID utilities), then each entity gets a wrapper + hook flip + consumer refactor in one cohesive child issue. Cleanup pass with ESLint guard last. Each child is independently shippable and reversible.

Child issues track the per-entity work; this epic exists to keep the larger goal coherent and to land the ESLint guard only once every entity has migrated.

title: Foundation: EntityID type + ID conversion utilities
description:
**Goal**: lay the foundation that every other child in gastrolog-2e2qs builds on — a typed entity-ID abstraction that hides Uint8Array at component boundaries.

**Scope**:
- Create `src/api/model/id.ts`.
- Export a branded type `EntityID` (string under the hood; the brand exists for editor hints and to discourage mixing IDs with arbitrary strings).
- Helpers: `idFromBytes(b: Uint8Array): EntityID`, `idToBytes(id: EntityID): Uint8Array`. These wrap the existing `encode` / `decode` in `src/api/glid.ts` so behaviour is unchanged.
- Helper: `eqID(a, b): boolean` to replace string-comparison-after-encode patterns (`encode(x) === encode(y)`) that appear in name-lookup loops.

**Out of scope**: no component refactor yet, no entity wrappers. This issue is the kit; subsequent issues consume it.

**Done when**:
- New module compiles, has a minimal unit test (round-trip bytes → ID → bytes, eqID truth table).
- No call sites changed (it's net-additive at this stage).

**Why this first**: every entity model needs to expose `id: EntityID` instead of `id: Uint8Array`. Doing the foundation as a standalone change keeps each entity issue small and reviewable.

title: Ingester entity model + consumer migration
description:
**Goal**: collapse the four+ inline copies of ingester-eligibility / running-count / display-label logic into a single `Ingester` model. Tightest target because we hit this code three times this week (gastrolog-my66y, gastrolog-3fftf, gastrolog-3syzn).

**Scope**:
- Create `src/api/model/ingester.ts` exporting an `Ingester` class (or plain factory; whichever fits the existing utils/ patterns better).
- Constructor takes `IngesterConfig` + optional alive map + live-node set; exposes:
  - `id: EntityID` (string)
  - `name`, `type`, `enabled`, `singleton`, `allNodes`
  - `pinnedNodeIds: EntityID[]` (encoded, not Uint8Array)
  - `isEligibleOn(nodeId: EntityID): boolean` — owns the `allNodes || nodeIds.length === 0 || nodeIds.includes(nodeId)` logic that we’ve now fixed twice
  - `eligibleNodes(liveNodes: Set<EntityID>): EntityID[]`
  - `selectedCount(liveNodes)`, `runningCount(aliveMap)`
  - `displayLabel`, `statusVariant(aliveMap, liveNodes): 'info' | 'warn' | 'error' | 'muted'`
- Flip `useIngesterAlive` if necessary so it returns `Map<EntityID, NodeStatus>` (already close).
- Add helper `useIngesters()` back (or rename) that returns `Ingester[]` derived from `useConfig` + `useIngesterAlive` + `useClusterStatus`. Single source of truth, single hook.

**Consumer migration**:
- `src/components/inspector/IngesterCard.tsx`
- `src/components/inspector/NodeDetailPane.tsx`
- `src/components/inspector/EntityListPane.tsx`
- `src/components/settings/IngestersSettings.tsx` (read paths only; the form continues to edit IngesterConfig directly)

Each consumer should stop importing `IngesterConfig` from `api/gen/` and stop calling `encode()` inline on ingester IDs.

**Done when**:
- `grep -r 'allNodes \?\|nodeIds.some(\|nodeIds.length' src/components` is empty.
- IngesterCard takes `Ingester`, not the inline structural type it has today.
- No re-exposed runtime behaviour change (UI unchanged, tests pass).

Depends on gastrolog-5l1bj (EntityID foundation).

title: Node entity model + node-registry hook
description:
**Goal**: kill the four-place duplication of `config?.nodeConfigs.find((n) => encode(n.id) === nodeId)` and `peerNameById` Map-construction (currently rebuilt inline in NodeBadge, IngesterCard, NodeDetailPane, EntityListPane).

**Scope**:
- Create `src/api/model/node.ts` exporting a `Node` wrapper around `ClusterNode + NodeConfig + NodeStats`. Computed properties:
  - `id: EntityID`, `name: string` (falls back to `id` when empty — current ad-hoc behaviour)
  - `role` and `suffrage` exposed as typed enums (today's call sites stringify these manually)
  - `isLeader`, `isLive`, `isLocal(localNodeId)`
  - `stats: NodeStats | null`
- Create `useNodeRegistry()` in `src/api/hooks/useNodes.ts` (or extend an existing hook) returning `{ all: Node[]; byId: Map<EntityID, Node>; localNodeId: EntityID }`. Backed by `useConfig` (for nodeConfigs) + `useClusterStatus` (for live state) + `useSettings` (for localNodeId).

**Consumer migration**:
- `src/components/settings/NodeBadge.tsx` — drop the inline find, take `Node` or `EntityID` and let the badge query the registry.
- `src/components/inspector/IngesterCard.tsx` — drop the inline nodeCfg find on line ~172.
- `src/components/inspector/NodeDetailPane.tsx` — drop `peerNameById` Map construction.
- `src/components/inspector/PeerBytesSection.tsx` — accept the registry instead of a `peerNameById` prop.
- `src/components/inspector/EntityListPane.tsx` — drop the inline find at line ~406.

**Done when**:
- `grep -r 'nodeConfigs.find\|peerNameById\|cluster?.nodes.find' src/components` returns 0 hits.
- The four call sites consume `useNodeRegistry()`.
- NodeBadge takes `nodeId: EntityID` (or a `Node`), not `nodeId: string` with implicit format.

Depends on gastrolog-5l1bj.

title: Vault entity model + consumer migration
description:
**Goal**: wrap `VaultConfig + VaultInfo + ChunkMeta[]` into a coherent `Vault` model so the inspector and settings views stop reaching into proto fields for derived state.

**Scope**:
- Create `src/api/model/vault.ts` exporting `Vault`. Computed:
  - `id: EntityID`, `name`, `enabled`
  - `type` as typed VaultType enum (currently 11 inline `VaultType.` checks scattered across components)
  - `placementNodeId: EntityID | null` — owns the existing `(encode(v.nodeId) || localNodeId) === nodeId` fallback logic
  - `isCloudBacked`, `cloudServiceId`
  - `activeChunk`, `sealedChunks`, `chunkCount`, `recordCount`, `bytes`
  - `displayLabel` (name fallback to id)
- Flip `useVaults()` to return `Vault[]`. Existing per-vault hooks (`useChunks`, `useIndexes`) can stay as runtime overlays.

**Consumer migration**:
- `src/components/inspector/VaultCard.tsx`
- `src/components/inspector/EntityListPane.tsx` (vault filtering)
- `src/components/inspector/NodeDetailPane.tsx` (per-node vault filter)
- `src/components/settings/VaultSettingsCard.tsx` (read-side; the form keeps editing VaultConfig)
- `src/components/settings/VaultsSettings.tsx` (read-side)

**Done when**:
- `grep -r 'VaultType\.' src/components` shrinks; remaining hits are inside the Settings forms (which legitimately edit the proto enum).
- `grep -r 'encode(v.nodeId)' src/components` returns 0 hits.

Depends on gastrolog-5l1bj.

title: Job entity model + consumer migration
description:
**Goal**: collapse the ~20 inline `JobKind.*` / `JobStatus.*` switches into typed predicates on a `Job` model.

**Scope**:
- Create `src/api/model/job.ts` exporting `Job`. Computed:
  - `id: EntityID`, `nodeId: EntityID`
  - `kind` as typed enum (today's call sites import `JobKind` directly 3+ times)
  - `status` as typed enum (likewise)
  - `isScheduled`, `isTask`, `isFinished`, `isFailed`, `isRunning` predicates
  - `displayDuration` (replaces inline elapsed/countdown calls from `utils/temporal`)
  - `nextRun` (for scheduled jobs)
- Flip `useJob` and `useWatchJobs` to return `Job` / `Job[]`.

**Consumer migration**:
- `src/components/inspector/JobCard.tsx`
- `src/components/inspector/ScheduledJobsTable.tsx` (if it exists separately) or the equivalent rendering site
- `src/components/inspector/NodeDetailPane.tsx` (tasks / scheduled split)
- `src/components/inspector/EntityListPane.tsx` (jobs entity list)

**Done when**:
- `grep -r 'JobKind\.\|JobStatus\.' src/components` returns 0 hits outside the model layer.
- Inspector job rendering reads only from `Job` typed predicates.

Depends on gastrolog-5l1bj.

title: Route entity model + consumer migration
description:
**Goal**: smaller-blast-radius companion to the other entity migrations. Wrap `RouteConfig + GetRouteStatsResponse` per-route entry into a single `Route` model.

**Scope**:
- Create `src/api/model/route.ts` exporting `Route`. Computed:
  - `id: EntityID`, `name`
  - `stages` typed (inline filter expressions live on stages per gastrolog-4kkoo)
  - `vaultTargets: EntityID[]` (resolved through Vault model)
  - `matchedRecords`, `forwardedRecords`, `droppedRecords` from the stats overlay
- Add a `useRoutes()` derivation that joins `useConfig().routes` with `useRouteStats()` and returns `Route[]`.

**Consumer migration**:
- `src/components/inspector/RouteStatsView.tsx`
- `src/components/settings/RoutesSettings.tsx` (read-side)

**Done when**: route consumers no longer import from `api/gen/` for runtime reads; they consume `Route`.

Lower priority than ingester / vault / node / job because routes have a smaller footprint and the existing code paths are simpler. Pick up after the higher-traffic entities.

Depends on gastrolog-5l1bj.

title: ESLint guard: forbid api/gen imports in src/components
description:
**Goal**: prevent regression of the entanglement that gastrolog-2e2qs cleaned up. Once every entity has a model wrapper and the consumers migrate, lock the door.

**Scope**:
- Add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule (or path pattern) in `frontend/.eslintrc` (or wherever the project's ESLint config lives) that bans imports from `../**/api/gen/**` inside `src/components/**`.
- Exception: settings *form* components legitimately edit proto enum values (VaultType, JobKind in create forms). Either grant per-file exceptions with an inline disable comment, or split forms into a sub-tree whitelist. Decide during the issue — both are acceptable, but pick one consistently and document the choice in a top-of-file comment near the lint rule.
- Allow `src/api/model/**` and `src/api/hooks/**` to keep importing `api/gen/**` — they're the bridge.

**Done when**:
- Lint runs clean on the current tree.
- Adding a fresh `import { IngesterConfig } from "...api/gen/..."` to any file under `src/components/` fails CI (or the pre-commit hook).

**Depends on** the per-entity migration issues completing first — without them, components have no model layer to import from, and the rule would block every existing read site. The dcat dep graph should reflect that:
- depends on gastrolog-3wkiu (Ingester)
- depends on gastrolog-10vew (Node)
- depends on gastrolog-3dyau (Vault)
- depends on gastrolog-w9p39 (Job)
- depends on gastrolog-24obv (Route)

This is the closing-bracket of the epic. Don't ship it until the bracket can actually close.

title: OnIngesterAlive Raft apply swallows errors — FSM alive map silently drops entries
description:
**Symptom**: an ingester is running and ingesting normally, but the inspector shows `0/N` (yellow/warn variant) on its status badge and yellow node chips in the expanded card. The CLI confirms the goroutine is producing data; the FSM alive map is empty.

**Root cause**: `backend/internal/app/app.go:230-238` — the `OnIngesterAlive` callback fired by `runIngester → setIngesterAlive(true)` has a 2-second timeout and discards the error:

```go
OnIngesterAlive: func(ingesterID glid.GLID, alive bool) {
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    _ = cfgStore.SetIngesterAlive(ctx, ingesterID, nodeID, alive)
},
```

During cluster startup the four nodes race to apply Raft commands while elections / catchup are still settling. If a per-call apply exceeds 2s the context times out, the error is silently dropped, and nothing re-fires the `SetIngesterAlive(true)` write. The ingester goroutine continues running, but the FSM never receives the alive record. Verified directly against the running cluster via `WatchSystemStatus` — `ingester_alive` entries are present (so the dispatch path is correct) but `node_status` is the empty map.

Latent companion to gastrolog-my66y. That issue made the ingester *start* on the right nodes; this hole means it just doesn't announce itself to the FSM.

**Fix options** (pick during the issue, document the choice):

1. **Retry on transient failure.** Wrap `SetIngesterAlive` in a bounded retry loop with backoff. Log every retry; alert if it keeps failing. Cleanest fix.
2. **Periodic re-affirmation.** A low-frequency goroutine sweeps every running ingester and re-writes `alive=true` if the FSM disagrees with the orchestrator. Self-healing safety net even if the initial write fails.
3. **Don't swallow the error.** At minimum, log it — currently there's no breadcrumb at all when the FSM diverges from reality.

Probably do (1) + (3). (2) is a belt-and-braces option for resilience.

**Tests**:
- Reliability test that injects a slow Raft apply (or temporary unavailability) during startup and verifies the alive map converges to the running set within a bounded window.
- Multi-node test that restarts the cluster, asserts every `AllNodes=true` ingester ends up with `alive=true` for every node in the FSM map, not just `Running: true` from the local orchestrator.

**Out of scope**: gastrolog-2e2qs frontend model layer work. The badge logic reads the data faithfully — this is a backend-only fix.

title: config node list-storage -o json ignores node-name filter argument
description:
**Symptom**: `gastrolog config node list-storage <node-name> -o json` returns the **full system NodeStorageConfigs list**, ignoring the node argument. The text-format (default) output respects the filter; only the JSON path is broken.

**Repro**:

```sh
# Two nodes, both with disk-1 storage:
gastrolog config node list-storage node-1            # one row, filtered correctly
gastrolog config node list-storage node-1 -o json    # entries for ALL nodes
```

**Root cause**: `backend/cmd/gastrolog/cli/node.go:222-224` — the JSON branch is unconditional:

```go
p := newPrinter(outputFormat(cmd))
if outputFormat(cmd) == "json" {
    return p.json(resp.Msg.NodeStorageConfigs)
}
```

The text branch (line 227) does respect `filterNodeID`. Fix is to apply the same filter to the JSON output: walk `NodeStorageConfigs` and emit only entries whose `NodeId` matches when `filterNodeID != ""`.

**Blast radius**: shipped a real deploy bug (gastrolog-e7pez) — the auto-wire scripts used `-o json | grep '"name":"disk-1"'` for idempotency. Once any node had disk-1, every subsequent check matched and every later node was skipped, so storage only landed on the bootstrap node. Scripts were patched to use the text path (gastrolog-e7pez), but the underlying CLI footgun is still live for any future automation.

**Acceptance**:
- `-o json` honors the node-name argument the same way the text output does.
- Regression test that covers both code paths: text + JSON, with and without a node filter.
- (Optional, low-priority) audit `-o json` branches elsewhere in the CLI for the same 'ignore the filter' mistake — there may be more.

**Why pri 3**: the scripts that hit this are already fixed; this is a future-footgun cleanup. Anyone writing new automation against `-o json` would otherwise rediscover it.

title: Outbound record sinks (Fluent Forward, cross-cluster forwarding) — open design questions
description:
## Context

Discussion thread on adding an outbound "sink" capability to GastroLog: emit records from a vault to an external Fluent Forward receiver. The downstream can be Fluentd, Fluent Bit, another log lake, or another GastroLog cluster — the sink doesn't care.

This is the symmetric counterpart of the existing `fluentfwd` ingester. We already speak the wire format on the receive side, so adding it on the send side reuses the same codec.

## Summary of discussion

- **GastroLog already receives Fluent Forward.** The `fluentfwd` ingester accepts records from Fluentd, Fluent Bit, or anything else speaking the protocol, on `:24224` by default. The "fluent-bit" container in `deploy/k8s-deps.yml` is a full Fluent Bit install used purely as a smoke-test source (dummy input → forward output).
- **A streaming sink fits the existing model.** `ExportToVault` already materializes search results into another *internal* vault; an outbound sink generalizes that to external targets. Suggested first implementation: a streaming sink that taps a vault's record stream, modeled as the mirror of the ingester registry. The on-demand query export (`| export-fluent host:…`) is a separate, secondary shape.
- **Cross-cluster forwarding falls out for free.** Cluster A → Cluster B over Fluent Forward is the same code path as Cluster A → Fluentd. The receiving cluster doesn't know or care that the sender is another GastroLog. This is *log shipping*, not *cluster replication* — chunk/vault identity is not preserved across the wire.
- **The sender must not know what's on the other end.** Sink config is just `addr`, `tag`, maybe `compress`, plus a record filter. No peer-identity branching.
- **EventID / NodeID / IngesterID don't cross the wire.** They're cluster-scoped identity by construction. The wire format carries `{tag, timestamp, record}`; that's the contract.
- **Two timestamps, not one.** `IngestTS` is local per cluster (paired with NodeID in EventID). The log line's own source time is data and travels in the record body unchanged. Multi-hop chains preserve source time naturally; each cluster's IngestTS stays local.
- **Loop prevention is explicitly out of scope.** Fluentd doesn't loop-protect either; operators learn not to point output at input. Symptoms are immediately visible (disk fills, record counts spike) and recoverable.

## Open questions to resolve before implementation

1. **Naming.** "Sink" mirrors "ingester" symmetrically and reads cleanly. "Exporter" collides with `ExportToVault`; "forwarder" collides with `cluster/forward.go`. Pick the canonical term and add it to `docs/ubiquitous_language.md` *before* any code is written.

2. **Placement.** Sinks vault-scoped (run where the vault leader lives, like ingesters), or node-scoped (each node runs its own sink, with upstream-side dedup)? Vault-scoped piggybacks on existing leadership/transfer logic; node-scoped requires a new placement model.

3. **Backpressure policy.** When a downstream Fluent Forward receiver is slow or unreachable: drop-oldest, drop-newest, spill-to-disk, block-the-vault? Memory-over-throughput rule says streaming + spill, never all-in-memory.

4. **Record selection.** Does a sink tap *every* record from a vault, or does it carry a query/filter (e.g. `level >= warn`) so operators can scope egress without piping everything?

5. **Provenance fields on egress.** Stamp opt-in record fields like `_glog_origin_cluster`, `_glog_seen_at` before forwarding? If yes, what's the namespace convention? If no, what's the debugging story for "where did this record originate" across multi-hop chains?

6. **Wire timestamp convention.** Forward-protocol timestamp = source time (if parsed) else IngestTS? Or always IngestTS? Receiving cluster behavior depends on this choice.

7. **Tag routing on the receive side.** When a receiving GastroLog cluster sees a tagged stream, does the existing `fluentfwd` ingester need a tag→vault routing capability? Today it ingests into a fixed vault per ingester config; cross-cluster forwarding will pressure this if a single ingester instance is meant to multiplex across vaults.

8. **Config storage / replication.** Sink configs live where? Same per-vault FSM as ingesters, replicated via Raft? Or separate cluster-wide registry?

9. **UI/CLI parity.** Per project rule, every sink config knob must exist in both UI and CLI. What does the surface look like — a "Sinks" tab next to "Ingesters" in the vault settings?

10. **Tests.** Multi-node coverage matrix: sink owner moves with leadership transfer; vault expands from 3 nodes to 5; downstream restarts; downstream slow; downstream returns invalid responses. `backend/internal/server/multinode_test.go` is the starting point.

11. **Sinks and vaults: shared abstraction, or distinct concepts?** Conceptually a vault and a sink are both "things that accept records." Unifying them into a single `Destination` abstraction (with queryability as a property, not the defining trait) is structurally what Fluent Bit's `OUTPUT` plugin model does. It would consolidate the orchestrator's dispatch path, the Raft FSM, the config tree, and the UI surface. But it has real costs: half the operations on a `Destination` (`Search`, `Explain`, `Histogram`, `GetFields`, `GetContext`) silently fail or return empty on a forward-typed instance — a leaky abstraction that lies about uniformity. Vault lifecycle (sealed chunks, indexes, retention, tier transitions, transferrers, leadership Raft groups) doesn't apply to forward sinks at all. And philosophically: the moment GastroLog's center of gravity becomes routing rather than storage + query, we're competing against Fluent Bit / Vector / Loki on their home turf — and we lose what makes the project distinctive. The likely middle ground: share an internal Go interface (`recordSink`-like: accept records, signal backpressure, report stats) so the dispatch path doesn't fork, but keep vaults and sinks as separate first-class concepts in config, UI, and `ubiquitous_language.md`. Internal symmetry, external distinction. This question deserves an explicit answer before any sink work begins, because it determines whether sinks live alongside vaults or under them — and that's the kind of architectural choice that's easy to drift away from one PR at a time without anyone realizing the identity of the project shifted.

title: vault-ctl Raft groups don't expand when cluster scales out
description:
When a new node joins the cluster (e.g. k8s StatefulSet scale-out from 3 to 5), the system-level Raft updates correctly (NodeConfig and NodeStorageConfig appear cluster-wide, the placement manager extends vault.placements to satisfy higher RF), but per-vault vault-ctl Raft groups stay frozen at their original membership.

## Symptom (reproduced live)

- Scale gastrolog StatefulSet 3 -> 5.
- Bump hot-vault RF from 3 to 4 via UI.
- vault.placements grows to [leader gastrolog-2, followers gastrolog-0/1/3] (correct).
- New chunks still show ReplicaCount=3 in the inspector; gastrolog-3 never receives chunks.
- gastrolog-3 is stuck '0/1 Running' (readyz returns 503).
- gastrolog-3 logs loop on: 'pre-vote campaign failed, waiting for election timeout … term=2 tally=2 refused=3 votesNeeded=3' for group 'vault/<vault-id>/ctl'.
- gastrolog-2 logs mirror it: 'rejecting pre-vote request since node is not in configuration … group=vault/<vault-id>/ctl from=<gastrolog-3 IP>'.
- Replication catchup on the leader only ever serves the two original follower GLIDs; gastrolog-3 never appears as a requester because its lifecycle reconciler can't run without quorum in its vault-ctl group.

## Root cause

vault-ctl Raft group desired membership is captured at the moment 'ensureVaultCtlMetadata' runs and is never refreshed on cluster growth.

- backend/internal/orchestrator/reconfig_vaults.go:1043-1054 — ensureVaultCtlMetadata captures clusterNodes (rt.Nodes) at call time and feeds them to vaultCtlLeaders.SetDesiredMembers.
- backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_ctl_leader_manager.go:161-200 — reconcile() converges actual Raft membership to the *desired* set via AddVoter/RemoveServer, but desired is never refreshed when the cluster grows.
- backend/internal/app/dispatch.go:106-107 — NotifyNodeConfigPut / NotifyNodeConfigDeleted is explicitly a no-op: 'No orchestrator side effects; configSignal fires below.' This is the missing hook.

This is the 'captured-at-start config' anti-pattern from the membership-aware-state feedback note.

## Fix

On NotifyNodeConfigPut (and likely NotifyNodeConfigDeleted), the dispatcher must:
1. Re-read the cluster node list (system.Config.Runtime.Nodes).
2. For every local vault instance with a vault-ctl group, recompute the desired Raft Server list (every cluster member is a voter — see dispatch.go:560 comment on gastrolog-292yi).
3. Call vaultCtlLeaders.SetDesiredMembers(vaultID, newDesired) so the leader manager picks up the new node on its next reconcile tick and issues AddVoter.

Removal handling on NotifyNodeConfigDeleted should be symmetric, with the safety the reconciler already provides.

## Acceptance criteria

- After scaling 3 -> 5 and bumping RF on an existing vault, gastrolog-3 / gastrolog-4 transition to 1/1 Ready within a small number of reconcile ticks (no manual pod restart).
- New chunks sealed after the RF bump report ReplicaCount equal to RF in the inspector.
- Existing sealed chunks get catchup-replicated to the new followers (via the standard follower-driven RequestReplicaCatchup path).
- No more 'rejecting pre-vote request since node is not in configuration' loops.

## Tests required (per CLAUDE.md Test Coverage section)

- Multi-node harness test: bootstrap 3-node cluster, create a file vault with RF=3, add 2 nodes via cluster.AddVoter + NodeConfig Put, bump RF to 5, verify the vault-ctl group membership grows to 5 voters and chunks reach 5 replicas.
- Failure-path test: new node fails to AddVoter (e.g. timeout) — reconciler retries on next tick without losing the desired set.
- Idempotency test: redundant NotifyNodeConfigPut for an already-joined node does not churn the vault-ctl group.
- Edge case: NotifyNodeConfigPut arrives before the local vault instance is built (cold-start ordering) — handler is a safe no-op for that vault and the eventual ensureVaultCtlMetadata picks up the latest node list.
closed_reason:
Fixes landed across cluster + dispatch + frontend:
- vault-ctl Raft groups now expand on cluster scale-out (RefreshVaultCtlMembers wired on NotifyNodeConfigPut/Deleted)
- VaultInstance leader pointer refreshes on every placement set, not only on role change
- vault-ctl reconciler rewrites stored addresses for known voters when the desired address differs (handles pod IP rotation)
- New --cluster-advertise flag + GASTROLOG_CLUSTER_ADVERTISE env so pods can advertise stable DNS names instead of pod IPs (k8s.yml updated)
- Headless service publishNotReadyAddresses=true so peer DNS resolves during bootstrap chicken-and-egg window
- cluster remove-node also deletes the system-FSM NodeConfig so scale-down doesn't leave stale entries
- Frontend useWatchChunks: replica tracking now derives from cache replica_node_ids, source nodeId merged on each event (grows naturally on catchup, no monotonic-grow accumulator)
- Local chunk events now stamp the local nodeId so the connected node is counted
- SEALED/UPLOADED events invalidate the sibling [indexes,vaultId,chunkId] React Query so detail panes expanded while active refetch indexes once they exist
- New just deploy kubernetes-redeploy recipe

Follow-up filed as an epic for the underlying React Query architectural gap (hand-wired cross-key invalidations vs tag-based system).

title: Frontend cache invalidation is hand-wired; adopt a tag/store architecture
description:
Owning the fuckup up front: I picked React Query and never set up a tag-based invalidation layer on top. Every cross-key relationship (chunks → indexes, vaults → chunks, config → chunks, etc.) is a hand-wired edge in some event handler, and any one I forget to draw becomes a silent UI staleness bug. We hit at least two of those during gastrolog-4zy8a:

- SEALED events refreshed the chunk meta but left the sibling ["indexes",vaultId,chunkId] query stale, so a detail pane expanded during the active→sealed transition showed all indexes "missing" forever.
- WatchSystem placement changes refreshed the system config but left the per-vault ["chunks",vaultId] cache stale, so RF decreases did not propagate until the user hard-reloaded.

The model/component split helps with derived state inside a single source. It does nothing for cross-source cache coherence, which is the actual failure mode here. Vue developers have had this solved for years with Vuex and Pinia (and React has comparable options: RTK Query with providesTags/invalidatesTags, Zustand/Jotai stores with entity selectors). We did not pick any of them and are paying for it with a steady drip of "X looks stale until I reload" bugs.

## Goal

End up in a state where: an event in stream A automatically refreshes every consumer of related state, without each consumer / event-handler pair having to be manually wired. Two viable directions; the epic scopes a decision plus a migration plan.

## Option A — Stay on React Query, add a tag layer

- Define entity tags per query: `chunk:<id>`, `vault:<id>`, `indexes:<chunkId>`, `config`, `node:<id>`, ...
- Replace the manual `qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [...] })` scatterings with `invalidateByTag(tag)`.
- Stream handlers (WatchChunks, WatchSystem, WatchSystemStatus) translate each event into a tag invalidation. A SEALED event invalidates `chunk:<id>` AND `indexes:<chunkId>` — wired ONCE at the tag-handler level instead of per-event-per-target.
- Reuse React Query underneath; smallest blast radius.

## Option B — Migrate to a real entity store (Zustand/Jotai/Pinia-equivalent)

- Define entity stores: Chunks, Vaults, Indexes, NodeConfigs, NodeStorageConfigs, Routes, Rotation/Retention policies, Ingesters.
- Selectors derive view state (e.g. inspector chunk row) from entities. Mutations are explicit and pure.
- Stream handlers apply normalized updates: SEALED event → patch the chunk entity + mark its indexes stale → derivations re-fire.
- Bigger lift but produces a real state model. The current `Vault` model class is one third of this picture.

## Acceptance criteria

- Stream-driven invalidation is declarative: each query declares what it depends on; each event declares what it invalidates. No more "X needs Y; remember to also invalidate Y in handler Z".
- A new cross-resource dependency can be added without grepping for invalidation edges.
- The two known staleness bugs (indexes-on-mid-transition; chunks-on-RF-change) are covered by acceptance tests that survive a refactor to either Option A or B.
- Docs in docs/ describing the chosen pattern and where to declare entity/tag membership for a new query.

## Child task suggestions

1. Decide between Option A and Option B (write a short ADR; capture trade-offs around bundle size, learning curve, test surface).
2. Audit existing `invalidateQueries` call sites; build a tag/entity table from them.
3. Land the tag/store skeleton without removing the current invalidations (parallel-write).
4. Migrate query-by-query, removing the old invalidations as each is covered.
5. Delete the old invalidation scatterings once nothing depends on them; the watch stream handlers become small.

## Background

Surfaced in gastrolog-4zy8a (closed) — a long debugging arc through cluster-side bugs that left several React-side issues exposed. The cluster-side fixes landed; the architectural gap is what this epic tracks.
closed_reason: All 9 child issues closed. Frontend cache invalidation migrated from React Query hand-wired invalidation to Zustand entity stores. title: slogCaptureCh fills + alerts when self ingester is disabled (producer-without-consumer)
description:
Observed: an operator running with the self ingester DISABLED sees a system alert fire after a while: `Channel "slogCaptureCh" at 90% capacity (3687/4096)`. Eventually drops start and the `self-ingester-drops` alert raises.

## Root cause

The `CaptureHandler` is wired into the slog chain unconditionally at process boot, before any config is loaded:

- `backend/cmd/gastrolog/main.go:62-63` creates `slogCaptureCh` (4096 buffer) and installs `CaptureHandler` as the top-level slog handler.
- `backend/internal/logging/capture.go:51` defaults the capture level to WARN, so every warning/error in the process tees to the channel.
- `backend/internal/logging/capture.go:78-103` (`Handle`) does a non-blocking send into the channel and increments `dropped` when full.

The channel has exactly one consumer: `backend/internal/ingester/self/ingester.go:80` (`Run`). That `Run` only fires when the orchestrator schedules the self ingester — which only happens when the self ingester is enabled in config.

With self disabled, nobody drains the channel. WARN+ records accumulate monotonically until the chanwatch threshold trips, then drops start and the drop monitor raises the alert.

The existing `SetMinCaptureLevel` knob in `capture.go:65` and the `SetPressureGate` adapter in `self/ingester.go:62` address the *overwhelmed-consumer* case. They do not help when there is no consumer at all.

## Reproduction

1. `just backend cluster-init` and `just backend cluster-run` without enabling the self ingester in config.
2. Generate any volume of WARN-level logs (any normal cluster activity produces some).
3. Watch the channel fill: `gastrolog --home backend/data/node1 inspect` (or the UI System Alerts panel).
4. Within a minute or so of warnings the buffer trips the 90% threshold; eventually drops begin.

## Fix sketch (preferred)

Add an `enabled atomic.Bool` to `CaptureHandler`. `Handle` gates the channel send on it:

```go
if !h.enabled.Load() {
    return h.inner.Handle(ctx, r)
}
```

The self ingester flips it on at the top of `Run` and off in the deferred teardown. Boot order stays the same; the slog chain installation in `main.go` is unchanged. Hot-reload-friendly: toggling the self ingester at runtime via config changes flips the gate without reinstalling handlers.

Alternative: gate the install of `CaptureHandler` itself on the self ingester being enabled. Cleaner end-state but requires loading config before slog setup, and breaks hot-reload when the operator enables self ingester at runtime — the handler would need to be re-installed in the chain.

## Acceptance

- With self ingester disabled, `slogCaptureCh` stays empty regardless of WARN+ traffic.
- With self ingester enabled, behavior is unchanged: records flow into the channel, the drop monitor still raises/clears.
- Toggling the self ingester via config flips the gate without restarting the process.
- Regression test: feed N records through `CaptureHandler.Handle` with the gate off, assert channel length stays 0; flip the gate on, assert records appear.

## Background

The capture path landed in gastrolog-5euo (self ingester). The drop-monitor alert is gastrolog-5d5a3. The pressure gate (SetPressureGate / SetMinCaptureLevel) is gastrolog-4fguu. None of those scenarios anticipated "self ingester disabled in steady state" — they all assume the consumer is running.

title: search returns ~10 records from the latest chunk only for last=5m queries
description:
Operator-visible symptom: a query like `last=5m reverse=true` against a vault with thousands of records in the window oscillates between showing a handful (3–10) and up to ~100 on every 5s polling refresh. The histogram correctly identifies thousands of records across the window but the result table is anemic.

## Wire evidence (from one search response)

- 10 records returned in 2ms.
- Every record carries the same `chunkId` (a single chunk) and the same `vaultId`.
- Record `ingestTs` spans only ~1.6 seconds (20:25:13.95 → 20:25:15.54) — the most recent slice of the active chunk.
- Histogram has 50 buckets covering the full 5m window (20:20:15 → 20:25:09). Only the latest bucket has `count: 11` with `groupCounts: {error:3, info:1, other:5, warn:2}`. Every other bucket has `timestampMs` only — no `count`, no `groupCounts`.
- Frontend sends only `{ expression: "last=5m reverse=true", limit: 100 }` plus `resumeToken` — no vault filter, no chunk hint, no node hint.

So the server is being asked for the full 5m window, knows about the time range (histogram buckets exist), but only reports records from the most recent ~1.6 seconds of a single chunk.

## Two leading hypotheses

1. **`reverse=true` parses as a filter expression, not a directive.** If the parser interprets it as the predicate `reverse == "true"`, the filter matches nothing, and some fallback path returns the latest few records from the active chunk + an empty histogram for the rest. Test by trying `last=5m` alone and comparing.
