- `kubectl scale --replicas=1` on a 10-pod RF=3 cluster: ends at 1 voter only if all 9 pods' demote-self refuses (per child B / C). At minimum, no chunks lost — every chunk had at least one surviving placement member at all times.
- 9 concurrent operator-driven `cluster remove-node` calls on a healthy 10-node cluster: same outcome — first few succeed, rest refused as placements shrink below RF.
- The reaper's batch-tick safety: each per-voter removal goes through the serializer, last few refused as cluster contracts.

## Out of scope

- The safety check itself (children B + C provide it).
- Pre-removal drain (child A): different mechanism — drain moves data; serializer just refuses.

## Related

- gastrolog-3xmtk (parent epic).
- gastrolog-2cb2r: joiner AddVoter race — same shape, opposite operation. Joiner-side handled by retry; remover-side handled by serialization.

title: cluster wait-catchup: synchronous primitive for placement-replica catch-up completion
description:
## Goal

Provide a synchronous "wait until this vault's surviving replicas have caught up to the leader's seal/index state" primitive. Used by child A (pre-removal drain) to know when it's safe to mark a node as drained, and useful operationally as `cluster wait-catchup <vault>` for any post-replication-change consistency check.

## Design

New cluster operation + RPC:

```
gastrolog cluster wait-catchup <vault-name> [--timeout 5m]
```

Per-vault primitive:

1. Query the vault-ctl FSM's manifest for the latest seal index + the placement membership.
2. For each placement member, query its `LastAppliedIndex` for this vault-ctl Raft group via raftadmin / a custom RPC.
3. A placement member is "caught up" when its `LastAppliedIndex >= leader.LastCommitted` AND its local chunk manager has all sealed chunks listed in the manifest.
4. Wait until either all placement members are caught up OR ctx deadline.

### Cross-process semantics

Catchup happens through two mechanisms:
- **Sealed chunk replication**: RequestReplicaCatchup (gastrolog-19241) pulls missing chunks to new placement members.
- **Active chunk records**: the real-time `AppendRecords` stream (gastrolog-617m6 step 1) keeps live record sequences in sync.

The wait check accounts for both: the vault-ctl FSM seal index covers the manifest state; the chunk-manager file presence check covers the disk state.

### Use sites

- **Child A (drain-node)**: blocks until drain target's vaults all show "surviving replicas caught up" before allowing the membership removal.
- **CI integration tests**: standardize on this primitive for assertions like "wait for the cluster to converge after a topology change."
- **Operator runbooks**: post-add-node workflow can `wait-catchup` before considering the cluster fully healthy at the new RF.

### Failure modes

- Timeout: returns `ErrCatchupTimeout` with per-replica progress in the error message.
- Replica unreachable: returns unreachable per-replica list; catchup stalled on this replica.
- Conservative: never returns "caught up" optimistically — only when both index AND chunk presence confirm.

## Acceptance

- `cluster wait-catchup hot-vault` returns nil once all current placement members have applied the latest seal index AND hold every sealed chunk in the manifest.
- `--watch` mode streams per-replica progress (similar to drain-node --watch).
- Timeout produces a clear per-replica error report.
- Used by child A's drain implementation.
- Multi-node + happy/unhappy/edge cases.

## Out of scope

- The drain operation itself (child A).
- New catchup transport mechanisms — this primitive only WAITS on existing mechanisms.

## Related

- gastrolog-3xmtk (parent epic).
- gastrolog-19241: RequestReplicaCatchup — this primitive is the operator-facing wait companion.
- gastrolog-617m6: reconcile-at-seal — once reconcile lands, "caught up" becomes a stronger signal (rolling hash convergence in addition to index/file checks).

title: cluster drain-node: proactively relocate replicas before allowing membership removal
description:
## Goal

Add a `cluster drain-node` operation that proactively copies replicas off the target node BEFORE allowing membership removal. Pairs with child E (catchup-completion wait) to provide the "right" graceful-removal semantic. Replaces the brittle "refuse if unsafe" gates (children B + C) with a proactive "make it safe, then remove" path for the common operator workflow.

## Design

New cluster operation:

```
gastrolog cluster drain-node <name> [--timeout 5m]
```

Workflow:

1. Operator runs `cluster drain-node g-2`.
2. Cluster marks g-2 as `draining=true` in NodeConfig (a new field). Placement manager treats draining nodes as alive-but-not-eligible-for-new-placements.
3. For each vault where g-2 is a placement member: placement manager re-elects to remove g-2, adding a new eligible node in its place. Catchup pulls missing chunks to the new placement member.
4. CLI polls until: no vault has g-2 as a placement member AND all newly-added placement members have caught up (via child E's wait semantic).
5. Once empty, CLI returns success. Operator now runs `cluster remove-node g-2` — which succeeds because the node is no longer a placement member of anything.

### Drain marker semantics

`draining=true` is a NodeConfig field. Persisted in system FSM. Survives leader changes. Cleared when the node is fully removed OR when operator runs `cluster undrain-node` (e.g. cancel mid-drain).

A draining node:
- Continues to serve queries from its local data (existing chunks).
- Does NOT accept new placements.
- Stays in Raft voter set (membership unchanged).
- Continues to be a healthy voter (no impact on quorum until child A's flow completes).

### Drain progress observability

`gastrolog cluster drain-node g-2 --watch` streams progress:

```
draining gastrolog-2:
  vault hot-vault: 3/5 chunks copied to gastrolog-7 (60%)
  vault warm-vault: 12/12 chunks present elsewhere (done)
  ...
  estimated completion: 2m17s
```

Or `gastrolog cluster status g-2` shows the drain state.

### Failure modes

- **Insufficient eligible storages**: drain refuses with "no eligible target storage class for vault X" — operator must add capacity first.
- **Catchup stalls**: drain stalls; alert fires. Operator can `--force` to remove regardless (data on the draining node's PVC remains; cluster forgets the chunks).
- **Operator cancels**: `cluster undrain-node g-2` clears the marker; placement manager re-includes g-2 as eligible.

### Relationship to preStop

K8s preStop `demote-self` is the unplanned / graceful-shutdown case. `drain-node` is the planned / operator-driven case. They have different urgency:

- `demote-self` (preStop, 30s grace period): refuses if unsafe (children B + C). No time to drain.
- `drain-node` (operator, minutes-to-hours): drains, waits for catchup, THEN removes.

Operator workflow for graceful scale-down:

```
gastrolog cluster drain-node gastrolog-9 --watch     # wait for drain
kubectl scale sts/gastrolog --replicas=9             # K8s removes the pod
```

## Acceptance

- `cluster drain-node g-N` waits for all replicas to be relocated; returns success only when g-N is no longer a placement member of any vault.
- Watched mode (`--watch`) streams per-vault progress.
- After drain succeeds, `cluster remove-node g-N` succeeds without any RF/last-replica gate firing (because the node holds no replicas).
- `cluster undrain-node g-N` reverses the drain marker.
- Failure modes are observable: alert fires on stall; operator can force-complete with data-loss acknowledged.

## Out of scope

- Last-replica gate (child C) and RF-preservation gate (child B): hard refusals, complement drain.
- Catchup-completion wait (child E): drain depends on E to know when catchup has finished.
- preStop semantics: drain is the planned-workflow companion to preStop's reactive refusal.

## Related

- gastrolog-3xmtk (parent epic).
- gastrolog-617m6: reconcile-at-seal — when reconcile lands (steps 4-5), drain's catchup-completion check becomes more robust.
- gastrolog-19241: RequestReplicaCatchup — drain depends on this to pull chunks to new placement members.

title: Orphaned-PVC chunks after node removal: detection, alert, and GC
description:
## Goal

After a node is removed from the cluster, the chunks on its local PVC are orphaned. The cluster forgets they existed. The K8s default `PersistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain` means the PVC and its data stick around until manual operator action. This is both a **disk-cost issue** (stale chunks accumulate, especially in test/dev clusters that cycle pods) and a **data-leak risk** (sensitive log data can be re-exposed if a stale PVC is later re-mounted to a fresh pod).

This issue covers the cluster-side accounting for orphaned data on removed-node PVCs: either automatic GC or, at minimum, a visible operator alert that survives until the orphaned data is acknowledged.

## Background

Today's removal flow (operator-driven, preStop-driven, or reaper-driven) updates:

- system Raft voter set
- system FSM NodeConfig
- vault placement
- vault-ctl Raft groups

It does NOT touch:

- Files in `/vaults/storage/disk-N/...` on the removed node's PVC.
- Chunk index files in the same location.
- Any cluster-side record that the removed node ever held those chunks.

If the K8s reclaim policy retains the PVC (the default), the data persists. If the pod is later recreated under the same StatefulSet name (`gastrolog-7` re-spawned), it re-mounts the old PVC and boots with the old data — BUT — its boot-time auto-rejoin (gastrolog-24iv4 Step C) detects "I'm not in the cluster" and wipes `/config/raft/*`. It does NOT touch `/vaults/`. So the chunks survive into the re-bootstrap, where they become *unowned* (not in the new cluster's placement either).

Net: stale chunks on disk, no cluster-side reference, no GC trigger.

## Proposed shape

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

### Option 1: Cluster-side GC sweep

A periodic sweep on each node walks `/vaults/storage/disk-N/...` and cross-checks each chunk against the vault-ctl FSM's placement+manifest:

- If the chunk is in this node's local vault placement AND in the FSM manifest → keep.
- If the chunk is not in this node's local placement (because the node was removed from the vault's placement) → GC.
- If the chunk is not in the FSM manifest at all (vault deleted) → GC.

GC = move to `/vaults/storage/disk-N/.orphans/<vault>/<chunk>/` for a configurable retention window (default 24h), then delete. The .orphans staging area gives operators a recovery window for misconfiguration mistakes.

Implementation: extends or replaces the existing `SweepLocalOrphans` in `vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go`. Today that sweep handles tombstoned-but-not-deleted chunks; this would extend it to chunks the cluster has *forgotten* about entirely.

### Option 2: Operator-visible alert

If full GC is too risky to automate, at minimum: on cluster startup, scan local storage, compare against FSM, and raise a persistent alert per orphan:

```
ALERT: 47 orphaned chunks on /vaults/storage/disk-1 (47.3 GB) — not referenced in any vault placement
  vault hot-vault: 23 orphans
  vault warm-vault: 24 orphans
  Run `gastrolog cluster gc-orphans --dry-run` to inspect, `--commit` to delete.
```

`gastrolog cluster gc-orphans` provides the CLI surface for review-and-delete.

### Recommended: option 2 first, option 1 later

Operators inspecting orphaned data once is much safer than automatic GC of data the cluster has decided to forget. Once option 2 has been running across enough deployments to be trusted, option 1 becomes the natural follow-up — alert plus automatic sweep with a long retention window.

## Acceptance

- Cluster startup scans local storage for chunks not referenced by any vault placement or FSM manifest entry.
- Orphan summary surfaced as an alert (count, total size, vault breakdown) until operator action.
- `gastrolog cluster gc-orphans --dry-run` lists orphan chunks per vault.
- `gastrolog cluster gc-orphans --commit` moves them to `.orphans` staging with a configurable retention.
- Audit-log records the GC operation: who, when, what.
- No false positives — chunks legitimately in this node's placement are never flagged.

## Out of scope

- The membership removal that creates the orphans (parent epic + children C/B/D/A/E).
- K8s PVC `reclaimPolicy` configuration (operator-territory; not gastrolog's to set).
- Cluster-wide chunk inventory beyond per-node scanning.

## Related

- gastrolog-3xmtk (parent epic).
- Existing `SweepLocalOrphans` handles a narrower case (tombstoned-but-not-deleted); this issue extends to the "removed from placement entirely" case.

title: ImportSealed packs entire chunk into one gRPC message; catchup wedged once chunks exceed 128 MiB
description:
## Problem

Replica catchup pushes a sealed chunk as ONE gRPC message: `ChunkReplicationImport { repeated ExportRecord records }` ([cluster.proto:244](backend/api/proto/gastrolog/v1/cluster.proto#L244)) sent via a single `SendMsg` call ([chunk_replicator.go:212](backend/internal/cluster/chunk_replicator.go#L212)). The cluster gRPC server caps receive size at 128 MiB ([cluster.go:45](backend/internal/cluster/cluster.go#L45) `maxChunkTransferBytes`). Once a chunk exceeds that cap, the server tears the stream down with `ResourceExhausted`, the client surfaces it as "recv ack: ... received message larger than max", and the catchup sweep retries forever without progress.

Observed in `gastrolog-1` pod log (2026-05-15):

```
recv ack: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc:
received message larger than max (135188568 vs. 134217728)
recv ack: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc:
received message larger than max (140642293 vs. 134217728)
recv ack: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc:
received message larger than max (155128278 vs. 134217728)
```

Same three chunk IDs (`06f2ijusodrmd…`, `06f2ikapepuu…`, `06f2iki45ttu…`) bounce every ~20 s against both peers. Followers stay permanently behind on these vaults.

## Why it matters

- Cluster-wide correctness regression: followers cannot catch up when chunks exceed the ceiling, so replication stays lossy and the system can't self-heal.
- Silent in normal load (small chunks); kicks in exactly when chunks grow large — i.e. during traffic spikes or busy ingesters — the moment recovery matters most.
- Raising `maxChunkTransferBytes` is a bandaid: the next chunk hits the next ceiling, and gRPC has a hard 2 GiB framing limit regardless. The protocol layout, not the cap, is the bug.

## Proposed fix

Make `ImportSealed` streaming over the existing bidi stream:

1. Replace the single `ChunkReplicationImport` message with a sequence: `ImportSealedBegin { chunk_id, total_records }` → N × `ImportSealedRecords { records[] }` → `ImportSealedCommit {}`.
2. Each `ImportSealedRecords` frame is bounded (e.g. ~4 MiB or 1k records) so individual messages stay well under any practical receive cap.
3. Follower accumulates records, materializes the chunk on commit, fails atomically if it sees a duplicate Begin or a Commit without a matching Begin.
4. Acks land on Begin (slot reservation) and Commit (success/failure). No per-record ack — the stream guarantees ordering.

Same pattern as how the active-chunk Append path already works at record granularity — just applied to sealed-chunk shipment.

## Acceptance

- New `ImportSealed*` frames added to `ChunkReplicationCommand` oneof; old `ImportSealed` variant removed (no compat shim — single-coordinated change per CLAUDE.md proto-cleanup rule).
- `ChunkReplicator.ImportSealedChunk` chunked into Begin/Records/Commit sends.
- Follower handler in [chunk_replication_handler.go](backend/internal/cluster/chunk_replication_handler.go) reassembles streaming import.
- New test in `chunk_replication_handler_test.go`: ship a chunk with >128 MiB of records, assert successful catchup, replica appears on follower.
- Multinode test: rotate at 200 MiB, pause a follower long enough to fall behind, resume, assert catchup succeeds.
- `maxChunkTransferBytes` can stay at 128 MiB after fix (or drop closer to a normal 16-64 MiB now that no path needs >cap messages).

## Notes

- Same shape exists for any other replication command that carries a `repeated` payload bounded only by chunk size. Audit oneof cases in [chunk_replicator.go](backend/internal/cluster/chunk_replicator.go) for siblings before closing.
- Discovered while inspecting `gastrolog-1` after gastrolog-3gewc work.
closed_reason: Fixed: streaming ImportSealed + ImportBegin preempt + eviction-shutdown gate; verified end-to-end on k8s cluster

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
## Heap blowup, same root cause

The single-frame issue is half the story. The same code path also materializes the entire chunk on the heap THREE times before a byte hits the wire:

1. `replication.go:278-288` — `var records []chunk.Record` is grown one append at a time by walking `cursor.Next()` to exhaustion. The cursor already streams; we then defeat the streaming by stuffing every record into a slice.

2. `chunk_replicator.go:208-211` — `exports := make([]*gastrologv1.ExportRecord, len(records))` allocates a parallel proto wrapper for every record. Strings/byte slices inside ExportRecord either share or copy from `Record`; either way the proto graph adds another full pass of allocations and live-set.

3. Proto marshal — when `SendMsg(cmd)` runs, the `ChunkReplicationImport` containing `Records: exports` is serialized to one contiguous bytes buffer. That's a third full copy of the chunk in heap, transiently, every time we push.

For a 155 MB chunk that's ~500 MB peak RSS PER push. Multiply by RF: leader does this per follower in series (or parallel — worse). With two followers and two chunks in flight, ~1 GiB of heap before GC can react. And the catchup sweep retries every 20s on failure, so the churn never settles.

This violates the "memory over throughput; never slurp full files into heap" rule that's been hit before (compressFile, gastrolog-pkfo, etc.).

## Fix folds into the streaming change

The Begin/Records/Commit redesign already proposed here deletes copies (1) and (2) entirely:

- `replication.go` calls the replicator with the cursor itself, not a materialized slice.
- `chunk_replicator.go` opens the stream, loops `cursor.Next()`, packs each batch of N records (e.g. 1000 or 4 MiB) into an `ImportSealedRecords` frame, sends, repeats. Per-batch heap usage is bounded by the batch size, not the chunk size.
- Marshal cost shrinks to one batch frame at a time.

So the acceptance criteria should also assert:

- No `[]chunk.Record` materialization on the leader side. Replication pushes consume the cursor directly.
- Memory test: catchup a 200 MiB chunk; assert leader RSS delta stays under a tight bound (e.g. ~10 MiB on top of baseline) for the duration of the push. The current shape would peak near 500 MiB.

Audit the same pattern for sibling commands while in there — anywhere we call `make([]*ExportRecord, N)` for N proportional to chunk size is the same bug.

title: Cloud upload fails with 'unseekable stream' checksum error over plain HTTP
description:
## Problem

Cloud uploads to S3-compatible mocks over plain HTTP fail with:

```
upload GLCB: operation error S3: PutObject, compute input header
checksum failed, unseekable stream is not supported without TLS
and trailing checksum
```

Observed in `gastrolog-1` pod log (2026-05-15). Every post-seal upload attempt against the in-cluster mock falls through to "cloud upload failed, keeping local". The chunk is preserved locally (degraded condition, no data loss) but the cloud tier never receives it, so retention sweeps that expect data to migrate stay stuck on the local side and disk pressure grows.

## Root cause

AWS SDK Go v2's S3 client wants to compute a trailing checksum on the request body. Trailing checksums require either (a) TLS, or (b) a seekable body that can be read twice (once for the header, once on the wire). Our upload path streams from an unseekable source, and the test/dev environment talks plain HTTP to whatever S3-compatible mock the k8s manifest spins up (azurite + fake-gcs visible in the pod list; whichever one accepts S3 PutObject is in this path).

Two AWS SDK behaviors interact here:

- `DisableInputOutputChecksum` / `RequestChecksumCalculation` defaults to "when supported" in newer SDK versions.
- The SDK refuses to fall back to a payload-signed body over plain HTTP, so it fails fast.

## Why it matters

- Cloud-backed vaults degrade silently — uploads warn-and-skip, no operator-facing alert.
- The local copy keeps growing until disk fills, even though the operator believes data is migrating.
- We already have an alert primitive ([CLAUDE.md memory: use alerts for degraded conditions]); this should be wired.

## Options

1. **Opt the upload path out of trailing checksums** when the cloud endpoint is plain HTTP. Concretely, set `request.Checksum: aws.RequestChecksumCalculationWhenRequired` (or a custom middleware that strips the trailing-checksum header) for the upload PutObject call. Minimal change; matches what the mocks support.
2. **Use HTTPS in the k8s mock setup** — workaround at the infra layer, not a code fix. Doesn't help operators who run their own non-TLS S3 mocks.
3. **Send seekable bodies** — would require buffering the GLCB in memory or to a temp file before upload, defeating the streaming-upload memory discipline ([CLAUDE.md memory: mmap/streaming over heap-buffering]).

Recommend option 1: keep streaming, just turn off the checksum middleware that requires seekability. AWS s3-compatible servers we target (MinIO, Azurite, fake-gcs's S3 mode) don't require trailing checksums.

## Acceptance

- Cloud upload PutObject call configured so that the trailing-checksum middleware does not fail when the endpoint is plain HTTP with an unseekable body.
- Alert raised when a cloud upload fails and falls back to local (set on failure, cleared on next successful upload of the same vault) — operators should not have to grep logs to notice.
- Test: upload against a non-TLS S3 mock returns success; chunk transitions to cloud-backed without "keeping local" warning.
- Multinode test: rotate a chunk on a cloud-backed vault, assert it becomes CloudBacked and DiskBytes reflects the blob size after upload.

## Notes

- Look at sibling upload paths for the same issue: archival to Glacier/Archive class likely uses the same `PutObject` shape.
- This is also why retention sweeps "stuck" investigations may turn up nothing in retention itself — the upload tier is the actual blocker.

## Discovered via

Reading `gastrolog-1` pod log while diagnosing replica-catchup wedges (gastrolog-4yvhh).

title: Active-chunk replication not reaching followers (only sealed chunks replicate)
description:
## Symptom

Inspector view: active chunk shows `replica_count = 1` (only the vault leader) on a vault with RF=3. Sealed chunks on the same vault correctly show 3 replicas after gastrolog-4yvhh's streaming-import fix landed. The CLI `gastrolog inspect vault hot-vault` confirms: active chunk's `replica_node_ids` lists only the leader; followers don't have it locally.

This is **not** a regression from gastrolog-4yvhh — the streaming-import work only touched sealed-chunk import; AppendRecords (the active-chunk replication RPC) was untouched. Sealed-chunk replication now works on chunks well beyond 128 MiB.

## What is supposed to happen

Per [vault_ops.go:909](backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_ops.go#L909), the leader's `appendRecord` path collects `remotes` via `forwardToFollowers` and fires them via `fireAndForgetRemote` outside the orchestrator lock. Each remote becomes a `ChunkReplicator.AppendRecords` RPC to the follower, which on the follower side hits `AppendToVault` → `cm.Append(rec)`, materializing the chunk locally with the leader's chunk ID.

Both the sealed-chunk replication path and the active-chunk path use the same `vaultInst.FollowerTargets` source and the same `chunkReplicator` instance, so the wiring is in place for one but apparently not the other.

## What is happening

Active records are written to the leader's chunk but never reach followers. No `replication: follower unreachable` warnings in the leader pod log, no `append failed` errors anywhere. The leader appears to not even be attempting the AppendRecords RPC, or the RPC succeeds on the wire but the follower drops the record before it lands on disk. Statically inspecting both paths, I cannot tell which.

## Diagnostic candidates

1. `appendRecord` is reached but `activeInst.ShouldForwardToFollowers()` returns false — `IsLeader() && len(FollowerTargets) > 0`. Sealed replication uses `followerReplicationTargets()` which also gates on `ShouldForwardToFollowers`, and it works. So FollowerTargets is populated and IsLeader is true. This path should fire.
2. `rec.WaitForReplica` is set on every record, routing through `ackAfterReplication` instead of fire-and-forget. That path *also* calls `AppendRecords` — it should still reach followers, just via the sync errgroup. Confirm whether the ingester (fluent-bit upstream) is in ack-gated mode.
3. The follower receives AppendRecords, then `AppendToVault` returns an error that the handler maps to a non-OK ack, but the leader's circuit-breaker `bumpReplicaBackoff` log only logs on the FIRST failure and powers of 2. If failures are constant, we'd still see one log line at startup — and we don't. So either the leader isn't getting back an error or it isn't sending the RPC.
4. The leader is sending AppendRecords successfully and the follower IS appending, but ListChunks on the follower doesn't include active chunks — so the inspector's per-chunk `replica_count` doesn't see them. Worth checking [vault_chunks.go](backend/internal/server/vault_chunks.go) for an active-vs-sealed gate on the per-node ListChunks executor.

## Reproduction

The user's k8s cluster (gastrolog-0..N) with RF=3 hot-vault on gastrolog-1. Inspector tab on any node shows the active chunk with the "1" replica badge; CLI `gastrolog --addr unix:///config/gastrolog.sock inspect vault hot-vault` confirms `replica_node_ids` has only the leader for the active chunk while sealed chunks list all three.

## Acceptance

- Active-chunk records reach followers as they're appended on the leader (RF=3 cluster: follower nodes show the chunk in their local ListChunks output with non-zero record count).
- New multinode test: leader appends N records to a vault with RF=2 followers, then assert each follower has the active chunk locally with the same records before any seal fires.
- Inspector `replica_count` for active chunks matches the configured RF when the cluster is healthy.
- Cause documented in commit / issue notes so we know what was actually wrong (not just "now it works").

## Notes

- Audit suggestion 4 (ListChunks gating active chunks) is the cheapest to confirm first — single grep. If active chunks DO get appended on followers but ListChunks hides them, the symptom is identical to the leader not sending, and that's a simpler bug than a hot-path replication failure.
- Audit suggestion 1's debug should be a single log line at the top of `fireAndForgetRemote` reporting `len(targets)` and target node IDs per record. One redeploy will tell us whether the call is happening.
closed_reason: Resolved by gastrolog-4yvhh's ImportBegin preempt fix combined with gastrolog-2yeie's placement work

title: preStop demote-self destroys cluster membership on every pod restart
description:
## Problem

Rolling restarts of k8s pods (or any pod cycle that hits a non-bootstrap node) unregister the node from cluster membership, which forces every restart to look like a brand-new node joining the cluster. Identity, storage IDs, and placement integrity all churn even though the PVC data is intact and the pod is back in seconds.

Observed during gastrolog-5z7l8 debugging. Each non-bootstrap pod runs preStop `demote-self` (added by [gastrolog-24iv4](backend/internal/lifecycle)). That removes it from cluster membership before SIGTERM. On restart, the cluster has no entry for the node, so the binary's auto-rejoin path fires:

```
auto-rejoin: cluster considers this node not a member; backing up stale raft state for fresh rejoin
node_id=06f2jnf939ru1brktg4acs8a8c   # brand-new node ID
```

Downstream consequences:

1. **Node ID changes** — old `06f2jilltduof37nqj7o8ljpu4` → new `06f2jnf939ru1brktg4acs8a8c`.
2. **Storage ID changes** — the deploy autowire (or first-start path) hits `config node add-storage` which always allocates a fresh `glid.New()` ([cli/node.go:164](backend/cmd/gastrolog/cli/node.go#L164)).
3. **Vault placements go stale** — placements referenced the old storage ID, which no longer exists. The placement manager treats the new storage as empty and re-balances followers on the fresh IDs.
4. **Chunks orphan in place** — `/vaults/storage/disk-1/<oldStorageID>/...` still has the data, but no current placement references it. Old chunks are dead weight; new chunks land under the new storage ID.
5. **Replication windows open up** — for several minutes after restart, FollowerTargets is empty (because NSCs haven't propagated for the new IDs yet), so active-chunk fire-and-forget is gated off. New sealed chunks reach only the leader.

## Root cause

`demote-self` was the right tool for **intentional scale-down**, but k8s preStop fires for any pod termination — including rolling restarts where the pod will come back in seconds. Treating restart and scale-down identically is what makes restart destructive.

k8s doesn't expose a clean "this is the last time you'll see me" signal at preStop, so we can't decide which case applies from inside the pod. The fix has to come from the design, not the hook.

## Proposed direction

Stop conflating restart and removal. preStop becomes light, membership-preserving:

1. **preStop: transfer raft leadership if leader, else no-op.** Cluster sees a brief disappearance via heartbeat timeout — which it already handles for crashes. Node ID and storage IDs stay intact. When the pod returns, it rejoins raft as a known follower, catches up from logs, ingest resumes.

2. **Permanent removal becomes an explicit operator action.** `gastrolog cluster remove-node <id>` (or equivalent) for true scale-down. K8s-side operator/script triggers it after a confirmed permanent removal, not from the pod itself.

3. **Stale-voter detection comes back, this time safely.** gastrolog-24iv4 deleted the stale-voter-reaper because it had real quorum-safety bugs (visible in the same epic's commit log). But the underlying need — detect voters who never came back and remove them — is real. Rebuild it as a quorum-gated sweep on a slow tick (e.g. evict only voters absent > 1 hour, only when the cluster has quorum without them). The fast removal path (preStop) is what was wrong; a slow background sweep with safety gates is fine.

## Acceptance

- Rolling restart preserves identity end-to-end: node ID, storage IDs, and vault placements unchanged across `kubernetes-redeploy`.
- Chunk replica counts hold steady at RF across the restart — no transient drops, no orphaned `<storageID>/` directories accumulating on the PVC.
- preStop hook: transfers leadership only when the terminating pod holds it; no membership-write side effects.
- Explicit `cluster remove-node` CLI / RPC for permanent removal, with operator-friendly UX (refuses without `--confirm`, refuses if would break quorum, etc.).
- Quorum-gated stale-voter sweep: removes voters absent > configurable threshold (default ~1h), only when the remaining cluster has quorum without them, never inside the absence window.
- New e2e test: `kubernetes-redeploy` while records are flowing, then assert no chunk reports `replica_count < RF` 30s after rollout completes (regression gate for the symptom that drove this issue).
- Multinode test: kill a node, restart, assert node ID + storage IDs are unchanged and placements remain pointing at the same IDs.

## Notes

- This is the right framing of the placement-convergence-delay symptom too: the leader's FollowerTargets is empty after a rolling restart because rejoined nodes show up with fresh storage IDs that haven't propagated. Fix preStop and the convergence delay vanishes — placements never went stale in the first place.
- See [feedback_membership_aware_state.md](memory) — every cluster-touching code path should ask "does this work after `kubernetes-redeploy`?". preStop demote-self failed that test.
- gastrolog-24iv4's commit log shows several real bugs in the old stale-voter-reaper (quorum-gate, boot-time auto-rejoin). Those fixes should inform the safer version; don't restore the old code blindly.

## Discovered via

User noticed during gastrolog-5z7l8 (active-chunk replication) debugging that storage IDs changed across redeploys. Traced through auto-rejoin → fresh node ID → fresh storage allocation → orphaned chunk data. Initial framing of this issue was "persist IDs on disk so rejoin restores them"; rewritten when the user pointed out that the persistent-IDs idea is downstream of a deeper wrong: pods shouldn't be unregistering on every restart in the first place.
closed_reason: Fixed: yield-leadership preStop + handleUnplaceable retain + delete autoRejoinIfEvicted; verified IDs preserved across kubernetes-redeploy

title: FSM-authority migration: lifecycle, learners, audit cleanup
description:
Close the multi-year migration of cluster-coordinated state from
"chunks-on-disk is the truth" toward "vault-ctl FSM is the truth"
at the **control-plane** layer: node lifecycle, learner-based Raft
membership, the disk-vs-FSM authority cleanup, and operational
features (orphan repatriation, naming consistency) that depend on
FSM authority being well-defined.

The data-plane redesign (fan-out writes, set-diff reconcile,
receiving/holding placement) is the companion epic
gastrolog-2ujjh. This epic ships first and provides the substrate.

## Motivation

The vault-ctl FSM already owns chunk existence, pending-delete state,
and tombstones. Several adjacent concerns remain inconsistent or
disk-derived:

- Node liveness is binary (in LivePeers or not). Transient absence
  during k8s rolling restarts is misclassified as permanent
  removal, triggering placement rotation that orphans chunks.
- New nodes join Raft groups directly as voters, briefly affecting
  quorum until they catch up.
- Multiple subsystems still treat local disk as the authority for
  "what chunks does this node have" — that view diverges from the
  FSM under restart, snapshot replay, and other transitions.
- Permanently-deleted vault entries (via FSM bugs, restore-from-
  backup, etc.) have no recovery path because chunks on disk that
  the FSM doesn't recognize are silently invisible.

## Scope

Six explicit states for node lifecycle (Live / Unreachable /
Maintenance / Draining / Decommissioning / Removed). Learner-based
join with per-group apply-index promotion. Audit and cleanup of
the disk-as-authority code paths. Orphan repatriation as
FSM-glitch insurance. The cluster-ctl rename for naming consistency.

What this epic does NOT include (moved to gastrolog-2ujjh):

- Residency tracking mechanism (Holding set lives in the data-plane
  redesign)
- Placement-rotation gate on soft-offline (subsumed by Holding set)
- Drain orchestration as a Draining-state machine (becomes a
  placement edit + reconcile under the new architecture)
- Active-chunk seal on preStop (no leader-only unsealed state
  under fan-out)
- Fan-out replication, set-diff reconcile, W-of-N ack policy

## Children

- gastrolog-gr6wy (in_review): Design — node lifecycle states + learner promotion
- gastrolog-5dfv7 (in_review): Audit — subsystems treating disk as authority
- gastrolog-5eu6v (open, P3): Refactor — cluster-ctl rename
- gastrolog-32bf2 (open, P3): Feature — orphan chunk repatriation

(gastrolog-5rh68 closed and superseded by gastrolog-2ujjh — residency
tracking moved out of this epic into the data-plane redesign.)

Implementation issues against the design + audit will be drafted
once the design issues close.

## Invariant

The cluster has explicit, well-defined node states with consistent
semantics across the placement, replication, and operator surfaces.
Local disk state is evidence to reconcile against the FSM, never
authority for cluster-coordinated decisions. Unknown orphans
(chunks on disk that the FSM doesn't recognize) are preserved, not
auto-deleted.

title: Design: node lifecycle states — soft-offline and learner promotion
description:
Design two related state-machine decisions that gate the
implementation issues for soft-offline and learner-based joins.
Combined into one design issue because they interact: soft-offline
triggers may inform learner promotion criteria, and both feed the
soft-offline behavior implementation.

## 1. Soft-offline state for cluster nodes

Introduce a third node liveness state between "live" and
"decommissioned":

- **Live**: heartbeats current; participates fully
- **Soft-offline**: heartbeats stale OR operator-marked; placement
  does NOT rotate off; reads to this node fail fast; new placements
  avoid it; cluster can opt in to preemptive replication off it
- **Decommissioned**: explicitly removed by operator; chunks
  transferred away first (orphan-refusal); voter set removed from
  all vault-ctl groups

Decisions to make:

- What triggers entry into soft-offline (reaper threshold? operator
  command? both?)
- What clears it (heartbeat resumes? operator confirms? both?)
- Threshold tuning: reaper interval, soft-offline window, defaults
- Can soft-offline stack with "draining" for operator-initiated
  preemptive rebalance, or is that a fourth state?
- UI/CLI surface: how the state is shown to operators

## 2. Learner promotion criteria

New nodes join as learners (non-voting) in both system Raft and
per-vault-ctl Raft groups. Decisions to make:

- Per-group promotion (each group promotes independently as it
  catches up) vs cluster-wide (all groups caught up before any
  voter promotion). Per-group is more incremental but more state
  to track; cluster-wide is simpler but slower convergence.
- Promotion criterion: log-index threshold vs FSM apply-index match
  vs stability window. Each picks a different tradeoff between
  "promote as soon as safe" and "promote only when caught up."
- Failure mode: what happens if a learner falls behind faster than
  it catches up? Revert to learner? Block? Operator alert?

## Acceptance

A design document or comment-on-issue that names the choices and
their tradeoffs, sufficient to open implementation issues for both
soft-offline behavior and learner-based joins. No code in this
issue.
closed_reason: Design accepted; node-lifecycle states + learner promotion design landed in docs/node-lifecycle-design.md. Three transitional pieces (placement guard, Draining orchestrator, active-chunk seal) noted in the doc as superseded when the data-plane epic gastrolog-2ujjh lands.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Design refinement landed: split SoftOffline into two states. Unreachable (cluster-detected, auto-set/auto-clear, warning-tone) and Maintenance (operator-declared, sticky, informational-tone). Both share the soft-offline placement-rotation gate; the difference is in entry/exit semantics and operator UX. The StateSource field is removed — state name encodes the source. CLI verb cluster soft-offline removed; cluster maintenance + cluster online are the operator verbs. See docs/node-lifecycle-design.md on the gastrolog-gr6wy branch (commit 5b097971).

title: Design: residency tracking mechanism — constrained placement vs pendingCatchups
description:
Design two alternative directions for residency tracking, then pick
the winner once the soft-offline state machine design
(gastrolog-gr6wy) converges. Replaces the original Holders-backfill
scoping — that direction conflicts with gastrolog-3qr8z principle
#4 ("reuse existing primitives") and is held in reserve as Option C
only if both A and B prove insufficient.

## Option A — Constrained placement, no new residency state

Residency continues to derive from placement
(placement_set - pendingDeletes.ExpectedFrom). Placement only
rotates leader storage on hard-decommission, not on transient
absence. Catchup windows handled by existing missing-replica sweep
with retries.

Requires:
- Reliable soft-offline gating (gastrolog-gr6wy must converge first)
- Placement guard in placement.go that distinguishes soft-offline
  from decommissioned
- Decommission refusal when destination wouldn't be a known holder

Zero new FSM state. Backfill is a non-question.

Failure mode: if soft-offline gating is wrong (e.g., a real
decommission misclassified as soft-offline, or a true permanent
failure misclassified as soft-offline), placement could get stuck
pointing at a permanently dead node. Tight coupling to gr6wy's
design correctness.

## Option B — pendingCatchups as the symmetric twin of pendingDeletes

Add explicit per-chunk per-node tracking of catchup obligations,
modeled on existing pendingDeletes shape:

    pendingDeletes[chunkID].ExpectedFrom = nodes still owing delete-ack
    pendingCatchups[chunkID].ExpectedTo  = nodes owing receipt-from-source

Residency:

    ChunkResidency = placement_set
                       - pendingDeletes.ExpectedFrom
                       - pendingCatchups.ExpectedTo

New FSM commands: CmdBeginCatchup, CmdAckCatchup. Lock discipline,
snapshot/restore, prune-on-node-removal all follow the
pendingDeletes pattern.

Failure mode: pendingCatchups must be reliably maintained — if
CmdBeginCatchup commits but CmdAckCatchup is never proposed (lost
under leader transfer, etc.), the new node stays excluded from
residency forever; need a recovery mechanism (similar to the
existing pendingDeletes self-heal in gastrolog-2eclw-unstick).

## Held in reserve: Option C — explicit Holders field

Per-chunk Holders []string field, mutated via CmdAddHolder /
CmdRemoveHolder. Conflicts with 3qr8z principle #4. Reach for only
if A and B prove insufficient during design.

## Pick criterion

Decide between A and B after gastrolog-gr6wy converges. The
deciding question is: "is the soft-offline gate alone reliable
enough to prevent placement from ever pointing at a
non-data-holding node?"

- If yes → Option A (cleanest, no new state).
- If no → Option B (explicit tracking, robust to soft-offline gate
  edge cases).

## Acceptance

A design document or comment naming the chosen approach and its
rationale, sufficient to open the implementation issue(s) for
placement-guard (Option A) or pendingCatchups (Option B). The
decision rationale should explicitly address why the chosen option
satisfies 3qr8z principle #4 and how it handles the catchup-window
correctness question.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Scope shifted from 'Holders backfill design' to 'mechanism choice between constrained placement (Option A) vs pendingCatchups twin (Option B), Holders held in reserve as Option C'. Reason: the original framing presupposed Option C, which conflicts with the existing gastrolog-3qr8z principle #4 ('reuse existing primitives'). The design conversation now develops A and B in parallel; pick happens after gastrolog-gr6wy converges on the soft-offline state machine, since A's correctness depends tightly on soft-offline gating reliability while B's does not. Backfill becomes a non-question for both A (no new state) and B (empty pendingCatchups starting state is correct).

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Resolved to Option A (constrained placement, no new FSM state) via the design document committed on the gastrolog-gr6wy branch: docs/node-lifecycle-design.md. Empirical finding from query_remote.go: read routing today consults only the placement leader (no LivePeers, no follower fallback, no ChunkResidency check). Since reads do not consult residency, Option B's pendingCatchups buys nothing for current read correctness. Option B and Option C remain available as escalation paths if future work adds residency-aware read routing (e.g., follower-based read fallback). Implementation surface for this issue is now the placement.go state-driven guard described in the design doc; no separate backfill design needed.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Closed as superseded by gastrolog-2ujjh (Fan-out data-plane architecture). The residency-tracking design conversation resolved here (Option A: constrained placement, no new FSM state) is replaced by the Receiving/Holding split that the data-plane redesign introduces. Under fan-out, ChunkResidency reads the Holding set directly rather than deriving from placement; the design tension this issue was framed around dissolves with the new architecture. The Option B (pendingCatchups twin) approach this issue analyzed is essentially what Holding⊃Receiving expresses, generalized. No code or design artifact from this issue is lost — the architectural direction here informed the new epic's design.

title: Audit: subsystems treating disk as authority
description:
As part of the FSM-authority migration, identify every code path
that treats local disk state as authoritative for information
that has migrated (or is migrating) to the vault-ctl FSM. These
are the cleanup targets: each needs to flip from "trust the disk"
to "trust the FSM; verify against the disk."

## Known example

Chunk-manager startup scan populates an in-memory map from local
files. Under FSM authority this should be reconciliation (compare
local files against FSM Holders for self) rather than the source
of truth.

## What to look for

For each subsystem, ask:

- Does it consult os.ReadDir / local file metadata for "what
  chunks does this node hold" or similar membership questions?
- Does it make cluster-coordinated decisions (replication targets,
  retention, search routing) based on the answer?
- If yes → flip to FSM consultation; the disk read becomes
  evidence to reconcile against, not authority.

## Likely areas to audit

- backend/internal/chunk/ — chunk manager startup, ListChunks
- backend/internal/orchestrator/ — retention, replication,
  missing-replica sweep
- backend/internal/server/ — search-engine chunk discovery
- backend/internal/vaultraft/ — FSM restore path

## Acceptance

A list of code locations + a one-line description of how each
should be reframed. This list itself becomes the set of cleanup
issues opened as children of the migration epic. No code changes
in this issue — just the inventory.
closed_reason: Audit deliverable at docs/disk-authority-audit.md is complete. Four cleanup targets identified plus the no-auto-delete-of-unknown-orphans invariant established as governing principle. Cleanup implementation issues will be drafted under gastrolog-2i1g9.

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Audit complete. Deliverable at docs/disk-authority-audit.md on the gastrolog-5dfv7 branch. Four concrete cleanup targets identified (loadExisting, RemoveVault, archivalSweepVault, ListChunkMetas split), with five sites verified as correctly per-node local (index rebuild, cloud health, FSM Restore, temp-file cleanup, managed-files). The orchestrator's existing SweepMissingReplicas + SweepLocalOrphans + projectAllSealedFromFSM are the prior art the cleanup work extends to the remaining consumers.

title: Refactor: rename system Raft group to cluster-ctl
description:
Rename the cluster-wide system Raft group from `system` to
`cluster-ctl` so it parallels `vault-ctl` for per-vault Raft
groups. Both then follow the `{scope}-ctl` convention:
`cluster-ctl` (one group, cluster-wide) and `vault-ctl` (N groups,
per-vault), each reading as "the control-plane Raft group for
that scope."

## Scope

Replace the `system` identifier across the backend wherever it
refers to the system Raft group, the system FSM, or the system
store:

- ~142 Go occurrences across the backend
- Three literal-string Raft group ID sites:
  - `backend/internal/app/node_id.go:39` (`wal.GroupStore("system")`)
  - `backend/internal/app/raft.go:203` (`wal.GroupStore("system")`)
  - `backend/internal/app/raft.go:205` (`opts.Home.RaftGroupDir("system")`)
- Type names where the `system` prefix is semantic (e.g.
  `raftSystemStore`)
- Comments and doc references

## Out of scope

- The `system` package directory (`backend/internal/system/`) and
  its types (`NodeConfig`, `VaultConfig`, etc.). These are domain
  data types, not Raft-specific, and the `system` package name is
  appropriate for "cluster-wide configuration types."
- The system FSM's *functionality* — only its Raft-group naming
  changes.

## Migration

Per the project's zero-production-deployments stance, the on-disk
Raft group ID can change atomically without a migration path:
existing local dev clusters wipe their `raft/` directories.

## Vocabulary doc update

Add `cluster-ctl Raft` as a canonical term to
`docs/ubiquitous_language.md` parallel to the existing `vault-ctl
Raft` entry. Phase out the `system Raft` term via the
consistency-rules table.

## Acceptance

- All references updated: type names, comments, string literals,
  test code
- Sweep beyond `src/` and `docs/` per
  [[feedback_rename_sweep_grep_scope]] — `scripts/`, justfile
  recipes, e2e fixtures
- Tests pass; local cluster bootstraps with the new naming
- Ubiquitous language doc updated
- Single atomic commit (or coherent stack) on the branch

## Why low priority

Pure naming cleanup; no functional bug. Defer until the epic's
core implementation issues land — those will produce more code
using these identifiers, and a rename done after they land sweeps
more in one pass than two separate sweeps.

title: Feature: orphan chunk repatriation (FSM-glitch insurance)
description:
Add operator tooling to detect and optionally repatriate orphaned
chunks found on local disk that the vault-ctl FSM doesn't know
about. The feature exists primarily as **insurance against FSM
glitches** — past incidents have seen FSM bugs cause vaults to be
obliterated, and this feature ensures local chunk files are not
silently lost or auto-deleted in those scenarios. It provides an
explicit operator path to recover from FSM-state corruption that
otherwise has no recovery story.

## Motivation

After the FSM-authority migration epic lands, the cluster's
authoritative answer to "what chunks should exist?" is the
vault-ctl FSM. A chunk on local disk falls into one of three
categories:

1. **Known** — present in `f.chunks[chunkID]`. Normal case.
2. **Tombstoned** — present in `f.tombstones`. Already handled by
   `SweepLocalOrphans`, which deletes locally.
3. **Unknown** — neither in `f.chunks` nor in tombstones. No
   current handler. The chunk manager loads it into `m.metas` but
   `ChunkResidency` returns nil; the chunk exists locally forever,
   invisible to the cluster, never replicated, never deleted.

Scenarios that produce unknown orphans:

- Operator restores the data directory from a backup, but the
  FSM state has moved on
- Cluster FSM wipe / reset with the disk preserved
- Node returns from very long absence where the chunks it held
  were tombstoned and finalized while it was offline
- **FSM bug obliterates entries that should not have been
  removed** — historically, this has caused vaults to be wiped
  with no recovery path. This is the primary motivation.

For all of these, the right default is "keep the chunk, raise an
alert, let the operator decide." Auto-delete is wrong (data loss
in benign scenarios; no recovery in the FSM-bug scenario).
Auto-ignore is wasteful but safe. This feature makes the
operator-driven recovery path explicit.

## Scope

1. **Orphan classification sweep** — periodic (or on-demand) pass
   over local chunks that classifies each as known / tombstoned /
   unknown against FSM state. Unknown ones raise a persistent
   alert with a count.

2. **Operator inspection** — CLI command (`gastrolog inspect
   orphans`) and UI surface listing unknown orphans with their
   reconstructed metadata (ChunkID, vault, size, record count,
   time range). Metadata is read from each chunk's local
   `idx.log` headers — no record replay needed.

3. **Repatriation operation** — operator chooses per-chunk:
   - Repatriate: propose `CmdAddSealedChunk` (or equivalent) to
     the vault-ctl FSM with the reconstructed metadata, then add
     the holding node to the chunk's placement set. The
     missing-replica sweep handles replication to other placement
     members if RF > 1.
   - Delete: remove the local file.
   - Ignore: leave it on disk; alert remains.

4. **Bulk operations** — for backup-restore scenarios where many
   chunks need the same action: `gastrolog cluster repatriate
   --all` / `--vault <id>` flags.

## Implementation surface

Most parts already exist:

- `idx.log` reading: `loadChunkMeta` in
  `backend/internal/chunk/file/manager.go` already reconstructs
  metadata from on-disk headers.
- FSM commands for sealed-chunk creation already exist (used
  during normal seal flow); repatriation reuses the same shape
  with reconstructed metadata.
- Placement and replication paths are unchanged — once the chunk
  is in FSM and the holding node is in placement, existing
  mechanisms take over.

The new code is the classification sweep and the operator CLI / UI
for inspection plus the per-chunk decision flow.

## Out of scope

- Active-chunk repatriation. Active chunks have in-memory state
  not captured in `idx.log` headers; reconstruction is messier.
  Repatriation applies to sealed chunks only.
- Tombstoned orphan handling (already done by `SweepLocalOrphans`).

## Acceptance

- Operator can list unknown orphans across all vaults with full
  metadata.
- Operator can repatriate a specific chunk; after the operation,
  the chunk is in the FSM, placement includes the holding node,
  and the chunk is reachable via normal read paths.
- Operator can repatriate-all for a vault or the whole cluster.
- Orphan-classification sweep raises a persistent alert when
  unknown orphans exist; alert clears when count drops to zero.
- Backup-restore scenario: after restoring the data directory on
  a fresh FSM, operator runs `gastrolog cluster repatriate --all`
  and the cluster recognizes the restored data.
- FSM-bug scenario: after the cluster obliterates known entries
  (whether by bug or operator error), the chunks remain on disk
  classified as unknown orphans, and the operator can repatriate
  to recover.

## Why low priority

The current behavior (silent retention) is wasteful but not
actively harmful in steady state. The feature is operational
insurance for rare but high-stakes scenarios. Defer until the
FSM-authority migration core issues land — the classification
only makes sense once the FSM is truly authoritative.

title: Fan-out data-plane architecture
description:
Redesign the cluster data-plane around fan-out writes and EventID-set
reconcile, replacing the current leader-driven record replication model.
Companion epic to the lifecycle/FSM-authority migration (gastrolog-2i1g9):
the control-plane work there lands first and provides the substrate;
this epic redesigns how records flow through that substrate.

## Motivation

The current data-plane model:

- Records arrive at the placement leader's node (one node per vault).
- Leader streams records to follower nodes via record-level replication.
- After seal, the canonical sealed chunk is re-shipped to followers
  via ImportSealedChunk (gastrolog-1bd56 marks this for removal).
- Reads route to the placement leader only; followers don't serve reads.

Pain this causes:

- Leader's outbound bandwidth is a single-node bottleneck per vault.
- Leader-node failure stalls writes until vault-ctl elects a new leader.
- Placement transitions need orchestrated drain coordination.
- "Single replica suffices for reads" relies on real-time replication
  being perfect; under load or transient failure, it isn't.
- RF=1 redeploy scenarios silently lose track of replicas because
  placement-as-residency lies during transitions.

## Direction

Three coupled mechanisms:

1. **Fan-out writes.** Ingester forwarder sends each record to every
   replica in the chunk's Receiving set in parallel. No leader-mediated
   hop. Tunable W-of-N ack semantics per vault (operator picks how many
   replicas must ack before write is considered durable).

2. **Set-diff reconcile via EventID Merkle summaries.** Replicas
   converge on set-equality, not byte-identity. Out-of-order arrival
   is NOT divergence — only actual missing records are. The IngestTS
   B+ tree provides canonical per-replica ordering; the dedupWindow
   substrate (keyed on chunk.EventID) handles cross-replica result
   deduplication for free.

3. **Receiving/Holding placement split.** Placement carries two sets
   per chunk: Receiving (where new records should be sent) and
   Holding (where records actually exist). Holding ⊇ Receiving by
   invariant; the difference is the catchup-in-progress state.
   Placement edits never silently lose data because removal from
   Holding requires explicit confirmation that other holders have
   the records.

## Consequences

The mechanisms compose:

- Multi-active chunks per vault become natural (each Receiving member
  is its own write target).
- Drain becomes a placement edit, not an orchestrated workflow.
- Soft-offline placement-rotation gates dissolve (the Holding set
  semantics enforce the same invariant by construction).
- gastrolog-617m6's hash-chain reconcile is replaced by set-diff
  (order-independent, no false positives from arrival jitter).
- Search must fan out to all Receiving replicas for active-chunk
  queries; sealed chunks remain single-replica. dedupWindow already
  exists and handles the cross-replica collapse.

## Scope

- New FSM fields per chunk: Receiving []NodeID, Holding []NodeID.
- New ingester routing: fan-out to all Receiving replicas with
  W-of-N ack policy.
- New reconcile mechanism: Merkle summary over sorted EventID set;
  on-demand exchange at seal time and on missed-ack triggers.
- Extend dedupWindow consumers to fan-out reads for active chunks.
- Replace ImportSealedChunk/post-seal record-shipping with reconcile.
- Remove placement-as-residency derivation; ChunkResidency reads
  Holding directly.

## Out of scope

- Lifecycle states, learner promotion, audit cleanups — those live
  in the companion epic gastrolog-2i1g9.
- Orphan repatriation (gastrolog-32bf2) — applies regardless.
- cluster-ctl rename (gastrolog-5eu6v) — applies regardless.

## Sequencing

Depends on gastrolog-2i1g9 landing first:

1. Control-plane work (gastrolog-2i1g9) provides the lifecycle states,
   learner join, FSM-authoritative audit posture this epic builds on.
2. Design issues for this epic: write design doc; resolve open
   questions on W-of-N policy defaults, Merkle tree shape, search
   fan-out detection logic.
3. Implementation issues: receiving/holding FSM fields, reconcile
   mechanism, fan-out ingester routing, dedup extension, removal of
   ImportSealedChunk.
4. Migration: existing clusters need a transition plan from
   leader-driven to fan-out. Likely flag-gated rollout.

## Acceptance

After this epic lands:

- Vault-write throughput scales with active-chunk count (multi-active
  works naturally).
- Leader-node bandwidth ceiling per vault is eliminated.
- Operator can tune per-vault durability via W-of-N ack policy.
- Placement transitions are non-disruptive (no orchestrated drain).
- Reconcile traffic is bounded by actual divergence size, not chunk
  size or replication factor.
- Cross-replica result consistency is mechanism-driven (dedupWindow),
  not assumed.
deleted_reason: Replaced by fan-out V2 epic and phased stack.

title: Implement node lifecycle state machine
description:
Implement the six-state node lifecycle machine described in
docs/node-lifecycle-design.md: Live / Unreachable / Maintenance
/ Draining / Decommissioning / Removed. Foundation for the other
lifecycle issues.

## Scope

- Add State (NodeState enum) and StateSince (time.Time) fields to
  system.NodeConfig
- New FSM command CmdSetNodeState with validators that enforce
  legal transitions (see "Transitions in detail" in the design doc)
- Apply handler updates NodeConfig.State and StateSince
- Existing voters get State=Live on first apply post-upgrade
  (lazy migration); new joiners get State=Live at JoinCluster time
- Snapshot/restore round-trips the new fields
- Reads via existing NodeConfig RPC paths surface the new fields

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover every legal transition and reject illegal ones
- Multi-node test: state transition via CmdSetNodeState propagates
  to all peers via Raft apply
- Existing cluster bootstrap with old NodeConfig records gracefully
  upgrades to State=Live without manual operator action
- No regressions in existing cluster bootstrap / join / restart paths
closed_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end on k8s cluster. Legacy records map to Live via EffectiveState; fresh joins record explicit State+StateSince. All tests pass; lint clean.

title: Implement state-driven placement guard
description:
Update placement.go to gate leader-rotation on node state.
Placement rotates the leader storage only on hard-decommission;
soft-offline states (Unreachable, Maintenance) retain placement.
Closes the RF=1 redeploy bug.

## Scope

- backend/internal/app/placement.go placeVault() reads node State
  from NodeConfig instead of using LivePeers() directly for rotate
  decisions
- Gate per the design doc's "Behavior gates by state" table:
  - Live: rotation permitted (existing behavior)
  - Unreachable / Maintenance: rotation refused (raise alert)
  - Draining / Decommissioning: rotation permitted (drain manager)
- Unit tests verify rotation behavior per state

## Acceptance

- RF=1 vault: simulated transient absence on the leader node does
  not cause placement rotation (regression test from gastrolog-2i1g9
  closes via this issue + #15)
- Existing placement tests still pass
- Alerts fire when rotation is refused due to soft-offline state
closed_reason: State-driven placement guard implemented. 5 new unit tests cover all gate cases; lint clean; k8s redeploy confirms backwards-compat. The RF=1 redeploy bug is now structurally fixed (gate refuses rotation off Unreachable/Maintenance) once the auto-trigger sweep (gastrolog-39m2k) transitions nodes to Unreachable on heartbeat lapse.

title: Implement Unreachable auto-trigger sweep and heartbeat-resume auto-clear
description:
Leader-side sweep that auto-transitions nodes to Unreachable on
heartbeat lapse past threshold, and auto-clears back to Live on
heartbeat resume.

## Scope

- New sweep on the system-Raft leader, low-frequency tick (~30s)
- For each peer with Live state and lapsed heartbeat > threshold:
  propose CmdSetNodeState{node, Unreachable}
- For each peer with Unreachable state (auto-set) and current
  heartbeat: propose CmdSetNodeState{node, Live}
- Threshold configurable via env var GLOG_UNREACHABLE_THRESHOLD
  (default 5 min)
- Sweep does NOT auto-clear if the State was set by operator
  (operator-set Maintenance is sticky; Unreachable is auto-only)

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover auto-trigger and auto-clear paths
- Multi-node test: node going briefly unreachable transitions to
  Unreachable then back to Live without operator action
- Env var override changes the threshold without code edit
closed_reason: Heartbeat-driven sweep transitions Live↔Unreachable on the system-Raft leader. K8s verified: gastrolog-3 → Unreachable after 37.5s heartbeat lapse → Live within 49ms of heartbeat resume. Closes the RF=1 redeploy bug loop together with the placement guard (gastrolog-slc6l).

title: Implement operator CLI verbs for node state transitions
description:
Operator CLI verbs for the node lifecycle state machine:
maintenance, online, drain, cancel-drain, remove-node. Idempotent
per the API surface principles in docs/node-lifecycle-design.md.

## Scope

- gastrolog cluster maintenance <node> — Live | Unreachable → Maintenance
- gastrolog cluster online <node> — Maintenance → Live
- gastrolog cluster drain <node> — Live | Unreachable | Maintenance → Draining
- gastrolog cluster cancel-drain <node> — Draining → Live (rare)
- gastrolog cluster remove-node <node> — convenience: drain + decommission + remove (must pass orphan gate, see #5)
- All verbs idempotent (repeated calls return success no-op, not error)
- All verbs support --output json for machine consumption
- Verbs propose the appropriate CmdSetNodeState via the
  existing cluster RPC surface

## Acceptance

- Each verb is idempotent
- json output mode produces parseable state for automation
- Multi-node test exercises each verb against the state machine
- Help text on each verb explains the state transition it triggers
closed_reason: Operator CLI verbs for node lifecycle state landed: cluster maintenance, online, drain, cancel-drain. New SetNodeState RPC routes through Raft via cfgStore.SetNodeState; FSM validates legality (idempotent same-state; illegal transitions surface as FailedPrecondition). All verbs support --output json. K8s end-to-end: Live→Maintenance, idempotent retry, drain progression, cancel-drain, online idempotency — all clean. remove-node 'drain + decommission + remove' convenience deferred (needs drain orchestrator that doesn't exist yet; operators use the manual sequence).

title: Implement decommission orphan-refusal gate
description:
cluster remove-node refuses to proceed if removal would orphan any
chunk (sole-replica-on-this-node case). --force flag for operator
override with explicit data-loss acknowledgement.

## Scope

- Pre-removal check: for every vault in placement, every chunk in
  vault-ctl FSM manifest, verify removal does not leave the chunk
  with zero remaining holders
- On refusal: error message enumerates affected vaults + chunk
  counts. Operator-actionable.
- --force flag bypasses the gate with audit-log entry
- Same gate applies when the auto-progression from Draining to
  Decommissioning would otherwise fire — refuses to promote if
  any chunks would orphan

## Acceptance

- RF=1 vault with sole holder: remove-node refused; clear error
- RF=3 vault with all healthy holders: remove-node proceeds (does
  not orphan because other holders exist)
- --force override succeeds with audit log entry
- Multi-node test covers both refusal and force-override paths
closed_reason: Orphan-refusal gate landed. cluster remove-node refuses if removal would leave any vault with zero placements; --force bypasses with a WARN-level audit log entry. Live-verified on k8s: refusal returns failed_precondition with full vault list + actionable suggestion, --force succeeds with structured log on the leader (orphaned_vaults), no-orphan removal proceeds cleanly. demote-self preStop path passes Force=true unconditionally (programmatic shutdown). 8 unit tests cover the gate helper across RF=1/2/3, mixed vaults, file-storage resolution, and the error-format contract.

title: Implement per-vault-ctl-group learner promoter
description:
Per-vault-ctl-group leader-side sweep that promotes learner
voters to full voters when their apply-index matches the leader's
commit-index and remains matched for one heartbeat interval.

## Scope

- New goroutine per vault-ctl group's leader epoch (in
  vault_ctl_leader_manager.go pattern)
- Polls learner peers' applied-index via existing Raft client APIs
- When learner's applied = leader's commit AND has remained matched
  through one heartbeat: propose ConfigChange to promote
- Stability check prevents flapping if learner momentarily catches
  up then falls behind
- Failure mode: learner falls behind faster than catches up → stays
  a learner; alert fires
closed_reason: Per-vault-ctl learner promoter landed. Same shape as gastrolog-2czh9 generalized to N groups: iterates every configured vault, acts only on groups this node leads, reads each follower's broadcast VaultStats.RaftAppliedIndex via PeerState. New proto field on VaultStats + plumbing through VaultSnapshot, StatsVaultSnapshot, and the orchStatsAdapter. 6 unit tests cover the helper logic (peer/vault matching, nil-tolerance, stale-counter pruning). Live promotion test deferred to gastrolog-41sut's end-to-end scale-up scenario — there's no current CLI verb to manually create a vault-ctl learner.

title: Implement system-Raft learner promoter
description:
Same shape as #6 but for the cluster-wide system Raft group. New
nodes join as learners; system-Raft leader's sweep promotes when
they catch up.

## Scope

- Leader-side sweep on system Raft
- Same apply-index match + stability window criterion as the
  per-vault-ctl-group promoter
- Coordinated with the JoinCluster-as-learner change (#8) — a
  newly-joined node enters as a non-voter and gets promoted by
  this sweep
closed_reason: System-Raft learner promoter landed. Leader-side tick (30s) scans system Raft membership for Nonvoter/Staging members, reads each learner's RaftAppliedIndex from the existing NodeStats broadcast, and promotes via AddVoter after a 2-tick stability window of sustained catchup. K8s verified: demoted gastrolog-4 → promoted back to Voter ~45s later, leader logged structured 'promoted learner to voter' with node_id + leader_applied_index. 9 unit tests via raftMembership/peerStatsReader interfaces (no real Raft needed).

title: Change JoinCluster to add new nodes as learners
description:
backend/internal/cluster/join.go JoinCluster path calls AddNonvoter
instead of AddVoter for new node additions. New nodes enter as
learners and get promoted by the per-group promoter (#6) and
system-Raft promoter (#7) once caught up.

## Scope

- backend/internal/cluster/join.go: AddNonvoter for the initial
  join (currently AddVoter)
- RefreshVaultCtlMembers in reconfig_vaults.go: add new nodes as
  non-voters in each vault-ctl group
- Existing voters during cluster bootstrap or upgrade stay as
  voters (only NEW joiners enter as learners)

## Acceptance

- New node joining a multi-node cluster enters as Raft non-voter
  in system Raft + every vault-ctl group
- Once caught up, promoted by #6/#7
- Cluster bootstrap (first node) still becomes voter immediately
  (no learner phase for the bootstrap node)
closed_reason: JoinCluster + RefreshVaultCtlMembers now add fresh joiners as nonvoters; existing voter restart still uses AddVoter for idempotent address refresh. Surfaced and fixed two pre-existing encoding bugs the change exposed: VaultSnapshots silently dropping vaults without local chunks, and StatsVaultSnapshot.ID being a string broadcast as ASCII bytes rather than the canonical glid.GLID. K8s end-to-end: scaled to 9, new pod entered NONVOTER in system + both vault-ctl groups, all three promoters (2czh9 system + 2× gcbx7 per-vault) upgraded to VOTER after stability window. The full learner trio (2czh9 + gcbx7 + 41sut) now composes correctly.

title: Reframe chunk-manager loadExisting as FSM-authoritative reconciliation
description:
Per audit finding F1 in docs/disk-authority-audit.md. The chunk
manager's startup scan (os.ReadDir over the vault dir) should
become reconciliation against the FSM, not the source of truth
for "what chunks does this node have."

## Scope

- backend/internal/chunk/file/manager.go loadExisting() reads the
  FSM's per-this-node residency claim first, then scans local
  disk and reconciles
- Files matching FSM-expected chunks: load normally into m.metas
- Files for chunks not in FSM expected set: raise orphan signal
  (do NOT auto-delete — see no-auto-delete-of-unknown-orphans
  invariant in the audit doc)
- Chunks in FSM expected set with no local files: raise catchup
  signal (existing missing-replica sweep handles)

## Acceptance

- m.metas is populated from FSM authority + disk evidence, not
  disk alone
- Orphan signals fire for unknown-on-disk chunks (no auto-delete)
- Catchup signals fire for missing-on-disk chunks
- Existing chunk-load tests still pass
closed_reason: F1/F2 reframing landed: SweepLocalOrphans now splits the ghost-deletion path by RecordCount. Rotation artifacts (records=0) still delete cleanly per gastrolog-66b7x; data-bearing unknown orphans (records>0, no FSM record, no tombstone) raise an operator alert and are preserved on disk per the no-auto-delete-of-unknown-orphans invariant. loadExisting docstring extended with full F1 lineage. 2 new unit tests cover both branches; existing tests still pass; k8s smoke confirms tombstoned-deletion path unchanged. Unblocks gastrolog-32bf2 (orphan repatriation).

title: Reframe RemoveVault empty check to consult FSM manifest
description:
Per audit finding F3. RemoveVault currently uses Chunks.List() to
check whether the vault is empty; the answer is disk-derived and
diverges from FSM under post-recovery or follower scenarios. Should
consult the FSM manifest first.

## Scope

- orchestrator/orchestrator.go RemoveVault() consults the vault-ctl
  FSM's chunks map for the emptiness check
- Local Chunks.List() is corroborating evidence at most, not
  authority
- Refuses removal if FSM still has chunks even when local disk is
  empty

title: Reframe archivalSweepVault to iterate FSM manifest
description:
Per audit finding F4. archivalSweepVault currently iterates
Chunks.List() (disk-derived) and overlays FSM state. The iteration
domain should be the FSM manifest (cluster-coordinated truth), with
disk presence as a per-chunk routing input ("am I the right node
to archive this one?").

## Scope

- orchestrator/archival_sweep.go archivalSweepVault iterates
  vault-ctl FSM manifest, not local Chunks.List()
- Per-chunk decision: is this node a holder? If yes and CloudBacked
  and Sealed, evaluate transition policy
- Preserves the existing OverlayFromFSM gating behavior

title: Split ListChunkMetas into local and cluster variants
description:
Per audit finding F5. Orchestrator.ListChunkMetas conflates "what
chunks does this node have locally" (disk-derived, correct for
per-node operations) with "what chunks exist for this vault in the
cluster" (FSM-authoritative, correct for RPC surfaces and display).

## Scope

- Split into two methods:
  - ListLocalChunkMetas(vault) — disk-derived per-node view
  - ListClusterChunkMetas(vault) — FSM-authoritative cluster view
- Audit each existing call site and route to the right one:
  - server/vault_chunks.go ListChunks RPC: cluster
  - server/query.go search engine chunk discovery: local
  - server/vault_info.go display: cluster
  - server/vault_operations.go: depends per-call
  - app/executors.go: per-call
- Existing ListChunkMetas method gets removed; compilation surface
  forces every caller to choose

## Acceptance

- Every call site has been explicitly routed
- Compile fails if a new caller uses the old (now-removed) API
  without choosing

title: Tune PodDisruptionBudget to Raft quorum
description:
deploy/k8s.yml PodDisruptionBudget maxUnavailable constrained to
floor((N-1)/2) so rolling restarts cannot exceed Raft quorum loss
threshold.

## Scope

- deploy/k8s.yml: PDB resource added (or maxUnavailable adjusted)
- Default is conservative — operators with higher RF can tune up
- Helm chart (if/when fixed for multi-node, per the audit's
  separate concern) inherits the same default

title: Implement UI surface for per-node lifecycle state
description:
Cluster inspector view surfaces per-node lifecycle state with
warning vs informational tone distinction.

## Scope

- Cluster overview shows each node with state (Live, Unreachable,
  Maintenance, Draining, Decommissioning) plus duration in state
- Unreachable: warning tone (yellow / amber icon) — cluster
  detected a problem
- Maintenance: informational tone (blue / neutral icon) — operator
  intent
- Draining: progress indicator (chunks remaining to transfer)
- Alerts fire when Unreachable duration exceeds an operator-tuned
  threshold; Maintenance alerts are silent or low-priority
- Follows the existing design system tokens (Observatory theme)

title: Multi-node redeploy regression test
description:
Multi-node harness primitive plus driver test that asserts the
RF=1 rolling-redeploy scenario survives. Closes the bug class that
motivated the FSM-authority migration epic.

## Scope

- Extend backend/internal/server/multinode_test.go with:
  - StopNode(t, nodeID) helper that gracefully shuts down a node
    while preserving its home dir
  - StartNode(t, nodeID, homeDir) helper that brings the node back
    up with the preserved home dir; node ID is read from disk so
    identity is preserved
- New driver test: TestMultiNode_NodeRestartPreservesReplication
  - 3-node cluster, RF=2, append records to vault V
  - Stop one node (preserving home)
  - Sleep past LivePeers TTL but well below soft-offline threshold
  - Assert placement did NOT rotate (per #2 placement guard)
  - Restart node with preserved home
  - Assert same node ID, same membership
  - Assert vault-ctl group on remaining nodes still lists returning
    node as voter
  - Append more records; assert replication to returned node
  - Read records from returned node directly; assert both pre- and
    post-restart records present

## Acceptance

- Test fails before lifecycle issues land (state machine + placement
  guard absent)
- Test passes once #1, #2, #3 land
- Test is in CI / just test recipe
closed_reason: Multi-node redeploy regression test landed as TestOrchRel_NodeRestartCatchupReplication in internal/orchestrator/reliability_orch_test.go. Stops a vault-ctl follower, appends batch 1 (5 records) pre-stop, batch 2 (5 records) while follower is down, restarts with preserved home dir, asserts: same node ID, voter still in vault-ctl Raft membership, all nodes converge to the union of batch 1 + batch 2 chunks via Raft replication. Passes 3x. Companion to TestUnreachableSweep_PlacementGuardChain which covers the FSM-state half of the redeploy story.

title: AllNodes:true ingesters don't start on nodes that join after configuration
description:
When a parallel (AllNodes:true) ingester is configured before
cluster scale-up, nodes that join afterward never start the
ingester locally. The IngesterAlive count stays at the pre-scale
node count even though the new nodes are healthy and Raft voters.

## Reproduction
1. Bootstrap cluster with 4 nodes
2. Configure a parallel ingester (e.g. chatterbox) with AllNodes:true
3. Wait for steady state — dashboard shows 4/4 alive
4. `just deploy kubernetes-scale 10` adds 6 new nodes
5. Wait for joiners to reach VOTER status
6. Dashboard still shows 4/10 — new nodes never started the ingester

## Suspected cause
Joiner orchestrators don't re-enumerate AllNodes ingesters when
they finish boot, OR ingester-config notifications fire only on
FSM PutIngester so joiners coming up after the original Put miss
the trigger entirely. Same shape as the gastrolog-2yeie / slc6l
placement bug: state evolved on Raft but the consumer didn't
re-evaluate on membership change.

## Acceptance
- Joining a node mid-life triggers it to start every AllNodes
  ingester whose eligibility matches
- Multi-node test: configure ingester → join node → assert
  IngesterAlive includes the new node
- IngesterAlive count converges to N/N after scale-up
closed_reason: AllNodes:true ingesters now register on fresh joiners. Two-part fix: ReplayConfigFromStore walks the cfg store after awaitReplication to catch snapshot-Restore-deposited entities; the replay skips entities the orchestrator already has so live Raft Apply notifications don't race with redundant remove+re-add cycles. K8s verified end-to-end: 13/13 chatterbox alive after scale-up from 10 to 13. Unit tests cover both branches.

title: *-up recipes aren't idempotent — destroy existing deployment instead of being a no-op
description:
Every `*-up` recipe in deploy/justfile pre-emptively destroys
