any existing deployment (containers, services, volumes, PVCs,
namespaces, Swarm secrets/configs, the works) before applying.
Running any of them twice wipes a healthy cluster — even though
the substrate underneath (kubectl apply, docker compose up -d,
docker stack deploy, etc.) already does the right thing
idempotently if you don't pre-destroy.

The dedicated `*-down` recipes exist for the destructive case;
the prelude is duplicated behavior with no escape valve.

Affected recipes:
- quickstart-up — docker rm -f + docker volume rm
- compose-up   — docker compose down -v
- swarm-up     — docker secret rm + docker config rm ×3 +
                 docker stack rm + docker volume rm
- podman-up    — podman compose down -v
- kubernetes-up — kubectl delete -f manifest + delete pvcs

## Fix
- Drop the destructive prelude from every *-up recipe
- Rely on each substrate's native idempotency: docker run errors
  if container exists (detect-and-skip), docker compose up -d
  reconciles services, docker stack deploy reconciles, kubectl
  apply reconciles
- Swarm secrets/configs are immutable — only create if missing;
  refresh via swarm-down
- kubernetes-up: patch replicas in-flight via sed so apply
  can't snap a scaled-up cluster back to the manifest's default
- kubernetes-up: accept optional SIZE arg (>= 3, default 3) as
  a grow-only floor; never shrinks (use kubernetes-scale for that)
- Always run setup-deps.sh + add-storage.sh where they apply —
  both upsert-by-name idempotent

## Acceptance
- `*-up` followed by another `*-up` of the same kind doesn't
  destroy cluster state or restart healthy pods
- Fresh-bootstrap and existing-cluster paths both succeed
- `kubernetes-up N` bootstraps or grows to N pods
- `kubernetes-up` (default 3) against a larger cluster is a no-op
- Invalid SIZE arg rejected with a clear error
- `*-down && *-up` gives the previous destructive-then-fresh
  behavior
closed_reason: All five *-up recipes now idempotent. kubernetes-up uses a grow-only SIZE floor + sed-patched replicas; compose/swarm/podman/quickstart use detect-and-skip. Live-verified on k8s (bootstrap 13, idempotent rerun, grow 13→14, validation), compose (IDENTICAL container IDs after rerun), swarm (same service IDs after rerun), and quickstart (same container ID + 0 restarts after rerun).

title: New joiners display as raw GLID until async NodeConfig write lands
description:
A fresh joiner is admitted to Raft membership before its
NodeConfig record exists in the FSM. The UI lists Raft voters
and looks up the friendly name via NodeConfig.Name, falling
back to the raw GLID when no record exists yet — so new nodes
briefly appear as e.g. `06f3a1pojdpht00ectgf4n7i7g` until the
joiner's own async write completes.

## Root cause

`finalizeNodeSetup` in backend/internal/app/app.go:847-855 dispatches
NodeConfig creation to a goroutine when `asyncNodeConfig` is true
(i.e. `fromLocalFSM || appSys == nil`, the fresh-joiner case):

```go
if asyncNodeConfig {
    go ensureNodeConfigAsync(...)  // waitForQuorum, then write
} else {
    ensureNodeConfig(...)
}
```

Meanwhile JoinCluster on the leader has already added the node
as a voter. The UI lists Raft voters via cluster.Servers() but
resolves names via cfgStore.GetNode(id) — for the new joiner the
latter returns nil until the async write completes.

Same shape as gastrolog-3hcfm and the placement-guard hazards:
admission to one source-of-truth happens before registration in
its dependent source-of-truth.

## Fix options (rough order of cost)

1. **UI fallback**: show "joining…" instead of the raw GLID.
   Cheapest, doesn't fix the data shape — the FSM still lacks
   the record for a window.
2. **Leader writes a placeholder NodeConfig at JoinCluster time**:
   the leader has cfgStore in scope; write
   `{ID, Name: petname.Generate(...), State: Unknown,
   StateSince: now}` as part of the admission sequence. The
   joiner's own ensureNodeConfig then updates Name if a
   preferred one was supplied. Closes the window structurally.
3. **Joiner sends NodeName in JoinClusterRequest**: so the
   placeholder gets the real name from the start, no later
   update needed. Requires a proto field on the join request
   plus the leader-side write from option 2.

Option 2 is the structurally clean fix; option 3 adds the
operator's preferred name at admission time.

## Acceptance

- A node freshly joining the cluster appears with its friendly
  name in the UI immediately, never as a raw GLID
- Multi-node test: stop a node and scale up by N; assert each
  new joiner's NodeConfig.Name is populated before it appears
  in the cluster.Servers() list (or atomically with it)
- The async ensureNodeConfig path remains as a Name-update
  mechanism for nodes that come up with a preferred-name flag
  override

title: Removed nodes linger as garbage entries displayed as raw GLIDs
description:
Removing a node via `cluster remove-node` cleans up NodeConfig
in the FSM but leaves per-peer satellite state behind:

- cluster.PeerByteMetrics has no Forget/Delete API; per-peer
  counters in `recv`/`sent` accumulate forever
- cluster.PeerState has Delete but it's not called from the
  remove-node path (only from the Raft peer-removal observer
  for membership reconcile)
- Possibly other per-peer caches (PeerConns, BroadcastSubscribers)

Symptom: the network stats panel shows GLID-only rows alongside
named pods, with stale 0 B/s rates that never go away. The GLID
display happens because NodeConfig was deleted, so the name
lookup falls back to the raw ID. Two bugs compounding:
1. Per-peer state isn't cleaned up on removal
2. UI doesn't gracefully handle "peer with state but no
   NodeConfig" — falls back to GLID instead of pruning the row

## Scope

- Add Forget(nodeID) to PeerByteMetrics
- Ensure PeerState.Delete is called on node removal (not just
  on Raft observer-driven membership reconcile)
- Audit other per-peer caches in internal/cluster/ for the
  same lifecycle gap
- UI: filter rows whose peer has neither an active heartbeat
  nor a NodeConfig (defensive — even if backend leaks, UI
  should not show the residue)

## Acceptance

- `cluster remove-node X` followed by checking the network
  stats panel shows X gone (not lingering at 0 B/s as a GLID)
- Multi-node test: scale-up, scale-down, assert PeerByteMetrics
  and PeerState contain only voters in current Raft membership
- Sibling issue gastrolog-4dqfs (new-joiner GLID display) is
  the symmetric case on the JOIN side

title: Resource tooltip wraps node names across lines (gastrolog-N becomes gastrolog-\nN)
description: The header-bar resource tooltip (CPU/memory per node, shown on hover over the CPU or memory pill) wraps node names like \"gastrolog-0\" across two lines: \"gastrolog-\" + \"0\". ## Cause `HoverStat` in [HeaderBar.tsx:322-331](frontend/src/components/HeaderBar.tsx#L322-L331) renders each row as: {middleTruncate(node.name || encode(node.id).slice(0, 8), 14)} The span has no `whitespace-nowrap`. When the tooltip column is narrow (min-w-40 = 10rem) and the node name contains a hyphen, the browser wraps after the hyphen. `middleTruncate` shortens long IDs but does nothing for hyphen-break behavior. ## Fix Add `whitespace-nowrap` to the name span (line 324) so node labels stay on one line. Same column already shrinks the value side via `shrink-0`; the label side should do the equivalent. ## Verify In a multi-node cluster, hover the CPU or memory pill. Each row reads \"gastrolog-N \" on one line.

title: Add sparklines to per-node resource tooltips (CPU/Memory/Storage)
description:
Each row in the header-bar resource tooltips (CPU, Memory, Storage)
currently shows a single point-in-time value per node. A small
sparkline next to each value would turn the tooltip into a
miniature trend view at no extra hover cost.

## Prior art

[PeerBytesSection.tsx](frontend/src/components/inspector/PeerBytesSection.tsx)
already keeps a per-peer ring buffer and renders trends via a local
`<Spark>` component (defined at line 133). The same component is
the natural fit; extract it from PeerBytesSection into a shared
location if multiple surfaces will use it.

## Scope

- New per-node, per-metric ring buffer (client-side state). One
  buffer per (nodeId, metric) — \`cpuPercent\`, \`memoryRss\`, and
  total storage bytes (sum of vault \`dataBytes\`).
- Buffer fills from the cluster-status poll the header bar already
  consumes; no proto or backend change required.
- \`HoverStat\` renders a \`<Spark>\` between the label and value
  columns on each row. Layout: name | spark | value.
- Open: window length (PeerBytesSection uses ~60 samples); pick a
  default and document.

## Notes

- Sparklines only make sense once history exists. While the buffer
  is empty, render nothing in the spark column (PeerBytesSection
  has the \`hasHistory\` precedent at line 93).
- Reset buffers on node-list change so removed nodes don't ghost.

title: K8s scale-down leaves orphaned Raft members; cluster never auto-removes vanished pods
description:
Scaling a StatefulSet down (e.g. \`kubectl scale\` or letting
\`kubernetes-up <N>\` shrink replicas) terminates pods but the
GastroLog cluster never learns to remove them from Raft. The vanished
pods linger as offline + nonvoter rows in \`cluster status\` and the
UI, with whatever NodeConfig was last written still in the FSM.

## Observed

After scaling 10→9 with a recent (now-removed) pod \`gastrolog-9\`:
- \`cluster status\` still lists 10 nodes, with \`gastrolog-9\` shown
  as offline + nonvoter
- No PeerObservation.Removed fires, because RemoveServer was never
  called against the leader's Raft instance
- The unreachable_sweep eventually flips State to Unreachable after
  \`GLOG_UNREACHABLE_THRESHOLD\`, but never removes — Unreachable is
  recoverable, not terminal

## Scope (decide direction first)

There are two reasonable shapes here; the issue should pick one
before implementation lands:

1. **Pod preStop hook calls SetNodeState DECOMMISSIONING + RemoveNode**:
   the existing preStop already calls YieldLeadership (gastrolog-2yeie);
   extend it to also remove self from the cluster on graceful shutdown.
   Problem: K8s scale-down with \`terminationGracePeriodSeconds=30\`
   may not give enough time for the RemoveNode Raft round-trip.
   Doesn't help force-deletions.

2. **Leader-side sweep that removes Decommissioning + long-Unreachable
   nodes**: extend unreachable_sweep with a third state — after N
   minutes Unreachable AND the node is a nonvoter AND placement
   is RF-safe, remove. Catches both intentional scale-down and crash-
   gone cases. More complex but covers all paths.

Adjacent: gastrolog-9ohip cleans up per-peer state on *manual*
RemoveNode. The auto-remove logic here should reuse the same
post-removal cleanup so we don't fork the lifecycle.

## Acceptance

- After \`kubectl scale --replicas=N-1\`, \`cluster status\` reflects
  N-1 nodes within a bounded window (document the window)
- No stale rows in the network panel, no ghost peer-bytes entries
- RF-safe: the cluster refuses auto-remove if it would drop any vault
  below configured RF (re-uses gastrolog-3vyex gate)

title: Ingester inspector card reports N/N healthy even when one or more nodes are offline
description:
The chatterbox (and any "runs on every node") ingester card in the
inspector shows aliveness as e.g. \`10/10\` even when one of those
ten nodes is offline, has been Unreachable for minutes, or has been
removed from the StatefulSet but still appears in cluster topology.

## Observed

In the same screenshot where \`gastrolog-9\` was clearly offline +
nonvoter (badges visible on the left), the chatterbox ingester card
on the right read \`10/10\` and rendered all ten node chips in green
— including \`gastrolog-9\`.

## Suspected cause

The ingester aliveness count consults the FSM's alive map, which
records "this node started this ingester" — not "this node is
currently reachable and the ingester is currently running." Once
\`gastrolog-9\` marked itself alive, that bit stays set in the FSM
until either:
- The node explicitly marks itself NOT alive (only happens on clean
  shutdown), OR
- Something else (lifecycle sweep, removal) clears the row

So an unreachable / crash-gone / scale-removed node stays
"alive" in the FSM. The UI rendering is correct relative to its
input — the input is what's wrong.

## Scope

1. **Backend**: ingester aliveness display value should be derived
   from (FSM alive set) ∩ (reachable nodes), where "reachable"
   means EffectiveState == Live (NodeState.LIVE post gastrolog-4pnht).
   Definition lives wherever the orchestrator computes the
   aliveness aggregate for the ingester card.
2. **UI**: node chip rendering in the ingester card should reflect
   per-node aliveness intersected with reachability — chips for
   offline/unreachable nodes should be dim or warn-toned, never
   green.
3. Same logic applies to passive ingesters and per-node ingesters,
   not just chatterbox. Audit IngesterCard / IngesterDetailPane.

## Acceptance

- Multi-node test: stop one of N nodes hosting a "runs on every
  node" ingester. The card shows (N-1)/N within
  \`GLOG_UNREACHABLE_THRESHOLD\`, with the absent node's chip
  visually distinguishable
- Same for a node removed from the StatefulSet (covered together
  with gastrolog-36cjs)

title: Surface time-since-last-heartbeat in inspector for offline nodes
description:
The existing \`offline\` badge in NodesSettings and the inspector
fires the moment \`cn.stats\` is missing — i.e. PeerState has no
recent broadcast — but shows no duration. The cku75 NodeStateBadge
surfaces \"unreachable Xm\" only once NodeConfig.State has flipped
to Unreachable, which happens after \`GLOG_UNREACHABLE_THRESHOLD\`
(5 min default). That leaves a 0–5 min window where the operator
sees \"offline\" with no idea whether the node has just blipped
(1s ago) or is genuinely gone (4m59s ago).

## Fix

Surface time-since-last-heartbeat for the 0–5 min window. Two
shapes possible:

1. Derive on the local viewing node from PeerState.LastSeen(id).
   No proto change. Limited to what the local node has observed —
   may differ slightly from peer to peer.
2. Plumb lastSeen into the wire format (ClusterNode message). Each
   node computes its own perspective and includes it in
   GetClusterStatus aggregation. More accurate but proto change.

Start with shape 1; shape 2 is a follow-up if cross-node
consistency becomes important.

## UI

Extend the offline badge to read \"offline Xs\" / \"offline Xm\".
Once duration exceeds GLOG_UNREACHABLE_THRESHOLD the badge transitions
into the existing \"unreachable Xm\" via NodeStateBadge — same visual
treatment, single elapsed counter from the operator's perspective.

## Acceptance

- A node that has been offline for 30s shows \"offline 30s\" in
  both NodesSettings and the inspector
- Transition to NodeStateBadge \"unreachable Xm\" is seamless past
  GLOG_UNREACHABLE_THRESHOLD — operator never sees a jump back to
  \"unreachable 0s\"
- Local-node-perspective is documented; cross-node consistency is
  out of scope for shape 1

title: Nodes flap offline/online every ~5s under broadcast jitter (PeerState TTL too tight)
description:
Operators occasionally see nodes flap offline → online every ~5
seconds. The cadence matches PeerState's TTL window almost exactly
(default broadcast interval 1s, TTL 4× = 4s), which suggests a
single missed or delayed broadcast pushes LastSeen past TTL → UI
flips offline → next heartbeat restores.

## Likely cause

\`backend/internal/cluster/peerstate.go\`: \`Entries expire after a
configurable TTL (typically 3× the broadcast interval).\` Production
default is 1s broadcast / 4s TTL (test reference at peerstate_test.go:130
documents the 4× safety factor and notes it was tightened from a prior
5s/20s shape).

A single late broadcast (network blip, scheduler hiccup, GC pause)
is enough to lapse the TTL — there is no hysteresis. The next
broadcast resets LastSeen, so the offline state is transient but
visible.

## Fix options

1. **Hysteresis**: require N consecutive missed broadcasts (e.g.
   3) before declaring offline. Independent of TTL; UI sees a stable
   state until evidence accumulates.
2. **Raise TTL multiplier**: 4× → 8× or 10×. Trades detection
   latency (4s → 8–10s) for stability. Cheapest change.
3. **Two-tier state**: \"recently silent\" (TTL just barely lapsed)
   vs \"clearly offline\" (multiple TTLs lapsed). UI renders both
   the same but the placement guard / unreachable_sweep treat them
   differently. More invasive.

Option 2 is the minimal viable fix; option 1 is the structurally
right answer. Start with option 2 + add a configurable
GLOG_PEER_TTL_MULTIPLIER while the design of option 1 settles.

## Acceptance

- Multi-node test: inject single missed broadcast — UI must NOT
  flap offline
- Inject N+1 consecutive missed broadcasts (whatever N ends up
  being) — UI DOES flap offline within bounded time
- Hysteresis or multiplier is configurable so operators in
  pathological networks can tune the trade

title: Migrate raw-ticker housekeeping to orchestrator job scheduler
description:
Several periodic-housekeeping subsystems run their own \`time.Ticker\`
goroutines instead of registering with \`orch.Scheduler()\`. The result:
they are invisible to the inspector's Scheduled view, can't be tuned at
runtime, and have inconsistent failure handling. Audit completed
2026-05-17.

## Why this matters

The inspector exposes scheduled jobs so the operator can see when each
periodic task last ran, when it next will, and whether it's currently
firing. Raw-ticker goroutines short-circuit that view entirely.
Planned future work to make scheduling adjustable at runtime depends
on every periodic operation being scheduler-registered.

## Children

Each migration is its own task / its own branch (one issue per branch
per project rules):

- gastrolog-XXX: unreachable_sweep
- gastrolog-XXX: system_raft_learner_promoter
- gastrolog-XXX: vault_ctl_learner_promoter
- gastrolog-XXX: managed_files reconcile
- gastrolog-XXX: placement reconcile
- gastrolog-XXX (question): vault_ctl_leader_manager per-group reconcile

## Pattern to adopt

Match \`backend/internal/orchestrator/cache_eviction.go\` and
\`archival_sweep.go\`:
- Own file named after the job
- Job-name + cron-schedule constants at the top
- A task function (one tick's body, not an infinite loop)
- A \`startXxxSweep()\` registrar calling \`scheduler.AddJob\` +
  \`scheduler.Describe\` — the Describe text shows in the inspector

## Precedent

gastrolog-9ohip's reconciler shipped with this pattern at
\`backend/internal/app/peer_cache_reconcile.go\` — register, describe,
done. Other migrations can mirror that file's shape.

title: Migrate unreachable_sweep to orchestrator job scheduler
description:
\`backend/internal/app/unreachable_sweep.go\` runs its own \`time.Ticker\`
(line ~121, \`unreachableSweepInterval = 30s\`) instead of registering
with \`orch.Scheduler()\`. The sweep has two phases:

1. **Transitions** (leader-only): Live↔Unreachable per PeerState
   heartbeat freshness — proposes Raft commands so only the leader
   acts.
2. **Alerts** (every node): time-in-Unreachable warning alerts — runs
   on every node because alerts live in the local alert.Collector
   (gastrolog-cku75).

## Suggested shape

Convert per the peer_cache_reconcile.go precedent:
- Job name: \`node-unreachable-sweep\`
- Cron: \`*/30 * * * * *\` (every 30s — matches current interval)
- Task fn: one call to the two-phase tick body; phase 1 stays leader-
  gated inside the function, phase 2 runs unconditionally
- \`scheduler.Describe\` text: explain both phases for the operator

## Acceptance

- Sweep appears in \`gastrolog job list\` on every node
- \`scheduler.Describe\` text shows in the inspector's Scheduled view
- Live↔Unreachable transitions still fire only from the leader
- Unreachable-duration alerts still fire on every node

title: Migrate system_raft_learner_promoter to orchestrator job scheduler
description:
\`backend/internal/app/system_raft_learner_promoter.go\` (line ~99)
uses a raw ticker for periodic learner-promotion checks. Leader-only
work (line ~106 gates \`if p.cluster.IsLeader()\`).

## Suggested shape

- Job name: \`system-learner-promoter\`
- Cron: \`*/30 * * * * *\`
- Task fn: scan voters, check stability window, promote eligible
  learners (existing tick body)
- Leader gate stays inside the task fn; scheduler fires on every node

## Acceptance

- Job appears in inspector's Scheduled view on every node
- Promotion still only happens on the leader
- gastrolog-41sut and gastrolog-2czh9 behavior preserved

title: Migrate vault_ctl_learner_promoter to orchestrator job scheduler
description:
\`backend/internal/app/vault_ctl_learner_promoter.go\` (line ~108)
uses a raw ticker. Per-vault-ctl-group leader logic (line ~154
checks \`g.Raft.State() != hraft.Leader\` per group), NOT system-Raft
leader gating — every node may lead different vault-ctl groups.

## Suggested shape

- Job name: \`vault-ctl-learner-promoter\`
- Cron: \`*/30 * * * * *\`
- Task fn: iterate every vault-ctl group, check per-group leadership,
  promote eligible learners on groups this node leads
- Scheduler fires on every node; per-group gate stays inside task fn

## Acceptance

- Job appears in inspector's Scheduled view on every node
- Promotions still scoped to groups this node leads
- gastrolog-gcbx7 behavior preserved

title: Migrate managed_files reconcile to orchestrator job scheduler
description:
\`backend/internal/app/managed_files.go\` (line ~98) runs a periodic
reconcile of the managed-file manifest against disk, pulling missing
files from peers. \`periodicReconcileEvery = 5 * time.Minute\`.

## Suggested shape

- Job name: \`managed-files-reconcile\`
- Cron: \`0 */5 * * * *\` (every 5 minutes on the minute)
- Task fn: call \`m.reconcileOnce(ctx)\` (already exists)
- Straightforward conversion — no leader gating, no multi-phase work.

## Acceptance

- Job appears in inspector's Scheduled view
- Reconcile still pulls missing files from peers
- No behavior change for happy or unhappy paths

title: Migrate placement reconcile to orchestrator job scheduler
description:
\`backend/internal/app/placement.go\` (line ~42) uses a raw ticker for
the periodic-fallback placement reconcile. \`placementInterval = 15s\`.

## Notes

Placement has THREE trigger sources:
1. Leadership change (Raft observer channel) → immediate reconcile
2. Manual trigger (Trigger() channel) → immediate reconcile
3. Periodic ticker → fallback

Only the ticker (3) should migrate to the scheduler. The
observer/manual paths stay as-is — they're event-driven, not periodic.

## Suggested shape

- Job name: \`vault-placement-reconcile\`
- Cron: \`*/15 * * * * *\` (matches current 15s)
- Task fn: enqueue a reconcile via the same channel the manual trigger
  uses, so the existing serialization stays unchanged

## Acceptance

- Periodic-fallback fires via scheduler; appears in inspector
- Leadership-driven and manual-trigger paths unchanged

title: Decide migration shape for vault_ctl_leader_manager per-group reconcile timer
description:
\`backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_ctl_leader_manager.go\` (line ~210)
runs a ticker INSIDE \`runLeaderEpoch(ctx, vaultID, group)\`. This is
NOT a global periodic sweep — it's a per-group safety fallback that
wakes the event-driven reconciler if the leadership-change /
desired-members-change signals miss something. Interval:
\`vaultMembershipReconcileInterval = 30s\`.

## Why this is a question, not a task

Migrating to the global scheduler would either:

a) Hoist the reconcile to a single cluster-wide job that iterates
   every vault-ctl group and checks per-group leadership. Breaks the
   tight coupling between \`runLeaderEpoch\`'s group context (the
   already-resolved \`group\` pointer + cancellation scoped to the
   leader epoch) and the reconcile state. Adds re-resolution and
   lock churn per tick.

b) Keep the per-group ticker as a safety fallback and accept that
   this one stays raw — argue it's not "scheduled housekeeping" but
   "per-group lifecycle timing" which is a different category.

## Decision needed before any migration lands

Which approach? If (a), the cron shape and behavior need to be
designed. If (b), document why this one is exempt from the migration
rule so future readers don't try to "fix" it.

title: Fan-out data-plane V2 implementation
description:
## Goal
Implement fan-out data-plane V2 end-to-end: destination-vault sequencing, spool-first accepted writes, leader-authoritative fence cuts, sequence-range materialization, and converge-sealed reconcile, with full operator parity and validation before any merge/cutover.

## Why This Epic Exists
The prior fan-out attempt failed because synchronous global invariants were coupled to the write hot path. V2 is explicitly designed to keep safety-critical ordering deterministic while allowing temporary replica divergence that is reconciled before sealed-final semantics.

This epic is the implementation vehicle for the finalized docs in `docs/fan-out/v2`, and must be executable by agents with no prior chat context.

## Architecture Baseline (Non-negotiable)
- Destination-vault `seq` is the ordering axis; `EventID` remains identity/dedup axis.
- `H` (ingest high watermark) advances only on destination-vault `W-of-N` durable success.
- Fence inclusion rule is deterministic: `prev_fence < seq <= curr_fence`.
- Route fan-out and replica fan-out are distinct operations and must stay distinct in code/tests.
- Active-path divergence is acceptable; sealed correctness requires converge-sealed gating.

## Implementation Scope
This epic includes all phased delivery from guardrails to cutover:
1. Phase 0: scope lock + per-vault feature gate ownership.
2. Phase 0.5: anchor decision lock (RecordRef/ChunkID migration contract).
3. Phase 0.6: placement-leader semantic direction lock.
4. Phase 1: allocator leases on vault-ctl raft (epoch-safe, replay-safe).
5. Phase 2: destination-vault sequence assignment in ingest and retention routes.
6. Phase 3: spool segmenting and crash model carry-over (index-last safety).
7. Phase 4: fence coordinator + stale-safe hint arbitration.
8. Phase 5: materialization + reconcile by sequence coverage.
9. Phase 6: anchor rollout completion (proto/backend/query/read surfaces).
10. Phase 7: placement-leader migration execution.
11. Phase 8: CLI config/inspection parity.
12. Phase 9: UI config/inspection parity.
13. Phase 10: mandatory verification ladder (unit, multinode, e2e, live k8s).
14. Phase 11: cutover + rollback-safe staged V1 cleanup.

## Mandatory Invariants Across All Children
- No V2 partial merge to `main` before full ladder validation and explicit approval.
- Bug fixes land on originating branch (or nearest parent in stack), not detached noise branches.
- No per-record raft logging for accepted data; allocator control state only.
- Hole discipline is strict: assigned-missing heals, unassigned gaps do not.
- Segment reclaim must be blocked until materialization + convergence safety watermark.
- CLI and UI must both expose operator-complete V2 config + diagnosis surfaces.

## Dependency and Execution Model
The child-issue dependency graph is authoritative and already wired; only true entry points should appear in `dcat ready`.

Phase edges:
- `P0 -> {P0.5, P0.6, P1}`
- `P1 -> P2 -> P3`
- `{P0.6, P3} -> P4`
- `{P3, P4} -> P5`
- `{P0.5, P5} -> P6 -> P7`
- `P5 -> {P8, P9}`
- `{P7, P8, P9} -> P10`
- `P10 -> P11`

## Verification Ladder (Release Gate)
V2 is not considered complete until all are green with evidence:
- single-node correctness
- multinode cluster behavior
- happy path
- unhappy path and failure recovery
- edge cases (retries, churn, replay, restart)
- end-to-end workflows
- live 4+ node k8s validation under load/failure

Required live-k8s scenarios include: burst ingest with tight rotations, node restart/eviction under traffic, leader failover during active leases, retention-route sequencing correctness, and CLI/UI/backend parity checks.

## Rollout and Rollback Policy
- Release N: V2 default-capable with kill switch available.
- Release N+M: remove V1 write path only after soak with no rollback-triggering regressions.
- Cutover and rollback must be rehearsed and documented before default-on promotion.

## Source of Truth
- `docs/fan-out/v2/implementation-plan.md`
- `docs/fan-out/v2/architecture-overview.md`
- `docs/fan-out/v2/high-watermark-contract.md`
- `docs/fan-out/v2/spool-state-machine.md`

## Out of Scope
- Unrelated refactors outside the V2 plan.
- Opportunistic cleanup not required for V2 contracts.
- Legacy design resurrection from obsoleted docs.
acceptance: All child phase issues and dependencies are implemented to completion; V2 invariants are preserved; unit/multinode/e2e/live-k8s ladder passes with reproducible evidence; CLI and UI parity are complete; cutover/rollback rehearsal is validated before any default-on promotion or V1 cleanup.
deleted_reason: V2 fan-out architecture abandoned; code peeled back off main in favor of V3 (see gastrolog-2m2h5). V2 design docs retained under docs/fan-out/v2.

title: [V2 P4] Fence coordinator and hint protocol
description:
## Goal
Implement leader authoritative fence coordination with stale safe replica hint arbitration.

## Why
Deterministic inclusion by sequence requires authoritative fence cuts even when hints arrive out of order and leader is not a holder.

## Scope
- Implement coordinator in vault ctl leader manager and rotation sweep paths.
- Process FenceHint sequence evidence from replicas.
- Reject stale overlapping hints from slower nodes.
- Persist fence decisions for replay and auditability.
- Expose ingest and fence watermark signals.

## Verification
- Leader not holder scenarios remain safe.
- Stale hint suppression prevents fence regression.
- Fence history survives replay and restart.

## Out of scope
- Materialization and converge sealed reconcile mechanics.
acceptance: Fence decisions are authoritative and replay safe, stale hint handling is correct, and operators can inspect fence history for inclusion debugging.

title: [V2 P1] Vault sequence allocator leases in vault-ctl Raft
description:
## Goal
Implement destination vault sequence allocator leases on vault ctl raft with epoch safety.

## Why
Destination scoped sequencing needs cluster consistent allocation without per record raft entries.

## Scope
- Add allocator control state and commands in vault raft fsm and command surfaces.
- Enforce monotonic non overlapping lease ranges and epoch checks.
- Define burned tail behavior for abandoned leases.
- Verify replay and persistence constraints with raftwal tests.

## Verification
- No overlap or regression across failover restart replay.
- FSM and reliability tests prove monotonic behavior.

## Out of scope
- Router integration for per record assignment.
acceptance: Allocator leases are epoch safe and replay safe, per record raft logging is avoided, and failover tests prove non overlapping monotonic allocation.

title: [V2 P5] Materialize and reconcile by sequence coverage
description:
## Goal
Materialize fenced sequence ranges and reconcile replicas to converge sealed state.

## Why
V2 allows temporary divergence while active but sealed correctness requires deterministic record level convergence by assigned coverage.

## Scope
- Implement sequence range materializer and reconcile path in lifecycle reconciler and manifest reader.
- Classify holes as assigned missing vs unassigned gap.
- Heal assigned missing holes only.
- Enforce converge sealed marker gate before full sealed semantics.
- Keep V1 and V2 coexistence via write model dispatch.

## Verification
- Assigned missing holes heal deterministically.
- Unassigned gaps remain untouched.
- Multinode tests prove record level convergence and gate behavior.

## Out of scope
- Anchor API rollout completion.
acceptance: Materialization and reconcile are deterministic by sequence coverage, hole class behavior is correct, and converge sealed gating is enforced in multinode tests.

title: [V2 P0.6] Placement-leader direction lock
description:
## Goal
Lock migration direction for VaultPlacement.Leader semantics in V2 write path.

## Why
V2 uses control leadership for coordination but placement leader residency must not remain write authority.

## Scope
- Define exact V2 meaning of VaultPlacement.Leader in write path.
- Define coexistence rules for non V2 paths.
- Identify migration targets in app placement and system vault config code.

## Verification
- Decision text is unambiguous and implementation ready for Phase 7.

## Out of scope
- Runtime code migration execution.
acceptance: Leader semantic direction is explicit, coexistence rules are documented, and Phase 7 can execute with no design ambiguity.
closed_reason: Locked placement-leader direction in docs/fan-out/v2/placement-leader-migration.md with V1/V2 coexistence rules, PlacementLeaderIsWriteAuthority guardrails, and Phase 7 migration target checklist.

title: [V2 P2] Router destination-vault seq assignment
description:
## Goal
Assign destination vault sequence after destination selection and before replica fan out for ingest and retention route paths.

## Why
Fence and materialization correctness requires destination vault ordering.

## Scope
- Integrate allocator lease usage in routing and ingest orchestrator paths.
- Apply same sequencing semantics to retention routing fan out.
- Persist EventID destination vault sequence metadata for spool phases.
- Preserve retry idempotency.

## Verification
- Stable destination sequence across replicas.
- Ingest and retention semantics match.
- Retry tests show deterministic assignment.

## Out of scope
- Spool crash model and accepted watermark implementation.
acceptance: Destination vault sequence assignment is deterministic for ingest and retention route paths, metadata is persisted, and idempotency tests pass.

title: [V2 P3] Spool ingestion and segment crash-safety
description:
## Goal
Implement spool first accepted write substrate with first_seq segment identity and crash safe recovery.

## Why
V2 decouples acceptance from materialization and requires durable replayable spool semantics.

## Scope
- Implement segment identity and bounds in file and memory chunk managers.
- Carry over index last crash model with tail truncation on restart.
- Enforce H advancement only after destination W of N durable success.
- Gate segment reclaim on materialization and convergence safety watermark.
- Expose spool watermarks.

## Verification
- Crash restart tests validate tail truncation behavior.
- H does not move on failed fan out.
- Segment lifecycle tests prove reclaim safety.

## Out of scope
- Fence coordinator logic and reconcile execution.
acceptance: Spool substrate is crash safe and first_seq addressable, H advancement follows durability contract, and reclaim safety is test validated.

title: [V2 P0] Scope lock, branch policy, and feature-gate contract
description:
## Goal
Provide the non-negotiable V2 execution guardrails before any data-plane changes.

## Why This Exists
V2 work is stacked and long-lived. Without explicit gate ownership and fan-out boundaries, implementation drifts and agents re-litigate decisions.

## Scope
1. Define and enforce per-vault V2 write-model gate in:

title: Materializer skip burned-tail unassigned gaps
description:
## Goal
Teach the sequence-range materializer to skip unassigned-gap sequences (burned lease tails) inside a fence range instead of failing the whole batch.

## Why
P5 hole classification already treats burned-tail sequences as unassigned gaps that must not be healed. `materializeFence` still fails on any missing seq in `(prev, upper]`, including documented gaps — so a fence that legitimately spans a burned tail cannot materialize locally even when all assigned sequences are present.

## Scope
- Use allocator burned-tail state (same source as `ClassifyFenceHoles`) when scanning `(M_r, F_n]`.
- Skip unassigned-gap seqs during spool read + chunk append; do not count them as `MissingSeqs`.
- Preserve strict failure for assigned-missing holes (seq not in burned tail and not locally present).
- Unit tests: fence spanning burned tail + assigned records materializes; assigned-missing still errors.

## Verification
- Happy: fence with burned tail in range materializes assigned records only.
- Unhappy: assigned-missing seq still returns `ErrMaterializeMissingSeq`.
- Edge: empty assigned subset after skipping gaps advances M_r correctly.

## Primary files
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/sequence_materializer.go`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/hole_classifier.go`
acceptance: Materializer completes fences that include burned-tail unassigned gaps without treating gaps as missing assigned data, while still failing on true assigned-missing holes.

title: [V2 P5.c] Spool slot heal for assigned-missing holes (recovery)
description:
## Goal
Background heal for **assigned-missing** sequenced spool slots on a replica: pull `(vault_id, vault_seq)` records from peers that already hold the slot, apply idempotently via `PutReplicaWrite`, then allow reconcile to advance `C_r`.

## Rescope (2026-05-26, post write-path rework)
The original scope assumed peer pull would compensate for broken cross-node ingest (chunk forward / incomplete follower landing). That path is **withdrawn** — see `docs/fan-out/v2/phase-rework-map.md` and the P10 write-path gate.

After the locked write path (swath assign → direct spool replica fan-out → W-of-N acceptance), **steady-state ingest must not rely on reconcile pull**. Assigned-missing becomes a **failure/recovery** concern, not a substitute for ingest.

## In scope
- Trigger only when `ClassifyFenceHoles` reports **assigned-missing** (seq was assigned; fan-out expected; local slot absent).
- **Never** heal **unassigned gaps** (burned swath tails) — already handled by materializer skip (`gastrolog-2wg3z`).
- Pull mechanism keyed by **`VaultSeq` spool slot**, not sealed-chunk catchup:
  - New narrow RPC or reuse of cluster transport to fetch one slot / seq range from a peer's spool (`ReadByVaultSeq`).
  - Apply locally with `PutReplicaWrite` (idempotent by `VaultSeq` + `EventID` policy).
- Background loop or reconcile pre-pass with retry/backoff; surface metric/alert when no peer has the slot.
- **Not** on the ingest hot path; **not** a workaround for failed W-of-N fan-out on the ingesting router.

## Out of scope (other issues)
- **Steady ingest parity** — write-path gate + W-of-N fan-out (`gastrolog-21ptb`, guardrail `gastrolog-3rab5`).
- **Post-reclaim / post-restart reconcile witness** — chunk or durable-`M_r` fallback (`gastrolog-21fdf`, blocked on `gastrolog-326i6`).
- **New-replica historical backfill** — may share transport but is a separate “spool catchup for placement join” concern if needed later.
- Chunk `RequestReplicaCatchup`, `ForwardRecords`, `ImportSealedChunk` — wrong abstraction for slot heal.

## Verification
- Unit: classified assigned-missing → pull stub fills slot → reconcile succeeds; unassigned gap never pulled.
- Multinode (4+ nodes): **inject** missing slot on one replica (dropped fan-out, not broken ingest path); heal converges; burned-tail gap unchanged.
- Unhappy: no peer has slot → heal stops, observable error/metric, `C_r` blocked.

## Primary files
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/sequence_reconcile.go` (classify + trigger)
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/spool_store.go` / `sequenced_write.go` (apply path)
- New or extended cluster RPC for spool slot fetch (not chunk replication)

## Supersedes
Original `5nj7s` title/description referencing chunk catchup as the primary heal path.
acceptance: Assigned-missing holes on a replica are filled from peer spool slots (not chunks) in background/recovery paths; C_r advances only after local slot presence is restored; unassigned gaps are never healed; steady ingest does not depend on this path.

title: Durable replica M_r and C_r watermarks
description:
## Goal
Persist per-vault replica materialization (M_r) and convergence (C_r) watermarks durably so restart/replay resumes without relying on in-memory state or spool-only probes.

## Why
`vaultSpoolStore` keeps M_r and C_r in memory only. After restart, materialization/reconcile progress is lost, `bySeq` is empty until new acceptance, and reconcile presence probes can false-negative unless chunk fallback exists. V2 docs (`high-watermark-contract.md`, `spool-state-machine.md`) require durable local checkpoint state.

## Scope
- Persist M_r and C_r alongside spool segment metadata (file spool manager and in-memory test store parity).
- Reload on vault instance startup; monotonic restore only.
- Wire metrics `vault_replica_materialization_watermark` / `vault_replica_convergence_watermark` to durable values.
- Restart tests: materialize + converge, restart node, verify watermarks and idempotent resume without re-materializing sealed output.

## Verification
- Single-node restart preserves M_r/C_r.
- Multinode restart on follower preserves progress and does not regress sealed chunks.
- Reclaim gating still respects `min(M_r, C_r, …)` safety watermarks after reload.

## Primary files
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/spool_store.go`
- `backend/internal/spool/file/manager.go`
acceptance: M_r and C_r survive process restart, reload monotonically, and materialization/reconcile resume idempotently from durable checkpoints.

title: Chunk presence fallback for reconcile probe
description:
## Goal
Extend `localSeqPresentForReconcile` with a materialized-chunk scan fallback so independent reconcile passes and post-restart runs can witness seq presence after spool reclaim or empty `bySeq`.

## Why
Primary probe is spool (`ReadByVaultSeq`). Secondary witness uses `LatestMaterializationCoverage` + M_r for the same fence batch. After spool reclaim or restart (before durable M_r), reconcile can false-negative on sequences already sealed in local chunks. Code TODO in `sequence_reconcile.go`.

## Scope
- Add fallback: if spool miss and coverage witness insufficient, scan local materialized chunks for vault_seq (or EventID index if available).
- Gate fallback: only when M_r or durable coverage proves the seq was materialized in-range (avoid treating stale chunk data as fence evidence).
- Unit tests: spool entry removed after materialize+reclaim, reconcile still sees seq via chunk fallback.
- Restart test (pairs with P5.d): without spool tail, chunk fallback + durable M_r allow C_r advance.

## Verification
- Post-reclaim reconcile does not report assigned-missing for materialized seqs.
- Fallback does not mask true assigned-missing holes (no chunk, no spool, no valid witness).

## Primary files
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/sequence_reconcile.go`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/sequence_materializer.go`
acceptance: Reconcile presence probe finds materialized sequences via chunk fallback when spool no longer holds them, without hiding real assigned-missing holes.

title: NodeStats FenceHint broadcast and leader ingestion
description:
## Goal
Deliver replica `FenceHint` evidence (node id, ingest H, timestamp) from data-bearing replicas to the vault-ctl leader across cluster nodes.

## Why
P4.a/b implemented local hint ingestion and leader-side arbitration, but hints are only submitted on the local node (`submitLocalFenceHint`). When the vault-ctl leader is not a data holder (leader-not-holder), fence decisions need cross-node hint transport. Deferred at P4 close.

## Scope
- Extend cluster broadcast / `NodeStats` (or dedicated ephemeral channel) with per-vault ingest H + observed-at for sequenced vaults.
- Replicas emit hints on H advancement / rotation sweep tick (existing local trigger).
- Leader ingests remote hints via `SubmitFenceHint` with stale-overlap rejection unchanged.
- Proto + codegen both sides if new fields required.
- Multinode test: leader on non-holder node receives hints from holders and publishes fence at min(valid H evidence).

## Verification
- Leader-not-holder path works with remote hints only.
- Stale overlapping remote hints suppressed (reuse P4.a tests extended to cross-node).
- Hint channel remains ephemeral — not authoritative state.

## Primary files
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/fence_coordinator.go`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/fence_hint.go`
- cluster broadcast / NodeStats proto
acceptance: Vault-ctl leader on a non-holder node receives replica FenceHints over the cluster broadcast path and publishes fences using existing stale-safe arbitration.

title: Multinode materialize and reconcile verification
description:
## Goal
Close the P5 verification debt: multinode suites proving record-level convergence, assigned-missing **recovery** heal, unassigned-gap discipline, and converge-sealed gating.

## Scope
- Multinode (4+ nodes, file-backed vaults): fence publish → materialize on all replicas → `C_r` convergence.
- **Normal ingest:** asymmetric ingesters; assert spool slot parity on all replicas (extends write-path gate — no assigned-missing under healthy fan-out).
- **Recovery heal:** inject missing slot on one replica (dropped `PutSpoolSlot`, not legacy chunk-forward path); verify spool-slot heal (`gastrolog-5nj7s`) and reconcile convergence.
- **Unassigned gap:** fence spans burned tail; gap not healed; materialization succeeds (`gastrolog-2wg3z`).
- Leader failover during active fence/materialize window.
- Restart survival where durable watermarks / chunk fallback apply (`gastrolog-326i6`, `gastrolog-21fdf`).

## Verification
- Tests in `reliability_orch_harness_test.go` and/or `multinode_test.go`.
- Repeatable under cluster harness; bounded waits only.

## Depends on
Functional completion of `gastrolog-5nj7s` (spool slot heal), `gastrolog-2wg3z` (closed). Ideally `326i6` / `21fdf` for restart scenarios.
acceptance: Multinode tests prove healthy ingest keeps replicas aligned without heal; injected assigned-missing heals via peer spool pull; unassigned-gap non-healing; converge-sealed gating; restart-safe reconcile where durable markers land.

title: [V2 P5 completion] Materialize and reconcile debt
description:

## Why

## Children

- Peer pull healing for assigned-missing holes

title: [V2 P4 completion] Cross-node fence hint transport
description:
## Goal

title: Joiner ApplyConfig(nil) skips groupMgr wiring — sequenced writes fail on nodes 1+
description:
## Symptom
Joiner pods spam `sequenced write path unavailable: vault-ctl allocator not wired` when ingesting to a sequenced vault (scatterbox all-nodes repro on k8s).

## Root cause
`Orchestrator.ApplyConfig(nil, factories)` returns before wiring `groupMgr` / `peerConns`. Joiners boot with `appSys=nil` (snapshot replication path) then `ReplayConfigFromStore`; sequenced assign never sees GroupManager.

## Fix
Wire `factories.GroupManager` and `factories.PeerConns` before the nil-sys early return. Regression test: `TestApplyConfigNilWiresGroupManager`.

## Evidence
k8s gastrolog-1/2 logs before fix; post-fix redeploy shows zero allocator-not-wired errors.

title: Sequenced vault: EventID seq conflict under symmetric multi-node ingest
description:
## Symptom
After joiner groupMgr fix, k8s nodes spam `write failed: spool: EventID seq conflict` (~770/pod) when scatterbox `--all-nodes=true` routes ingest to one sequenced vault (p10-seq). Channel pressure hits 90%+, cluster RPCs hang.

## Mechanism
`vaultSpoolStore.checkSeqAssignmentLocked`: same `vault_seq` assigned to two different EventIDs on one node (local assign vs replica write collision).

## Repro (invalid for P10 but exposes bug)
1. k8s 3-node cluster, sequenced vault RF=3
2. scatterbox enabled all-nodes → single sequenced destination
3. Observe logs on all pods

## Not covered by Stage 1 gate
`TestWritePathGate*` uses **asymmetric** ingest (two ingesters, two routers). This is **symmetric** triple-router fan-in with one ingester ID.

## Blocks
gastrolog-1cqdh Stage 2 k8s validation until resolved or runbook uses asymmetric ingest (kafka/chatterbox on one node only).

title: [V2 P12] Persistent router delivery queue — nothing ingested is lost once routed
description:
## Why

**Cardinal rule: nothing that is ingested is lost** — provided a route destination captures the record. No matching route → intentional silent drop (unchanged).

Once routed, loss from transient delivery failure is a bug. Today \`writeLoop\` attempts delivery once and logs \`write failed\` — routed records are lost on:

- vault-not-ready bootstrap windows,
- peer partition / unreachable replicas,
- ingest nodes without a local vault replica (sequenced path requires \`vault.Instance != nil\`),
- process restart before delivery completes.

There is no persistent pre-vault buffer. Cross-node \`RecordForwarder\` buffers help chunk-append remote routes only; sequenced vaults bypass that path entirely.

## What

Implement a **router delivery queue**: persistent, node-local, bounded on disk, **not** vault spool / not RF. Holds **routed** digested records until delivery into the locked write path succeeds (sequenced assign + replica fan-out + W-of-N, or chunk-append forward).

Design: \`docs/fan-out/v2/router-delivery-queue.md\`

## Scope notes

- Enqueue only after route match; unrouted drops stay as-is.
- Sequenced ingest on nodes without vault replicas also requires W-of-N / \`appendLocalSequenced\` changes (assign on router, fan out to replicas only — no local spool slot on non-replica nodes).
- Retention-route replay should use the same queue for uniform durability.
- Register queue depth on PressureGate; inspect surfaces (depth, oldest age, drops).
acceptance:
- [ ] Persistent queue under node home: enqueue fsync before default upstream ack; survives restart
- [ ] Drain worker retries delivery with backoff; successful delivery dequeues
- [ ] Bounded disk cap with observable oldest-entry eviction
- [ ] Sequenced delivery works from ingest node **without** vault replica (assign + fan-out to replicas; W-of-N without local spool slot)
- [ ] Chunk-append failures and vault-not-ready enqueue instead of drop
- [ ] PressureGate + inspect metrics (depth, bytes, oldest age, drops)
- [ ] Tests: single-node restart; 4+ node asymmetric ingest + partition heal; unhappy paths per design doc
- [ ] Ubiquitous language + v2 docs linked from issue remain accurate
notes: Phase 12: post-cutover (after P11). Design locked in docs/fan-out/v2/router-delivery-queue.md. Not gating P10/P11.
deleted_reason: V2 fan-out architecture abandoned; code peeled back off main in favor of V3 (see gastrolog-2m2h5). V2 design docs retained under docs/fan-out/v2.

title: Migrate vault-ctl Raft FSM command + snapshot encoding from hand-rolled binary to protobuf
description:
## Summary

The vault-ctl Raft consensus layer (`backend/internal/vaultraft`, `backend/internal/vaultraft/vaultctlfsm`) serializes every replicated command and every FSM snapshot with **hand-rolled binary** (`opcode byte + big-endian fixed-width fields`, manual byte-offset slicing, hand-written snapshot sections). This is brittle, error-prone to extend, and inconsistent with the rest of the system (the gRPC/API boundary is protobuf). It must move to protobuf. This work is **independent of the V2 fan-out implementation** (gastrolog-4ecqt and its children); it lands on a branch from `main`, and the fan-out branches rebase onto `main` to pick it up once merged.

## What is hand-rolled today

Command opcodes (first byte of the Apply payload), all encoded by bespoke `Marshal*` functions and decoded by bespoke `apply*` functions:

- Chunk metadata: `CmdCreateChunk`(1), `CmdSealChunk`(2), `CmdCompressChunk`(3), `CmdUploadChunk`(4), `CmdDeleteChunk`(5, replay-only), `CmdRetentionPending`(6), `CmdAttachOffsets`(11), `CmdBeginSeal`(12), `CmdRepatriateChunk`(13).
- Delete-receipt protocol: `CmdRequestDelete`(7), `CmdAckDelete`(8), `CmdFinalizeDelete`(9), `CmdPruneNode`(10).
- Sequence allocator: `CmdReserveSeqRange`(14), `CmdReleaseSeqLease`(15).
- Fences: `CmdPublishFence`(17).
- Wrapper opcodes in `vaultraft/cmd.go`: `OpNoop`(1), `OpVaultChunkFSM`(2) + `MarshalVaultChunkCommand` (vaultID-scoped envelope).

Snapshot serialization — 5 hand-rolled sections with paired `encode*Section`/`read*Section`:
`sectionEntries`(1), `sectionTombstones`(2), `sectionPendingDeletes`(3), `sectionSeqAllocator`(4), `sectionFences`(5).

Plus a parallel hand-rolled command decoder in `backend/cmd/walinspect/main.go`.

## Why this is a problem

Adding or changing a single field requires editing, in lockstep:
1. the `Marshal*` function (write the new bytes at the right offset),
2. the `apply*` function (read them back, and bump the payload-length guard, e.g. `if len(payload) < 32`),
3. the snapshot `encode*Section` (persist the field), and
4. the snapshot `read*Section` (restore it, in the exact same field order).

Any mismatch — a wrong offset, a forgotten length-guard bump, an encode/decode order divergence — does **not** fail loudly. It silently corrupts Raft replay and/or snapshot install: a follower restoring a snapshot or replaying the WAL reconstructs **wrong FSM state** (wrong chunk metadata, wrong fence boundaries, wrong seq allocator counters), which is a cluster-wide consensus/data-integrity hazard, not a local glitch. There is no schema, no field tags, no codegen keeping the four sites in sync, and the bespoke codec carries its own large test burden.

## How it surfaced

While implementing the gastrolog-39g6p data-loss fix, we needed to add an "expected accept count" field to `FenceRecord` (`fsm_fence.go`). Doing so requires touching `MarshalPublishFence`, `applyPublishFence` (incl. the `len(payload) < 32` guard), `encodeFencesSection`, and `readFencesSection` by hand — exactly the lockstep, offset-arithmetic hazard above. That made the cost of the status quo concrete and motivated this epic.

## Safety analysis — protobuf is viable here (the usual blocker does not apply)

The classic reason to hand-roll Raft commands is **byte-determinism**. It is not required in this codebase:

- **Log commands:** hashicorp/raft replicates the **leader's** encoded command bytes verbatim; followers apply those exact bytes and never re-encode. Cross-node encoding determinism is therefore irrelevant for commands.
- **Snapshots:** taken per-node and shipped opaquely via `Snapshot`/`Restore`/`InstallSnapshot`; they are never byte-compared or hashed across nodes. (The only hashing in the layer is `ManifestEntry.Hash`, the GLCB cloud-blob integrity digest — unrelated to FSM encoding.)
- **WAL (`raftwal`):** stores opaque entry bytes and is agnostic to payload format, so this migration does **not** touch the correctness-critical WAL layer.
- **No deployment compat window:** the project has zero production deployments and permits cluster re-init, so there is no need for a wire-compat shim — this is a one-shot cutover (delete-and-renumber discipline still applies).

Net: protobuf's non-canonical encoding cannot break consensus here. The migration buys safety, field-level evolution, codegen-enforced encode/decode parity, generic tooling (walinspect), and one serialization model across the stack. The only real costs are the port effort (cheap given no compat shim) and a small marshal/alloc overhead on the seq-lease-reserve hot path (mitigable with vtprotobuf).

## Scope

In: all `vaultctlfsm` command marshal/apply paths, all 5 snapshot sections, the `vaultraft/cmd.go` wrappers, `walinspect`, and their tests; `buf generate` wiring for the new messages.
Out: the WAL (`raftwal`) internals; the gRPC/API protos (already protobuf); the V2 fan-out behavior.

## Process / sequencing

- Branch from `main`; this epic is **not** part of the V2 fan-out branches.
- The data-loss fix (gastrolog-39g6p) continues in parallel on its own branch; once this epic merges to `main`, fan-out branches rebase to build on protobuf (the fence "expected accept count" field then lands as a proto field rather than hand-rolled bytes).
design: Keep the 1-byte Op/Command opcode framing and the MarshalVaultChunkCommand WAL wrapper; replace each command PAYLOAD and each snapshot SECTION body with a protobuf message. Evaluate vtprotobuf for deterministic + allocation-free marshal (needed only if future anti-entropy hashes snapshots; also mitigates hot-path alloc on seq-lease reserve). walinspect switches to generic proto decoding. Suggested child breakdown: (1) define .proto messages + buf wiring; (2) port chunk-metadata commands (Create/Seal/BeginSeal/Compress/Upload/AttachOffsets/RepatriateChunk/Retention); (3) port delete-receipt protocol (RequestDelete/AckDelete/FinalizeDelete/PruneNode); (4) port seq allocator (ReserveSeqRange/ReleaseSeqLease); (5) port fences (PublishFence); (6) port all 5 snapshot sections; (7) walinspect; (8) round-trip + WAL-replay + InstallSnapshot tests.
acceptance: Every vault-ctl FSM command and all 5 snapshot sections encode/decode via protobuf with round-trip tests. WAL replay of a pre-existing log produces identical FSM state. Multi-node InstallSnapshot/restore verified on a 4+ node cluster. walinspect decodes all command types. No hand-rolled binary.Read/binary.Write or manual byte-offset slicing remains in vaultctlfsm command/snapshot paths. Seq-lease-reserve hot path shows no throughput regression vs baseline.

title: vault-ctl FSM protobuf: proto schema + buf wiring (vaultctlfsm.proto)
description:
Phase A of epic gastrolog-5lrg7. Author backend/api/proto/gastrolog/v1/vaultctlfsm.proto defining the protobuf replacement for vault-ctl Raft FSM command + snapshot wire formats, then run codegen and commit generated Go.

Schema (package gastrolog.v1, go_package gastrolog/api/gen/gastrolog/v1;gastrologv1):
- Outer envelope (replaces vaultraft/cmd.go opcode byte): VaultRaftCommand { oneof command { NoopCommand noop=1; VaultScopedCommand vault_scoped=2; } }; VaultScopedCommand { bytes vault_id=1; VaultCtlCommand command=2; }.
- Inner command (replaces Command opcodes 1-17 in vaultctlfsm): VaultCtlCommand { oneof command { CreateChunkCommand create_chunk=1; SealChunkCommand seal_chunk=2; CompressChunkCommand compress_chunk=3; UploadChunkCommand upload_chunk=4; DeleteChunkCommand delete_chunk=5; RetentionPendingCommand retention_pending=6; RequestDeleteCommand request_delete=7; AckDeleteCommand ack_delete=8; FinalizeDeleteCommand finalize_delete=9; PruneNodeCommand prune_node=10; AttachOffsetsCommand attach_offsets=11; BeginSealCommand begin_seal=12; RepatriateChunkCommand repatriate_chunk=13; ReserveSeqRangeCommand reserve_seq_range=14; BurnSeqLeaseTailCommand burn_seq_lease_tail=15; BumpSeqAllocatorEpochCommand bump_seq_allocator_epoch=16; PublishFenceCommand publish_fence=17; } } (preserve 1-17 tags matching current opcodes on main).
- Snapshot (replaces 5 hand-rolled sections): VaultCtlSnapshot { repeated ManifestEntry entries=1; repeated Tombstone tombstones=2; repeated PendingDelete pending_deletes=3; SeqAllocatorSnapshot seq_allocator=4; FenceSnapshot fences=5; }.
- ManifestEntry message carries all fields incl Hash/CloudServiceID/KeyScheme (current 123-byte codec drops these). RepatriateChunkCommand embeds ManifestEntry.
- Use bytes for 16-byte GLIDs, int64 unix nanos for times, matching vault.proto conventions.

Design against main-branch code (HEAD fe9344af): fence record {ID,UpperBoundSeq,PrevBoundSeq,CreatedAtNanos}; seq allocator {NextSeq,Epoch,ActiveSwaths,BurnedTails} with opcodes 14 reserve / 15 burn / 16 bump / 17 fence.

Run: just backend gen (cd api/proto && buf generate). Commit .proto + generated backend/api/gen/gastrolog/v1/vaultctlfsm.pb.go.

Acceptance: proto compiles, codegen produces Go types for all command + snapshot messages, generated code committed. Blocks phases B/C/D.

title: vault-ctl FSM protobuf: migrate command encoding (Marshal*/apply* + envelope)
description:
Phase B of epic gastrolog-5lrg7. Depends on phase A (proto schema, gastrolog-794re).

Replace hand-rolled binary command marshal/apply with protobuf VaultRaftCommand/VaultCtlCommand (from vaultctlfsm.proto).

Files:
- backend/internal/vaultraft/cmd.go: MarshalNoop, MarshalVaultChunkCommand, MarshalVaultReserveSeqRange, MarshalVaultReleaseSeqLease/burn, MarshalVaultPublishFence -> build proto VaultRaftCommand and marshal.
- backend/internal/vaultraft/fsm.go: outer Apply dispatch (OpNoop/OpVaultChunkFSM byte switch) -> unmarshal VaultRaftCommand, dispatch on oneof; extract vault_id; delegate inner bytes/message to sub-FSM.
- backend/internal/vaultraft/vaultctlfsm/fsm.go: Apply/applyLocked + all Marshal*/apply* for opcodes 1-13 (CreateChunk, SealChunk, CompressChunk, UploadChunk, DeleteChunk, RetentionPending, AttachOffsets, BeginSeal, RepatriateChunk).
- fsm_receipts.go: opcodes 7-10 (RequestDelete, AckDelete, FinalizeDelete, PruneNode).
- fsm_allocator.go: opcodes 14-16 (ReserveSeqRange, BurnSeqLeaseTail, BumpSeqAllocatorEpoch).
- fsm_fence.go: opcode 17 (PublishFence).
- announcer.go + orchestrator callers: keep public Marshal* signatures stable where possible so callers are unaffected; otherwise update callers.

Remove all manual byte-offset slicing / binary.BigEndian.PutUint*/Uint* on command paths and the len(payload)<N guards (proto handles framing).

Tests: round-trip marshal->unmarshal for every command type; Apply produces correct FSM state; cover happy + unhappy (malformed/empty payload) + edge (empty strings, max holder ID len). Update existing cmd_test.go, fsm_test.go, fsm_receipts_test.go, fsm_allocator_test.go, fsm_fence_test.go.

Acceptance: no hand-rolled binary remains in command paths; all command round-trip tests pass; go build + go test ./internal/vaultraft/... green.

title: vault-ctl FSM protobuf: migrate snapshot encoding (5 sections -> VaultCtlSnapshot)
description:
Phase C of epic gastrolog-5lrg7. Depends on phase A (proto schema, gastrolog-794re). Parallelizable with phase B.

Replace the hand-rolled snapshot format (magic GLTRSNAP + version + 5 typed sections) with a single protobuf VaultCtlSnapshot message.

Files (backend/internal/vaultraft/vaultctlfsm):
- fsm.go: fsmSnapshot struct, FSM.Snapshot(), fsmSnapshot.Persist(), FSM.Restore(), decodeSnapshot, writeSnapshotHeader/readSnapshotHeader, writeSectionHeader, encodeEntry/readEntriesSection, inline tombstones encode + readTombstonesSection.
- fsm_receipts.go: encodePendingDeletesSection/encodePendingDeleteEntry/readPendingDeletesSection.
- fsm_allocator.go: encodeSeqAllocatorSection/readSeqAllocatorSection (+ swath/lease/burned-tail helpers).
- fsm_fence.go: encodeFencesSection/readFencesSection.

New flow: Snapshot() builds VaultCtlSnapshot proto from FSM state; Persist() writes proto.Marshal(snapshot) to the sink; Restore() reads all bytes, proto.Unmarshal, repopulate f.chunks/tombstones/pendingDeletes/seq allocator/fences.

Remove section-kind framing, magic/version bytes, binary.Read/Write and manual offset slicing on snapshot paths. ManifestEntry proto now carries Hash/CloudServiceID/KeyScheme (snapshot previously dropped these) - verify Snapshot populates them.

Tests: round-trip Snapshot->Persist->Restore equality for FSM state incl all 5 section kinds; empty sections; large entry counts; restart survival; cover unhappy (truncated/garbage snapshot bytes -> error, not panic). Update fsm_test.go and section tests.

Acceptance: no hand-rolled binary remains in snapshot paths; round-trip restore reproduces identical FSM state; go test ./internal/vaultraft/... green.

title: vault-ctl FSM protobuf: migrate walinspect command decoder
description:
Phase D of epic gastrolog-5lrg7. Depends on phase B (command encoding, gastrolog-2lz79).

backend/cmd/walinspect/main.go has a parallel hand-rolled command decoder (decodeFSMCmd, commandName) that reads cmd=Command(data[0]) and guesses chunk ID from data[1:17]. Replace with proper proto.Unmarshal of VaultRaftCommand/VaultCtlCommand so all command types decode fully (seq/fence/prune currently show misleading/empty chunk IDs).

Keep the WAL segment + raft log entry layer decoders (walkSegment, decodeLog) as-is (raftwal format, out of scope). Only the FSM command payload decode changes.

Tests: decode each command type, assert correct command name + key fields. Cover all 17 command kinds.

Acceptance: walinspect decodes all command types via protobuf; no hand-rolled FSM command decoding remains in walinspect.

title: vault-ctl FSM protobuf: cross-cutting verification (multi-node, replay, benchmark)
description:
Phase E of epic gastrolog-5lrg7. Depends on phases B (gastrolog-2lz79), C (gastrolog-1n428), D (gastrolog-62ywk).

Cross-cutting verification of the protobuf migration:
- Multi-node (4+ node, file-backed vaults, real transferrers): InstallSnapshot/Restore across nodes reproduces identical FSM state; follower catch-up via snapshot works.
- WAL-replay determinism: replay a proto-encoded raft log reconstructs identical FSM state (chunk metadata, fences, seq allocator counters, pending deletes, tombstones).
- Seq-lease-reserve hot path: benchmark proto marshal/unmarshal vs baseline. Acceptance requires no throughput regression. Only if a real regression appears, wire vtprotobuf (add protoc-gen-go-vtproto to backend/api/proto/buf.gen.yaml + go install, regenerate, use MarshalVT/UnmarshalVT on the hot path). vtprotobuf is NOT currently wired and should remain unwired unless the benchmark forces it.

Tests/dimensions: single-node + multi-node, happy + unhappy (snapshot install during churn, corrupt snapshot rejected), edge (restart survival, empty FSM, max entries).

Acceptance (closes epic gastrolog-5lrg7): all epic acceptance criteria met - every command + all 5 snapshot sections via protobuf with round-trip tests, WAL replay identical FSM state, multi-node InstallSnapshot verified on 4+ nodes, walinspect decodes all commands, no hand-rolled binary.Read/Write or manual byte-offset slicing in vaultctlfsm command/snapshot paths, no seq-lease-reserve throughput regression.

title: Excise hot/warm/cold tier vocabulary (keep cache terminology)
description:
The hot/warm/cold "temperature tier" metaphor is NOT a real GastroLog concept. Storage classes are opaque numeric identifiers (StorageClass uint32 in backend/internal/system/storage.go, matched against NodeStorageConfig.StorageClass), not named hot/warm/cold. The temperature vocabulary crept in via agent cargo-culting and should be excised so it stops bleeding into new design and code.

WHY: it implies a storage-tier taxonomy the system does not have, confuses readers, and keeps reappearing in generated prose. Removing it now (zero production deployments) is cheap.

SCOPE (excise the temperature-tier framing):
- scripts/cluster.sh: the demo two-vault retention chain is named hot-vault / warm-vault, with routes ingest-to-hot and hot-retention-to-warm, a HOT_VAULT_ID variable, and several comments (~lines 102-115, 259-304). Rename to role- or backing-based names. The two vaults are: (1) file-backed on local disk with short rotation/retention, (2) file-backed but cloud-served (S3). Candidate naming: local-vault / cloud-vault (by backing) or ingest-vault / retention-vault (by role). Pick one and apply consistently to vault names, route names, the resolved-ID variable, and comments.
- docs/ubiquitous_language.md (~line 521): 'a retention-trigger route directing records to another vault is how hot/warm/cold chains are expressed.' Reword to describe retention-routing chains without the temperature metaphor.
- Sweep remaining docs for temperature-tier framing of storage/retention and reword: docs/vision.md, docs/vault-control-plane-architecture.md, README.md, docs/file_formats.md, docs/advanced_indexing.md, and any others (grep for hot/warm/cold tier/chain/vault phrasing). Judge each: tier/storage/retention framing -> reword; cache framing -> keep.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (KEEP — this is valid, standard terminology):
- warm cache / cold cache / cold start in the chunk caching layer (backend/internal/chunk/file/*, backend/internal/orchestrator/cache_eviction.go, etc.). Cache temperature is a real, separate, correct concept and must NOT be touched.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- No hot/warm/cold storage/retention/data-tier vocabulary remains in scripts, proto comments, or docs.
- scripts/cluster.sh demo vaults/routes/IDs/comments renamed consistently; the script still bootstraps and the retention chain still works end to end.
- Cache temperature terminology (warm cache / cold cache / cold start) is left untouched.
- A grep for the temperature-tier framing returns only legitimate cache uses.

NOTE: replacement vocabulary for the demo vaults is an open decision (local/cloud vs ingest/retention) — confirm with the user before applying.

title: [V3 prep] Remove abandoned V2 fan-out code
description: Forward-remove the abandoned V2 fan-out data-plane code from main to reach a clean V3 starting point. Keep all V2 documentation (docs/fan-out/v2), the V3 design notes (docs/fan-out/v3), and the vault-ctl FSM protobuf encoding for pre-existing commands (gastrolog-5lrg7). Remove V2 code: destination-vault sequencing, spool, fence coordinator/hints, sequence materialize/reconcile, anchor model, sequenced diagnostics, write_model config, and the V2 FSM allocator/fence commands. Tombstone the open V2 issues (gastrolog-4ecqt epic + 390uk, ix0z0, 5n9nn, 2qrec). Branch point reference: 019dde6d.

title: Fan-out V3 pipeline implementation
description:
Implement the V3 fan-out data-plane on the **pipeline-v3** integration branch.

## Spec (flexible)
Authoritative starting point: `docs/fan-out/v3/design-notes.md` — especially
"Where the thinking leans" and "Phases & managers". Treat as a **flexible spec**:
details may change, but only after explicit discussion — not drive-by edits.

## Delivery model (isolation first)
- Build each pipeline phase as **testable units in isolation** (`backend/internal/pipeline/...` + unit tests).
- Wire phases together in **`backend/internal/pipeline/flow_test.go`** (and similar harness tests) with test doubles for vault-ctl, leadership, and peer homes — **before** touching production paths.
- **Do not import V3 managers into `backend/internal/orchestrator`** until **`gastrolog-214bz`** (the Rubicon). No issue other than `214bz` may wire into the orchestrator or live ingest path.
- Child issues cover the seven pipeline managers; sub-sub-issues are testable slices. Phase parents close when their slices + harness coverage are done — not when orchestrator wiring exists.

## Pipeline (manager order)
Ingestion → Digestion → Routing → Segmentation → Distribution → Collection → Chunking
(Orchestrator supervisor wiring is **`gastrolog-214bz` only**.)

## Branch / merge policy
- All V3 implementation work lands on **`pipeline-v3`**, not `main`.
- When closing an issue: merge its branch onto **`pipeline-v3`** only.
- **`main`** updates only via PR after explicit cutover approval.

## Prerequisites

Everything before this issue must be provable in isolation and in **`backend/internal/pipeline/flow_test.go`** (and phase unit tests) with test doubles. Do not start this until all seven phase parents are closed and their harness slices land.

## Scope

Implement via child issues; **close this parent only after `gastrolog-5xn20` (E)**:
- **A** `gastrolog-3kx8v` — supervisor skeleton + queue graph
- **B** `gastrolog-jiwlf` — write path through durable segment
- **C** `gastrolog-2z3oa` — distribution + collection on vault-ctl
- **D** `gastrolog-hl6cp` — chunking lifecycle on vault-ctl

Slices A–D may temporarily coexist with legacy V0 orchestrator wiring for incremental merge; **E removes the V0 write pipeline entirely** — V3 becomes the sole active production path.

- Ingestion integration: PressureGate under backpressure; Ack nil/error after durable segment write; checkpoint periodic save + Raft failover restore
- **Clean cutover (slice E):** no legacy V0 write pipeline remains active in orchestrator — V3 is the sole production ingest→sealed-chunk path

title: V3 segment SourceTS index tail (sparse, post-EventID index)
description:
Add a sparse **SourceTS** sorted index tail on finalized V3 segment files, appended **after** the existing EventID index at `Finalize` / `BuildIndex` time. Required before **`gastrolog-214bz`** (Rubicon); segment-layer only — no orchestrator imports.

## Context

V0 active chunks carry separate B+ trees for ingest-time and source-time order. On V3 segments:

- **Ingest / canonical order** is already covered by the **EventID index** tail (IngestTS lives inside EventID). No separate ingest index.
- **SourceTS** is stored on each record frame but is **not indexed** today. `QueryOpenChunk` and span merges walk EventID order only; there is no `source_start` seek.

Records always carry SourceTS in the frame (8 bytes); **`zero = unknown`**. Match GLCB / V0 behavior: **only index non-zero SourceTS** (`record.Record`, `chunk/cloud/writer.go`).

Spec: design-notes point 18 (query order vs storage order); chunking query direction D may consume this later.

## On-disk layout (segment format v2)

```
[header v2]
[record frames]
[EventID index: RecordCount × IndexEntrySize]   ← existing
[SourceTS index: SourceCount × 12 bytes]        ← new, sparse
```

**SourceTS index entry** (same shape as GLCB `tsIndexEntry`, 12 bytes):

- `int64` SourceTS nanoseconds (LE)
- `uint32` **event-order position** (0 … RecordCount−1), not file offset

Entries sorted by SourceTS; ties broken by event-order position (mirror GLCB `sortEntries`).

**Header v2 extension** (after existing v1 fields — bump segment `formatVersion` to `0x02`):

- `FirstSourceTS`, `LastSourceTS` (uint64 nanos; 0 when no indexed sources)
- `SourceIndexOffset` — byte offset where source tail starts (= end of EventID index when `SourceCount == 0`)
- `SourceIndexCount` — number of sparse entries
- `SourceIndexChecksum` — CRC32/IEEE over source tail

`recordsEnd()` / `verifyIndexedLayout()` must account for both tails. v1 segments (no source tail) remain readable if any tests still emit them; new writes use v2.

## Implementation scope

**`backend/internal/pipeline/segment/`**

- Extend `BuildIndex` (or finalize helper) to scan frames once, build EventID index as today, then append sorted sparse SourceTS index.
- Track `FirstSourceTS` / `LastSourceTS` in header during scan.
- `FindSourceStartPosition(ts)` — binary search on source tail; returns event-order position (reuse logic from `chunk/cloud/tsindex.go`).
- Open / reconcile: validate source tail checksum and file size.

**`backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/`** (minimal, no orchestrator)

- `OrderedIndex` (or segment API) wrapper for source seek on a finalized segment.
- Optional: trim manifest span start using source index when a caller passes `SourceStart` — **unit + harness tests only**; live query engine wiring stays in **`gastrolog-214bz`**.

## Out of scope

- Orchestrator / production query engine integration (`gastrolog-214bz`)
- Separate ingest-time index (redundant with EventID index)
- Indexing zero / unknown SourceTS

## Test dimensions

- Single-node: empty source index (all zero SourceTS), mixed zero/non-zero, sort order, tie-break
- BuildIndex idempotency / already-built errors unchanged for EventID path
- Open + verifyIndexedLayout with truncated or bad source checksum (unhappy)
- Multi-record segment: seek returns correct event-order start position
- Harness or chunking unit: span trimmed by SourceStart when index present
acceptance:
- Finalized segments (v2) append sparse SourceTS tail after EventID index; header fields and checksums verified on open
- Zero SourceTS records omitted from source index; bounds fields correct when count is 0
- FindSourceStartPosition matches GLCB semantics for equivalent data
- Existing segment / chunking tests updated; new tests cover happy, unhappy, and edge cases above
- No imports from backend/internal/orchestrator
