- Close **`gastrolog-214bz`** only after this slice passes user validation

## Explicit gate
This slice is the **definition of done** for Rubicon — not an optional QA pass. Prior slices must not close 214bz early. Dual V0+V3 orchestrator wiring during A–D is **transitional**; E is the deliberate removal of V0.

Spec: **`gastrolog-214bz`** acceptance criteria (full text).
acceptance:
- 4+ node dev cluster: full V3 path from ingest through sealed GLCB on holder homes
- Ingester reassignment and vault placement churn: pipeline recovers without manual repair
- **No active V0 write pipeline** in orchestrator after merge — grep/reconcile confirms V3-only ingest→sealed-chunk path
- Cluster bootstrap and dev workflows use V3 exclusively without WriteModel opt-in to legacy path
- User sign-off; then `dcat close gastrolog-214bz`
closed_reason: E1–E3 complete: V3-only write path, queryable pipeline chunks, 4+ node cluster acceptance validated by user.

title: Rubicon E1: make pipeline sealed GLCB queryable (minimal)
description:
First child of Rubicon E (gastrolog-5xn20). Make pipeline-built sealed GLCB chunks readable by the query engine on holder nodes.

Chunk discovery already works: query lists chunks from the vault-ctl FSM via EntriesForVault, which already includes pipeline SealChunk entries. The gap is byte access: chunk.Manager has no metas entry for pipeline chunks and the GLCB lives at ChunkRoot (<homeRoot>/chunks/<id>/data.glcb), not the vault chunk-manager dir, so OpenCursor returns ErrChunkNotFound and search silently skips the chunk.

## Scope
- chunk.Manager: register an externally-built sealed GLCB by absolute path (mirror cloud-backed RegisterCloudChunk); lookupMeta/openLocalGLCBCursor resolve that path
- Orchestrator: register pipeline GLCB into the vault chunk.Manager on seal (extend projectAllSealedFromFSM/onSeal to resolve the vault ChunkRoot)
- Query reads via the existing GLCB cursor: sequential scan + embedded TS index

## Out of scope
- token/KV/glob index sidecar parity (bool filters fall back to sequential scan) -- follow-up
- legacy write-path removal and retention/archival delete-path for pipeline chunks (E2)
- 4+ node acceptance (E3)

## Test dimensions
- Single-node: pipeline ingest -> seal -> query returns records (time + attribute filter)
- Empty-attribute records query correctly
- Multi-node: holder that built the GLCB serves query; node with the FSM entry but no bytes skips gracefully

## Acceptance
- Records ingested through the pipeline are returned by query.Engine.Search on a holder node, end-to-end, with no legacy write path involved
- Bool filters return correct results (sequential); index-sidecar parity explicitly deferred
closed_reason: Pipeline sealed GLCB registered in chunk.Manager; query returns pipeline-built records on holder nodes.

title: Rubicon E2: drain and remove the legacy write pipeline
description:
Second child of Rubicon E (gastrolog-5xn20). Stacked on E1. Migrate all non-ingester writers onto the pipeline and delete the legacy write spine so the pipeline is the sole production write path.

Ingesters already write only through the pipeline. The legacy write spine still serves non-ingester writers and maintains a parallel routing table and parallel rotation cron.

## Scope
- Migrate writers off legacy Append/Ingest/AppendToVault: cluster record-forward (app.go SetRecordAppender), HTTP ImportRecords, export append, retention fireRetentionEvent (route via pipeline routing.Input + retention source), active-chunk follower replication (replaced by segment distribution/collection)
- Remove dual routing (orchestrator RouteSet writes), dual rotation (cronrotation.go + legacy rotationsweep branch), ingest.go (Ingest/ingestLocked/appendLocal), legacy vault_ops.go append/forward, chunk_progress.go, dead ingesterCancels field, unused orchestrator/v3pipeline package
- Retention/archival delete-path for pipeline chunks (delete at ChunkRoot)

## Keep
- chunk reads, retention/archival logic, sealed-chunk replication, index managers, query, chunk metadata FSM

## Acceptance
- No active legacy ingest->chunk write path in orchestrator (grep/reconcile confirms pipeline-only)
- Import/export/forward/retention all write via the pipeline
- Retention/archival correctly see and delete pipeline chunks
closed_reason: Legacy write spine removed; pipeline is sole production ingest path.

title: Rubicon E3: 4+ node cluster acceptance for the pipeline
description:
Third child of Rubicon E (gastrolog-5xn20). Stacked on E2. Prove the full pipeline path on a 4+ node cluster.

## Scope
- 4+ node harness (extend newOrchRelHarness with SegmentPuller + pipeline supervisor + real peer conns, and/or scripts/cluster.sh real-process acceptance): ingest -> sealed GLCB on holder homes -> cross-node query/inspect
- Singleton ingester reassignment and placement/home-set churn survive reconcile without manual repair
- Manual dev validation via cluster.sh + CLI (query/inspect)

## Out of scope
- Closing the parent epic gastrolog-214bz (explicit user sign-off required separately)

## Acceptance
- 4+ node cluster: full pipeline path from ingest through sealed GLCB on holder homes
- Ingester reassignment and vault placement churn recover without manual repair
- Cross-node query returns ingested records
- Do NOT close gastrolog-214bz; gather user sign-off
closed_reason: User validated 4+ node cluster acceptance: pipeline ingest through sealed GLCB, cross-node query, soak at production-like rates.

title: Batch vault-ctl pipeline writes to cut Raft quorum round-trips
description:
## Problem

At high ingest (~4000 rec/s on a 4-node dev cluster), vault-ctl leadership flaps even though Raft uses a **dedicated multiraft ClientConn** separate from PeerConns. Root cause is not TCP head-of-line blocking on segment pulls — it is **too many synchronous vault-ctl Raft applies**, each waiting for quorum (up to `cluster.ReplicationTimeout`).

Every pipeline step is one entry replicated to all followers:

| Step | Command | Where |
|------|---------|-------|
| Distribution | `PublishCompletedSegment` | `pipeline/distribution/vaultctl_publisher.go` |
| Collection | `AckSegmentHolder` (per home) | `orchestrator/pipeline_collection.go` |
| Chunking | `OpenChunkManifest`, **`AddOpenChunkSegmentRef` (one per ref)**, `SealOpenChunkManifest`, `SealChunk` | `pipeline/chunking/leader.go`, `manager.go` |

Chunking is the worst multiplier: `planCatchUp` loops up to 32 times but `planOnce` issues **one** `Applier.Apply` per iteration (`leader.go`). With many segments in `head/` (no `ReleaseSegments` yet), filling one 10k-record chunk can mean **80+ quorum round-trips** for refs alone.

Followers apply entries serially (hashicorp Raft); each apply fires FSM callbacks waking collection/chunking. Shared `raftwal` amplifies fsync load across cluster-ctl + all vault-ctl groups. Leader lease is 500ms — little margin.

## Goal

Reduce vault-ctl write volume and/or amortize replication so pipeline progress does not saturate Raft under realistic cluster ingest.

## Implementation notes (suggested slices)

1. **Batch segment refs** — new vault-ctl command (e.g. `AddOpenChunkSegmentRefs`) carrying multiple refs; planner proposes all refs from one `Plan()` decision in a single apply. Highest impact.
2. **Optional: coalesce holder acks** — debounce `AckSegmentHolder` per segment/home (trade slightly stale holder-set visibility for fewer entries). Harder; evaluate after (1).
3. **Fold chunk metadata announcer steps** where safe — `AnnounceBeginSeal` / `SealChunk` paths may duplicate applies (`vaultctlfsm/announcer.go`, chunking `buildOnce`).
4. **Complements** `gastrolog-hl6cp` `ReleaseSegments` — shrinks registry/refs per chunk but does not fix the one-ref-per-apply pattern.

## Key files

- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/leader.go` — `planOnce`, `planCatchUp`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_ctl_apply.go` — `ApplyVaultControlPlane`
- `backend/internal/cluster/vault_apply_forwarder.go` — synchronous `raft.Apply`
- `backend/internal/vaultraft/vaultctlfsm/` — FSM commands + proto
- `backend/internal/raftgroup/groupmanager.go` — 1s heartbeat / 500ms leader lease

## Stack

`pipeline-v3` / Rubicon program (`gastrolog-214bz`).
acceptance:
- New batched vault-ctl command for multiple open-chunk segment refs; chunking planner uses it instead of one apply per ref
- Proto + buf generate both sides; rename through stack per project rules
- Unit tests: planner emits one batched command for multi-ref plan; FSM applies all refs atomically
- Reliability or orchestrator test: high segment count does not require N sequential quorum waits to fill a manifest (mock or harness assertion on apply count)
- Manual or harness soak: leadership stable (or materially improved) at dev-cluster ingest rates that previously caused vault-ctl leader flapping

title: Include multiraft traffic in per-peer byte metrics and inspector
description:
## Problem

Node inspector **Network** section (`PeerBytesSection`, `NodeStats.peer_bytes`) claims to cover "ALL cluster transport traffic — Raft, broadcast, …" but **multiraft (Raft) bytes are largely invisible**.

Instrumentation today (`gastrolog-47u85`, `backend/internal/cluster/peer_bytes.go`):

- **Outbound tx**: `clientStatsHandler` installed only on **PeerConns** dials (`peer_conns.go`). Multiraft transport dials its own `ClientConn` in `multiraft/transport.go` with **no** stats handler and **no** `x-gastrolog-node-id` interceptor (`cluster.go` `Transport()`).
- **Inbound rx**: server `serverStatsHandler` attributes RPCs only when `x-gastrolog-node-id` is present. Multiraft clients do not stamp that header, so inbound AppendEntries / BatchHeartbeat / pipeline streams are **skipped** (`peer == ""` → no track).

What **is** counted: PeerConns traffic — segment pulls, chunk transfers, search forwarding, broadcast, `ForwardVaultApply`, etc.

Both stacks share the **same cluster gRPC server and port**; the gap is instrumentation, not wiring.

This misled soak analysis: modest inspector tx/rx while vault-ctl Raft replication on the dedicated conn was hot.

## Goal

Per-peer tx/rx in inspector (and `PeerByteMetrics` snapshot in stats broadcast) reflects **all** inter-node cluster-port gRPC bytes, including multiraft.

## Implementation notes

- Install the same `clientStatsHandler` + node-ID interceptors on multiraft dial options (map `raft.ServerAddress` → peer node ID; may need reverse lookup from Raft config or explicit peer ID on dial).
- Ensure inbound multiraft RPCs are attributable: stamp `x-gastrolog-node-id` on multiraft outbound contexts **or** derive peer from mTLS / connection metadata if available (today cluster cert CN is shared — header approach matches PeerConns).
- Update misleading comments: `peer_bytes.go`, `PeerBytesSection.tsx`, `cluster.proto` NodeStats docs.
- Consider separate breakdown labels (raft vs app) in a follow-up; this issue is **correct totals first**.

## Key files

- `backend/internal/cluster/peer_bytes.go`
- `backend/internal/cluster/peer_conns.go`
- `backend/internal/multiraft/transport.go`
- `backend/internal/cluster/cluster.go`
- `backend/internal/cluster/statscollector.go`
- `frontend/src/components/inspector/PeerBytesSection.tsx`
- `backend/api/proto/gastrolog/v1/cluster.proto`
acceptance:
- Multiraft outbound replication and heartbeat bytes increment `PeerByteMetrics` per peer
- Inbound multiraft RPC bytes attributed to the calling peer (same counters as PeerConns traffic)
- Inspector Network table reflects Raft traffic during active vault-ctl replication (visible increase vs today)
- Tests: unit test for stats handler on multiraft dial; end-to-end or integration test mirroring `peer_bytes_test.go` for multiraft path
- Comments/proto docs no longer claim Raft is included unless it actually is

title: Unify multiraft and PeerConns into one outbound dial per peer
description:
## Problem

Cluster inter-node communication uses **two separate outbound gRPC ClientConns per peer pair**:

1. **multiraft.Transport** (`backend/internal/multiraft/transport.go`) — all Raft groups (cluster-ctl + per-vault vault-ctl): AppendEntries, BatchHeartbeat, pipeline streams, snapshots.
2. **PeerConns** (`backend/internal/cluster/peer_conns.go`) — app plane: segment pulls, chunk transfer, search forward, broadcast, ForwardVaultApply, etc.

Both hit the **same cluster gRPC server** on the same port. Early design (single multiplexed connection per node pair) was never completed for the client side: PeerConns consolidated app pools (Mar 2026) but multiraft kept its own transport dialer.

Consequences:

- Duplicate TCP/TLS handshakes and HTTP/2 connections per peer
- Split instrumentation (see traffic-metrics bug — Raft conn untracked until fixed)
- Operational confusion about which conn carries what
- Theoretical extra flow-control competition (less important than vault-ctl write volume, but still wasteful)

## Goal

**One shared outbound ClientConn per peer** used by both multiraft and PeerConns (and any `NewPeerConnsPool` bulk pools if still needed).

## Implementation notes

- PeerConns already owns dial options (TLS, backoff, node-ID interceptors, byte metrics). Expose `Conn(nodeID)` or a lower-level `Dial(peer)` that multiraft `getPeer` uses instead of `grpc.NewClient` with a parallel option set.
- Multiraft `getPeer` today keys by `raft.ServerAddress`; map to node ID via system Raft configuration (same as PeerConns `resolveAddr`).
- Lifecycle: `Disconnect` / `Invalidate` / peer removal must not break the shared conn while the other consumer still needs it — reference counting or single owner with subscribers.
- Do not regress gastrolog-5oofa RPC deadlines or pipeline stream behavior.
- **Independent of** vault-ctl write batching; merge is hygiene + observability, not a substitute for reducing apply count.

## Key files

- `backend/internal/multiraft/transport.go` — `getPeer`, `Disconnect`
- `backend/internal/cluster/peer_conns.go`
- `backend/internal/cluster/cluster.go` — `Transport()`, `SetRaft`, `PeerConns()`
- `docs/ubiquitous_language.md` — cluster transport terms if updated

## Stack

`pipeline-v3` / cluster program.
acceptance:
- Each node pair uses one outbound gRPC ClientConn for both multiraft Raft RPCs and PeerConns app RPCs
- All existing multiraft transport tests pass; PeerConns tests pass
- Multi-node cluster test or reliability harness: Raft replication + segment pull + forward RPC coexist on shared conn without regression
- Peer disconnect / Invalidate / peer removal cleans up safely (no use-after-close for the surviving consumer)
- Document the unified model in code comments (and ubiquitous_language if terms change)

title: Inspect vault segment staging areas (working, completed, pre-head, head)
description:
## Problem

V3 pipeline segment lifecycle spans on-disk **staging areas** per vault home (`docs/fan-out/v3/design-notes.md`, `docs/ubiquitous_language.md`):

| Area | Role |
|------|------|
| `working/` | Active segment being written (segmentation) |
| `completed/` | Closed segment awaiting distribution publish |
| `pre-head/` | Collection receive buffer before verify/promote |
| `head/` | Verified segments available for chunking |

`gastrolog inspect vault` today shows vault config and **chunk** manifest only (`backend/cmd/gastrolog/cli/inspect.go`) — not segment layout. Debugging pipeline stalls (e.g. growing `head/` without `ReleaseSegments`, stranded `completed/`, collection lag) requires manual `find`/`du` on node homes.

During Rubicon E3 soak we observed symmetric `head/` growth (~80+ files) while `completed/` and `pre-head/` stayed empty — hard to see without SSH/filesystem inspection.

## Goal

First-class **inspect** surface for per-vault segment staging on any cluster node (cluster-first: works regardless of which node the user is connected to).

## Scope (suggested)

**CLI** (minimum):

```
gastrolog inspect vault <name> --segments
# or subcommand: gastrolog inspect vault segments <name>
```

Per home node that holds the vault (or local node only with `--local`):

- Count + total bytes per area (`working`, `completed`, `pre-head`, `head`)
- Optional: list segment IDs (cap/limit for large dirs)
- Cross-reference vault-ctl registry: published vs held vs pending collection (segment IDs in FSM `ListCompletedSegments` vs on-disk layout)

**API** (if needed for UI later): extend inspect/system RPC with segment layout summary; keep facts server-side (no client heuristics).

## Implementation notes

- Reuse layout helpers: `pipeline/collection/discover.go` (`vaultSegmentLayout`), `pipeline/paths/`
- Orchestrator knows vault roots per node (`orchestrator/pipeline.go` SegmentsDir wiring)
- Cluster-first: for remote homes, forward RPC to peers that hold the vault (same pattern as other cross-node inspect) OR aggregate in system handler from broadcasted peer state — follow existing cluster inspect patterns
- Do not conflate with chunk GLCB inspect; this is **segment staging** only

## Related

- `gastrolog-hl6cp` — `ReleaseSegments` will shrink `head/` after seal; this issue helps verify that behavior landed
- Ubiquitous language: use canonical terms (leader not primary, cloud-backed chunk, etc.)

## Stack

`pipeline-v3` / Rubicon.
acceptance:
- CLI command reports per-area segment counts and byte totals for a vault on the targeted node(s)
- JSON output mode for scripting
- Works on a multi-node dev cluster from any node (cluster-first) or documents `--local` limitation if first slice is local-only
- Tests: unit test for layout aggregation; integration test with temp vault dirs covering working/completed/pre-head/head
- Help text describes what each area means and when it should be non-empty

title: Fix routing panic when vault re-registers during live ingest
description:
## Problem

Cluster restart with scatterbox running panics node1/node2:

```
panic: send on closed channel
routing.deliver (manager.go:292)
```

`route()` snapshots segmentation channel pointers under `RLock`, then delivers after `RUnlock`. Pipeline reconcile `UnregisterVault` removes the vault and closes the segmentation input channel concurrently → routing worker sends on a closed channel.

Observed at 2026-06-13 19:09:15 on `/Volumes/Storage/Gastrolog` after `vault placement added`. Node1/node2 exit; node3/node4 cannot reach raft quorum (2/4 voters) and spin in eternal elections.

## Fix

Track per-vault delivery sinks with in-flight wait on unregister so no worker can still be sending when the segmentation channel is closed.

## Acceptance

- Unit test reproduces unregister/close during active routing without panic
- `go test ./internal/pipeline/routing/...` passes
closed_reason: Per-vault routing sinks drain in-flight deliveries before segmentation closes input; unregister order already routes before seg.

title: Chunk planner loadSegmentViews re-opens every active registry segment per planOnce
description:
## Problem

The vault-ctl leader planner calls `loadSegmentViews()` on **every** `planOnce` step. That walks the full completed-segment registry (~4k on a live 4-node scatterbox soak) and calls `BuildOrderedIndex` (open segment file + attach on-disk EventID index) for **each non-exhausted segment**, then closes all handles in `defer closeViews()`.

Nothing is cached between steps. At ~32ms per segment open (measured on `/Volumes/Storage/Gastrolog` cluster, Jun 2026), ~3.7k active segments ⇒ **~2 minutes of file opens per planner step**, while each successful step adds only **one** `AddOpenChunkSegmentRef` Raft command.

## Symptom (live cluster, first-vault)

- Ingest queue pegged 1000/1000 on all nodes; durable ~800–900 rec/s vs 4k/s configured scatterbox.
- vault-ctl snapshot: ~4k completed segments, open manifest **2 refs / 3375 records**, **~11.3M records** as registry orphans (`ExtraRefs` in `BuildPipelineQueryInput`).
- `--explain` virtual pipeline-open-chunk `records=` matches orphan backlog (~10.6M+).
- Inspector: 0 FSM chunks listed but thousands of files in `head/`; GLCB count >> `fsm.List()` sealed entries.

## Code

- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/leader.go` — `loadSegmentViews`, `planOnce`, `planCatchUp` (cap 32)
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/index.go` — `BuildOrderedIndex`
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/planner.go` — `Plan` / `pickSegment` only need one segment's index per step
- Partial mitigation already shipped: `segmentExhaustedForPlanning` (commit 45744abe) skips fully consumed segments; comment documents O(n²) but active orphans still indexed every step.

## Fix direction (not prescriptive)

- Cache `OrderedIndex` per segment ID (invalidate on `ReleaseSegments`), **and/or**
- Two-phase pick: choose next segment from FSM metadata, open/index **only that segment** for slicing.
- Consider raising/removing `planCatchUp` 32-iteration cap after perf fix.

## Acceptance

- With sustained scatterbox ingest on 4-node cluster, open manifest refs grow toward rotation policy (10k records) without multi-million orphan backlog.
- Planner step time does **not** scale linearly with total registry size when only one ref is added.
- Unit/integration test fails on old behavior: N segments ⇒ O(N) index opens per `planOnce` (or bounded constant).
acceptance:
- [ ] `planOnce` no longer opens indexes for all active registry segments each step
- [ ] 4-node soak: orphan registry records stay bounded (manifest keeps pace with ingest)
- [ ] Regression test guards per-step index open count

title: Soak test: chunk planner keeps manifest fill pace under sustained ingest
description:
## Why

Acceptance tests (`gastrolog-18f9r`) use small record counts and few segments. The planner O(registry) re-indexing bug survived because CI never held thousands of **active** completed-segment registry entries while ingest continued.

## Scope

Add a reliability/soak test (or extend `reliability_pipeline_test.go`) that:

1. Runs 4+ in-process nodes with real pipeline path and scatterbox-like steady ingest.
2. Asserts completed-segment registry size and/or orphan record count stay bounded relative to rotation policy + segment close policy — not millions behind manifest.
3. Asserts sealed GLCB / FSM chunk count advances over wall time (not stuck at 1 sealed chunk with 100+ GLCB dirs on disk).

## Context

Live cluster Jun 2026: ~4k registry segments, 2 manifest refs, ~11M orphan records, ingest queues pegged. Root cause tracked separately (planner `loadSegmentViews`); this issue ensures we cannot regress.

## Files

- `backend/internal/orchestrator/reliability_pipeline_test.go`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/reliability_orch_harness_test.go`
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/leader_test.go`
acceptance:
- [ ] Test fails on pre-fix planner (or documents baseline) and passes after fix
- [ ] Runs in CI without multi-hour runtime (may use accelerated segment close / smaller cluster duration with scaled thresholds)

title: ReleaseSegments leaves segment files in head/ (purge gap)
description:
## Problem

After chunk seal, segment files should leave the hot `head/` staging area. Live first-vault cluster (Jun 2026) shows **~9.6k–13k files in `head/`** per node while vault-ctl completed-segment registry holds **~4k** entries — roughly 2–3× disk debris.

`proposeSealChunk` calls `paths.PurgeHeadStaging` for releasable segment IDs after `CmdSealChunk`, and `releaseOnce` proposes `ReleaseSegments` when all required homes have holder receipts. Something in this chain is incomplete: files remain and planner/query still traverse them via `VaultSegmentLocator` (head then completed).

## Code

- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/manager.go` — `proposeSealChunk`, `releaseOnce`, `pendingRelease`
- `backend/internal/pipeline/paths/purge.go` — `PurgeHeadStaging`
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/release.go` — `releasableSegmentIDs`, holder gating

## Live evidence

`/Volumes/Storage/Gastrolog/node{1..4}/segments/<first-vault>/head` file counts vs FSM registry ~4k.

## Acceptance

- After steady ingest + successful seal/release cycle, `head/` count tracks active registry (not unbounded multiple).
- Test: seal chunk with holder receipts ⇒ segment files removed from head on all homes (or documented intentional retention with bounded policy).
acceptance:
- [ ] Identified which path leaves head/ files behind
- [ ] Fix + test for purge after ReleaseSegments / seal
- [ ] No unbounded head/ growth in pipeline soak test

title: Completed-segment registry zombies (no holders, no on-disk file)
description:
## Problem

vault-ctl FSM `completed_segments` registry can retain entries that have **empty `Holders`** and **no segment file on any home** (`head/`, `completed/`, `pre-head/`). Live first-vault snapshot (Jun 2026): **18** such segments among ~4k; example IDs include `06fc67nvfhu9t7k0e55p5vhio0` (origin node-1, 2173 records) — absent on all four nodes' disks.

These entries still participate in `ListCompletedSegments` iteration in `loadSegmentViews` (skipped at index open if path missing, but still scanned). They may block `ReleaseSegments` holder gating and confuse collection pull source resolution.

## Code

- `backend/internal/vaultraft/vaultctlfsm/segments.go` — publish, ack holder, release
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/pipeline_collection.go` — `segmentLogReader.Roll`, `segmentPullSources`
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/leader.go` — registry walk

## Acceptance

- Registry does not accumulate immaterial segments with no file and no holders (reap on release, or reject stale acks, or periodic reconcile).
- Test reproduces publish → release → file gone ⇒ registry entry removed.
acceptance:
- [ ] Root cause for zombies identified (release without purge, failed collection, etc.)
- [ ] Reaper or stricter lifecycle prevents unbounded zombies
- [ ] Unit test for registry entry removal when segment material is gone

title: Pipeline GLCB files on disk without FSM sealed chunk entries
description:
## Problem

Homes build `data.glcb` under `segments/<vault>/chunks/<chunkID>/` at seal, but FSM `List()` sealed manifest entries can lag far behind on-disk artifacts. Live cluster Jun 2026 first-vault: **node1 ~112 GLCB files**, **fsm.List() ~1** sealed chunk in vault-ctl snapshot; inspector shows **0 chunks** for vault.

Records remain queryable via virtual pipeline-open-chunk (orphan segments), masking the gap. Users expect sealed GLCBs to become normal FSM-backed queryable chunks.

## Code

- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/manager.go` — `commitDoneBuild`, `proposeSealChunk`, `OnBuilt`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/pipeline.go` — `registerBuiltPipelineChunk`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go` — onSeal, pipeline GLCB registration
- `backend/internal/chunk/file/manager.go` — pipeline GLCB registration path

## Related log noise

`cluster.log` has historical `replication: sealed chunk failed` on first-vault (legacy replication vs pipeline path).

## Acceptance

- After build+seal, every home GLCB has matching FSM sealed entry cluster-wide (eventual consistency bounded).
- Inspector/`list chunks` reflects pipeline-sealed chunks.
- Test: seal in harness ⇒ FSM entry + GLCB on all homes + queryable as sealed chunk meta.
acceptance:
- [ ] Diagnose why GLCB count >> FSM sealed count on live cluster
- [ ] Fix seal registration / reconciler gap
- [ ] Multi-node test asserts FSM and on-disk GLCB stay aligned
closed_reason: Follower homes now propose CmdSealChunk via Applier forwarder; GLCB count matches FSM sealed entries on live cluster (manual validation).

title: Wire supervisor queue depths as pressure gate probes
description:
## Problem

`lifecycle.go` creates a `PressureGate` for `PressureAware` ingesters, but **`AddProbe` is never called** with supervisor queue depths (TODO references gastrolog-jiwlf id in comment but that issue is the closed Rubicon B slice). Gate stays `normal` forever; scatterbox `pressureGate.Wait()` is a no-op.

**This does NOT fix chunking throughput** — ingest is already throttled by blocking `out <- msg` on the bounded 1000-slot digestion queue. Wiring probes is still needed for:

- Alerts (`ingest-pressure` collector path exists)
- Cooperative throttle **before** hard channel block (optional UX)

## Code

- `backend/internal/orchestrator/lifecycle.go` — TODO ~line 49
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/pipeline/supervisor.go` — `IngestQueueDepth`, `IngestQueueCapacity`
- `backend/internal/chanwatch/pressure.go`

## Acceptance

- Gate probes include ingestion→digestion queue depth (and optionally downstream queues).
- When queue > elevated threshold, gate transitions; scatterbox/test ingester observes `Wait()` blocking.
- Test in `pressure_test.go` or pipeline integration test.
acceptance:
- [ ] Probes wired at orchestrator Start
- [ ] Pressure transitions fire under artificial queue fill
- [ ] Document that primary backpressure remains bounded channel blocking

title: Query --explain misreports pipeline-open-chunk record count
description:
## Problem

`gastrolog query --explain` shows `records=` on `mode=pipeline-open-chunk` chunks using `PipelineQueryRecordCount`: manifest `TotalRecords` + **all** orphan `ExtraRefs` + working segment records. That is **lifetime backlog**, not records matching the query time window.

Live example (Jun 2026): `last=1m` explain still showed **~10.7M records** on the virtual chunk while `last=1m --count` returned ~40k.

## Code

- `backend/internal/query/plan.go` — `ChunkPlan.RecordCount` from meta
- `backend/internal/query/pipeline_open_chunk.go` — `appendPipelineOpenChunkMetas`, `PipelineQueryRecordCount`

title: Query search and histogram: virtual pipeline open chunk coverage and perf
description:
## Problem

During scatterbox soak investigation (Jun 2026), live queries with `last=5m` were slow or appeared empty because:

1. Virtual pipeline-open-chunk records were excluded or poorly handled in GLCB histogram paths.
2. Full frame scans of all pipeline records for histogram `level` grouping were prohibitively slow at multi-million orphan backlogs.
3. Limited reverse-tail path needed for `reverse=true` + `limit` searches on open chunk.

Uncommitted work exists on branch `pipeline-v3` in:

- `backend/internal/query/pipeline_open_chunk.go`
- `backend/internal/query/histogram.go`
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/ingest_window.go`, `ingest_ts_merge.go`, `query_filter.go`

## Distinction

This is the **read path**. Throughput collapse is primarily **write path** (chunk planner); fixing query does not fix ingest queue pegging.

## Acceptance

- `last=5m` search returns scatterbox records while ingest active (including pipeline staging chunk).
- Histogram renders in reasonable time with millions of unstaged records (index-only ingest_ts path for counts).
- Tests: `TestPipelineOpenChunkSearchLast5m`, `TestPipelineOpenChunkHistogram`, ingest_ts merge tests.
- No full-frame scan of entire orphan backlog for default histogram.
acceptance:
- [ ] Search includes pipeline open chunk with time filter
- [ ] Histogram completes under soak-scale record count (test with synthetic orphans)
- [ ] Reverse tail fast path covered by test

title: Defer vault-ctl after-restore hook off FSM restore path
description:
## Problem

On cluster restart, node3 can wedge during vault-ctl snapshot restore for the second vault. Logs show `snapshot restore progress` at 100% every 10s forever, but never `restored from snapshot`, `vault-ctl after-restore reconcile complete`, or `orchestrator started`.

This is not slow snapshot I/O — second-vault snapshots are ~22 bytes and complete in <1ms when healthy. The gap between vault restores on node3 (3–9s) is chunk-manager `loadExisting()` scanning local GLCB dirs, not Raft snapshot read time.

## Root cause

`raftgroup.GroupManager.CreateGroup` holds `groupMgr.mu` (write lock) for the entire `hraft.NewRaft` call, which synchronously runs `fsm.Restore` → `vaultraft.FSM.onAfterRestore` → `orchestrator.afterVaultCtlRestore`.

That hook calls `rewireVaultInstanceAfterCtlRestore` → `groupMgr.GetGroup()` (read lock) while `CreateGroup` still holds the write lock — classic `sync.RWMutex` self-deadlock when a vault instance exists during restore (e.g. dispatcher `AddVault` racing `applyVaults`).

Even when `has_instance=false`, synchronous hook work during restore widens the startup race window (node3 spuriously winning vault-ctl elections while still in `ApplyConfig`).

## Fix

1. Make `afterVaultCtlRestore` schedule work on a goroutine and return immediately (same pattern as pending-delete ack deferral in `VaultLifecycleReconciler.ReconcileFromSnapshot`).
2. Coalesce per-vault: at most one pending after-restore pass per vault.
3. Extend `reconcileVaultInstanceFromSnapshot` (startup path in `reconcileVaultChunksAfterStartup`) to call `rewireVaultInstanceAfterCtlRestore` before `ReconcileFromSnapshot`, since cold-start hook fires before instances exist.

## Key files

- `backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_ops.go` — `afterVaultCtlRestore`, `reconcileVaultInstanceFromSnapshot`
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/reconfig_vaults.go` — `rewireVaultInstanceAfterCtlRestore`
- `backend/internal/raftgroup/groupmanager.go` — `CreateGroup` holds lock across `NewRaft`
- `backend/internal/vaultraft/fsm.go` — `Restore` fires hook synchronously

## Observed on soak cluster

`/Volumes/Storage/Gastrolog/node{1..4}`, vault `second-vault` (`06fcegb205vgf583rtliaoejr4`), 2026-06-14 21:09:30 — node3 stuck; peers completed in milliseconds.

## Acceptance

- Unit test: `CreateGroup` + restore with registered vault instance does not deadlock.
- Startup reconcile rewires reconciler to post-restore sub-FSM.
- Cluster restart harness: all nodes reach `orchestrator started`; no infinite 100% restore progress without `restored from snapshot`.
acceptance: afterVaultCtlRestore returns immediately; rewire + reconcile run async; startup reconcile rewires before ReconcileFromSnapshot; unit deadlock regression test passes

title: Pipeline segment registry: blocking FSM reconcile on vault register
Multi-chunk search primes one iterator per chunk; reorderByTSWithBounds buffers full chunk in RAM
description:
## Problem

On a 4-node pipeline soak with ~1,300 FSM sealed chunks (10k records each), a single search/histogram on a node that serves the query can drive **multi-GB RSS** and hundreds of suspended iterator coroutines.

Observed on node4 (Jun 2026, `/Volumes/Storage/Gastrolog`):

- **~6 GB RSS** vs **~150 MB** on peer nodes
- pprof heap **inuse ~1–2 GB**, cumulative alloc **~800 GB** since process start
- **~490** `iter.Pull2` coroutines in `searchChunkWithRef.func1-range1` per active multi-chunk search
- Top live allocators:
  - `query.reorderByTSWithBounds` (~650 MB) — buffers **all** records from a chunk before yielding the first
  - `chunk.DecodeWithDict` / `cloud.Reader.ReadRecord` (~1 GB cum) — GLCB decode for pipeline chunks

## Root cause

`primeHeapWithResume` / `primeHeap` call `openAndPrimeScanner` for **every** overlapping chunk before the merge loop starts (`search.go`). Each call does `iter.Pull2(searchChunkWithRef(...))`, spawning a coroutine per chunk.

For sealed pipeline GLCB chunks without an embedded TS index, `buildTSOrderedScanner` falls back to `reorderByTSWithBounds`, which **loads the entire chunk into a `[]recordWithRef` buffer** before returning the first record (`scanner.go`). With ~500 successfully opened chunks × 10k records, that is hundreds of MB to GB per search, held until the scanner is advanced to exhaustion or `mergeState.cleanup()` runs.

This is orthogonal to the planner index-cache fix (gastrolog-3bn3q): query dominates node4 heap, not chunking.

## Triggers

- Multi-chunk queries (typical `last=…` / scatterbox over full retention)
- Cluster fan-out: node4 stacks show `forwardSearchStreamHandler` → `Search.func1` → `primeHeapWithResume` even when the UI hits another node
- Concurrent searches (search + pagination + remote forward) multiply buffers

## Fix direction (not prescriptive)

1. **Lazy chunk open**: only `Pull2` a chunk when it enters the merge heap (or a bounded window of top candidates), not all ~N at prime time.
2. **Streaming TS reorder**: replace full-chunk buffer in `reorderByTSWithBounds` with bounded merge / external sort, or require embedded ITSI in pipeline GLCBs.
3. **Cap in-flight chunk scanners** per query; cancel and `stop()` iterators promptly on client disconnect (verify ForwardSearch ctx propagation).
4. **Metrics**: in-flight scanners, reorder buffer bytes, skipped FSM-without-cm chunks (gastrolog-3ukgz) — aggregate, don’t log per chunk.

## Non-fix

- Silently skipping `ErrChunkNotFound` without fixing registration (rejected in gastrolog-3ukgz).
- Relying only on `registerPipelineGLCB` startup sweep — helps consistency but does not fix O(chunks) buffers per search.

## Related

- gastrolog-3ukgz (FSM vs local cm skip — WARN spam, not primary memory)
- gastrolog-2kysn (pipeline GLCB registration — many GLCBs on disk but not in cm)
- gastrolog-wwbh0 (pipeline-open-chunk query coverage; separate from heap merge path)
acceptance:
- [ ] Single search over 1k+ sealed 10k-record chunks on one node stays below a defined RSS budget (e.g. <500 MB heap inuse for one concurrent search)
- [ ] pprof shows no O(chunks) live memory in reorderByTSWithBounds per query
- [ ] Iterator coroutines per search bounded (not ~1 per chunk at prime time)
- [ ] Cluster fan-out ForwardSearch on a peer does not balloon that peer to multi-GB RSS for the same query window
- [ ] Regression test or benchmark guards chunk count vs heap growth

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
## Investigation note (Jun 2026): filtered histogram amplifier

**Covered here** — no separate issue needed.

`forwardSearchAfterParse` (`executors.go`) runs `ComputeHistogram` then `eng.Search` on every `ForwardSearch` RPC. For **unfiltered** queries (`last=5m`, no `BoolExpr`), histogram uses the fast binary-search path in `runTimechartStrategy` and does **not** call `primeHeapWithResume`.

For **filtered** queries (`BoolExpr != nil`), histogram falls back to `timechartScanPath` → `Search()` → `primeHeapWithResume` (`histogram.go` ~L112–120, ~L608). That is the same eager per-chunk priming + `reorderByTSWithBounds` full-chunk buffers as the record stream. The two passes run **sequentially** per RPC (histogram finishes and `mergeState.cleanup()` runs before the record `Search` opens), but a filtered forward search still pays **two** full prime cycles back-to-back — a likely peak-RSS amplifier on scatterbox nodes.

pprof on node4 during active forward search showed this stack:
`forwardSearchStreamHandler` → `ComputeHistogram` → `timechartScanDirect` → `Search.func1` → `primeHeapWithResume`.

**Not** gastrolog-wwbh0 — that issue is pipeline **open-chunk** histogram coverage and orphan-backlog scan avoidance, not sealed multi-chunk heap merge / double prime on filtered histogram.

title: Record search routes to vault leader instead of distributing across replica holders
description:
## Problem

Record search always executes on the **vault placement leader**, even when RF>1 nodes hold complete sealed replicas.

Observed during scatterbox soak (Jun 2026): UI on node1, vault leader node4, GLCB copies on all nodes. Every `Search` on node1:

1. `LeaderVaultQueryEngine` skips follower instances (`!IsFollower` in `leaderVaultRegistry`).
2. `collectRemote` → `remoteVaultsByNode` sends `ForwardSearch` only to `system.LeaderNodeID` (`query_remote.go`).
3. Node4 scans ~1,300 chunks; peers idle.

This concentrates CPU/heap on the leader and streams records leader → coordinator → client. Contradicts cluster-first / no-query-primary design.

## Regression

V2 fan-out read design (`docs/fan-out/obsoleted/fan-out-data-plane-design.md`): sealed chunks readable from any `Holding` node; active chunk fan-out + dedup.

V3 landed placement-leader shortcuts flagged as transitional in `docs/fan-out/v2/placement-leader-migration.md`. They became de facto behavior.

## Fix direction: distribute sealed-chunk search across replica holders

V3 pipeline + pull replication makes sealed GLCB replicas on holder nodes **trustworthy enough to search in parallel**. The fix is **not** “coordinator reads its own local replica instead of RPCing the leader” — that only optimizes one node’s hop and still leaves all scan work on a single machine when the UI happens to be on the leader. **Distribute** work.

1. Coordinator resolves chunk set from **local FSM** (every node has `manifest.Reader`).
2. **Partition sealed chunks** across nodes with complete, queryable replicas (hash/mod-N, time bands from chunk bounds, etc.).
3. Parallel search per holder — scoped `ForwardSearch` or local engine with **chunk subset** filter.
4. **k-way merge** at coordinator (`mergeAndStream` / `kWayMerge` — same machinery as multi-vault fan-out today).
5. **Active / pipeline-open chunk** on vault leader only (or Receiving fan-out + dedup) — not sharded.

### Replica completeness gates

Include a holder in the partition only when its replica is complete (GLCB in cm, record count matches FSM, holder ack from V3 segment registry, etc.). Skip 3ukgz nodes (FSM chunk, local cm missing).

### Resume tokens

Encode per-holder chunk subsets, or fall back to time highwater when partition assignment changes.

## Non-fix

- **Coordinator-local read** as the primary strategy — different direction; does not spread load across RF.
- Leader-only reads for sealed chunks.

## Related

- gastrolog-2o9e9 — per-node memory (lazy-prime) still matters on whichever nodes search.
- gastrolog-wwbh0 — pipeline open-chunk coverage (orthogonal).
- gastrolog-67a41 — benchmark fan-out cost (blocked).
acceptance:
- [ ] Sealed-chunk search partitioned across RF holder nodes; coordinator merges streams
- [ ] Vault leader pprof shows no full-chunk-set scan when UI is on a non-leader node
- [ ] Load spreads roughly across holders (not concentrated on placement leader)
- [ ] Active / pipeline-open chunk still correct (leader or fan-out + dedup)
- [ ] Multi-node test: RF>1 cluster, query from any node, results match single-node reference
- [ ] Resume tokens and pagination survive partition assignment

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text:
## Target architecture: distribute sealed-chunk search across replica holders

Local-read on the coordinator (described above) is the minimal fix. The **end state** V3 replication unlocks is better:

**Partition sealed-chunk search across every replica node that holds a complete copy**, merge at the coordinator — same pattern as multi-vault fan-out today, but per-vault across homes instead of funneling everything through the placement leader.

### Why this is viable now

V3 pipeline + pull replication gives much higher confidence that sealed GLCB replicas on holder nodes are **complete** (same FSM `ManifestEntry` on every node; segment/chunk materialization at homes). Pre-V3 / early fan-out had to treat followers as potentially lagging or divergent — hence leader-only reads as a safe shortcut. That shortcut should not survive once replicas are trustworthy.

### Sketch

1. Coordinator resolves vault chunk set from **local FSM** (`manifest.Reader` — already on every node).
2. Split **sealed** chunks across holder nodes with local queryable GLCB (hash/mod-N, or time-range bands from chunk bounds).
3. Open parallel `ForwardSearch` (or local `LocalVaultQueryEngine`) per holder with a **chunk subset** scope — `chunk_id` filter / explain-style plan slice.
4. **k-way merge** at coordinator (existing `mergeAndStream` / `kWayMerge` infrastructure).
5. **Active / pipeline-open chunk** stays on vault leader (or Receiving fan-out + dedup per V2 design) — not sharded.

### Benefits vs leader-only or coordinator-local-only

- Spreads CPU + heap (`primeHeapWithResume`, `reorderByTSWithBounds`) across N nodes linearly in RF.
- No single-node query hot spot when UI connects anywhere.
- Uses replicas for what replication built them for.

### Preconditions / gates

- Replica completeness signal before including a node in the partition (local GLCB registered in cm, record count matches FSM, or explicit holder ack from V3 segment registry).
- Skip nodes in 3ukgz state (FSM chunk, local cm missing) — don't assign partition work there.
- Resume tokens must encode per-node chunk subsets or fall back to time highwater when partition assignment changes.

### Phasing

1. **Phase A:** coordinator local read when replica complete (no RPC) — fixes the obvious regression.
2. **Phase B:** partition sealed chunks across all complete holders — this comment.

Related symptom issue: gastrolog-2o9e9 (per-node memory still needs lazy-prime regardless of which node searches).

comments.author: kluzz@radical.org
comments.text: Correction: coordinator-local read is **not** a step toward this fix — it's a different direction (optimizes RPC hop, doesn't distribute scan work). Comment 2qj7m-c1 phasing A/B was wrong; issue description updated accordingly.

title: Full backend architecture audit (8 criteria)
description:
Systematic audit of the entire `backend/` tree (all `internal/*` packages, `cmd/*`, `api/proto`, `api/gen`, justfile) against eight criteria:

1. Indexes used where possible
2. No unnecessary heap loading
3. Cluster-first
4. Correctness
5. Performance
6. No compensating workarounds (understand flows; invariant ledger)
7. No leaky abstractions
8. Separation of responsibilities / coherent patterns

**Execution:** audit-only — findings filed as child issues; remediation is separate epics.

**Tracking:** `docs/audits/` (coverage matrix, invariant ledger, per-phase memos).

**Phases:** Storage → Ingestion → Query → Cluster → Orchestration → Replication → Transport → Observability → Shared libs → API+cmd → system/config → Cross-cut → Synthesis.

**Out of scope:** repo-root frontend, deploy, scripts, e2e, CI implementation.

title: Audit: completed channel drop forces distribution rescanInterval (2s)
description:
**Audit ID:** sweep-001 / audit-ingestion-001, audit-ingestion-002  
**Criterion:** 6 (compensating workaround), 8 (pattern coherence)  
**Severity:** P1

## Violation

`pipeline/segmentation/writer.go` `closeSegmentLocked` uses a **non-blocking** send on the `completed` channel. Under burst load the notification can be dropped.

`pipeline/distribution/manager.go` runs `rescanInterval` (2s) to scan `completed/` on disk and republish stranded segments — compensating for the dropped event.

## Root cause chain

Segment closed + fsync → completed/ durable on disk → **channel notify may drop** → registry publish delayed up to 2s per vault worker → extra disk walks under steady ingest.

## Correct fix (remediation epic, not this issue)

Reliable handoff: blocking send with backpressure, durable outbox, or FSM-driven publish trigger that cannot be lost. **Remove or narrow `rescanInterval`** once upstream is reliable.

## Ref

`docs/audits/sweep-catalog.md`, `docs/audits/findings/02-ingestion.md`

title: Audit: collection recollectInterval (2s) compensates for missed collect wakes
description:
**Audit ID:** sweep-002 / audit-ingestion-003  
**Criterion:** 6, 8  
**Severity:** P2

## Violation

`pipeline/collection/manager.go` `recollectInterval` (2s) periodically retries collect when FSM publish-driven wake is insufficient (transient pull failure, quiet vault, missed callback).

## Root cause

Collect should be fully event-driven from vault-ctl publish / assignment log. Periodic recollect papers over wake gaps.

## Correct fix

Ensure every path that assigns a segment to a home emits a collect wake; surface pull errors. Narrow or remove ticker.

**Ref:** `docs/audits/sweep-catalog.md`

title: Audit: chunking replanInterval (2s) compensates for incomplete event graph
description:
**Audit ID:** sweep-003 / audit-ingestion-004  
**Criterion:** 6, 8  
**Severity:** P1

## Violation

`pipeline/chunking/manager.go` `replanInterval` (2s) runs plan/build catch-up on every home worker because FSM callbacks + wakes do not fully drive chunking (e.g. segment pull has no vault-ctl Raft event, `pendingSeal` retained after seal clears manifest).

Related: `sealRetryInterval` (15s) rate-limits `CmdSealChunk` retries after forward/apply failures (sweep-004).

## Root cause

Event graph incomplete → timing/state patches (`pendingSeal`, `doneSealProposed`, `releaseWake` split) compensate.

## Correct fix

Complete event-driven graph; remove replan tick except explicit watchdog with alert.

**Ref:** `docs/audits/sweep-catalog.md`, `docs/audits/findings/02-ingestion.md`

title: Audit: vault-ctl ForwardVaultApply lacks read-after-write barrier (extends 2nxij)
description:
## Finding
audit-cluster-001 (Phase 4 cluster audit, gastrolog-2p313)

## Problem
System config mutations use `ForwardApply` + `applied_index` + follower `waitForLocalApply` (gastrolog-2nxij — fixed for cluster-ctl Raft). Vault-ctl chunk/config apply paths (`ForwardVaultApply`, `vault_apply_forwarder.go`, `vault_ctl_chunk_apply_forwarder.go`) return on RPC success **without** waiting for the follower's local FSM to catch up. `ForwardVaultApplyResponse` has no applied index.

## Impact (P0)
Follower can read stale vault-ctl FSM state immediately after a forwarded mutation — cluster-first correctness violation; races with query/ingest paths that assume post-apply visibility.

## Correct pattern
Mirror system path: leader returns applied index; follower polls `AppliedIndex` (or FSM notify) before returning from forward.

## Acceptance
- Vault-ctl forward paths return applied index and block until local FSM ≥ that index (same contract as system `ForwardApply`)
- Regression test: follower read after forwarded vault-ctl mutation sees new state
- Remove or narrow any compensating polls that only exist because of this gap

## References
- docs/audits/findings/06-cluster.md
- docs/audits/findings/13-synthesis.md (Epic B)

title: CLI add-storage: NodeId decode mismatch prevents merging existing storages
description:
## Finding
audit-cmd-002 (Phase 10 API+cmd audit, gastrolog-2p313)

`cli/node.go` `add-storage` compares `glid.FromBytes(nsc.NodeId).String() == nodeID` but `list-storage` uses `string(nsc.NodeId)`. Node IDs in proto are UTF-8 GLID strings (`[]byte(cfg.NodeID)`), so add-storage fails to find/merge existing node storage configs.

## Acceptance

title: StorageIDForNode silent class fallback places leaders on wrong disk class
description:
## Finding

## Problem
`system/storage.go` `StorageIDForNode` (L278–281): when no `FileStorage` matches `requiredClass`, returns `FileStorages[0]` silently. `app/placement.go` `eligibleStorages` / `storageEligible` require exact class match for followers — inconsistent policy. Leader reassignment via `replaceLeaderPlacement` can use the fallback path.

title: Audit: vaultCatchupSweepAll (20s) runs six reconciler compensators
description:

title: Audit: cloud backfillCloudUploads (5s) compensates missed upload announce

title: Inspector: replication backpressure telemetry (vault + node)
description:
## Why

The catchup-storm investigation (gastrolog-2o9e9) showed that replica backlog, sweep catchup, stale-fsm ghost deletes, and pipeline chunking segment lag are invisible in the product UI. Operators only see WARN log spam (`missing_total`, `chunking build failed`, `ImportBegin preempting`) with no trend or per-node/per-vault signal.

Batch-16 catchup throttling is a band-aid on the existing 20s `vaultCatchupSweepAll` compensator (gastrolog-8gmd0). Until event-driven reconciliation lands, we need **observability** so operators can tell healthy convergence from a returning storm without parsing logs.

## What to expose

Add replication/pipeline backpressure stats to the existing **5s NodeStats gossip** (`VaultStats` in `backend/api/proto/gastrolog/v1/vault.proto`), collected in orchestrator at the same points that currently log:

| Signal | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `missing_replica_count` | FSM sealed entries missing on local disk (today's `missing_total`) |
| `catchup_in_flight` | Active async catchup push batch (`catchupPushInFlight`) |
| `catchup_transferred_total` | Counter — successful sweep-path chunk pushes |
| `catchup_no_eligible_total` | Counter — batch requested, no peer had bytes |
| `catchup_failed_total` | Counter — push failed / preempt / ack reject |
| `replication_preempt_total` | Counter — `ImportBegin` preempt on cluster handler |
| `stale_fsm_deletes_total` | Counter — ghost chunks retired by leader sweep |
| `chunking_missing_segments` | Current count of manifest segments absent from `head/` (homes) |

Derived in UI: backlog trend (delta of `missing_replica_count`), catchup yield.

## Where in the inspector

**Vault inspector (`VaultCard`)** — primary. New **Replication** section in expanded card (above chunk table), same visual language as `ChunkReplicaBadges`. Shows this node's view of that vault's backpressure.

**Node inspector (`NodeDetailPane`)** — rollup. Aggregate across vaults on the node (total missing, any catchup in flight). Natural home: **Network** section beside `PeerBytesSection`, or slim **Replication** block under System.

Data path: `VaultStats` → `NodeStats.vaults[]` → pass matching entry into `VaultCard` via `nodeInfo.stats` in `NodeDetailPane`. No new RPC — gossip only.

## Proto sketch

```protobuf
message VaultReplicationStats {
  int64 missing_replica_count = 1;
  uint32 catchup_in_flight = 2;
  uint64 catchup_transferred_total = 3;
  uint64 catchup_no_eligible_total = 4;
  uint64 catchup_failed_total = 5;
  uint64 replication_preempt_total = 6;
  uint64 stale_fsm_deletes_total = 7;
  uint32 chunking_missing_segments = 8;
}
// VaultStats.replication = next tag (renumber per proto cleanup rules)
```

## Backend touchpoints

- `backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go` — `SweepMissingReplicas`, stale-fsm sweep
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/replication_catchup.go` — catchup scheduling/completion
- `backend/internal/cluster/chunk_replication_handler.go` — preempt
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/manager.go` — missing-segment build failures
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go` — `VaultSnapshots()` / stats adapter
- `backend/internal/cluster/statscollector.go` — broadcast path

## Frontend touchpoints

- `frontend/src/components/inspector/VaultCard.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/inspector/NodeDetailPane.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/inspector/SystemStatsView.tsx` (optional vault-stats table columns)

## References

- sweep-010 / gastrolog-3fu9t / gastrolog-6c1an (compensator retirement — separate epic)
- `docs/audits/findings/04-sweep-compensators.md`
acceptance:
- VaultStats carries VaultReplicationStats per vault on each node; values update on the existing NodeStats broadcast cadence (~5s).
- Expanded VaultCard shows a Replication section with missing count, catchup in-flight, and pipeline segment lag when non-zero.
- NodeDetailPane shows a node-level rollup (total missing across local vaults, catchup in-flight indicator).
- Counters increment at the documented backend instrumentation points; no new periodic sweeps introduced for metrics collection.
- `just gen` run after proto changes; backend + frontend tests updated as appropriate.

title: Recover pipeline Active/Sealing chunks after process shutdown
description:
## Problem

After a controlled or uncontrolled process shutdown, pipeline vault homes can be left with **local sealed GLCB bytes** while the vault-ctl FSM still shows the chunk as **Active** or **Sealing** (no `CmdSealChunk` applied). This is a lifecycle deadlock:

- **Retention** only acts on FSM-sealed chunks (`selectRetentionCandidates` requires `meta.Sealed`; `OverlayFromFSM` forces `Sealed=false` while FSM is Active/Sealing).
- **`SweepIdleActiveChunks`** skips entries where local chunk manager already reports `Sealed=true` (e.g. `RegisterExternalGLCB`) even though FSM is still Active — see `sealIfIdleActive` guard in `vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go`.
- **Chunking build loop** retries segment materialization; it does not seal from an existing local `data.glcb` when segments are gone.
- **Legacy `resumeSealingFromFSM`** targets post-seal assembly of active-form files in the vault CM dir, not pipeline GLCBs under `segments/<vault>/chunks/`.

### Observed on soak cluster (`first-vault`)

Five FSM **Active** chunks with **0 records** in the inspector (FSM projection), while pipeline GLCBs exist on disk for four of them (~10k–100k records each). Ingesters disabled for ~24h; retention never ran. Chunking still logs `manifest segments missing locally` on a pending sealed manifest.

Relevant paths:
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/manager.go` — build/seal loop
- `backend/internal/pipeline/chunking/recover.go` — **new** recovery path (uncommitted WIP)
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go` — idle-active + reconcile-from-snapshot
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/retention.go` — sealed-only candidates
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/pipeline/supervisor.go` — home catch-up wiring

## Required behavior

The system must **converge Active/Sealing pipeline chunks to Sealed** after restart (and on periodic sweeps) when a home already has the materialized GLCB, without requiring raw segments to still be present.

### Core recovery (`RecoverOnce`)

When `segments/<vault>/chunks/<chunkID>/data.glcb` exists locally but FSM entry is not Sealed:

1. Read seal metadata from the GLCB (`readGLCBSealMeta` / `BuildResultFromExistingGLCB`).
2. Propose `CmdSealChunk` via the vault-ctl applier (idempotent).
3. Run post-seal hooks (`afterSealBuild`: head purge queue, `ReleaseSegments` when holder-gated).

Wire recovery on:
- Chunking worker startup
- Pipeline home late-registration catch-up
- `ReconcileFromSnapshot` / vault-ctl after-restore (pipeline vaults)
- `SweepIdleActiveChunks` (before legacy idle-active pass)

### Follow-ups (separate commits or child issues if needed)

- **Vault CM–only GLCB** (`storage/.../vaults/.../data.glcb` without pipeline chunk-root copy): recover via CM meta or repatriate path.
- **Missing segments + no local GLCB**: peer GLCB catchup / `ImportSealedChunk` fallback when build cannot proceed.
- **Disk orphans**: pipeline GLCB dirs after FSM tombstone/retention — reconcile or reap separately (`gastrolog-4trvb` family).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single-node: build GLCB, simulate shutdown before `CmdSealChunk`, restart → FSM shows **Sealed** with correct record count; retention can act on next sweep.
- [ ] Multi-node (4+): same scenario on one home; other homes converge via existing FSM replay + local recover where GLCB exists.
- [ ] Orphan **Active** FSM entry + local pipeline GLCB (no pending `sealedManifest` in FSM) → recover seals cluster-wide.
- [ ] Idempotent: repeated recover/sweep ticks do not re-propose or spam applies.
- [ ] Unhappy: no local GLCB → recover no-ops; build/nudge path unchanged.
- [ ] Soak: `first-vault` zombie Active chunks seal and become retention-eligible after deploy + restart (or within one idle-active sweep interval).

## Test plan

- `TestRecoverOnceSealsFromExistingGLCB` — sealed manifest pending + GLCB on disk
- `TestRecoverOnceSealsOrphanActiveGLCB` — Active FSM + GLCB without sealed manifest
- Orchestrator/reconciler: pipeline vault uses recover in `resumeSealingFromFSM` instead of legacy post-seal only
acceptance: RecoverOnce seals pipeline chunks from existing local GLCB when FSM is Active/Sealing; wired at startup, after-restore, and idle-active sweep; tests cover pending-manifest and orphan-Active cases; soak first-vault zombies converge to Sealed and retention-eligible.
closed_reason: Empty active chunks cleaned out after recovery; seals from existing local GLCB on restart.

Stack traces (e.g. Java, Python, Go), indented continuation lines, and similar patterns span multiple physical lines but represent one event. Current ingestion treats each line as a separate record. title.new: Separate certificate storage from TLS server settings in config store

description.new:
PutTLSConfig and GetTLSConfig on the Store interface conflate two unrelated concerns: certificate data (PEM content, file paths) stored in the tls_certificates table, and TLS server settings (enabled, redirect, default_cert) stored in the settings table as part of server config JSON. This coupling causes a non-atomicity issue — PutTLSConfig writes server settings first, then certs in a separate transaction — and is redundant with PutServerConfig which already manages TLS server settings through its own read-modify-write path.

Replace GetTLSConfig/PutTLSConfig with dedicated certificate CRUD methods on the Store interface (e.g. ListCertificates, GetCertificate, PutCertificate, DeleteCertificate). TLS server settings stay exclusively in server config. The API layer's PutCertificate calls both independently: save the cert, then update server config if set_as_default is set.

description.new:
## Problem

When a file store's data directory is missing (deleted, `/tmp` cleanup, disk failure), the chunk manager silently recreates it via `os.MkdirAll` and starts with zero chunks. The server comes up normally with no warning, no error, and no indication that an entire store's worth of log data has been lost.

This is dangerous because:
- An admin would have no way to detect the data loss without manually checking record counts
- `/tmp`-based stores are especially vulnerable to OS cleanup
- Accidental `rm -rf` or disk issues become invisible

## Expected Behavior

On startup, if a file store's directory is missing or empty (no chunk subdirectories) but the store has been previously configured (i.e., it's not a brand-new store being created for the first time), gastrolog should:

1. Log a prominent warning (e.g., `WARN store "foo" data directory was missing or empty, recreated with 0 chunks`)
2. Optionally refuse to start (configurable) if data loss is detected

## Location

- `backend/internal/chunk/file/manager.go` — `NewManager` calls `os.MkdirAll` unconditionally at line ~139
- `backend/internal/orchestrator/factory.go` — `ApplyConfig` creates chunk managers during startup

## Possible Approaches

- Before `MkdirAll`, check if the directory already exists. If it doesn't, set a flag. After `loadExisting()`, if the flag is set and zero chunks were found, log a warning.
- Alternatively, track "expected chunk count" in the config store and compare on startup.

description.new:
After deleting the data directory and restarting, the frontend still holds an old JWT token in localStorage (signed with the now-gone secret). API calls fail with Unauthenticated but the user is never redirected to login — they just see empty data.

Root causes:

1. The Connect RPC transport has no global error interceptor for 401/Unauthenticated responses. Only search and follow errors are caught in App.tsx; all other hooks (config, stores, ingesters) silently fail.

2. useFollow treats 401 as a transient error and enters a reconnect loop instead of redirecting to login.

3. The router's beforeLoad guard only checks that a token exists in localStorage, not that it's valid.

Fix: add a global error interceptor at the transport layer (in client.ts) that catches Code.Unauthenticated, clears the token, and redirects to /login. Remove the per-hook 401 handling in App.tsx once the global interceptor is in place.

title.new: Consolidate orchestrator store registries into a Store struct

description.new:
The orchestrator currently maintains three parallel maps (chunks, indexes, queries) keyed by store ID, with the invariant that every store ID must exist in all three. This is maintained by careful code in reconfig.go and factory.go but isn't structurally enforced.

Introduce a lightweight Store value type:

```go
type Store struct {
    ID      string
    Chunks  chunk.ChunkManager
    Indexes index.IndexManager
    Query   *query.Engine
    Enabled bool
}
```

Replace the three parallel maps with a single `map[string]*Store`. This makes the triplet invariant structural, simplifies the registry accessors, and gives servers (StoreServer, QueryServer) a cleaner interface to work with.

NOT a new abstraction layer or StoreManager — the orchestrator remains the single coordinator. This is purely an internal data structure improvement.

Introduce a lightweight Store type:

```go
type Store struct {
    ID      string
    Chunks  chunk.ChunkManager
    Indexes index.IndexManager
    Query   *query.Engine
    Enabled bool
}
```

Replace the three parallel maps with a single `map[string]*Store`.

## What moves into Store

Anything that operates on a single store's triplet:

- **Append + seal detection + index triggering** — currently spread across ingest.go, becomes `store.Append(rec)` with seal-detect-then-index as the Store's responsibility
- **Factory wiring** — creating the CM/IM/QE triplet from a StoreConfig becomes a Store constructor
- **Enable/disable** toggling
- **Per-store shutdown** — close CM, wait for index builds

## What stays in the orchestrator

Anything that's cross-store coordination:

- The ingest channel and loop
- Filter routing (`FilterSet.Match` → which stores get a message)
- Ingester lifecycle
- The store registry itself (add/remove/rename/list)

## Non-goals

This is NOT a new abstraction layer or StoreManager — the orchestrator remains the single coordinator. This is purely consolidating per-store logic into a proper type instead of scattering it across orchestrator methods.

description.new: When merging stores, copyRecords calls dstCM.Append(rec). The chunk manager's Append always overwrites record.WriteTS with m.cfg.Now(), discarding the original write timestamp. This causes merged records to appear as if they were written at merge time rather than their original ingest time. Time-range queries (which use WriteTS for Start/End bounds) will exclude merged records that fall outside the merge-time window—e.g. a record originally from Jan 1 merged on Jan 15 will have WriteTS=Jan15 and be missed by a query for Jan 1–5. Fix requires either: (a) Append variant that preserves WriteTS when caller can guarantee monotonic order, or (b) sort merged records by WriteTS before appending and use such a variant. Non-empty destination merge may need special handling to preserve monotonicity.

notes.new: Design: The only correct way to merge is to merge two stores into a third, empty store. Merging into an existing destination inherently risks non-monotonic WriteTS or wrong ordering.

description.new:
When merging stores, copyRecords calls dstCM.Append(rec). The chunk manager's Append always overwrites record.WriteTS with m.cfg.Now(), discarding the original write timestamp. This causes merged records to appear as if they were written at merge time rather than their original ingest time. Time-range queries (which use WriteTS for Start/End bounds) will exclude merged records that fall outside the merge-time window—e.g. a record originally from Jan 1 merged on Jan 15 will have WriteTS=Jan15 and be missed by a query for Jan 1–5.

## Revised approach: move chunks, don't rewrite records

The query engine already handles overlapping time spans across chunks in the same store via heap-based merge-sort (by IngestTS). This means we can simply **move the source store's chunks (and their indexes) into the destination store** instead of reading/rewriting every record.

Benefits:
- WriteTS is preserved (fixes the bug)
- Indexes are preserved (no rebuild needed)
- Much faster (no record-by-record I/O)
- No ordering concerns within chunks

### Same-backend merge (e.g. file→file)
Move/rename chunk directories from source store into destination store. Trivial.

### Cross-backend merge (e.g. memory→file)
Requires rewriting chunks into the destination backend format. Could use a header flag on the destination chunk to mark it as "merging" so the query engine ignores it until the rewrite is complete. Records must be copied preserving all timestamps (WriteTS, IngestTS, SourceTS). Once rewrite finishes, clear the flag and build indexes.

description.new:
The current store operations (clone, merge, migrate) overlap. Clone serves no real purpose — the query engine searches all stores, so having a copy is pointless. Simplify to two operations: Migrate and Merge.

## Remove CloneStore

Delete the RPC, handler, frontend UI, and hook. No longer needed.

## MigrateStore (three-phase move)

The primary operation for moving a store to a new name, type, and/or location. Orchestrates existing primitives:

1. **Create destination store** with the same filters/policy as the source, enable it — new ingested data starts flowing there immediately.
2. **Disable source store and seal all unsealed chunks** — source is now frozen, no new records flow in (back pressure handles in-flight data).
3. **Merge source into destination, delete source when done** — drains the now-static source into the active destination.

This avoids the race condition of copying while new data arrives. The source becomes a frozen snapshot the moment migration starts.

## Restrict MergeStores

Keep for consolidating stores, but add safety guards:
- Target store must be disabled or have no filters applied, to prevent silent data loss from filter mismatches.
- Auto-seal any unsealed chunks in the source before merging.

Note: the merge restrictions are naturally satisfied during MigrateStore because step 2 disables the source.

description.new:
server/store_operations.go (613 lines) contains business logic that belongs in the orchestrator layer. MigrateStore (127 lines), MergeStores (106 lines), copyRecordsTracked (65 lines), and moveChunksTracked (59 lines) all make decisions about when to seal chunks, how to move them between stores, and when to build indexes. These are orchestration concerns, not RPC handler concerns.

The fix is to add orchestrator methods like MigrateStoreAsync(src, dst, opts) and MergeStoresAsync(src, dst, opts) that encapsulate the multi-phase workflows. The server layer should only parse proto requests and call orchestrator methods.

title.new: Eliminate direct ChunkManager/IndexManager access from server

description.new:
The server package bypasses orchestrator coordination by reaching directly into internal managers via s.orch.ChunkManager(storeID) and s.orch.IndexManager(storeID) — at least 15 call sites across store_info.go, store_chunks.go, and store_operations.go. This allows the server to call .Seal(), .Append(), .BuildIndexes() etc. without going through orchestrator routing logic, breaking encapsulation.

The fix is to either:
1. Add orchestrator facade methods for the operations the server needs (ReindexChunk, ListChunkMetas, GetChunkDetails, etc.)
2. Or make ChunkManager/IndexManager accessors package-private and expose purpose-specific APIs instead.

title.new: Move histogram and context queries from server to query engine

description.new:
server/query.go contains ~370 lines of index query logic that belongs in the query engine:

- Histogram() (157 lines): performs binary searches on idx.log, reads WriteTS from chunks, buckets results by time. Uses cm.FindStartPosition() directly.
- histogramChunkFast() (46 lines): binary search on ChunkManager.
- histogramChunkSeverity() (79 lines): opens KV indexes, extracts positions, reads timestamps.
- GetContext() (133 lines): seeks to record positions and reads surrounding records.

The server is constructing index.NewKVIndexReader() and doing low-level position lookups — this is query engine work. The fix is to add query.Engine.Histogram(query) and query.Engine.GetContext(ref, before, after) methods, then have the server handlers only do proto conversion.

title: Move histogram and context queries from server to query engine

The Orchestrator type has 52 public methods across 14 files (6569 total lines) and handles too many responsibilities: component registration, configuration management, lifecycle management, scheduling, and statistics tracking.

Candidates for extraction into dedicated types:
- Scheduler (already in scheduler.go, 539 lines, 16 methods) — could become a standalone managed component with its own initialization
- FilterManager — filter compilation, filter set management, and routing logic
- LifecycleManager — Start/Stop/ingestLoop/processMessage
- StatsTracker — ingester statistics collection

The orchestrator would still coordinate these components but delegate the actual work, reducing its method count and making each concern independently testable.

orchestrator/factory.go ApplyConfig() is 188 lines and blends three distinct concerns:

1. Chunk/Index manager factory invocation (lines 101-120): looks up factory by type, clones params, injects _expect_existing, creates manager
2. Filter compilation (lines 88-98, 131-162): resolves filter ID to expression, compiles filter expressions, manages FilterSet

description.new:
ConfigServer (45 methods across 8 files) both reads/writes the config store AND coordinates with the orchestrator for hot updates (UpdateFilters, UpdateRotationPolicies, etc.), creating bidirectional coupling: server → config store and server → orchestrator → config store.

The hot-update path means the server is acting as a mediator between config and orchestrator. Consider:
1. An event-based approach where config changes emit events that the orchestrator subscribes to
2. Or moving the hot-update coordination into the orchestrator itself, so the server only writes to the config store and the orchestrator picks up changes

description.new:
When a Follow stream is active and a store is migrated (e.g. memory → file), the stream silently stops producing records. The frontend remains in follow mode but never receives new data.

Root cause: Engine.Follow() captured the store list once at initialization. After migration deletes the old store and creates a new one with a different UUID, the poll loop kept querying the deleted store ID — getting nil back and silently producing nothing.

Fixed by re-evaluating the store list on each poll iteration, initializing positions for newly discovered stores so history isn't replayed.

description.new:
attr.log currently encodes attributes per-record as [count:u16][keyLen:u16][key bytes][valLen:u16][val bytes]... — every record repeats the full key strings. With ~20K records per chunk sharing the same handful of keys (host, service, level, etc.), this wastes significant space. attr.log is the largest file in a chunk (36% of total with chatterbox data).

Introduce a per-chunk key dictionary:
- New file: attr_dict.log — append-only list of [keyLen:u16][key bytes], key ID = positional index
- Writer maintains map[string]uint16 in memory for the active chunk, appends to attr_dict.log on first occurrence of a key
- attr.log record format changes from [keyLen:u16][key bytes][valLen:u16][val bytes] to [keyID:u16][valLen:u16][val bytes] per attribute
- Reader loads the dictionary file on cursor open, uses it to decode attr records
- No special seal-time processing — dictionary is complete by seal time
- Dictionary file is tiny (hundreds of bytes for typical key sets)

This is fully append-only on both files, preserving the existing write pattern. Estimated savings: 25-40% of attr.log size depending on key/value ratio.

title.new: Support human-friendly and locale-aware timestamp formats in queries

description.new:
Query time bounds (start, end, source_start, source_end, ingest_start, ingest_end) currently only accept RFC 3339 format (2024-01-15T08:00:00Z) and Unix timestamps. This is verbose and unfriendly for non-developers.

Add support for:

- Relaxed ISO formats: 2024-01-15, 2024-01-15 08:00, 2024-01-15T08:00 (no seconds), no-Z implies local timezone
- Locale-aware date parsing: Use the browser's regional settings to determine date component order — 1/15/2024 (US) vs 15/1/2024 (EU) vs 2024/1/15 (ISO). Frontend parses to RFC 3339 before sending to backend.
- Natural language: yesterday, today, 3 hours ago, last monday, this morning
- Time-only: 08:00 (implies today)

Parsing should happen on the frontend (which has access to locale and timezone info), normalizing to RFC 3339 before the query hits the backend. The backend remains strict.

description.new:
The Docker ingester currently uses three separate, simple filter params (label_filter, name_filter, image_filter) with no boolean logic between them — they're just ANDed. The querylang filter engine already supports full boolean expressions (AND, OR, NOT, globs, regex) over map[string]string, which is exactly what Docker container metadata is.

Replace the three standalone filter params with a single `filter` param that accepts a querylang expression. Container metadata would be flattened into attributes like:

- `image` — image name/tag
- `name` — container name
- `label.<key>` — Docker labels with prefix

Example: `image~"nginx*" AND (label.env="prod" OR label.env="staging")`

Steps:
1. Export the evaluation functions from orchestrator (matchesAttrs, evalAttrPredicate) — or move them to querylang where they arguably belong
2. In the Docker ingester, flatten container metadata into a map[string]string
3. Replace containerFilter struct with a compiled querylang DNF filter
4. Deprecate label_filter, name_filter, image_filter in favor of the unified `filter` param
5. Update the ingester-docker help page and the Docker mTLS recipe (recipe-docker-mtls) to document the new filter syntax

description.new:
Searching for bare tokens like IP addresses (e.g. 72.11.138.26) returns no results even when records containing them are visible.

Root cause: tokenization mismatch between query parser and record indexer. The query parser treats dotted values as a single bareword, but the record tokenizer splits on dots and discards pure-numeric segments. The runtime filter (matchesSingleToken) then looks for the full IP as a single token in the record's token list, which can never match.

When a bare token is not indexable (contains characters outside the token alphabet), the search should fall back to a raw content scan of chunks that match the rest of the expression, rather than silently returning no results.

description.new:
Add a migration policy that automatically moves sealed chunks from one store to another based on age (and potentially size). This enables tiered storage similar to Splunk's hot/warm/cold model:

- Active chunk = hot (accepting writes)
- Sealed chunk in fast store = warm (recent, fast queries)  
- Auto-migrated to cheaper/slower store = cold (older, still searchable)
- Retention policy deletes = expired

A migration policy would attach to a source store and specify a destination store plus conditions (e.g., maxAge: 168h moves chunks older than 7 days). The mechanism is similar to the existing manual Migrate operation in StoresSettings but triggered automatically by the scheduler.

Design considerations:
- New policy type (migration policy) alongside rotation and retention
- Backend-agnostic: works between any store types (file→file, file→S3, memory→file, etc.)
- May require new storage backends (S3, GCS) to be useful for cold tier
- Multiple tiers possible: chain migration policies (fast-file → slow-file → S3)
- Chunks remain searchable at every tier
