title.new: vault leader transfer during rolling redeploy leaves orphan active chunk on previous replica set

description.new:
## Symptom

After a K8s rolling redeploy that causes a hot-vault leader transfer, the inspector shows **two active chunks** in the same vault. The vault should only ever have one active chunk at a time.

Observed on 2026-05-13 with hot-vault leader transitioning from a g-1/g-2/g-5 leader to g-3:

- `06f23079i9u1t62u3930fa8g8k` — `active 4`, residency `{g-1, g-2, g-5, g-3}` — the new active chunk started by g-3 after taking the leader role.
- `06f22vei6do1v5a7lnrfc5njf4` — `active 3`, residency `{g-1, g-2, g-5}` — the old active chunk from the prior leader. Missing on g-3 because the chunk was created before g-3 became leader.

Both chunks appear in `ListChunks` with `sealed=false`. Both are physically present on their respective node sets (verified via `gastrolog inspect chunk` on each placement member). The old active has records but is permanently stuck — no records flow to it, no path to seal, never converges.

## Probable root cause

Leadership transfer for the vault-ctl Raft group correctly replicates the FSM manifest (so g-3 sees both chunks in its FSM), but the active-chunk **lifecycle** lacks a clean handshake for leader role changes:

1. Old leader has open active chunk X.
2. Vault-ctl Raft leadership transfers to g-3 (was the case when k8s rolling redeploy cycled the prior leader's pod).
3. g-3 takes the leader role, sees chunk X in the FSM but doesn't have its records locally (catchup didn't cover it because chunks in the "active" state aren't subject to seal-replication).
4. g-3 starts its own active chunk Y because the leader is supposed to have an active chunk.
5. X stays in the manifest as `state=active` on the former replicas. New writes go to Y. X has no path forward — it will never seal (no leader proposing CmdSealChunk for it), will never replicate to g-3, will never get retired.

## Acceptance

- After any leader transfer (rolling redeploy, scale-out, leader-step-down, eviction), the previous leader's active chunk MUST either:
  - be sealed via a CmdSealChunk proposed by the OLD leader before stepping down, OR
  - be sealed by the NEW leader's takeover handshake (e.g., the lifecycle reconciler proposes CmdSealChunk for any state=active FSM entry that isn't the leader's current active).
- Inspector NEVER shows two active chunks for the same vault simultaneously, regardless of scale-out / scale-in / redeploy sequence.
- Existing orphans can be retired via an operator-initiated cleanup (CLI or RPC) — even with the structural fix, surviving orphans from before need a sweep path.

## Related

- gastrolog-19241 (peer-to-peer catchup): handles sealed chunks the new leader is missing, but explicitly excludes active chunks because their content is mutable.
- The "stuck retention pendingDelete" leak (separate filing) — same root cause family: leader-transfer-during-rolling-redeploy leaves stranded FSM state. Different stage of the chunk lifecycle.

## Severity

Pri 2 — operator UX (two-actives looks broken to the inspector eye), not data loss for current ingestion. The old-active chunk's records ARE preserved on the three nodes that hold it; they just can't be queried via the active-chunk path post-rotation, and a future seal could resolve them. But over time, every rolling redeploy adds a new orphan, and the FSM accumulates unsealable state — eventually that's a correctness problem.

title: vault leader transfer during rolling redeploy leaves orphan active chunk on previous replica set

description.new:
## Symptom

After a K8s rolling redeploy, chunks marked `retention_pending=true` in the FSM stay visible in the inspector with the orange "ret" badge indefinitely. The chunks have records on every placement member; the receipt protocol started its delete cycle but never finalized. Page reload doesn't help — it's backend state, not UI cache.

Observed on 2026-05-13 in hot-vault: 5 chunks sealed at 10:40-10:44 stuck with `retention_pending=true` for 2+ hours after the rolling redeploy cycled the leader pod. Direct `gastrolog inspect chunk` confirms they're physically present on all 4 placement nodes; ListChunks reports `pending_ack_node_ids=[]` for each.

## Probable root cause

The receipt protocol's finalize step is a one-shot inline callback with no retry path:

1. Leader proposes `CmdRequestDelete` → applied → `pendingDeletes[chunkID]` populated with `ExpectedFrom = {placement members}`.
2. Each node fires `onRequestDelete`, deletes its local copy, proposes `CmdAckDelete`.
3. Each `CmdAckDelete` apply removes one node from `ExpectedFrom` and fires `onAckDelete` only on the leader.
4. `onAckDelete` checks `len(ExpectedFrom) == 0` and, if so, proposes `CmdFinalizeDelete` in a goroutine.

The leak window: if leadership transfers AFTER the final ack applies but BEFORE the leader's `onAckDelete` goroutine successfully applies `CmdFinalizeDelete`, the new leader doesn't fire `onAckDelete` (the apply already happened) and there's no other path that scans `pendingDeletes` looking for entries with `ExpectedFrom={}` to finalize.

With a rolling redeploy each pod cycle is a forced leadership transfer, so this window is hit reliably on every batch of in-flight deletes.

A `gastrolog inspect chunk` from each node shows the records still there (the per-node deletes did happen via fulfillObligation — that part of the flow completes BEFORE the ack RPC fires). But — wait, this is the contradiction worth tracking down:

Actually, observed state: records ARE present on every node. So either:
- The receipt-protocol started, fulfillObligation NEVER ran (no per-node delete), pendingDeletes still has the full ExpectedFrom set, and finalize hasn't happened yet, OR
- Something else entirely.

The user-observable symptom — `ret` badge persists across page reloads for hours — needs a definitive backend probe to distinguish these. A new inspect surface that exposes `fsm.PendingDelete(chunkID).ExpectedFrom` directly would resolve the ambiguity in one query.

## Acceptance

- Periodic leader-side sweep: walk `fsm.PendingDeletes()`, find entries with `len(ExpectedFrom) == 0`, propose `CmdFinalizeDelete`. Mirror of the existing `SweepPendingObligations` / `SweepMissingReplicas` / `SweepStaleLeaderFSMEntries` pattern in `vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go`. Wire into `vaultCatchupSweepAll` at the same 20s cadence.
- An operator-callable inspector surface that distinguishes "no pendingDelete entry" from "pendingDelete with empty ExpectedFrom" — currently both render as `pending_ack_node_ids=[]` on the wire.
- After a rolling redeploy, no chunk stays `retention_pending` for more than ~30 seconds; the finalize-recovery sweep catches stranded entries on the first post-redeploy tick.

## Related

- gastrolog-51gme is the receipt-protocol design that this leak surfaces in.
- gastrolog-2eclw (orphan active chunk after leader transfer) — same root cause family: leader-transfer-during-rolling-redeploy leaves stranded FSM state at different chunk-lifecycle stages. The two probably want to land in the same epic.
- gastrolog-1gh5s (rolling-upgrade Raft fix) — the workflow under which this surfaces. Pre-1gh5s the cluster wedged before getting here.

## Severity

Pri 2 — chunks accumulate in the FSM and consume operator attention via false "stuck" badges. Not a data loss bug per se (records physically deleted on each node per the receipt protocol), but the unbounded FSM growth is real. With one rolling redeploy a day and ~5 in-flight retention deletes per cycle, that's ~150 stuck entries a month per vault.

title.new: active-chunk reconcile at seal: per-chunk EventID hash chain + record-level divergence resolution

description.new:
## Problem

Active chunks accept appends on the leader and replicate to followers via `AppendRecords`. If something happens mid-replication — leader transfer, transient network blip, retry races — follower copies can silently diverge from the leader copy. When the leader seals, only the leader's record sequence is canonical. Records that landed on a follower but not the leader (or vice versa) are silently dropped at seal time.

The chunk seal is a natural cluster-wide synchronization point — replicas have to coordinate the seal anyway. Reusing that coordination to detect and reconcile divergence costs no new round-trips in the happy path.

## Design

### Per-chunk running hash

- Each replica maintains a single `xxh3` running hash per active chunk, updated on every `AppendRecords` apply.
- Combiner: `running = xxh3(running || event_id_bytes)`. Order-sensitive (sequential fold). Deterministic across replicas because every replica sees the same `EventID` for each record (EventID is minted at ingest time as `(IngesterID, NodeID, IngestTS, IngestSeq)` — see `chunk/types.go:229`).
- 8 bytes per active chunk stored alongside `RecordCount` / `Bytes` in the FSM's manifest entry. NOT per-record; just the running fold value.
- Content corruption with EventID intact is a separate bug class and out of scope here. This protocol detects "different set of records OR same set in different order."

### Happy-path seal

- Leader proposes `CmdSealChunk` carrying its final hash.
- Each follower's `applySealChunk` compares its own running hash against the leader's.
- Match → normal seal, ack.
- Mismatch → trigger the divergence-resolution sub-protocol below.

### Divergence resolution

When hashes mismatch on apply:

1. Leader collects the full ordered `EventID` list from every replica (one round trip; ~4 KB per 1k records).
2. Leader computes the union of EventIDs, sorts lexicographically by EventID tuple (`IngestTS, IngesterID, NodeID, IngestSeq` — naturally ordered by ingest time with the other fields disambiguating sub-clock-precision collisions).
3. Leader proposes `CmdReconcileSeal` carrying the canonical ordered EventID sequence.
4. Each replica applies it: walks its local records, keeps those whose EventID is in the canonical list, requests any missing records from peers via the record-level extension of gastrolog-19241's `RequestReplicaCatchup`.
5. When the replica's local sealed chunk matches the canonical list, it acks the seal.

Dedup is implicit: each EventID appears once in the canonical list. Records with identical EventIDs across replicas are the same record by construction.

## Why this composition works

- Per-record state cost: zero (no new per-record fields). EventID already exists; the running hash is one accumulated value per chunk.
- Happy-path overhead: `xxh3` update per append (a few nanoseconds), one fixed-size value compared at seal time.
- Divergence path: ~3 MB transferred for a 50k-record chunk in the worst case. Rare by assumption.
- Reuses existing primitives:
  - `EventID` for identity (already canonical, already used by the query `dedup` operator).
  - `IngestTS`-ordered storage + indexes for natural ordering.
  - `RequestReplicaCatchup` / `CatchupSelectedChunks` (gastrolog-19241) for the peer fetch — just at record granularity instead of chunk granularity. Both protocols become symmetric: chunk-level "we agree this chunk should exist; bring it to me" and record-level "we agree these records should be in this chunk; bring me the ones I'm missing."

## Acceptance

- Every active chunk carries a running hash updated on each apply.
- Seal-time hash mismatch triggers reconcile; matching hashes seal without extra work.
- After a forced divergence (test harness drops some `AppendRecords` to one replica then triggers seal), the sealed chunk on every replica is byte-identical and contains the union of all records that any replica saw.
- Steady-state append throughput regresses by no more than ~1% from the hash update (measured at the ingest rate where seal cadence matters).

## Related

- gastrolog-19241 (peer-to-peer catchup): the chunk-level half of the symmetric protocol; this issue is the record-level half.
- gastrolog-2eclw (orphan active chunk after leader transfer): closely adjacent. If 2eclw's cure is "transiently multiple actives, drain to one by routing new records to the existing one," then those records eventually need to flow through reconcile-at-seal anyway. This protocol is the safety net under that cure.
- gastrolog-15fm8 (finalize leak): unrelated mechanism, same general "leader-only post-apply callback" disease family.

title: active-chunk reconcile at seal: per-chunk EventID hash chain + record-level divergence resolution

description.new:
## Theme

GastroLog's chunk-state machine assumes leader-only post-apply work converges silently — every Raft apply that needs follow-up (propose finalize, seal the orphan active, request the missing replica) runs as an inline callback on the *current* leader. When leadership transfers during the window between apply and callback — the routine case under K8s rolling redeploys, scale-out, eviction — the follow-up work is dropped, and the cluster ends up with stranded FSM state at various points in the chunk lifecycle.

This epic captures the design direction for closing those gaps coherently rather than stacking one new periodic sweep per failure mode.

## Disease

**Leader-only inline post-apply callbacks without atomic guarantees.** The pattern recurs throughout `vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go`:

```go
func (r *VaultLifecycleReconciler) onAckDelete(chunkID, ackingNodeID) {
    if !r.vaultInst.IsRaftLeader() { return }
    // ... check FSM state ...
    go r.vaultInst.ApplyRaftFinalizeDelete(chunkID)
}
```

Three failure modes share this shape:
- Leadership transfers between the apply that triggered the callback and the callback's `go ... Apply(...)` reaching the new leader. The new leader didn't fire `onAckDelete` (the apply already happened in its predecessor's epoch); the followup never lands.
- The leader's goroutine dies (pod cycled mid-flight).
- The followup `Apply` itself fails (network blip) with no retry.

Each manifestation gets a different child issue. The reflex was to add a new periodic sweep per failure mode (the codebase already has `SweepPendingObligations`, `SweepLocalOrphans`, `SweepMissingReplicas`, `SweepStaleLeaderFSMEntries`); each new sweep is polling at the Raft-apply level — the same anti-pattern as `refetchInterval` is at the event-stream level.

## Cure principles

1. **Fold FSM-local state transitions INTO the apply handler.** When the follow-up work is pure FSM mutation (delete map entry, set flag, tombstone), the apply handler that triggered it can do it atomically. No second Raft round trip; every node's apply produces identical state by construction. `applyAckDelete` should remove the `pendingDeletes` entry when `ExpectedFrom` drains to empty, not defer that to `onAckDelete` (gastrolog-15fm8).

2. **Trigger non-FSM-local work from leadership-change events at apply time.** When the follow-up needs network or local-FS work (seal an active chunk that has records, fetch missing records from a peer), the trigger should be "the apply that observed me becoming leader" rather than a periodic sweep. Each leadership change is one event; the work fires once and is retried on failure via a sweep — but the sweep is the safety net, not the primary path.

3. **Relax invariants that lack a clean transfer protocol.** Where the cure-by-handshake is structurally heavy, relax the invariant instead. "Exactly one active chunk per vault" was an accidental simplification; "transiently multiple, drain to one" is the cluster-native version that makes leader-transfer-active-orphan stop being a bug (gastrolog-2eclw).

4. **Reuse existing primitives.** Identity → `chunk.EventID`. Ordering → `IngestTS` + sorted index. Cluster-wide chunk residency → vault-ctl FSM's `placement_set - pendingDeletes.ExpectedFrom`. Per-peer fetch → `RequestReplicaCatchup` from gastrolog-19241. Don't invent new state when existing primitives cover the sub-problem.

## Child issues (concrete instantiations)

- **gastrolog-15fm8** — receipt-protocol finalize leak. Cure: fold finalize into `applyAckDelete`. Smallest landing point; structurally cleanest.
- **gastrolog-2eclw** — orphan active chunk after leader transfer. Cure: relax "one active per vault" to "transiently multiple, drain to one." Routing change is small; rotation policy must include time-based trigger.
- **gastrolog-617m6** — reconcile at seal (per-chunk EventID hash chain + record-level divergence resolution). Safety net under 2eclw's cure: when records have flowed through a chain of active chunks across leader transfers, seal-time reconciliation guarantees no records are silently lost. Depends on 2eclw's design direction being resolved first.

## Out of scope (related but distinct)

- gastrolog-19241 (closed) — peer-to-peer catchup for missing sealed chunks. Currently uses a periodic sweep on the leader; its follow-up is to convert that sweep into a takeover-triggered event with the sweep relegated to safety-net. Worth filing as a separate child under this epic when we're ready to revisit.

## Acceptance

- After a K8s rolling redeploy of 10 pods:
  - Zero "ret"-badged chunks that don't progress (gastrolog-15fm8's symptom).
  - Zero duplicate active chunks (gastrolog-2eclw's symptom — either eliminated by structural cure, or all chunks remain valid actives that drain naturally).
  - Sealed chunks are byte-identical across all replicas (gastrolog-617m6's guarantee).
- Audit of `vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go` finds no `if !IsRaftLeader() return; ... go Apply(...)` pattern remaining outside of explicit operator-triggered paths.

## Design audit (proposed first step before any implementation)

Grep the codebase for the leader-only-post-apply-callback shape:
- `r.vaultInst.IsRaftLeader()` / `r.vaultInst.HasRaftLeader()` checks gating a goroutine that calls `Apply...`.
- Every `SetOn...` callback in vault-ctl FSM (`OnRequestDelete`, `OnAckDelete`, `OnFinalizeDelete`, `OnPruneNode`, etc.) where the callback proposes a downstream Raft command.

Enumerate the full bug family in one pass. Some callbacks may be safely FSM-local; some may justify the sweep-as-safety-net pattern explicitly. The audit itself is the right starting point.

description.new:
## Symptom

Scaling a K8s StatefulSet down via \`kubectl scale\` (instead of the supported \`just deploy kubernetes-contract <count>\` path) leaves the cluster in a fragile-quorum state:

- Pods terminate cleanly.
- Raft membership keeps the terminated nodes as VOTERs forever.
- The system FSM keeps their \`NodeConfig\` entries forever.
- Quorum tolerance shrinks: an N-voter cluster with K dead voters needs (N/2)+1 reachable, but only (N-K) are reachable. If K > N - quorum, losing one more live node halts writes.

Observed on a 10→3 contract experiment in this session: \`gastrolog cluster status\` reports 5 voters (g-0, g-1, g-2 reachable + g-3, g-4 unreachable), \`config node list\` reports 6 entries (zombies g-3/g-4/g-5). Vault placements DID converge correctly to the live 3 nodes via the placement manager — the cluster is functional, just fragile.

From the operator's perspective it looked like "the cluster refused to let go of those last 2 nodes because they were needed for the replication." The cluster did not actively refuse; the design simply has no path that auto-prunes voters whose pods went away, and the vault with RF=5 generated replication-degraded alerts that read as "still need those nodes."

## Root cause

The supported scale-down recipe (\`deploy/justfile:461-490\` \`kubernetes-contract\`) does two things in order: (1) call \`gastrolog cluster remove-node gastrolog-N\` per pod-to-be-deleted, which fires \`RemoveServer\` against Raft + \`DeleteNode\` against the system FSM; (2) \`kubectl scale --replicas=<target>\`. \`kubectl scale\` alone only does step (2).

There is no automatic detection of "voter has been unreachable for N minutes — propose RemoveServer." [internal/cluster/cluster.go](backend/internal/cluster/cluster.go) has \`RemoveServer\` wired only as the implementation of the explicit \`cluster.RemoveNode\` RPC. Auto-prune isn't trivially safe — "unreachable for 10 minutes" could be a transient partition versus a true decommission, and getting it wrong evicts a real voter and loses one quorum slot worth of fault tolerance.

This is structurally the same shape as the leader-only-callback family captured in gastrolog-3qr8z: a multi-step convergence (pod terminate → Raft RemoveServer → NodeConfig DeleteNode) whose first step can fire independently of the others. The system trusts the operator to drive scale-down through \`cluster.RemoveNode\`, but K8s' default scale-down primitive has no awareness of that contract.

## Acceptance

At least one of the following, preferably both:

1. **K8s preStop hook in the StatefulSet pod spec** that calls \`cluster demote-self\` (or equivalent) before SIGTERM. Lets the pod tell the leader to RemoveServer / DeleteNode for itself before it goes away. Aligns the K8s lifecycle with the Raft lifecycle. Tradeoff: forced terminations (OOM, node failure) skip the hook — those still need (2).

2. **Periodic leader-side reconciler that proposes RemoveServer for voters that have not heartbeated in N minutes.** Configurable threshold (default high — 10 min? 30 min? — to avoid pruning during transient partitions). Logs a warning + alert before pruning. Operator override to disable.

3. **Document the failure mode prominently.** Anyone running \`kubectl scale -- replicas=X\` directly on the gastrolog StatefulSet should be warned in CLAUDE.md / docs that the supported path is the contract recipe.

After fix, the post-scale-down state should be: \`gastrolog cluster status\` reports exactly the number of currently-running pods as voters, \`config node list\` matches, and quorum tolerance is at the structural maximum for that node count.

## Workaround (current operator action)

For a cluster stranded as described, manually clean up each ghost voter:

\`\`\`
kubectl exec -n gastrolog gastrolog-0 -- /gastrolog --home /config cluster remove-node gastrolog-3
kubectl exec -n gastrolog gastrolog-0 -- /gastrolog --home /config cluster remove-node gastrolog-4
...
\`\`\`

Going forward: use \`just deploy kubernetes-contract <count>\` not \`kubectl scale\`.

## Related

- gastrolog-3qr8z (epic) — chunk-state convergence under cluster topology changes. Same disease shape: multi-step convergence whose first step can fire without the others. Worth parenting this issue under that epic.
- The vault placement manager's correct re-placement (placement.go:84-135) saved the cluster from being broken; the stranded-voter state is fragile but functional. Without the placement manager doing its job, this bug would be much worse.

description.new:
## Symptom

Inspector renders ingester status as e.g. \`10/3\` (10 running of 3 selected) after a cluster scale-down + voter cleanup. The 10 reflects stale \`IngesterAlive\` entries in the FSM keyed by node IDs that have been removed via \`cluster remove-node\`.

Reproduces from any cluster contract: scale down N→M, run \`cluster remove-node\` for the departed nodes, refresh the inspector. The ingester-status badge counts stale alive entries forever.

## Root cause

[\`memory/store.go:501\`](backend/internal/system/memory/store.go) and [\`raftstore/store.go:376\`](backend/internal/system/raftstore/store.go) implement \`DeleteNode\` as a single-map mutation: \`delete(s.nodes, id)\`. It does not sweep related FSM state that references the deleted node ID:

- \`IngesterAlive[*][deletedNode]\` — every ingester's alive map keeps the deleted node's status flag.
- \`NodeStorageConfig\` for the deleted node — placement helpers carry a ghost storage.
- \`IngesterAssignments\` if any point at the deleted node — singleton ingesters can be assigned to a node that no longer exists.

Same disease shape as gastrolog-15fm8 (closed): an apply handler mutates one map but defers related state cleanup to a callback that may never fire. \`DeleteNode\` should be a full sweep — every reference to the node ID atomically removed.

## Acceptance

Backend (load-bearing):
- \`DeleteNode\` apply removes \`IngesterAlive[*][nodeID]\` for every ingester, \`NodeStorageConfig\` keyed by the node, and any \`IngesterAssignments\` pointing at it.
- Tests pin: after \`DeleteNode\`, no surviving FSM key references the deleted node.

Frontend (defense-in-depth, also worth doing):
- [\`ingester.ts:runningCount\`](frontend/src/api/model/ingester.ts) intersects the alive map's keys with the current \`liveNodes\` set before counting. Stale entries past the backend sweep don't inflate the badge.

After fix: inspector badge reads \`N/N\` for an AllNodes ingester running healthily on every alive node, regardless of how many nodes have been added and removed over the cluster's history.

## Related

- Parent: gastrolog-3qr8z. Same multi-step-convergence disease as gastrolog-15fm8 (fixed), gastrolog-6bfwk (sibling). \`DeleteNode\`'s apply handler is the natural home for the sweep.
- Sibling: gastrolog-6bfwk — K8s scale-down via \`kubectl scale\` strands Raft voters. Both bugs combine into the same operator-visible "scale-down doesn't fully scale down" complaint; fixing one without the other leaves the other half of the stranding visible.

description.new:
## Problem

When a vault has a SizeRetentionPolicy with maxBytes = N (e.g. 10 GB), the vault appears to plateau well below N in the UI (observed: ~6 GB for a 10 GB policy on the warm vault). Looks like retention is firing early or the policy is broken. It isn't — the two numbers measure different things.

- **Retention** sums chunks by **logical** `ChunkMeta.Bytes` (raw + attr + idx, uncompressed). See [backend/internal/chunk/retention.go:109](backend/internal/chunk/retention.go#L109).
- **UI / stats RPC** sums `ChunkMeta.DiskBytes` when populated (compressed `.glcb` size), falling back to `Bytes` only when `DiskBytes == 0`. See [backend/internal/server/vault_info.go:154-159](backend/internal/server/vault_info.go#L154-L159) (`accumulateChunkBytes`).

Net effect with typical zstd compression (~60% ratio on log records): a 10 GB logical cap displays as ~6 GB on disk. The cap IS firing where it should — the operator can't tell.

## Why it matters

Operators set retention limits to bound disk usage. Today the configured number and the displayed number measure different things, with no label distinguishing them. An operator who sees "vault is at 6 GB / 10 GB cap, plenty of room" is wrong about both halves of the fraction:

- The 6 GB is on-disk; the cap is logical.
- The headroom they think they have doesn't exist.

This is also why retention sweeps can appear ineffective during incident debugging.

## Options (pick one or combine)

1. **Dual-field stats (safest).** Expose both `logical_bytes` and `disk_bytes` in the VaultStats proto and surface them in the UI. Label the retention cap explicitly as "logical". Don't change retention math.
2. **Label-only fix.** Keep proto and behavior; just rename UI labels: "On-disk" for current DataBytes, and annotate retention-cap settings with "(uncompressed)".
3. **Switch retention to DiskBytes.** Tempting but bad: `DiskBytes` depends on the compression algo/level a given replica wrote with, so two replicas with different write paths would disagree on whether the cap is exceeded. Retention must be deterministic across replicas. **Do not pick this unless we also nail down `DiskBytes` as cluster-canonical, which is a bigger change.**

Recommendation: **option 1**. Operators want to see both numbers, and the cap-vs-display mismatch only confuses if the labels don't disambiguate.

## Acceptance

- VaultStats proto exposes logical and on-disk bytes as separate fields (single `data_bytes` field gone, or kept with a clear name).
- UI shows both, with the retention cap visibly aligned to the logical number (or whichever field retention uses).
- Settings UI for SizeRetentionPolicy explicitly labels the input as logical/uncompressed.
- Existing single-node and multi-node retention tests still pass.
- New test asserts: with a SizeRetentionPolicy of N logical bytes against a vault with compressed chunks where `DiskBytes < Bytes`, retention triggers at logical size N (not disk size N).

## Notes / open questions

- Does `DiskBytes` get populated reliably for all chunk sources (incl. cloud-backed chunks, transition destinations)? If it can be zero, the fallback path in `accumulateChunkBytes` masks the issue in some cases — worth auditing.
- Help page for the retention settings tab probably needs an update too (see CLAUDE.md rule on help/topics.ts + markdown).

## Discovered via

User asked: "why doesn't the warm vault go past ~6 GB with a 10 GB retention cap?" Traced to logical-vs-disk mismatch above.

description.new:
## Problem

The per-vault metadata strip currently lives **under** the chunk table's column header row, and is laid out as a wrapping inline-flex "sentence":

> FILE on GASTROLOG-8  5 chunks  448,659 records  RF=3  → GASTROLOG-6, GASTROLOG-1

This is hostile to scanning. The operator reads column headers (CHUNK ID / TIME RANGE / STATUS / RECORDS / SIZE), then hits a sentence-shaped row of badges and numbers that have no relationship to those columns, then finally hits the actual chunk rows. The vault-level summary is the most important orientation info on the page and it's buried under the table header pretending to be a row.

Source: [frontend/src/components/inspector/VaultCard.tsx:281-326](frontend/src/components/inspector/VaultCard.tsx#L281-L326) (the `<tr>` with the colSpan-5 inline-flex span at line 290).

## Goals

1. **Reorder.** Vault metadata renders **above** the chunk table's column header, not as a pseudo-row inside the table.
2. **Restructure.** Replace the inline-flex sentence with a labeled grid / definition-list layout. Each fact gets a label and a value, scannable column-by-column.
3. **Add the missing facts** an operator actually needs to assess the vault at a glance:
   - **Disk bytes** (sum of `ChunkMeta.DiskBytes`) — "how much storage is this vault consuming on this node"
   - **Logical bytes** (sum of `ChunkMeta.Bytes`) — pairs with disk to show compression ratio and aligns with the retention cap (see gastrolog-3gewc)
   - **Cloud bytes** when applicable — same split for cloud-backed chunks
   - **Records/sec ingest rate** — derived from ingest counter delta over a rolling window (already on backend in `NodeStats` / orchestrator counters)
   - **Sparkline** — ingest rate over the last N minutes, inline, single-row height. Quiet by default, no axes, just a shape.
   - Retention policy summary inline ("size: 10 GB logical" / "ttl: 7d" / "count: 1000") so the operator can compare current usage against the cap without leaving this page.

## Proposed layout (rough)

```
┌─ hot-vault ────────────────────────────────────  [5 chunks]  [448,659 records]  ⚙ ─┐
│                                                                                   │
│  TYPE        file on GASTROLOG-8 → GASTROLOG-6, GASTROLOG-1   RF 3                │
│  RETENTION   size 10 GB logical · ttl 24h                                         │
│  STORAGE     6.8 GB on disk · 10.3 GB logical · — cloud                           │
│  INGEST      ▁▂▃▅▇▆▄▃▂▁▂▃▄  1,245 rec/s · 1.2 MB/s                                │
│                                                                                   │
│  ─── chunks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────   │
│  CHUNK ID         TIME RANGE          STATUS       RECORDS    SIZE                │
│  06f2g6up…7kgi8   May 14 22:09:34…    active 3     12,639     3.2 MB              │
│  ...                                                                              │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Exact labels and grouping are up for refinement, but the principle is: each row is **LABEL  VALUE**, top-aligned, monospace numbers, three-level text hierarchy (label = muted, value = normal, key numbers = bright).

## Notes / things to verify before implementing

- **Backend stats:** `GetStats` already returns `DataBytes` and `SealedChunks` per vault ([backend/internal/server/vault_info.go:154](backend/internal/server/vault_info.go#L154)). Adding logical-vs-disk split is the proto change tracked separately by **gastrolog-3gewc** — that issue is a prerequisite for the storage row above.
- **Ingest rate:** check whether per-vault rate is already aggregated in `PeerState` route stats / orchestrator counters. If not, this needs a new stat to flow up. Per multi-node memory rules, **must aggregate via PeerState broadcast** — single-node ingest counters won't reflect ingesters on other nodes.
- **Sparkline:** prefer reusing whatever histogram / chart primitive the dashboard already uses (search for existing sparkline / mini-chart components before writing one). Re-use the existing CSS palette tokens — no raw hex.
- **React Compiler:** no `useMemo` / `useCallback`; let the compiler handle memoization.
- **Help system:** if this exposes new operator-facing concepts (logical vs disk, cloud bytes), update the relevant help topic + markdown.
- **CLI parity:** `gastrolog inspect vault` and friends should expose the same numbers. Don't ship UI-only.

## Acceptance

- Vault metadata renders above the column header, not inside the table.
- Layout is a labeled grid / definition-list, not a wrapping inline sentence.
- Storage row shows disk bytes, logical bytes, and cloud bytes separately (depends on gastrolog-3gewc landing first or in parallel).
- Ingest rate (rec/s and bytes/s) shown per vault, aggregated across all cluster nodes (multi-node verified).
- Sparkline shows ingest activity over a rolling window. Quiet styling, no axes.
- Retention policy summary surfaced inline with current values, in units matching the cap (logical bytes for size cap).
- Works on all cluster nodes regardless of vault leader location.
- New multi-node test asserts ingest rate aggregation reflects ingesters on remote nodes.

## Discovered via

User screenshot review: hot-vault details row under column header reads like a sentence and lacks key numbers (disk/cloud bytes, ingest rate). Operator-hostile in incident-pressure scenarios.

description.new:
## Goal

Refactor leader-side replication dispatch to one FIFO writer goroutine per `(vault, follower)` pair, drop per-record bidi acks on the hot path, and simplify the documented ack contract to **"durable on the leader at ack time; cross-replica durability provided by the protocol up to retention."**

This is **step 1 of the gastrolog-617m6 reconcile-at-seal epic.** See parent c3–c7 for full design. Standalone refactor — no protocol change yet. The FIFO invariant is the precondition that makes the rolling-hash protocol from steps 3+ deterministic.

## Why

Today's leader-side dispatch is not strictly FIFO per `(vault, follower)`:

- `fireAndForgetRemote` (`backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_ops.go:547`) does `wg.Wait()` per record → ordering preserved per target. OK.
- `ackAfterReplication` (`backend/internal/orchestrator/replication.go:69`) runs in its own goroutine, parallel with the next record's dispatch. The per-target mutex in `ChunkReplicator.send` serializes the wire-send but is **not FIFO** — two concurrent ack-gated dispatches can race on the lock and land in either order on the wire.

The reconcile-at-seal protocol (steps 3+) folds a rolling `xxh3` hash over the active chunk's record sequence on every replica. The fold is order-sensitive. If leader-side dispatch is not FIFO, two replicas can see the same records in different orders → hashes diverge → reconcile fires on every seal, defeating the "rare path" assumption.

We also collapse the two ack paths: with reconcile-at-seal as the cross-replica durability proof, per-record follower→leader acks become redundant. Drop the `Record.WaitForReplica` field and the entire `pendingAcks` / `replicationTask` machinery.

## Design

### Per-(vault, follower) stream lifecycle

- Each leader maintains one outbound stream per `(vault, follower)` pair.
- One **writer goroutine** drains a bounded FIFO queue → `SendMsg` on the stream.
- One **reader goroutine** consumes whatever the follower sends back. Its only job: detect protocol errors / stream EOF / gRPC keepalive failure and call `closeStream` + `bumpReplicaBackoff`. No per-record decoding.
- gRPC keepalives (already enabled cluster-wide) handle "TCP died but no application traffic" detection.

### Enqueue contract

- Append path → enqueue record into each follower's stream queue.
- Rotation path → enqueue `SEAL N` into each follower's stream queue **before returning from rotate**. Ensures wire order: `... record_k (chunk N), SEAL N, record_{k+1} (chunk N+1) ...` on every follower.
- Bounded queue size. Default policy per c6: **drop on overflow** (slow followers fall behind silently; reconcile-at-seal catches them up at seal time). Increment a per-stream `enqueue_drops` counter and log at info on first drop in a window.

### Ack contract simplification

- `cm.Append` succeeds locally → ingester gets the ack. Single durability point.
- No per-record waiting for follower acknowledgments anywhere on the ingest hot path.
- Document the contract (deferred to step 7 of the epic; just note here that the user-visible behavior changes).

### Code that dies

- `Record.WaitForReplica` field in `backend/internal/chunk/types.go`.
- `pendingAcks` / `replicationTask` / `forwardTask` plumbing in orchestrator.
- `ackAfterReplication` goroutine path (`backend/internal/orchestrator/replication.go:69`).
- The `WaitForReplica`-driven branching at `AppendToVault` (`backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_ops.go:891-897`).
- RELP / HTTP X-Wait-Ack code paths setting `WaitForReplica` (grep `WaitForReplica` for the full list).
- The per-record `wg.Wait()` in `fireAndForgetRemote`.

### Code that lives, refactored

- `ChunkReplicator.send` (`backend/internal/cluster/chunk_replicator.go`) — driven now by the writer goroutine drain, not by per-call mutex acquisition.
- `fireAndForgetRemote` → renamed / inlined as the enqueue helper.
- `ImportSealedChunk` (`backend/internal/cluster/chunk_replicator.go:207`) — **stays for now**; killed in step 6 of the epic after reconcile-at-seal makes it unreachable.

## Acceptance

- Every `(vault, follower)` pair has exactly one writer goroutine and one reader goroutine.
- Wire order on every follower matches leader-side enqueue order, demonstrated by a test that ingests N records + rotations across a 4-node cluster (`setupMultiNode`) and asserts the follower-applied record sequence equals the leader's local sequence.
- `Record.WaitForReplica` field and all consumers are deleted.
- `pendingAcks`, `replicationTask`, `forwardTask`, `ackAfterReplication` are deleted.
- `enqueue_drops` counter is exposed per `(vault, follower)` stream; a slow-follower test (artificial sleep in the follower's apply path) shows ingest does not block on the leader and `enqueue_drops` increments on the slow target only.
- Existing replication tests pass with the new dispatch (`backend/internal/orchestrator/replication_test.go`, `forward_test.go`, `reliability_ingest_lock_test.go`).
- `just backend audit` passes (race + lint + vet + deadcode).
- No protocol additions yet — `CmdSealChunk`, `applySealChunk`, FSM state shape, etc. are unchanged.

## Test coverage required

Per CLAUDE.md "Test Coverage — MANDATORY": all dimensions.

- **Single-node**: dispatch refactor doesn't regress single-node ingest (existing tests cover this).
- **Multi-node**: FIFO order preserved across a 4-node placement; rotation `SEAL N` lands before any `chunk N+1` record on every follower.
- **Happy path**: ack returns to ingester after local durability only; never waits for followers.
- **Unhappy path**: follower-side stream EOF → reader goroutine closes the stream + bumps backoff; subsequent enqueues short-circuit until backoff expires.
- **Edge cases**: queue full → drop + counter increment, no ingest block; rotate path enqueues SEAL between record_k and record_{k+1} even under load; restart survives in-flight enqueues (lost on restart by design — pre-rotation records that hadn't reached the follower are subject to reconcile-at-seal at next seal).

## Out of scope

- The rolling-hash fold itself (step 3).
- Hash compare on `applySealChunk` (step 3).
- Reconcile sub-protocol (steps 4–5).
- Killing `ImportSealedChunk` (step 6).
- User-facing documentation (step 7) — note the contract change in the commit body and tag the docs work for step 7.

## Holes addressed

- **C1.1 (hash determinism)** — closed by this step's FIFO invariant.
- **#8 (slow-follower policy)** — closed by drop-on-overflow.

description.new:
## Goal

Make every code path that appends a record to an active chunk's record sequence go through a **single canonical append-and-fold function**, and enforce that with a compile-time + runtime check. Lays the groundwork for the rolling `xxh3` hash in step 3 of gastrolog-617m6.

**Step 2 of the gastrolog-617m6 reconcile-at-seal epic.** See parent c3–c7 for full design.

## Why

The rolling-hash protocol (step 3) folds `running = xxh3(running || event_id_bytes)` on every active-chunk append. The fold is order-sensitive **and append-path-sensitive**: if any code path appends to the active chunk without going through the canonical function, that replica's hash diverges from the leader's even though the records are identical.

The leader-side fold happens at **local-append time** (the leader does not Raft-apply its own outbound replication RPCs). For the leader's hash to match every follower's hash, every leader-side append into an active chunk MUST go through the single canonical path that also folds the hash.

## Design

### Canonical path

Define one function in the chunk manager that:
1. Appends the record to the active chunk's local files.
2. Folds the record's `EventID` into the active chunk's running hash.
3. Increments `RecordCount` / `Bytes` in the chunk-manager-local view.

Existing append entry points (`cm.Append`, the Raft-apply path for follower `AppendRecords`, the rotation handoff path) all converge to this one function.

### Paths to audit

Per c4, these paths must be checked or refactored to converge through the canonical path:

- `cm.Append` — the normal record-stream path. Already canonical; verify.
- `ImportRecords` (`backend/internal/chunk/file/`) — creates a fresh sealed chunk, NOT the active one. The hash fold does not apply here. Verify it cannot accidentally land on an active chunk.
- **Drain queue replay on startup** — does this write records back via `cm.Append`, or via some other path? Audit and refactor if non-canonical.
- **Retention transition source-read** — should NOT append to an active chunk on the destination; it imports as sealed via `ImportRecords`. Verify.
- **gastrolog-2eclw orphan-active cure** — any "transient multiple actives" path that takes appends needs to either fold the hash on the orphan too, or be explicitly grandfathered (see C1.5 resolution in c7: orphan-swept seals carry hash=0 sentinel). Document the choice for the orphan path here.

### Enforcement

Two layers:

1. **Static**: rename the underlying mutator to something like `appendAndFold` and make the lower-level "write to file without folding" function unexported / package-private to the chunk manager. Callers outside the chunk manager cannot bypass the fold.

2. **Runtime invariant**: in `applySealChunk` (step 3), every active-form whose record count is non-zero must have a non-default running hash. Detect default-hash + non-zero count as a protocol violation and panic on the leader / log+halt on followers. Orphan-swept seals (sentinel hash=0 via the explicit grandfather path) are the only exception.

Optionally add a lint check (`semgrep` or `gofmt`-style AST rule) so future agents cannot reintroduce a non-canonical path.

## Acceptance

- A single exported function on the chunk manager is the only way to mutate an active chunk's record sequence.
- Every existing append path is audited. The audit findings are documented in the commit body (one line per path: canonical / converged / sealed-only / grandfathered).
- Tests demonstrate that bypass attempts (e.g., a deliberately-broken test that writes records without folding) trip the runtime invariant.
- No protocol changes shipped yet — this issue is the audit + plumbing.

## Test coverage required

Per CLAUDE.md "Test Coverage — MANDATORY":

- **Single-node**: canonical append correctly folds; runtime invariant detects bypass attempts.
- **Multi-node**: drain replay on startup is canonical; retention transitions don't append-to-active on the destination.
- **Happy path**: every normal append routes through `appendAndFold`.
- **Unhappy path**: deliberately-bypassed append in test code trips the runtime invariant cleanly.
- **Edge cases**: empty chunk → no fold needed; orphan-swept seal path → sentinel hash=0 path documented and tested.

## Out of scope

- The hash data structure itself (step 3 — this step just routes through a stub `appendAndFold` that has a placeholder hash field).
- `applySealChunk` hash compare logic (step 3).
- Reconcile (steps 4–5).

## Holes addressed

- Sets up the **single-path append invariant** (c4 hole #5 in disguise; load-bearing for step 3).

description.new:
## Goal

Add a per-chunk rolling `xxh3` hash as durable state in the vault-ctl FSM (`backend/internal/vaultraft/vaultctlfsm/fsm.go`). The hash is folded over the chunk's `EventID` sequence on every append, persists across snapshots, applies to both active and sealed chunks, and is shipped in the `CmdSealChunk` payload so followers can compare on apply.

On hash mismatch at `applySealChunk`, the chunk transitions to a `needs-reconcile` sub-state and the seal **proceeds** with a marker — no synchronous network I/O in apply. (Reconcile execution itself is step 4; this issue just wires the detection + state transition + a stub trigger that logs.)

**Step 3 of the gastrolog-617m6 reconcile-at-seal epic.** See parent c3–c7 for full design.

## Why

`EventID` is already canonical and globally unique (`backend/internal/chunk/types.go:229`). Folding it into a running 8-byte hash gives a constant-size, order-sensitive proof-of-content for any chunk. Shipping the leader's final hash in `CmdSealChunk` lets every follower's `applySealChunk` detect divergence cheaply. Persisting the hash in FSM state — for both active AND sealed chunks — turns reconcile into a chunk-state property rather than a seal-time event (per c5):

- Late-arriving replicas apply `CmdSealChunk` optimistically; if local hash mismatches canonical, transition to `needs-reconcile` and run the merge async (closes C2.7).
- Background integrity sweeps recompute the hash over a sealed chunk and detect silent corruption against the FSM-canonical value (closes the broader integrity story).
- Operator "verify this chunk" RPC becomes trivial (step 5).

## Design

### Hash combiner

- `running = xxh3(running || event_id_bytes)`. Order-sensitive sequential fold.
- `event_id_bytes` = canonical 16-byte encoding of `(IngesterID, NodeID, IngestTS, IngestSeq)`. Use the same encoding the dedup operator uses; do not invent a new one.

### Storage

- 8 bytes per chunk stored in the FSM manifest entry alongside `RecordCount` / `Bytes`.
- Survives snapshot install (`fsm.go` snapshot/restore paths).
- Recomputable on demand from the chunk's record sequence — used by integrity sweeps and bootstrap repair (step 5 wires those triggers; the recompute primitive ships here).

### Append-side fold

- Wired into the canonical `appendAndFold` from step 2.
- On the leader: folded at local-append time.
- On followers: folded at `AppendRecords`-apply time (Raft apply is serial per group, so the fold is deterministic given step 1's FIFO wire order).

### `CmdSealChunk` payload extension

- Add `RunningHash uint64` (or `[]byte` for forward-compat) to the proto.
- Leader populates it from its active-chunk state at seal proposal.
- Followers' `applySealChunk` compares against their own running hash.

### Apply behavior on mismatch

- Match → normal seal. Record `RunningHash` in FSM sealed-chunk state.
- Mismatch → record canonical hash in FSM, mark chunk `state=Sealed, needs_reconcile=true`. Local chunk manager keeps the active-form **mutable** (or holds it in a side-state — implementer's call, must be reversible by step 4's reconcile). Log + emit a one-shot alert per (vault, chunk).
- Reconcile execution is the **next issue** (step 4). This issue just lands the state transition + a stub trigger that logs that reconcile would run.

### Orphan-sweep grandfather (C1.5)

- `SweepIdleActiveChunks` produces `AnnounceSeal` carrying `RunningHash = 0` (all-zeros sentinel).
- `applySealChunk` interprets hash=0 as "skip verification; recovery seal." Records the orphan-swept flag in FSM for audit visibility.
- Runtime / lint check: only the orphan-sweep path may produce hash=0. Every other seal must produce a real hash; an accidentally-zero hash from a normal path is a protocol violation.

## Acceptance

- Active and sealed chunks in the FSM carry a `RunningHash` field; it survives snapshot install.
- `CmdSealChunk` carries the leader's canonical hash; followers compare on apply.
- Match → normal seal flow proceeds unchanged.
- Mismatch → chunk enters `needs-reconcile` state, alert + log fire, reconcile is **stubbed** (logs "would reconcile chunk X"). The chunk is NOT lost or silently sealed-degraded.
- Recompute-on-demand primitive (walk records, fold hash, compare to FSM-canonical) is available and tested.
- Orphan-swept seal path (`SweepIdleActiveChunks`) ships hash=0 sentinel; runtime check rejects hash=0 from any other path.
- Steady-state ingest regresses by no more than ~1% from the hash update (acceptance criterion from the original issue body).

## Test coverage required

Per CLAUDE.md "Test Coverage — MANDATORY":

- **Single-node**: canonical fold matches the recompute-from-records primitive.
- **Multi-node**: 4-node cluster (`setupMultiNode`) where leader and all followers fold the same record sequence in the same order → hashes match at seal.
- **Multi-node forced divergence**: harness drops some `AppendRecords` to one replica → hashes mismatch at seal → that replica enters `needs-reconcile` state cleanly, others seal normally.
- **Happy path**: normal seal → all hashes match → all replicas seal.
- **Unhappy path**: leader proposes seal while a follower is behind → follower enters `needs-reconcile`; cluster continues.
- **Edge cases**: snapshot install propagates hash; orphan-swept seal path skips compare via sentinel; bypass attempt (test code with a non-canonical append) trips the runtime invariant from step 2.

## Out of scope

- Reconcile execution (step 4 — k-way merge + cross-replica fetch + local rebuild).
- Reconcile trigger wiring (step 5).
- `ImportSealedChunk` removal (step 6).

## Holes addressed

- Detection half of seal-time mismatch + late-apply mismatch (C2.7).
- Foundation for background integrity sweep (step 5) and operator-triggered verify (step 5).

description.new:
## Goal

Implement a generic `Reconcile(chunkID)` operation that produces a byte-identical sealed chunk on every replica via a chunk-scoped k-way merge over cross-replica record streams, deduped by `EventID` and sorted by EventID-tuple order. Single implementation, multiple callers (step 5 wires the four triggers).

**Step 4 of the gastrolog-617m6 reconcile-at-seal epic.** See parent c3–c7 for full design — especially c5 (state-driven shape) and c4 (set-difference protocol).

## Why

Per c5: every replica has the same input records via the FIFO-disciplined real-time stream from step 1. When a chunk enters `needs-reconcile`, the protocol is symmetric — each replica independently runs the merge against its peers and arrives at the same answer because EventID-sorted union with dedup is deterministic. No leader has chunk-data authority post-mismatch; the leader's role narrows to proposing the protocol transitions (handled in step 5).

## Design

### Inputs

- `chunkID` to reconcile.
- The chunk's placement set from the FSM.
- The chunk's canonical hash from the FSM (written by step 3 on seal apply).

### Algorithm (each replica runs independently)

1. Open a **chunk-scoped cross-replica cursor** to each peer in placement. Reuses the same RPC the query engine uses for cross-node search — this is already a streaming cursor of `(EventID, Record)` pairs ordered by EventID.
2. Also open a local cursor over the replica's own active-form / partially-sealed copy.
3. Run a streaming **k-way merge** over all cursors, deduped by `EventID` (the query engine's `dedup` operator semantics).
4. Stream the merged record sequence into a **fresh local sealed-chunk write**, computing the rolling `xxh3` hash as records are written.
5. On completion, compare the computed hash to the canonical hash from the FSM:
   - Match → atomically swap the new sealed chunk in for the local active-form / pre-reconcile copy. Transition FSM state to `Sealed, needs_reconcile=false`.
   - Mismatch → **stall the chunk in `needs-reconcile` state** (C1.2 resolution). Next sweep tick retries. Log + alert.

### Streaming, not buffering

- Memory rule from MEMORY.md: never slurp into the heap. The merge is record-by-record across streaming cursors; the destination write is a streaming chunk writer; no `[]Record` buffer.
- Worst-case memory = small constant (one record per cursor + the merge heap header), independent of chunk size.

### Partial-failure semantics (C1.2)

- Peer unreachable mid-merge → abort this attempt cleanly, leave chunk in `needs-reconcile`, retry next sweep.
- Peer's own copy in `needs-reconcile` → same; treat that peer as temporarily unavailable for reconcile sourcing.
- Placement change mid-reconcile → reread placement, restart against the new set.
- No partial seal, no degraded-seal marker; the chunk is fully reconciled or stays needs-reconcile.

### Record-level fetch transport

- Per c4 §2 + c5: no new RPC. The existing per-(vault, follower) FIFO stream from step 1 (its bidirectional shape per c4 §1) carries record-level `RequestSpecificRecord(eventID)` requests when the local replica is acting as a consumer of a peer's stream.
- For chunk-scoped cursor reads (the dominant reconcile path), reuse the cross-node query cursor RPC — `eng.Search` peer fan-out already does this. Reconcile is just a different consumer of the same primitive.

### Position-stability rule (C1.3)

- Reconcile rebuilds the chunk's record sequence in EventID-sorted order. Local positions WILL change for any record that was at a non-EventID-sorted position in the divergent copy.
- That is fine because positions are not stable identifiers; consumers use `EventID` for cross-time identity (documented in step 7).
- Cursor-based readers (live tail) operate on the active-form before seal; reconcile fires on sealed chunks. Sealed cursors are invalidated via the existing chunk-lifecycle / mmap invalidation path (same way as chunk deletion).

## Acceptance

- `Reconcile(chunkID)` is a single function callable from the four trigger sites in step 5.
- Streaming-only: heap memory used during reconcile is bounded by a small constant regardless of chunk size.
- On forced divergence (step 3's harness extended), `Reconcile` produces a byte-identical sealed chunk on every replica.
- After reconcile, every replica's recomputed rolling hash equals the canonical hash in the FSM.
- Partial failure → chunk stays in `needs-reconcile`; next call retries cleanly.
- Reconcile does NOT block other ingest, other chunks' seals, or query reads.

## Test coverage required

Per CLAUDE.md "Test Coverage — MANDATORY":

- **Single-node**: not meaningful (reconcile requires peers). Verify the merge primitive in isolation with synthetic peer cursors.
- **Multi-node**: 4-node cluster forced-divergence test → reconcile produces byte-identical chunks on every replica.
- **Multi-node, late joiner**: node joins mid-stream with no copy of the chunk → reconcile pulls the full record set from peers and seals correctly (also exercises C2.7 once step 5 wires the late-apply trigger).
- **Happy path**: divergent → reconcile → match.
- **Unhappy path**: peer dies mid-reconcile → chunk stays needs-reconcile; next attempt with peer back succeeds.
- **Edge cases**: empty divergence (one replica has zero records for the chunk); all-replicas-divergent (every replica has a different subset of records); reconcile of an orphan-swept chunk (sentinel hash=0) should be a no-op or refuse (record the choice in tests).

## Out of scope

- Wiring the four trigger sources to call `Reconcile` (step 5).
- `ImportSealedChunk` removal (step 6).

## Holes addressed

- C1.2 (partial reconcile failure) — closed by stall-in-state + retry.
- C1.3 (cursor reordering) — closed by EventID-as-stable-identity rule.
- C1.6 (EventID list cost under storms) — closed by streaming merge (no manifest payload).
- C2.7 — half closed (the reconcile primitive is the answer; step 5 wires the late-apply trigger).

title.new: Wire four reconcile triggers: seal mismatch, late-apply, integrity sweep, operator RPC

description.new:
## Goal

Wire all four trigger sources for the `Reconcile(chunkID)` operation from step 4:

1. **Seal-time hash mismatch** — `applySealChunk` detects mismatch (step 3 stub) → schedule reconcile.
2. **Late-apply hash mismatch (C2.7)** — replica applying `CmdSealChunk` after a partition / restart sees its local hash doesn't match the canonical → schedule reconcile.
3. **Background integrity sweep** — periodically recompute hash on sampled / systematically-walked sealed chunks, mismatch → schedule reconcile.
4. **Operator RPC** — explicit `ReconcileChunk(chunkID)` admin command for incident response, post-restore verification, or "cluster doesn't trust this chunk."

**Step 5 of the gastrolog-617m6 reconcile-at-seal epic.** See parent c3–c7 for full design — especially c5 §2 (state-driven reconcile, four triggers, one implementation).

## Why

Per c5, the rolling hash being durable FSM state turns reconciliation into a chunk-state property rather than a seal-time event. That collapses several previously separate problems into one trigger + one implementation:

- C2.7 (late-arriving replica) → just another trigger.
- Silent corruption detection → integrity sweep trigger.
- Operator-triggered repair → operator RPC trigger.
- Bootstrap / restore validation → falls out for free; restored copies fail hash check, integrity sweep schedules reconcile.

## Design

### Trigger 1: seal-time mismatch

Already half-implemented as a stub in step 3. Replace the stub with a scheduling call:

- `applySealChunk` mismatch → mark FSM `needs_reconcile=true` + emit a one-shot work item to the local reconcile scheduler (NOT inside the apply — apply schedules, doesn't execute).
- A local reconcile worker drains the queue, calls `Reconcile(chunkID)`, updates FSM on completion via a `CmdReconcileComplete` (or equivalent) Raft command so all replicas observe the final state transition.

### Trigger 2: late-apply mismatch (C2.7)

- The same `applySealChunk` mismatch handler covers this case — a late-applying replica running through replay reaches `CmdSealChunk` apply with a stale local hash. Same code path schedules reconcile asynchronously.
- Apply does NOT block on network I/O. The mismatch is just FSM state + a scheduled work item.

### Trigger 3: background integrity sweep

- New periodic task in `backend/internal/orchestrator/vault_lifecycle_reconciler.go` (next to existing sweeps like `SweepLocalOrphans`, `SweepIdleActiveChunks`, `SweepStalePendingDeleteAcks`).
- For each sealed chunk owned by this node, recompute the rolling hash (cheap streaming read using the recompute primitive from step 3). Compare to the FSM-canonical value.
- Mismatch → schedule reconcile via the same scheduler.
- Cadence: configurable; default conservative (e.g., one chunk per minute per node, or sampled at a low rate). Goal is steady drumbeat, not burst I/O.
- Skip orphan-swept chunks (sentinel hash=0 per C1.5).

### Trigger 4: operator RPC

- New Connect RPC: `ReconcileChunk(VaultID, ChunkID) → (Status)`.
- Operator-only path; authenticated cluster admin.
- Schedules reconcile via the same scheduler; returns immediately. Status RPC (or follow up with another existing chunk-state RPC) shows current `needs_reconcile` state for visibility.
- CLI: `gastrolog reconcile chunk <vault>/<chunk>` (Cobra-wired in `backend/cmd/gastrolog/`).
- UI surface: optional for this issue; if added, lives in the chunk-detail view in the frontend. Per CLAUDE.md UI/CLI parity rule, if RPC + CLI ships, UI surface follows in the same PR or as a tracked follow-up.

### Scheduler

- One local reconcile worker pool per node (small — reconcile is I/O bound, not CPU bound). Default 2 concurrent workers per node.
- Backoff on repeated failures for the same chunk (chunk stays in `needs-reconcile`; next sweep tick retries with exponential delay).
- Reconcile completion fires a Raft command (`CmdReconcileComplete` or reuse an existing transition) to clear `needs_reconcile` in FSM on all replicas.

## Acceptance

- `Reconcile` is the single execution primitive; four triggers schedule it.
- Seal-time mismatch → reconcile schedules and completes; FSM `needs_reconcile` clears cluster-wide.
- Late-arriving replica → applies `CmdSealChunk` cleanly, transitions to `needs-reconcile`, reconciles in the background, FSM clears.
- Integrity sweep recomputes hash on sealed chunks; mismatch schedules reconcile; cadence is configurable and metered.
- Operator RPC + CLI ship; calling them schedules reconcile and is observable in chunk state.
- No apply-time network I/O. Reconcile is always async-post-apply.

## Test coverage required

Per CLAUDE.md "Test Coverage — MANDATORY":

- **Single-node**: integrity sweep correctness against a deliberately-corrupted sealed chunk.
- **Multi-node**: all four triggers exercised in a 4-node cluster.
- **Happy path**: seal-time match → no reconcile scheduled; sweep finds no mismatches; operator RPC on a healthy chunk is a no-op.
- **Unhappy path**: seal mismatch → reconcile fires → cluster converges. Sweep finds corrupted chunk → reconcile fires → cluster converges. Operator RPC against a chunk with unreachable peers → stays needs-reconcile, retried.
- **Edge cases**: late-applying replica through Raft replay (C2.7); chunk currently being read by a query while reconcile runs (must not break the reader); operator RPC against an orphan-swept chunk (refused or no-op, documented).

## Out of scope

- The `Reconcile` execution primitive itself (step 4).
- `ImportSealedChunk` removal (step 6).
- Documentation contract (step 7).

## Holes addressed

- C2.7 → fully closed.
- Silent corruption detection → addressed via integrity sweep trigger.
- Operator repair surface → addressed via operator RPC + CLI.

## Goal

Remove the sealed-chunk record-shipping subsystem (`ImportSealedChunk` and its supporting code paths) now that the reconcile-at-seal protocol (steps 1–5) makes leader→follower post-seal record transfers unreachable.

**Step 6 of the gastrolog-617m6 reconcile-at-seal epic.** See parent c5 §1 for why this can die. Strictly depends on steps 1–5 landing first.

## Why

Per c5: with FIFO-disciplined real-time replication (step 1) + rolling hash detection (step 3) + symmetric per-replica reconcile (step 4) + triggers wired (step 5), there is no remaining scenario where a leader needs to ship a complete sealed chunk's records to a follower. Either:

- The follower already has the same record sequence (happy path → both seal locally, hashes match).
- The follower's sequence diverges → reconcile fires → each replica independently rebuilds via the k-way merge against peers.

`ImportSealedChunk` was the workaround for "follower missing records at seal time; ship the canonical body." That workaround is now replaced by per-replica reconcile that doesn't require any leader→follower record transfer.

## Code that dies

Per c5 §1, the following are deletable end-to-end:

- `ImportSealedChunk` RPC handler (`backend/internal/cluster/chunk_replicator.go:207`).
- `ChunkReplicator.ImportSealedChunk` caller.
- `scheduleReplication`, `replicateSealedChunk`, `replicateToTarget` in `backend/internal/orchestrator/replication.go` and adjacent files.
- The "buffer the whole chunk in memory" path that hit the gRPC 128MB limit.
- Legacy `DeleteChunk`-via-stream path (if still present).
- Proto definitions for the import RPC + any helper messages exclusive to it; renumber remaining tags per CLAUDE.md (no `reserved` declarations).
- Tests covering import behavior (replaced by reconcile tests already written in steps 3–5).

## What stays

- Real-time `AppendRecords` stream (FIFO-disciplined per step 1).
- Cross-replica cursor reads (already exists for query; reused by reconcile in step 4).
- `RequestReplicaCatchup` from gastrolog-19241 (chunk-granularity; now extended to record-granularity in step 4 if needed).
- `ChunkReplicator` as a wrapper — keep the type, drop the dead methods.

## Approach

1. Confirm reconcile (step 5) is wired and tested in steady-state cluster operation. **All cluster tests in the multinode harness must pass without ever exercising `ImportSealedChunk`** — verify with a panic-on-call assertion temporarily inserted into the import handler, then remove the call site + handler + proto fields.
2. Re-run proto generation (`just gen`) after removing fields. Renumber tags. No `reserved` per CLAUDE.md.
3. Sweep call sites — orchestrator, ChunkReplicator, tests, CLI, scripts. Per MEMORY.md `[feedback_rename_sweep_grep_scope.md]`: grep beyond `src/` and `docs/` — check `scripts/`, `e2e/`, `justfile`, `prime.md`, fixture files.
4. Update tests: any test that referenced `ImportSealedChunk` should now reference reconcile or be deleted as redundant.

## Acceptance

- `git grep -i ImportSealedChunk` returns zero hits across the whole repo (excluding historical commit messages).
- `git grep -i "import.*sealed.*chunk"` returns zero false positives.
- All multinode tests pass (`just backend audit`).
- Sealed-chunk record transfers no longer happen on the wire; confirm via a multinode test that asserts `ChunkReplicator` records zero `ImportSealedChunk` invocations across forced-divergence + late-joiner + seal scenarios.
- Memory: the "buffer the whole chunk in memory" path is gone; confirm by RSS regression test or by code review (search for any remaining `[]Record` accumulators at sealed-chunk scope).
- Frontend / CLI documentation referring to the import RPC are updated or removed.

## Test coverage required

Per CLAUDE.md "Test Coverage — MANDATORY":

- **Single-node**: not applicable (no replication paths to remove).
- **Multi-node**: forced-divergence + late-joiner + post-restore scenarios all converge via reconcile, no `ImportSealedChunk` calls observed.
- **Happy path**: normal seals on a healthy cluster — no `ImportSealedChunk` calls.
- **Unhappy path**: every previous "follower missing chunk" scenario now resolves via reconcile.
- **Edge cases**: stale follower in placement that hasn't observed any records for the chunk → reconcile pulls the full set from peers; orphan-swept chunks bypass reconcile per C1.5 grandfather.

## Out of scope

- Any new feature work.
- Documentation contract (step 7).

## Holes addressed

- This is the cleanup half of c5's "ImportSealedChunk dies entirely" finding.

description.new:
## Goal

Land user- and operator-facing documentation that reflects the new cluster-durability shape introduced by gastrolog-617m6. Three documents (or three sections of existing documents) must ship before this epic is considered done:

1. **Ack contract** — "ack means durable on the leader; cross-replica durability provided by the protocol up to retention."
2. **Position non-stability** — `RecordRef{ChunkID, Pos}` is not stable across reconcile; use `EventID` for cross-time identity.
3. **Partial-failure semantics** — chunks may stall in `needs-reconcile`; visible in operator tooling; reconcile retries via background sweep until partition heals or placement changes.

**Step 7 of the gastrolog-617m6 reconcile-at-seal epic.** Per CLAUDE.md `[feedback_update_query_docs.md]` and `[feedback_docs_arent_historical.md]`, docs describe the current system (steady state), not its evolution. No "previously," "in earlier versions," "we used to."

## Why

The user-visible contract changes meaningfully in this epic:

- Acks no longer wait for follower replication (was: optional via `Record.WaitForReplica`; now: never).
- Record position within a chunk is no longer a stable identifier (was: arrival order on the leader; now: may rebuild in EventID order if reconcile fires).
- Some chunks may visibly stall in `needs-reconcile` during cluster instability (new operator-facing state).

Each of these has compatibility implications for users of the API and the operator tooling. Without docs, operators will see new states and reach for the wrong remediation; users may build clients that assume `Pos` stability.

## Design

### Doc 1: Ack contract

Lives in `docs/` (likely `docs/durability.md` or a section of an existing operator guide — check what already exists; do not duplicate). Content from c4 §5:

> A successful append acknowledgment from gastrolog means the record has been durably written to the vault leader's local storage. The record is then fire-and-forget streamed to placement followers' active chunks as soon as possible — best-effort, no per-record acknowledgment. At chunk seal time the reconcile-at-seal protocol verifies that all replicas hold the same set of records via a rolling EventID hash; any divergence (dropped record, reordering, missed write during a transient outage) is detected and repaired before the sealed chunk is fully committed cluster-wide. If at-multiple-replica durability before-ack is required for your workload, gastrolog is not the right system.

### Doc 2: Position non-stability

Lives in the query / record-reference API docs. Content from c7 §C1.3:

> Record positions within a chunk are not stable identifiers. They may change if reconciliation rebuilds the chunk (happens at seal-time hash mismatch or background integrity check). Consumers that need stable cross-time record identity should use `EventID`. The `RecordRef{ChunkID, Pos}` references returned in query results are valid until reconcile fires on the referenced chunk.

### Doc 3: Partial-failure semantics

Lives in operator runbook content (likely `docs/operations/` or wherever existing chunk-lifecycle states are documented). Content from c7 §C1.2 + step 5:

- A chunk in `needs-reconcile` state is sealed-but-not-finalized. Reads against it should treat the latest reconcile-completed version on the local replica as authoritative; absence on the local replica means fetch via cross-replica cursor.
- Reconcile retries automatically via background sweep. Manual remediation (operator RPC from step 5) is the lever for permanent partitions.
- Permanent stalls (peer permanently gone) are resolved by removing the peer from placement — the existing `SweepStalePendingDeleteAcks`-style mechanism then prunes the chunk's per-peer obligations and reconcile converges among the remaining replicas.

### Vocabulary

Per CLAUDE.md, before writing prose check `docs/ubiquitous_language.md`. New terms introduced by this epic:

- "Reconcile-at-seal" — the protocol family.
- "Rolling hash" — the per-chunk xxh3 fold over EventIDs.
- "Needs-reconcile" — the durable FSM sub-state.
- "Canonical hash" — the FSM-recorded hash for a chunk.
- "Orphan-swept seal" — recovery-path seal with sentinel hash=0.

Extend `docs/ubiquitous_language.md` in the same PR if these terms appear in user-facing prose. If they stay internal, no extension needed but record the decision in the commit body.

### Help page wiring

Per MEMORY.md "Always update help system":

- If any of these docs surface as `?` help in the UI, register a `helpTopicId`, a topic in `help/topics.ts`, and the markdown file in `help/`.
- If the operator RPC from step 5 surfaces a UI button, that surface needs help wiring too.

- Position-non-stability doc lives in the query / record-reference API docs.

- `docs/ubiquitous_language.md` is extended for any new terms in user-facing prose (or the omission is justified in the commit).
- Any UI surfaces from step 5 have `?` help wired per the help-system rule.
- No "previously" / "in earlier versions" / historical narration anywhere.

Documentation; no runtime tests required. Verify:

- Links to the new docs from any existing doc TOC / index.
- Markdown renders correctly (mermaid diagrams ok; ASCII box-drawing forbidden per `[feedback_mermaid_for_charts_and_schemas.md]`).

## Out of scope

- Code changes (all live in steps 1–6).
- New protocol decisions.

- Closes the documentation half of the epic — required before the parent (gastrolog-617m6) can be marked done.
